> **For agentic workers:** this plan is dispatched as a wave to a `ccrc-worker` session. Follow the `ccrc-worker` skill for the protocol: ack, claims, asks and wave-done. - **Safety subject (spec §6):** which tree `git worktree remove` may delete. It is one PR from a fresh child.
- **Deploy class (R42): `ccd/ccd` plus one server string. The fleet box moves first**, which is `ccrc rollout`'s default order, without `--server-first`.
  - `ccd/ccrc` changes only by one byte-identical line in its platform block (R4), which ccrc's own code never calls.
  - `server/src/wsaudit.ts` changes one sentence (R24).
  - No frame field and no field the server reads changes. Ids come from `*.uuid` names only (`server/src/registry.ts`, the `listedIds` filter). The reclaim audit document (and the expire one, under workspace-lifecycle's consent to R45's request) gains two additive keys, `legacyRows` and `pendingRows`, and no server reader is added. `legacyRows` counts the other rows whose field is in a `legacy-*` state, and `pendingRows` those whose field reads `pending`; an unmeasured field is in neither, and it holds the child (R75). There is no `FLEET_PROTO` bump and no coord.db migration. `pwa/**` and `agent/**` are untouched.
  - **Rollback:** an older ccd ignores `$REG/<id>.workdirid`, and its `_reg_purge` loop still unlinks it (every dot-free suffix).
  - **Re-upgrade:** a field written before the rollback either matches its logical spelling or reads stale or legacy. A valid field that went stale under the older ccd (the session respawned with no pane write) can only add a placement or a hold. It never releases a row (R12).
  - **The one-sentence server change:** in the window between the two boxes, the old server shows the old sentence for `worktree-remove-failed`. It is true of every failure the old ccd emits, and slightly incomplete for a new ccd's cwd refusals. Nothing is decided on it.

**Goal:** after this wave:
- **Every placement of another session's row against the child may only add a hold** (PI3 B, PI6 M4, PI7, PI8 B2):
  - the rows rung also places rows by **device and inode ancestry** of their resolved spelling;
  - it **holds the child unmeasured** when a mount stands at or under it, or one of its file system's roots lies at or under it;
  - it refuses a **link into `/proc`** (`unproc`), by raw target or by walked position;
  - it does all of this in **one bounded walk per call** (`WS_RECLAIM_WALK_S=5`). A walk that times out answers unmeasured, never "no row".
- **Each session records where it entered** (PI1 B, PI2 L1):
  - one field, `$REG/<id>.workdirid`, in the v1 grammar with a `pending` form;
  - the parent writes `pending` before every spawn, and the pane replaces it after its `cd` and before `exec`;
  - `start` and `ws-add` seed a valid value;
  - a valid field adds placements (P2's terminal SHARED included) and an unplaceable mismatch holds;
  - a pending or unreadable field holds;
  - a legacy field falls back to today's string rule plus current identity.
- **R54's gone-row recovery gains an identity moved-check** that may hold and never releases.
- **The main checkout is refused by identity too:** `-ef` at the ladder and at the owned check, and refusal-only identity in the record reader (PI10 O2).
- **One refusal-only cwd probe**, `_ws_cwd_users`, matches by path string against the PHYSICAL spelling of the tree (its parent resolved, its leaf not followed) OR by dev:ino ancestry (PI4 D). It is bounded, and ws-expire moves onto it. The reclaim and expiry tail asks it inside the post-kill wait (which only waits), and again before each standing forced removal.
- **The tail window is narrowed** (PI5 A). Directly before each standing nested checkout's and the child's `keep_of`, and again directly before each forced removal, the tail, in R55's order:
  - re-runs the cwd probe;
  - re-asks `_ws_reclaim_owned` whole;
  - re-derives the identities it recorded and compares them.

  The re-ask stands before W2's mount ask at each site, and owned's rows rung now reads the mount table itself, so W2's step-3 and step-4 asks become a backstop for a mount that appears in the instant after the re-ask (`w2-mount-asks-shadowed-by-the-reask`, P19).
- **The wordings are true** (PI7 P1): the `..` detail, the two `//` remedies ("restore", never "re-point") and the `unproc` clause.

## Global Constraints

Each line binds every task.

- **Fixtures and fixture HOMEs only.**
  - No test or scratch command runs ccd against the live `$HOME`. Every ccd call goes through `makePrHarness` or `makeCcdHarness`. Quote every path, and never pass an unquoted `~`.
  - Never touch tmux, `~/.cc-sessions`, `~/.cc-limits`, `~/.cc-tmp` or `claude-session@*`. The one exception is Task 0 Step 6's counts, under R34.
  - No `ccd ws-*` verb runs against a live box.
  - No test starts or attaches to a tmux server. The pane command is executed by a bash `tmux()` stub (`PANE_EXEC`).
- **The spawn census.**
  - Every new file whose name matches `/^ccd.*\.ts$/` falls under `ccd-workspaces.test.ts`'s containment scan. It spawns a shell only through the harness (`h.sh`, `h.run`). A case that runs the pane command under sh, zsh or fish runs that shell from inside a harness snippet.
  - Every new `ccd-collect-*.test.ts` takes its git `env:` from `inheritedEnv()`.
- **Mounts and process tables are faked, never made** (R35).
  - Mounts go through `MOUNTS_SEAM` with `realMounts` and appended lines.
  - Process tables are `$HOME/fp` fake roots through `_ws_expire_proc_root`, or `holdProc`/`holdCwd` real processes in fixture directories.
  - A bind is stood in by a symlink plus the `BIND_STANDIN` resolver wrapper (R10: the walk follows links).
  - No session runs a privileged container.
- **Darwin.**
  - The rows rung's mount request is omitted by ONE caller line, pinned by a forced-Darwin poison case (R13). W2's `_ws_removal_mounts_clear` guard stays the one spelling of its own text.
  - The ancestry arm stands alone on Darwin.
  - The cwd probe uses ws-expire's lsof arm, compared against the tree's physical spelling.
  - Every ccd-side stat goes through `_plat_devino` or `_plat_btime`. The pane writer's per-OS stat lives in the platform block.
  - A forced-Darwin case on a Linux host adds host-conditional shims (`process.platform === 'darwin' ? '' : SHIMS`). GNU `stat -f '%d:%i' DIR` treats the format as a file name and exits 1 (measured), so from Task 8 on every forced-Darwin full tail needs `DARWIN_IDENT_SHIMS` (both functions), and from Task 10 on `DARWIN_LSOF_STUB` (P13, R50).
- **Add-only (the wave's invariant).** No identity input may release a row, or turn a refusal into a pass, or turn a stronger refusal word into a weaker one (R71 and R75 except two shapes by name, the numbered departures `record-by-another-spelling-reads-unmeasured` and `record-two-spellings-reads-unmeasured`: each is a refusal either way, an added hold, and nothing is removed). Each one may only add a placement (SHARED, NESTED or THROUGH) or a hold (unmeasured). The fence (Task 1) is re-run after every task that edits `ccd/ccd`.
- **No overloaded null.** Each of these sets of answers stays distinct:
  - the field: `valid`, `pending`, `legacy-absent`, `legacy-stale`, `legacy-unparseable`, `legacy-link`, `unmeasured`;
  - the walk: complete, unmeasured (timeout, a failure, a short reply, a reply to a request list it was not given whole: R64, or a last request record with no NUL after it: R68);
  - a birth time: a number, `-` (the file system keeps none), `un` (the read failed). `un` is never read as `-` (P20);
  - a recorded path in the walk: `F ok`, `F gone` (expected for a gone row; adds nothing by itself), `F un` (unmeasured);
  - a path identity: measured, decided not-a-tree (absent, link, notdir), unmeasured;
  - the probe: nobody, in use, unmeasured;
  - the legacy count: a count, or `null` when it was not counted (the rung was never reached, or could not list the registry).
- **Single definition.**
  - One field grammar, held by its one reader's regex. One composer of every valid line, the K composer, which serves the pane and both seeds. One pending writer.
  - One bounded walk.
  - One identity format and match rule (`_ws_ident_compose`, `_ws_ident_eq`). One path-identity measure (`_ws_path_ident`).
  - One cwd probe, shared by the tail and ws-expire. The probe owns the physical resolve of its argument; the expiry adapter keeps its own resolve before the call (R22), and the probe's second resolve of that already physical parent is idempotent (P12).
  - One mountinfo seam, read by exactly two functions (R13), besides the pre-existing `CCD_MOUNTINFO` reader, which is not touched.
  - No identity compare reuses `_ws_collect_ident`, which compares raw btime.
- **The corpus.**
  - Every `ccd/ccd` edit at or before line 19162 is line-neutral, and there are exactly the four hunks the HARD BOUNDARY names.
  - `ccd/ccrc`'s one hunk is line-neutral.
  - The five citation passes stay green at `'ccd/ccd': 147` and `'ccd/ccrc': 5`, with no number edited:
    `(cd server && ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/session-hook.test.ts -t 'CITATION DEBT|README HAS ITS OWN CENSUS|LOCATION INDEXES|ROW PASS|RANGE BOUND|backticked _identifier')`
- **The stamp, after every `ccd/ccd` edit:** `bash ccd/ccrc restamp ccd/ccd && bash -n ccd/ccd && node shared/mark.mjs --check ccd/ccd`, then `ownership.test.ts` and `mark-check.test.ts`.
- **`ccd/contexts.tsv`.** One row per new function, in definition order. The cross-context count stays exactly at its base value (521 at the export; after an absorb of `main`, the value `main` carries, re-measured before the next task), and `BASELINE` is never raised by this wave. A new function calls only K functions or functions of its own context, and its body text names no function of another context.
- **The budget.**
  - The collect audit's sum stays under 90 s at the widest grace: 30 + 10 + 30 + 5 + 8 = 83 s (R20).
  - Each act's re-asks are bounded per call. Their sum against the 240 s act row is the stated residual `tail-reasks-can-outrun-the-act-row`.
- **The 300-byte cut.**
  - Every reason a NEW tail journal row carries passes `_ws_leaf_why_line`, and new reasons put their decisive words first. The existing owned rc-1 site in `_ws_reclaim_tail` carries `$_WS_OWNED_WHY` uncut today and is not edited.
  - New rung clauses are appended after the existing ones and asserted through the ladder's uncut `REAP_DETAIL`, never through the collect why.
- **vitest.** Run it in the foreground, from `server/`, as `./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/<file>`, with a timeout of at least 600000 ms. Never use bare `npx vitest`.
  - A red in a CLAUDE.md load flake is re-run ALONE before it counts.
  - `ccd-tick-diet-equivalence.test.ts` is excluded from local shards. Task 14's full CI run judges it (R39).
- **Load flakes are measured, never assumed.** A new file whose cases shell the real `/proc` walk joins CLAUDE.md's list in its own task's commit (R25), measured by a `PROC_SPY` count. A walk counts whether it is `_ws_path_users`', the expiry probe's or `_ws_cwd_users`'. Every verb tail walks the real `/proc` in its post-kill wait (`CHILD_STUBS` does not stub `_ws_path_users`), so every new file with a verb case is measured (Tasks 1, 3 and 6 to 11). Measured is not listed: a verb file whose `PROC_SPY` records no walk (as drafted, Task 3's `ccd-rows-rung-identity`, Task 6's `ccd-rows-rung-entry` and Task 8's `ccd-reclaim-main-identity`) stays off CLAUDE.md's list, and its task records that measurement in the ledger, where Task 14 reads it beside the listed files. A case that runs a real reclaim or expiry tail runs `_ws_cwd_users` from Task 10 on.
- **New cases go in NEW files.** An existing file is edited only where the HARD BOUNDARY names it. This wave's own new files may be edited by later tasks of this wave.
- **No `D-` token in a commit message, and no four-digit number range in a commit or in the as-built prose.** A departure is named by its slug, and the allocator assigns its number.
- **Branch discipline.**
  - One commit per task, on this workspace's own branch, never a feature branch.
  - Absorb `main` only with `git merge`, on a clause-16 trigger, and then do the second lander's duties:
    - re-run `session-hook.test.ts` whole;
    - re-measure the citation and census pins, `BASELINE` included;
    - run `ccd-collect-race-spawn-late` and `ccd-workspaces`.
  - On the `ccd/ccd` line-2 conflict, take either side of THAT LINE only, then restamp.
  - Every commit message ends with one blank line, then the attribution line the worker's own session is given.
- **Cite the SPEC** ("path-identity spec §4.5"), never the contract. Every backticked `_name` in a `ccd/ccd` comment exists (the danglers scan).
- **Locate code by CONTENT.** Line numbers are export hints. Task 0 re-grounds every anchor.
- **ws-expire.** It reaches the rows rung, the record reader, the moved-check, the owned check, the tail and its probe through shared code. Only the functions the PG2 A consent lists change. `_ws_expire_cwd_users` keeps its name, its contract and its `_ws_dir_physical` parent resolve (R22).
- **Commands are approval-free:** plain reads, git, grep, sed, awk, node, python3, vitest and `gh` reads, plus Task 14's push, PR and `workflow_dispatch`. Never `pkill` or `killall`: kill only a PID you recorded. Subagents never send mail, and never invoke the `ccrc-worker` skill.
- **The repository is public.** Nothing goes into code, tests, commits or the PR body that names a host, an absolute home path, a private project, an account or a lane. Use neutral stand-ins (`the fleet box`, `<projects-root>`, `demo-*` fixture ids).

## Rulings that amend the task text (binding; the coordinator, 2026-10-20)

The plan is built on W2's frozen head, `a03861c55` (#1008: `origin/main` `3cc6e5fce` with W2 merged). W3 branches from `main` once W2 lands, and its Task 0 re-grounds every anchor by content.

The operator's working rulings from the W0 merge stand: PI1 B, PI2 L1, PI3 B, PI4 D, PI5 A, PI6 M4, PI7 P1 (P2 for rows with a valid field), PI8 B2, PI9 K1, PI10 O2, PG1 B and PG2 A. A slug marks each place where a ruling narrows, widens or spells out the spec's text, and the as-built note names each slug. **Every ruling is add-only: no identity input may release a row, or turn a refusal into a pass.**

**The entry field (PI1 B, PI2 L1).**
- **R1. The grammar** is the spec's v1 line, `v1<TAB><dev>:<ino>:<btime or -><TAB><at_ms><TAB><physical pwd -P><TAB><logical spelling>`, at `$REG/<id>.workdirid`. It adds one `pending` form: `v1<TAB>pending<TAB><at_ms><TAB>-<TAB><logical>`. One grammar, one reader, one composer. Slug: `workdirid-pending-form`.
- **R2. The parent writes `pending` before every `_tmux_new_session`**, the primary and the retry. The pane replaces it after its `cd` succeeds and before `exec`.
  - A `pending` line whose logical spelling equals the current `.workdir` reads unmeasured, a hold. Its detail names the row and the remedy ("restart that session").
  - A stale earlier field must never survive a failed write.
- **R3. The reader's states are distinct:** `valid`, `pending`, `legacy-absent`, `legacy-stale` (its logical spelling differs from the current `.workdir`), `legacy-unparseable` and `legacy-link`.
  - A field that is not a regular file, or that cannot be read, reads **unmeasured**. Slug: `workdirid-unreadable-holds`.
  - The reader checks the type before it reads, and reads a bounded number of bytes.
  - It lives in C4 beside the rows rung, and mirrors `_reg_read`'s refusals without calling into C1. `BASELINE` is never raised.
- **R4. The in-pane writer** is one K-context composer inside the `_plat_` sentinel block, mirrored byte-identically into `ccd/ccrc`.
  - It prints a brace-free `/bin/sh -c '<script>'` fragment.
  - The script measures `pwd -P` and the per-OS stat of `.`. It refuses control characters, writes temp-then-rename into `$REG`, and exits 0 on every path.
  - It works under sh, bash, zsh and fish.
  - Its btime comes from the same per-OS form `_plat_btime` uses (`-` when there is none).
  - The pane still enters the logical `.workdir`.
- **R5. The seeds.**
  - `start` writes an initial valid value after `.workdir`.
  - ws-add keeps PI1 B's letter only if it can do so with no new cross-context edge and line-neutrally above line 19162. Otherwise its seed is dropped (slug `ws-add-seed-subsumed-by-spawn-pending`).

R56 sets the command-string lines' shape, and R60 their one spelling.

**The rows rung (PI3 B, PI6 M4, PI7, PI9 K1).**
- **R10. One batched walk per `_ws_reclaim_workdir_shared` call** (PI8 B2).

Every mismatch adds a placement or a hold. One helper, `_ws_path_ident`, measures a path for ccd-side compares: `dev:ino:btime|-`, a btime ≤ 0 reads `-`, and a failure is never `-`.

- **R56 (the pane writer cannot gate the exec).** The launch command becomes `cd '<wd>' && <fragment> 2>/dev/null; cd '<wd>' && exec env …`.
  - It uses no braces, so it works under fish.
  - A writer that cannot fork, is killed or fails still leaves the second `cd` and the `exec` to run. A failed first `cd` execs nothing new.
  - The second `cd` enters the same logical spelling, so, for an absolute `.workdir`, the transcript path is unchanged (R72; a relative one is `relative-workdir-second-cd-does-not-enter`). The microsecond re-point window between the two `cd`s can only leave a field that adds holds.
  - R47's consent words cover these two edited command-string lines.
- **R57 (the reader).** A read error after a successful open answers `unmeasured`, never legacy, and a shim pins it. The grammar's regex excludes control characters from the path groups (`[^[:cntrl:]]`).
- **R58 (stdin and `_plat_timeout`).** The walk's requests reach the bounded child as arguments, never as its stdin, because `_plat_timeout`'s pure-bash arm gives a background command `/dev/null`.
  - The child's stdin is `/dev/null` on both arms.
  - A reply that is not exactly one line per request (its kind and index, in order), plus the `B` lines and `end <n>`, is unmeasured.
  - On Darwin the cwd probe's lsof listing is parsed directly, as today, never under `_plat_timeout`. Residual: `darwin-cwd-parse-unbounded-as-today`.
- **R59 (Task 2's census sentence).** Task 2's wording stands: "so it is counted once." Task 9 is aligned to it.
- **R60 (round 2, one launch shape).** Tasks 4 and 5 as built are canonical. The composer prints `/bin/sh -c '<script>' ccd-workdirid '<reg>' '<id>' '<logical>' 2>/dev/null && ` (followed by a space).
  - It prints nothing when an argument is empty, when any argument holds a control character or a `'` (both of which `.workdir` refuses, in `cmd_start` and `cmd_ws_add`), or when the id holds a `/`.
  - Every `\` is spelled `\0134`, and the script decodes each argument with `printf %b`, so a backslash workdir round-trips to `valid` (R54).
  - Each launch line reads `cd '$workdir' && $(_plat_workdirid_pane "$REG" "$id" "$workdir")true; cd '$workdir' && exec env …`. At run time that is `cd '<wd>' && /bin/sh -c … 2>/dev/null && true; cd '<wd>' && exec env …`, or with nothing printed `cd '<wd>' && true; cd '<wd>' && exec env …`. This is R56's behaviour: the writer never gates the second `cd` and the `exec`.
  - §Interfaces, Review Focus, Task 0's consent wording, Tasks 13 and 14's checks and lens 2 all use exactly this spelling. The spelling difference from R56's text (`&& true;` for `;`) goes under `D-6145` (`w3-task-5-plan-text`).
- **R61 (round 2, the `_ws_dir_physical` census).** P12 stands: twelve call sites. Nine stand at the export; `_ws_path_ident` adds the tenth and eleventh (its two branches, Task 2); `_ws_cwd_users` adds the twelfth (Task 9).

### Proposed by the frame (confirmed by R44; binding)

These settle the places where the rulings, the spec and the measured code meet, and the rulings do not name the shape. R44 confirms each one as written, and P14 reads as R55 amends it.

- **P1. Where the K composer lives (R4 meets R41).** The platform block lies wholly under the corpus anchor (ccd `:41-1221`, ccrc `:70-1250`). The corpus also cites `ccd/ccrc` lines below ccrc's block (`'ccd/ccrc': 5`).

- **P2. The pending writer is a C2 helper** with no C1 call: `_spawn_workdirid_pending`, defined directly after `_spawn`.

  - On a failed write it unlinks the field, which then reads legacy, so a stale valid field never survives a failed write (R2). Only a registry directory that refuses both the write and the unlink (where `_reg_set` fails too) keeps what stood there: the stated residual `workdirid-pending-unwritable-keeps-the-old-field`.
  - `_spawn_start` already calls `_reg_set` (C1), but a new C2 helper calling `_reg_set` would be a new pair, which is +1 and red.
- **P3. R1's "one composer"** is the K composer, for every VALID line: the pane's, start's seed and ws-add's seed. The PENDING line has one writer, P2's.
  - The grammar's single definition is the reader's one regex.
  - A parity pin requires every writer's line to parse as the state it means.
- **P4. The ws-add seed is built (R5, measured).** Line `:7417` gains, in place, after `_reg_set "$id" uuid "$uuid"`:
  `; ( CDPATH= builtin cd -- "$wt" >/dev/null 2>&1 && eval "$(_plat_workdirid_pane "$REG" "$id" "$wt"):" ) || :`

- **P5. R19's two branches, measured (R49 rules branch 2).** The R54 arm the rung calls, `_ws_reclaim_recorded`, answers in globals (`_WS_RECORDED_AT`, `_WS_RECORDED_G`); its transitive closure is 16 functions at the export, `_ws_reclaim_record` and `_ws_reclaim_log_of` among them, whose own answers (`RECLAIM_REC_*`, `_WS_LOGS`) the arms shadow and read after return.
  - **Branch 1 is feasible with no change to those bodies.** A call-site transplant runs the arm in a child, `_plat_timeout <remaining> "$BASH" -c "<declare -f of the closure, and of a caller's git function if one is defined>; <declare -p of every global the closure reads>; set -uo pipefail; _ws_reclaim_recorded \"\$1\" \"\$2\"; rc=\$?; declare -p _WS_RECORDED_AT _WS_RECORDED_G; exit \$rc"`, and evals the reply. Containment survives, because `_ws_reclaim_contained` exports its git environment with `local -x`. Its costs:
    - a census of every global the closure reads, which a sibling programme's later edit to one of the 16 bodies can outgrow; each miss fails closed under `set -u`, as an unmeasured hold on every child beside a gone row;
    - a test's `git()` stub must be carried by `declare -f`;
    - a per-call bound does not bound the pass (N gone rows times the knob), so the knob must be a pass-level deadline, each call given what remains;
    - the knob joins the collect sum: 83 s + K < 90 s, so K ≤ 6 s;
    - one `"$BASH" -c` per gone row.
  - **Branch 2:** the git reads stay unbounded. Item 9 reads `Built (W3), git reads standing`, the residual is `rows-rung-git-reads-unbounded`, and a runner's kill there yields no document, which the server reads as a failed audit and retries: it fails closed.
  - R49 rules branch 2, which the frame builds. No Task 3b is built, the carry is narrowed, not closed, and item 9 reads `Built (W3), git reads standing`. Task 0 re-measures the closure and the globals, and records them.
- **P6. The reader's answer.** `_ws_workdirid_read ID LOGICAL` always sets `_WS_WDID_STATE` to one of R3's words or `unmeasured`.
  - rc 0 is `valid`; rc 1 is any `legacy-*`; rc 2 is `pending` or `unmeasured`.
  - The rule order is fixed (§Interfaces), with the stale check before pending, so a stale pending line reads legacy.
- **P7. The walk's grammar** is §Interfaces' request and answer format: NUL-separated requests on the walk function's stdin, which it reads whole and hands to the bounded child as arguments, never as the child's stdin (R58); and a reply of ASCII lines carrying indices and numbers, never a path. The reply ends `end <n>`. A reply that is not exactly one line per request (its kind and index, in order), one `B` line per btpath and `end <n>` is unmeasured. The walk checks that against the requests it read; the rows rung checks it again against its own list, because a request stream cut short reads to the walk as a clean end of file (R64).
- **P8. The identity format and rule are spelled once:**
  - `_ws_ident_compose DEVINO BTIME` (the format);
  - `_ws_ident_eq A B` (R11's rule, answering 0/1/2, where 2 means unparseable);
  - `_ws_path_ident PATH [follow]` (the measure).

  The walk's bash side composes through `_ws_ident_compose`.
- **P9. The rows rung's shape.**
  - Pass A is today's loop, byte-identical in every decision. It adds per-row field reads and walk requests before the first `continue` that follows the `.workdir` read.
  - Then one walk.
  - Pass B maps the reply and may only add to the buckets.
  - Today's outrank line moves after pass B. New not-asked buckets (`unwalk`, `unmount`, `unpend`, `unfield`, `unrec`) are decided after it.
- **P10. The legacy count's spelling (R9).**
  - The rung sets `_WS_LEGACY_ROWS` and `_WS_PENDING_ROWS` (integers) after its registry loop on every call that lists the registry. `_ws_reclaim_reset` clears them to `''`, and so does the rung at its entry, beside `_WS_RECORDED_GDIRS`, so its early `return 2` (a failed registry listing) leaves them `''`.
  - The reclaim document prints `"legacyRows":<n|null>,"pendingRows":<n|null>`, where `null` means "not counted": the ladder never reached the rung, or the rung could not list the registry.
  - `legacyRows` counts the other rows whose field is in a `legacy-*` state, and `pendingRows` those whose field reads `pending`. A field that reads `unmeasured` is in neither, and it holds the child (R75 (d)).
  - `parseChildReclaimAudit` tolerates extra keys (measured).
- **P11. The record reader's why.** `_WS_REC_WHY` is set on every rc 2.
  - The list-failure cause keeps its exact prefix, "could not read $main's worktree list".
  - The three callers print `"$_WS_REC_WHY, so whether git [still] records … was never asked"`, byte-identical for that cause.
  - `_ws_reclaim_recorded_git` and `_ws_reclaim_recorded_crumb` shadow it, and `_ws_reclaim_reset` clears it.
- **P12. `_ws_cwd_users DIR [SAY]` owns the physical resolve.** SAY is the spelling its reasons use (default DIR).
  - Its preamble is ws-expire's, moved into the shared probe: DIR must be one plain absolute path (else 2); a PROVEN absence answers 0 with nothing read; DIR's parent is resolved by `_ws_dir_physical` (a newline in it, or a parent that cannot be entered, answers 2) and the leaf is appended unfollowed. The walk compares that physical spelling, never DIR's own. `/proc/<pid>/cwd` and lsof both print physical paths, so a tree spelled through a linked root (the fleet's worktrees root; macOS's `/var`) would never string-match otherwise, and on Darwin and for a deleted cwd the string arm is the only arm.
  - The adapter `_ws_expire_cwd_users` keeps its own preamble (plain path, absent, `_ws_dir_physical` parent) and its pinned texts (R22), then calls `_ws_cwd_users "$wt" "$workdir"`; the probe's second resolve of an already physical parent is idempotent.

A caller that reaches it through `_ws_removal_mounts_clear`'s `resolve` is not counted again (R59: Task 2's "so it is counted once" stands, and Task 9 aligns to it). Task 2 moves both census sentences to `its eleven callers` and names the tenth and eleventh; Task 9 moves both to `its twelve callers` and names the twelfth, renumbering no earlier ordinal; Task 14 checks `its twelve callers` at 2 and nine, ten and eleven at 0 (R61).

Task 6's gates run the four files, and a red there through a `B un` moves the shims into Task 6 (recorded in its plan-text slot).

- **P14. The re-ask's order at each of the four sites (as R55 amends it)** is Task 10's `_ws_cwd_users "$workdir"` line, then `_ws_reclaim_reask` (owned, then the identities), then W2's mount ask, then `keep_of` or the forced removal. The shared test fixture.** A new `server/test/worktreeIdentityFixture.ts` holds the names later tasks share, each defined in the first task that uses it: `writeField` and `FAKE_PROC_SELF` (Task 1), `DARWIN_IDENT_SHIMS` (Task 2), `BIND_STANDIN` and `walkSpy` (Task 3), `PANE_EXEC` and `paneFragment` (Task 5), `DARWIN_LSOF_STUB` (Task 9).

W2's tail-mount suite keeps its assertions; its plants move.** From Task 3 the in-lock ladder recompute (`_ws_reclaim_locked` re-runs `_ws_reclaim_fork`) reads the mount table through the rows rung, and a resumed tail's `_ws_reclaim_owned` reads it at the tail's start, so a mount planted under the child before the verb answers `probe-unmeasured` (fresh) or owned's `worktree-remove-failed` (resumed) before W2's ask is reached. From Task 11 the re-ask does the same before W2's second ask.
  - `ccd-reclaim-tail-mounts.test.ts` gains one in-file helper, `MOUNT_AT_ASK(spelling, p, nth)`: a wrapper of `_ws_removal_mounts_clear` that appends `MOUNT_LINE(p)` to the faked table immediately before its `nth` call for `spelling`, then asks the real one (composed inside `ASK_LOG` where a case uses both).

- **P20. What `B un` and `F gone` mean (no overloaded null).**
  - Identities measured at the same instant (an `A`, `F` or `T` hit) compare dev:ino alone: one inode is one directory at one instant. Identities compared across time (a field's recorded identity against T0's or a row's current one, and a recorded path's identity now against the one recorded) compare through `_ws_ident_eq`, birth time included.
  - So a `B` answer is read only by rule (a) (P2: the field against T0) and rule (d) (the mismatch rule: the row's current path, and the recorded path when it stands). A `B <j> un` that one of those rules needs adds the row to `unwalk`. It is never read as `-`.
  - `F <i> gone` adds nothing by itself; it only tells rule (d) the recorded path does not stand. `F <i> un` adds `unwalk`.

Its two `_ws_path_ident` measures run after the moved-check, directly before `return 0`, so a measure failure (2, retryable) never pre-empts a proof (1, `containment-refuted`). R30's refusal compares the two identities' dev:ino (`-ef`), never their birth times.
- **P22. Every child shell is `"$BASH" -c`.** The walk's envelope and any later child ccd starts for this wave run the interpreter the entry proved (bash ≥ 4.4), never a `bash` resolved from `PATH`, which a launchd `PATH` can make 3.2. `_lc_obs`' existing `bash -c` is not edited. A source pin holds it.
- **P23. Gate lists that a new registry file reaches are generated, not typed.** Task 0 records two lists in the ledger: every test file whose snippets run the real `cmd_ws_add`, `cmd_start` or `_spawn_start` (132 files match the wide grep at the export; 20 of them define a `_spawn_start` stub), and every forced-Darwin file whose cases reach the shared tail. Task 4 runs the first list's seed-reaching files, Task 5 its real-spawn files, Tasks 8 and 10 the second. A red file outside the HARD BOUNDARY is a STOP, `registry-file-census-<file>` or `darwin-suite-outside-the-licence-<file>`.

Each conflict is ruled, and the task text carries its ruling. Only C1 still waits on an outside party's answer.
- **C1. R9's expire half against R41: R45.** The expire audit document is printed only inside `_ws_expire_audit_contained` (export hints `:34842`, in the function defined at `:34822`; Task 0 re-measures both), which R41 fenced.

With that consent, R41's fence is amended by exactly those edits.
  - If the consent is refused, the expire half is dropped as the substantive departure `legacy-count-expire-half-fenced`.
  - Task 6 builds the reclaim half either way, and STOPs before the expire half until the brief carries the consent or the refusal. Consent 7443 has answered it (R75), so C1 is (a) and no conflict's gate remains.
- **C2. R13's "both boxes": R46.** In remote mode, ccd's reclaim, expiry and collect verbs run only on the fleet box. The server box drives the fleet through the agent and never runs them, so its device match is moot. In local mode the single box is the fleet box. The worker reads the fleet box only, and CI's match is Task 3's real-table CONTROL case, read at Task 14's full run.

## Review Focus (the five failure modes most likely to bite)

1. **A row that holds today is released.**
   - Input:
     - legacy rows (absent, stale, unparseable or link field);
     - a field that is a directory or a FIFO;
     - a pending field;
     - a valid field recording a path outside while the current spelling resolves inside;
     - a gone row with a valid field recording an outside path, beside a blank admin entry (R97);
     - a gone row released by either R54 arm, now carrying a field;
     - a record naming the child only through another spelling;
     - two records naming the child, one by its string and one under another spelling, through the reclaim and through ws-expire (R75);
     - a row naming the main checkout by git's own spelling, beside a record naming it under another spelling (R67);
     - a bind-spelled main checkout;
     - a birth time that could not be read (`B un`) on a recycled inode;
     - each fence row.
   - Expected:
     - every pre-W3 hold stays a hold (the Task 1 fence, re-run after each task);
     - the field never releases;
     - `-ef` never grants: the record reader never hits by identity, and only `REC_MAIN` or rc 2 come of it; once git's main stanza names the tree, no later stanza weakens the ladder's terminal `not-a-workspace` to `unmeasured` (R67);
     - the mismatch rule is never asked of a gone row;
     - `B un` is never read as `-`.
2. **A tree is removed while another session lives inside it.**
   - Input:
     - a re-pointed alias, with a valid field before and after a respawn;
     - a bind spelling (ancestry);
     - a bind sourced inside the child (field 4, `//deleted` included);
     - `/proc/self/cwd`, `//proc/self/cwd`, `///proc/self/cwd` and a relative link into `/proc`;
     - a row written inside the child after the ladder's map was built;
     - a nested checkout or the child swapped for a copy between owned and the removal;
     - a re-pointed main checkout;
     - a tree that reappears after owned proved it absent;
     - a live process that entered through an alias (ancestry) or whose cwd was removed (string);
     - a tree spelled through a linked root, with a process inside it, on Linux and on forced Darwin;
     - a process that enters during `keep_of`.
   - Expected: each refuses or holds before every standing nested-checkout and child forced removal, with the word R29 names.
3. **"Not inside", "no row" or "nobody" when nothing was measured.**
   - Input:
     - a timed-out walk (a FIFO table, or a slow python3);
     - a short reply, a reply to a request list cut short on its way to the walk (R64), or a last request record cut before its NUL (R68); python3 missing; a child that stands but cannot be stat'd;
     - a field-3 versus `st_dev` mismatch;
     - an empty, unreadable or malformed table;
     - a probe walk failure, or a cwd whose `..` cannot be walked;
     - EACCES beyond the ruled exception;
     - an lsof that is missing or slow;
     - a timed-out re-ask;
     - a `_ws_path_ident` failure (never `-`);
     - a pending or unreadable field.
   - Expected: unmeasured, or `worktree-remove-failed`, retryable, with the tree, branch and breadcrumb kept.
4. **The spawn regresses.**
   - Input:
     - the pane writer failing (stat, date, mv);
     - a control character, a quote or a backslash in REG, the id or the logical spelling;
     - forced Darwin;
     - a pane `cd` that fails;
     - the primary and the retry spawn;
     - an alias re-pointed between the parent's read and the pane's `cd`;
     - pane shells sh, bash, zsh and fish;
     - the generation lock's order;
     - stdout `[0]`;
     - the composed length.
   - Expected:
     - the spawn execs exactly as before, apart from the fragment and the second `cd`, whether `/bin/sh` starts or not, fails or is killed: the fragment ends in `&& ` and the command string closes it with `true; `, so the writer never gates the second `cd` and the `exec` (R56's behaviour, R60's spelling);
     - a workdir that `.workdir` accepts, a backslash included, gets a writer, and its field round-trips to `valid` under sh, bash and zsh, and under fish for every spelling without `\\` or a trailing `\` (R65: under fish the launch line's own `cd '<wd>'` reads those as escapes, `fish-spawn-cd-reads-backslash-escapes`); only an empty argument, a control character or a `'` (both of which `.workdir` refuses) or a `/` in the id makes the composer print nothing (R54, R60);
     - the field records the directory reached after `cd`;
     - a pane write that fails after the parent's pending write stays pending, a hold;
     - a parent pending write that fails unlinks the field, so the row reads legacy-absent (today's rule) until a later spawn's writes succeed; it never reads a stale valid field, save under a registry directory that refuses the unlink too (the stated residual `workdirid-pending-unwritable-keeps-the-old-field`);
     - a failed `cd` execs nothing;
     - for an absolute `.workdir` (the only form `cmd_start` and `ws-add` store), the second `cd` enters the same directory, so the transcript path is unchanged (no physical-path `cd`). A relative one, which an older row may hold, makes the second `cd` resolve against the first, so that row's respawn execs nothing or execs elsewhere: R72's residual `relative-workdir-second-cd-does-not-enter`, which Task 0 Step 6's `spell-not-absolute` STOP keeps off the fleet box.
5. **Something moves that a census or a sibling programme reads.** Expected:
   - corpus `'ccd/ccd': 147` and `'ccd/ccrc': 5`;
   - exactly the four in-place hunks at or before line 19162, and ccrc's one;
   - the stamp regenerated;
   - contexts at the base's value, with the K list +1 and every new row placed;
   - the collect budget at 78 s and 83 s, with the header prose re-stated, not weakened;
   - one id-cap row;
   - refusal-scan at 16;
   - the archived-expiry census unedited;
   - ws-expire changed only by consented functions;
   - #435's and delegation's lines untouched beyond R7's two launch statements;
   - `ccd-workspaces`' RM_CALLS at 29;
   - `macos-platform` green;
   - the W1b and W2 prose suites green;
   - `expiry-lane-prose` and `lifecycle-refusal-word` green unedited;
   - the tail's six destructive calls;
   - W2's tail-mount adjacency pins, and its behavioural cases green with only their plant timing moved (P19);
   - `ccd-reg-get-census` at 204/173;
   - `docs-parity` green;
   - `single-definition`'s literal-source-pin ratchet unmoved (no new literal pin over a W1a file).

## Execution order and dependencies

Task 0 → 1 → … → 14, strictly serial.
- Tasks 2 to 12 each edit and restamp `ccd/ccd`. Each task is one commit, and every commit leaves every suite it touches green.
- The fence (Task 1) is re-run after every task from 2 to 12.
- **Tasks 4 and 5 are one deployable unit.** A seed without the spawn's pending write would leave a valid field that goes stale at the next respawn. The wave ships as one PR, and no intermediate commit is deployed.
- If R7's consent is absent, Task 5 STOPs. Tasks 6 to 12 read no Task 5 code. The worker continues with them only on the coordinator's mail. Task 5 then lands after Task 12, red-first as written, and the order change is recorded under `D-6145` (`w3-task-5-plan-text`).
- Task 6 builds the reclaim half of the count either way, and STOPs before the expire half (its printf and R53's expire key pin) until the brief carries workspace-lifecycle's answer to R45's request: consent, or refusal (then `legacy-count-expire-half-fenced`). C2 to C7 are ruled (R46 to R51), and no other task waits on a ruling.

## Interfaces (canonical)

Every name the tasks share. A later task uses exactly these names and contracts.

### The field grammar (R1, P3, P6)

```
valid:   v1 TAB <dev>:<ino>:<btime> TAB <at_ms> TAB <physical> TAB <logical>
pending: v1 TAB pending TAB <at_ms> TAB - TAB <logical>
```
- The file is `$REG/<id>.workdirid`. Its body is the line alone, with no trailing newline, as every `_reg_set` field is written.
- `<dev>:<ino>`: decimal, as `_plat_devino`'s `%d:%i` prints them.
- `<btime>`: `[1-9][0-9]*` or `-` (0, −1 or a printed `-` is written `-`).
- `<at_ms>`: exactly 13 digits.
- `<physical>`: absolute, and plain by `_ws_reclaim_plain_path`.
- `<logical>`: absolute, byte-equal to the `.workdir` value the writer was given.
- No control character appears anywhere but the four TAB separators.
- The cap is 8320 bytes. A body over the cap is unparseable.
- **The one regex**, held in `_ws_workdirid_read` alone, read under `LC_ALL=C` with `BASH_REMATCH` copied before any other `=~`:
  `^v1	(([0-9]+):([0-9]+):([1-9][0-9]*|-)|pending)	([0-9]{13})	([^[:cntrl:]]+)	(/[^[:cntrl:]]*)$`
  - The separators are literal TABs. The two path groups are `[^[:cntrl:]]`, which under `LC_ALL=C` excludes TAB, newline, CR and every other control byte, so the regex itself states the rule that no control character appears but the four separators (R57).
  - For the pending form, group 6 is exactly `-`. For the valid form, group 6 must pass `_ws_reclaim_plain_path`.

### `ccd/ccd` names (the fleet box's executor; outside the server's rings)

**Identity (Task 2; C4; directly after `_ws_reclaim_absent`).**
```bash
_WS_IDENT=''; _WS_IDENT_KIND=''; _WS_IDENT_WHY=''
_ws_ident_compose() {   # devino btime -> prints "<dev>:<ino>:<btime|->"; rc 2 (prints nothing) when devino is not
  #                        ^[0-9]+:[0-9]+$ or btime is not ^-?[0-9]+$. A btime <= 0 is '-'. Never '-' for a failure
_ws_ident_eq() {        # a b -> 0 the dev:ino are equal and, where BOTH carry a btime, the btimes are equal; 1 they
  #                        differ; 2 either is not ^[0-9]+:[0-9]+:([1-9][0-9]*|-)$ (path-identity spec §4.5, R11)
_ws_path_ident() {      # path [follow] -> 0 with _WS_IDENT, the identity of the DIRECTORY path names: by default its
  #                        parent resolved physically (`_ws_dir_physical`) and its leaf never followed; with `follow`,
  #                        the whole path resolved first (for $main, which `git -C` follows). 1 with _WS_IDENT_KIND
  #                        `absent` (PROVEN by `_ws_reclaim_absent`), `link` or `notdir`. 2 with _WS_IDENT_WHY: a
  #                        spelling that is not plain, a parent that cannot be resolved, an absence not proven, or a
  #                        `_plat_devino`/`_plat_btime` that failed or answered malformed. Clears all three first.
  #                        Prints nothing, never dies
```

**The walk (Task 2; C4; directly after `_ws_path_ident`).**
```bash
WS_RECLAIM_WALK_S=5   # the bound on the ONE identity walk a rows pass makes: every prefix's identity, every link on a
#                       row's spelling, the mount table and the birth times (healthy: tens of ms; path-identity spec §4.9)
_WS_IDWALK_OUT=''; _WS_IDWALK_WHY=''
_ws_reclaim_idwalk() {   # mi [btpath...] ; NUL-separated requests on THIS function's stdin, read whole here (an empty
  #                        record is no request) and handed to the bounded child as arguments, never as its stdin
  #                        -> 0 with _WS_IDWALK_OUT: one reply line per request, in request order, then one `B <j> …`
  #                        line per btpath, then `end <n>`; 2 with _WS_IDWALK_WHY: a request stream that ends any way
  #                        but EOF "the identity walk's requests could not be read whole (read exit <rc>)"; a last
  #                        record with no NUL after it, cut inside its path,
  #                        "the identity walk's requests could not be read whole (a record without its end)"; rc 124/137
  #                        "the identity walk did not finish within ${WS_RECLAIM_WALK_S}s"; any other non-zero "the
  #                        identity walk could not be measured (exit <rc>)"; a reply that is not exactly one line per
  #                        request (its kind and index, in request order), one `B` line per btpath, in order, then
  #                        `end <n>`, "the identity walk's reply was not read whole". Never 0 with a partial reply.
  #                        Prints nothing. mi '' asks no table
```
- **Envelope.** Exactly one exec under the bound (P22, R58):
  `out=$(_plat_timeout "$WS_RECLAIM_WALK_S" "$BASH" -c "$(declare -f _plat_btime)"$'\n'"$envelope" _ "$CCD_OS" "$mi" "$py" "$#" "$@" "${req[@]}" </dev/null 2>/dev/null); rc=$?`
  The requests ride the child's ARGUMENTS, never its stdin. `_plat_timeout`'s pure-bash arm starts its command in the background, and bash gives a background command `/dev/null` for stdin (measured), so a request stream left to the child would reach python empty there and still end in a well-formed `end 0`. The child's own stdin is `/dev/null` on both arms.
  - The envelope pipes its request arguments, NUL-separated, to `env LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 python3 -I -c "$py" "$mi"` (only when there is one), and prints its reply.
  - Then, for the btpaths, it asks `_plat_btime` once with every path. It accepts that answer only on rc 0 with exactly one line per path; otherwise it asks each path alone.
  - It prints `B <j> <raw>`, or `B <j> un` for a path whose own call failed or printed a non-integer.
  - Then `end <n>`, n being the number of lines before it.
  - The bash side composes identities through `_ws_ident_compose`.
- **Requests.** Each is `<kind><TAB><index><TAB><path>`, NUL-terminated. An empty record is no request. A last record with no NUL after it is refused, rc 2, "the identity walk's requests could not be read whole (a record without its end)" (R68): a record cut inside its path keeps its kind and index, so the rung's reply match (R64) could not see the cut. Python splits each one at most twice.

  | Kind | Index | Path | Asked |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `T` | k: 0 the child, 1 and 2 the standing directory leaves (`lr`) | physical | the targets; T0 only when the child's own basis is `complete` and it stands |
  | `A` | row i | the row's `complete` resolved spelling | ancestry of the row |
  | `P` | row i | the row's raw `.workdir` | the m1 link walk |
  | `F` | f: the field's own index in Task 6's field list (`efo`), not the row's | a valid field's recorded physical path | ancestry of the recorded path |
  | `M` | 0 | the table path from `_ws_collect_mountinfo`, which must equal `mi` (any other path answers `M 0 un unreadable`) | only with T0, and never on Darwin (the caller's one line) |

- **Answers.** One line per request, indices and numbers only:
  - `T <k> ok <dev>:<ino> <maj>:<min>` | `T <k> gone` (ENOENT) | `T <k> un <word>`.
  - `A <i> ok <dev>:<ino> <hit>` | `A <i> gone` | `A <i> un <word>`.
    - `os.stat` of every prefix from `/` down, following links (R10).
    - `<hit>` is `eq:<k>` when the path's own identity is target k, `in:<k>` when a proper prefix is target k, or `-`. Target 0 is checked before the leaves.
    - ENOENT at any prefix is `gone`; any other error is `un eacces|enotdir|error`.
  - `F <i> …`: exactly as `A`.
  - `P <i> proc` | `P <i> clean` | `P <i> un eacces|eloop|error`.
    - The walk lexically drops `.` and resolves `x/..`, as `cd -L` does.
    - It then walks component by component with `os.lstat`. On a link it reads `t = os.readlink`, and a raw `t` matching `^/+proc(/|$)` is `proc`.
    - Otherwise it follows `t`: an absolute target restarts at `/`, a relative one continues from the link's directory, and a `..` takes the physical parent.
    - `proc` is also answered when the link-free position it forms matches `^/+proc(/|$)`. That test is textual, made as the position is formed, before its lstat (R15).
    - More than 40 hops is `un eloop`. ENOENT is `clean`.
  - `M 0 clear <lines>` | `M 0 hold point|root|deleted` | `M 0 un empty|malformed|unreadable|devmismatch|nochild`.
    - The child's physical path is encoded as `_ws_collect_mounts_clear` encodes it (`\134 \040 \011 \012`), and compared as text, never decoded.
    - `point`: a mount point equal to the child, or under it.
    - The containing mount is the longest mount-point component prefix of the child, the last listed on a tie. Its field 3 must equal `os.major/os.minor` of the child's `st_dev`, else `devmismatch`.
    - The device-relative path is that line's root plus the remainder.
    - `root` or `deleted`: a line with that same field 3 whose root, with one trailing `//deleted` removed, equals the device-relative path or lies under it.
    - `nochild`: T0 was not `ok`.
  - `B <j> <raw>` | `B <j> un`, j being the btpath's position among the call's btpath arguments (Task 6's `wbt`). Read per P20: `un` is never `-`.
  - `end <n>`.
- Python wraps the whole pass in `try: … except Exception: sys.exit(3)`. A reply never carries a path.

**The field (Task 4, Task 5).**
```bash
# Task 4, K, ONE line on the blank line after `_plat_epoch_ms` (P1), byte-identical in ccd/ccrc:
_plat_workdirid_pane() { …; }   # reg id logical -> the pane's brace-free entry-identity writer, or nothing (path-identity spec §4.3)
```
- **Output.** `/bin/sh -c '<script>' ccd-workdirid '<reg>' '<id>' '<logical>' 2>/dev/null && `, followed by a space (R60). Each launch line closes it with `true; ` (below) and each seed with `:`, so the writer's exit, a `/bin/sh` that cannot be forked or started, or a writer that is killed never gates the second `cd` and the `exec` (R56's behaviour).
- **What it refuses (R54, R60).** It prints nothing when reg, id or logical is empty, when any of them holds a control character or a `'` (both of which `.workdir` refuses: `cmd_start` refuses both, and `cmd_ws_add` refuses a `'` in the path it composes), or when the id holds a `/`. Nothing else is refused. A workdir that `.workdir` accepts, a `\` included, gets a writer, and its field round-trips to `valid` under sh, bash and zsh, and under fish for every spelling without `\\` or a trailing `\` (R65: under fish the launch line's own `cd '<wd>'`, which W3 does not change, reads those as escapes, so that pane never enters and its `pending` stands: `fish-spawn-cd-reads-backslash-escapes`). Task 4 pins the fragment's own round trip, entered from bash, under sh, bash, zsh and fish, and for the start seed. A byte that one locale classes as a control character and another does not can leave a field `pending` for good, which fails closed (R66: `workdirid-physical-control-byte-stays-pending`).
- **The encoding (R54, R60).** fish reads `\\` and `\'` inside single quotes, so no quoted argument may carry a raw `\` (a `'` is refused above).
  - After the refusals, the composer spells each `\` of reg, id and logical as `\0134`, exactly as Task 4's line spells it: `local s m x='\' a1 a2 a3; a1=${1//"$x"/"$x"0134} a2=${2//"$x"/"$x"0134} a3=${3//"$x"/"$x"0134}`. It prints `"$a1" "$a2" "$a3"` into the three quoted arguments.
  - Each quoted argument then holds no `'` and no raw `\`, so sh, bash, zsh and fish read it alike inside single quotes.
  - The script decodes each argument once with POSIX `printf %b`, which reads `\0ddd` as one octal byte (measured under dash). The line it writes therefore holds the logical byte-equal to `.workdir`, and the one grammar and its reader are unchanged.
- rc 0 always. It calls no function. Its text names no ccd function outside K.
- `<script>` is POSIX sh, with no `'` inside it. It is spelled as concatenated single-quoted bash segments, so bash expands none of its `$`. The per-OS parts are chosen from `$CCD_OS` when the fragment is composed, as `_plat_btime` chooses.

  ```sh
  REG=$(printf %b "$1") id=$(printf %b "$2") l=$(printf %b "$3")
  p=$(pwd -P && echo .) || exit 0
  p=${p%?.}
  case $p in /*) ;; *) exit 0;; esac
  case $p$l in *[[:cntrl:]]*) exit 0;; esac
  s=$(stat -c %d:%i:%W . 2>/dev/null) || exit 0          # Darwin: stat -f %d:%i:%B .
  d=${s%%:*} r=${s#*:}
  n=${r%%:*} b=${r#*:}
  case $d in ""|*[!0-9]*) exit 0;; esac
  case $n in ""|*[!0-9]*) exit 0;; esac
  case $b in 0|-1|-) b=-;; [1-9]*) case $b in *[!0-9]*) exit 0;; esac;; *) exit 0;; esac
  a=$(date +%s%3N 2>/dev/null)
  case $a in ""|*[!0-9]*) a=$(date +%s 2>/dev/null)000;; esac
  case $a in [0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]) ;; *) exit 0;; esac
  t=$REG/.$id.workdirid.$$.tmp f=$REG/$id.workdirid
  printf "v1\t%s:%s:%s\t%s\t%s\t%s" "$d" "$n" "$b" "$a" "$p" "$l" >"$t" || { rm -f "$t"; exit 0; }
  mv -fT "$t" "$f" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$t"              # Darwin: if [ -d "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ]; then rm -f "$t"; exit 0; fi; [ -L "$f" ] && rm -f "$f"; mv -f "$t" "$f" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$t"
  exit 0
  ```
  GNU `%W` prints `0` for an unknown birth time (coreutils 9.4, measured); the `-` arm is defensive for a stat that prints `-`.
- **The seeds** (Task 4) are one statement each:
  `( CDPATH= builtin cd -- "<wd>" >/dev/null 2>&1 && eval "$(_plat_workdirid_pane "$REG" "$id" "<wd>"):" ) || :`
  - in `cmd_start`, directly after its `.workdir` write (`<wd>` = `$workdir`);
  - in `cmd_ws_add`, appended in place to `:7417` (`<wd>` = `$wt`, P4).
  - The fragment's trailing `&& ` takes the `:`, so a seed runs the writer, then `:`; a refused input evals `:` alone, and the subshell's `|| :` absorbs a writer that fails (R60).

```bash
# Task 4, C4, directly above `_ws_reclaim_workdir_shared`'s globals line:
_WS_WDID_STATE=''; _WS_WDID_WHY=''; _WS_WDID_IDENT=''; _WS_WDID_AT=''; _WS_WDID_PHYS=''
_ws_workdirid_read() {   # id logical -> 0 `valid` (_WS_WDID_IDENT "<dev>:<ino>:<btime|->", _WS_WDID_AT, _WS_WDID_PHYS);
  #                         1 `legacy-absent` | `legacy-link` | `legacy-unparseable` | `legacy-stale`; 2 `pending`, or
  #                         `unmeasured` (_WS_WDID_WHY: not a regular file, or could not be read). _WS_WDID_STATE always
  #                         names the answer. Clears every global first. Prints nothing, never dies, calls nothing in C1
```
- **The rule order** (P6), under `LC_ALL=C`:
  1. no name and no link → `legacy-absent`;
  2. a link → `legacy-link`, and the target is never read;
  3. not a regular file → `unmeasured`, and it is never opened;
  4. a failed open, or a read error after a successful open → `unmeasured`, never legacy (R57; a shim pins the read error);
  5. a body over 8320 bytes → `legacy-unparseable`;
  6. the regex fails, or a valid physical path is not plain → `legacy-unparseable`;
  7. the logical spelling differs from LOGICAL → `legacy-stale`;
  8. `pending` → `pending`;
  9. otherwise → `valid`.
- The read is one bounded `LC_ALL=C head -c 8321` of the opened descriptor, piped through `tr '\000' '\n'` and ended by a sentinel (`_ws_leaf_read_small`'s form; R62). Bash's `read` is not used: it answers 1 at the end of the file and on an error alike. The pipeline's status under ccd's `pipefail` tells a read error (rule 4, `unmeasured`, R57) from the end of the file, and a NUL read as a newline fails the grammar (rule 6). The window between rule 3's type check and the open is `_reg_read_to`'s own (`[[ -f "$f" ]] && _file_read_to`): a FIFO swapped in there blocks the open, which no byte cap or `read -t` prevents. Stated residual: `workdirid-fifo-swap-after-type-check`.

```

- On any failure it removes the temp, then runs `rm -f -- "$REG/$id.workdirid"`.
- **R7's two launch statements in `_spawn_start` (R47: "the two launch statements: the two inserted `_spawn_workdirid_pending` lines and the two edited command-string lines"):**
  - `_spawn_workdirid_pending "$id" "$workdir" || :` is inserted directly above each `_tmux_new_session -d -s "$tname" …` line: the primary after the generation block's last `fi`, the retry after the retry's generation `fi`.

A relative one, which an older row may hold and `cmd_ensure` respawns as stored, makes the second `cd` resolve against the directory the first entered, so that respawn execs nothing, or execs in another directory (R72: Task 0 Step 6's `spell-not-absolute` STOPs on a live one, and the stated residual is `relative-workdir-second-cd-does-not-enter`). A re-point of that spelling between the two `cd`s can only leave a field that adds holds.

- `BIND_STANDIN(prefix)`: wraps `_ws_reclaim_resolve` (the `eval "_t_real()$(declare -f … | tail -n +2)"` idiom). For spellings under `prefix/` it answers the spelling unchanged with basis `complete`, as `pwd -P` answers on a real bind (Task 3).
- `walkSpy`: wraps `_ws_reclaim_idwalk`, appending one line per call, and the request kinds it was given, to `$HOME/walk-calls` (Task 3).
- `PANE_EXEC(shell)`: a bash `tmux()` stub. On `new-session` it runs `$PANE_PRE` if set, then `<shell> -c "<last argument>"` inside the snippet. Otherwise it records argv as the existing stubs do (Task 5).
- `paneFragment(h, id, workdir, os?)`: the composer's output, read from ccd's own `_plat_workdirid_pane` and never typed, kept whole (read bracketed, so its trailing space survives the harness's trim). It is what `_spawn_start` splices between a command string's first `cd '<workdir>' && ` and its `true; cd '<workdir>' && exec env` (R56's behaviour, R60's spelling). `os` forces an arm (Task 5).
- `DARWIN_LSOF_STUB`: `_ws_expire_lsof() { printf 'p%s\nfcwd\nn%s\n' "$$" "$HOME"; };`. The exact `-Fpn` shape is copied from `ccd-ws-expire-ladder.test.ts`'s stubs (Task 9).

The worker runs this on the fleet box. It prints numbers, never a name, a path or a body.

The reads are R34's list. Listing `$REG` to find the `.workdir` bodies, and `$HOME/projects` (ccd's own `PROJECTS_ROOT`, (b32)) to find each `<common>/worktrees`, are the means of R34's licensed reads. Three reads go beyond its letter, and R52 licenses all three. Each is named in `W3_T0_LICENSED` (comma-separated), so none is skipped; a read that did not run for any other reason is recorded by its slug:
- `suffixes`: counts of the registry suffixes other than `.workdir`, which the legacy count and `rows-workdirid` need (skipped: `legacy-count-unmeasured`);
- `cctmp`: one stat of `~/.cc-tmp`, for the collector's leaf device match, which R13 reaches through R14 (skipped: `cc-tmp-device-match-unmeasured`);
- `records`: a stat of each worktree a `<common>/worktrees/*/gitdir` names, for Task 8's two new holds (skipped: `records-sharing-unmeasured`).

def linkwalk(w):
    pos, hops, seen_link = '/', 0, False
    q = [p for p in w.split('/') if p and p != '.']
    while q:
        x = q.pop(0)
        if x == '..': pos = os.path.dirname(pos.rstrip('/')) or '/'; continue

chains = {}
for i, (r, ident, dev) in standing.items():

def devcheck(path, key):

for i, (r, ident, dev) in standing.items():

    inc('rows-with-a-second-spelling', second); inc('rows-spelled-through-the-wider-mount', wider)
if 'cctmp' in LIC: devcheck(os.path.join(H, '.cc-tmp'), 'devmatch-cc-tmp')
for p in (os.listdir(PR) if os.path.isdir(PR) else []):
    main = os.path.join(PR, p); wt = os.path.join(main, '.git', 'worktrees')
    if not os.path.isdir(wt): continue
    mainid = None
    if 'records' in LIC:
        try: ms = os.stat(main); mainid = (ms.st_dev, ms.st_ino)
        except OSError: inc('records-main-unstattable')
    seen = {}

        except OSError: inc('admin-gitdir-unreadable'); continue

        try: s = os.stat(d); k = (s.st_dev, s.st_ino)

The pane-shaped measure runs `/bin/sh` with its working directory at each standing workdir (as the pane's `cd` reaches it) and reads only `pwd -P` and the stat of `.`, which is R34's "cd -P and stat of the workdirs".

**STOP rule (R34).** Each of these is a new live hold W3 would make, or a respawn its launch line would break (R72), so the coordinator sees it first. Any one STOPs the wave, reported as counts, never as names:
- `devmatch-workdir-mismatch>0`, `devmatch-workdir-nocontaining>0` or `devmatch-cc-tmp-mismatch>0` (R13);
- `mounts-at-or-under-a-workdir>0` (the rows rung's new hold at the audit);
- `roots-at-or-under-a-workdir>0` (field 4);
- `pairs-by-identity-not-string>0` (ancestry);
- `link-into-proc-raw>0`, `link-into-proc-by-position>0` or `link-walk-unwalkable>0` (m1);
- `cwd-in-a-workdir-by-identity-only>0` (a new in-use answer);
- `cwd-unwalkable>0` (every reclaim and expiry would be unmeasured);
- `cwd-readlink-error>0` (a cwd link that fails with anything but ENOENT, ESRCH or EACCES makes `_ws_cwd_users` answer unmeasured, so every reclaim's step-3 and step-4 ask would fail: R21, R23);
- a `step6-error=<class>` line in place of the counts (an uncaught read failure, printed as its class alone): re-run once, and STOP if it repeats;
- `cwd-deleted>0`, but only when (f3) did not print `rmdir-dotdot=ok`;
- `pane-stat-would-fail>0` or `btime-nonnumeric>0` (every respawn of that row would stay `pending`, a box-wide hold that "restart that session" cannot clear);
- `spell-c1>0` (R66: a `.workdir` holding a C1 control byte, 0x80 to 0x9f, which a UTF-8 locale classes as a control character and the reader's C locale does not, can leave its field `pending` for good, so it would hold every reclaim on the box, and restarting that session would not clear it: `workdirid-physical-control-byte-stays-pending`);
- `spell-not-absolute>0` (R72: not a hold, but a launch W3's line would break. The launch line asks `cd '<wd>'` twice, and for a relative `.workdir` the second `cd` resolves against the directory the first one entered, so that row's next respawn, which `cmd_ensure` makes with the stored value, would exec nothing, or exec in another directory: `relative-workdir-second-cd-does-not-enter`. The coordinator reports the count to the operator, who restarts each such row with `ccd start <id>`, which stores the absolute spelling, or purges it, before the wave goes on. A re-run of this step must then print no `spell-not-absolute` line);
- `records-sharing-an-inode>0` or `records-main-by-identity>0` (Task 8's new rc 2 and `REC_MAIN` by identity);
- `rows-workdirid>0` (no field may exist before W3: something wrote one);
- `mountinfo-malformed>0` or `mountinfo-lines=0` (the walk's `M 0 un malformed|empty`: every rows-rung call on this box would hold every child unmeasured, R13).

Recorded only:
- the row counts, with `legacy rows = rows-workdir - rows-workdirid` (or `rows-workdir` with `legacy-count-unmeasured` recorded), for the wave-done and §4.12 (R9);
- the spelling classes other than `spell-c1` and `spell-not-absolute` (STOPs above), `spell-backslash` among them (R54: counts only; each such row gets a writer and round-trips to `valid` under sh, bash and zsh, and under fish for every spelling without `\\` or a trailing `\`, as Tasks 4 and 5 pin). A non-zero `spell-backslash` is recorded, not a STOP (R65): under a fish pane shell such a row's launch `cd` reads those as escapes, so its `pending` stands (`fish-spawn-cd-reads-backslash-escapes`), as its pane failed to start before W3, and purging the row clears it;
- `rows-gone` and `rows-gone-with-crumb` (they hold every child today);
- `btime-nonzero`, `btime-none`, `prefixes`, `prefix-depth-max`;
- `rows-with-a-second-spelling` (W0: all) and `rows-spelled-through-the-wider-mount` (W0: 0);
- `admin-entries` and `admin-entries-blank` (R97's reach);
- `cwd-eacces`, `cwd-on-network-or-fuse` (Lens 4 judges the hang risk);
- `probe-stats`, `probe-ms`, the load and the versions.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the fence, `server/test/ccd-worktree-identity-fence.test.ts`**

```ts
// path-identity W3, Task 1 (path-identity spec §4; the wave's add-only invariant, R33). THE FENCE: every hold the rows
// rung, the record reader, `_ws_reclaim_owned` and the shared reclaim and expiry tail give TODAY, frozen as a table
// before W3 changes any placement. Each row names its caller, the word it gives on W2's head (`today`), and the words
// it may give after any later W3 task (`allowed`): today's word and only stricter ones. A retryable hold may become a
// terminal refusal. A tail's `worktree-remove-failed` may become `containment-refuted`. A FRESH verb may stop earlier,
// at its in-lock recompute's `probe-unmeasured`, before the kill. A row never releases: no token, no `reclaimed` or
// `expired`, no rc 0 that clears. A tail row leaves its tree, its branch and its breadcrumb standing. The CONTROL
// cases pin today's PASS on a clean child through every caller, against the host's own mount table. A CONTROL that
// reds after a later task is a narrowing on the clean layout, never a fence row to relax.
// THESE ARE FENCES, NOT RED-FIRST TESTS. They were measured green on W2's head, and each is proven to bite by a
// mutation that deletes an EXISTING guard of ccd and is measured red (the path-identity W3 plan's Task 1 table). Every
// later W3 task that edits `ccd/ccd` re-runs this file. `W3_FENCE_BASE=1` adds the base check: each row's word, and a
// tail row's breadcrumb, equal what this table says they were on W2's head.
// Every other row is HAND-PLANTED (`.uuid` and `.workdir` written here, `.project` where git's record must place it),
// so it stays a legacy row whatever W3 seeds for new ones. The one exception is the MOVED family of
// `containmentRefutedFamilies.ts`, whose row `cmd_ws_add` mints. The fence asserts words, never reasons.
// FIXTURE HOME ONLY (`makePrHarness`): every repository, row, leaf and mount table is under the harness's HOME. The
// unit and the pane are recorded, never touched (`CHILD_STUBS`, `EXP_STUBS`). Mounts are FAKED (`MOUNTS_SEAM` over a
// copy of this process's table), never made. The expiry ladder's working-directory probe reads a fake process root
// (`FAKE_PROC_SELF`), except where a row needs a real process in the tree (`holdCwd`). The reclaim and expiry tail's
// post-kill wait walks the real `/proc` (counted by `PROC_SPY`), so CLAUDE.md lists this file as a load flake. Linux
// only: the faked table, the `//` spelling bash keeps and the expiry's `/proc` probe are Linux shapes.
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { makePrHarness, type PrHarness } from './ccdPrHelpers.js';
import { CHILD_BRANCH, CHILD_ID, childReclaimVerb, evalOf, makeChild, type Child } from './childReclaimFixture.js';
import { verbHelpers } from './childReclaimVerbHelpers.js';
import { FAMILIES } from './containmentRefutedFamilies.js';
import {
  EXP_BRANCH, EXP_ID, EXP_STUBS, expireAudit, expireToken, expireVerb, holdCwd, makeArchived, type Archived,
} from './wsExpireFixture.js';
import { COL_ID, MOUNTS_SEAM, realMounts } from './wsCollectFixture.js';
import { FAKE_PROC_SELF } from './worktreeIdentityFixture.js';

let h: PrHarness;
beforeEach(() => { h = makePrHarness('ccrc-wtid-fence-'); });
afterEach(() => { h.cleanup(); });
const { interrupted, resumeToken, unsupervised } = verbHelpers(() => h);

const LINUX = process.platform === 'linux';
/** `W3_FENCE_BASE=1`: each row's word, and a tail row's breadcrumb, must equal what this table says for W2's head. */
const BASE = process.env['W3_FENCE_BASE'] === '1';
const WAIT = 'CCD_RECLAIM_TMPROOT_WAIT_S=2;';
/** Every walk of the real /proc the tail's wait makes (`_ws_path_users`, through its seam), one line each. */
const PROC_SPY = '_ws_path_users_proc_root() { echo walk >> "$HOME/proc-walks"; printf "%s" /proc; };';
/** git's worktree list cannot be read; every other git call is the real one. */
const LIST_FAILS = 'git() { case "$*" in *"worktree list"*) return 128 ;; esac; command git "$@"; };';

type Run = { code: number; stdout: string; stderr: string };
type Caller = 'L' | 'X' | 'C' | 'O' | 'R' | 'V' | 'E';
interface Tail {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly act: 'reclaim' | 'expire';
  /** Files that must stand afterwards: the subject's tree, or another session's work. */
  readonly stands: readonly string[];
  readonly branches: readonly { readonly main: string; readonly name: string }[];
}
interface Outcome {
  /** The ladder's verdict, the audit document's verdict, an rc, or the verb document's `failed`/`refused` word. */
  readonly word: string;
  /** A token, a `reclaimed`/`expired` document, or an rc 0 that clears. */
  readonly minted: boolean;
  readonly detail: string;
  readonly tail?: Tail;
}
interface Row {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly caller: Caller;
  readonly title: string;
  readonly today: string;
  /** A tail row's breadcrumb on W2's head. */
  readonly crumb?: string;
  readonly allowed: readonly string[];
  readonly run: () => Outcome;
}

// The words a row may give after a later task: today's, and only stricter ones.
const UNMEASURED = ['unmeasured', 'containment-unproven', 'not-a-workspace'] as const;
const UNPROVEN = ['containment-unproven'] as const;
const IN_USE = ['in-use'] as const;
const RC1 = ['1'] as const;
const RC2 = ['2', '1'] as const;
const LIST_RC2 = ['2'] as const;
const FAILED_FRESH = ['worktree-remove-failed', 'containment-refuted', 'probe-unmeasured'] as const;
const FAILED_RESUMED = ['worktree-remove-failed', 'containment-refuted'] as const;
const REFUTED = ['containment-refuted'] as const;

const reg = (file: string): string => path.join(h.home, '.cc-sessions', file);
const linesOf = (name: string): string[] => {
  const p = path.join(h.home, name);
  return fs.existsSync(p) ? fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean) : [];
};
/** Another session's row, HAND-PLANTED as `ccd start` writes one: `.uuid`, `.workdir`, and `.project` when given. */
const otherRow = (id: string, workdir: string, project?: string): void => {
  fs.writeFileSync(reg(`${id}.uuid`), `u-${id}`);
  fs.writeFileSync(reg(`${id}.workdir`), workdir);
  if (project !== undefined) fs.writeFileSync(reg(`${id}.project`), project);
};
/** `$HOME/alias` a link to `tree`, `<tree>/server` standing, and a row spelled `$HOME/alias/server`: inside by its
 *  resolution only. */
const aliasRow = (tree: string): void => {
  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(tree, 'server'), { recursive: true });
  fs.symlinkSync(tree, path.join(h.home, 'alias'));
  otherRow('demo-alias', path.join(h.home, 'alias', 'server'));
};
/** A linked worktree of `main` at `wt` on `branch`, recorded by git, and a hand-planted row naming it in `project`.
 *  Answers its admin directory. */
const sibling = (main: string, project: string, id: string, wt: string, branch: string): string => {
  fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(wt), { recursive: true });
  h.git(main, 'worktree', 'add', '-q', '-b', branch, wt);
  otherRow(id, wt, project);
  return h.git(wt, 'rev-parse', '--absolute-git-dir');
};
/** git's admin entry `<main>/.git/worktrees/<slug>`: its `gitdir` rewritten with `body`. */
const emptyGitdir = (main: string, slug: string, body: string): void => {
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(main, '.git', 'worktrees', slug, 'gitdir'), body);
};
/** `projects/demo2`: a LINKED worktree of the child's repository, used as a project directory. */
const linkedProject = (c: Child): string => {
  const demo2 = path.join(h.home, 'projects', 'demo2');
  h.git(c.main, 'worktree', 'add', '-q', '-b', 'proj2-main', demo2);
  return demo2;
};
/** A mount point as the kernel's table writes it: space, tab, newline and backslash encoded. */
const encoded = (p: string): string =>
  p.replace(/\\/g, '\\134').replace(/ /g, '\\040').replace(/\t/g, '\\011').replace(/\n/g, '\\012');
const MOUNT_LINE = (p: string): string => `9999 1 0:99 / ${encoded(p)} rw,relatime - tmpfs tmpfs rw`;
/** Appends a mount at `p` (physical) to the faked table at `$HOME/mountinfo`. */
const mountAt = (p: string): void => { fs.appendFileSync(path.join(h.home, 'mountinfo'), `${MOUNT_LINE(p)}\n`); };
const childFiles = (c: Child): string[] => [path.join(c.wt, 'f1.txt'), path.join(c.wt, 'f2.txt')];
const archivedFiles = (a: Archived): string[] => [path.join(a.wt, 'f1.txt'), path.join(a.wt, 'f2.txt')];

/** The verb's one JSON document, or `{}` when it printed none. */
const lastJson = (r: Run): Record<string, unknown> => {
  try { return JSON.parse(r.stdout.trim().split('\n').pop() || '{}') as Record<string, unknown>; } catch { return {}; }
};
/** L: `_ws_reclaim_eval`, the audit's call. */
const L = (pre = ''): Outcome => {
  const a = evalOf(h, { pre });
  return { word: a.verdict, minted: a.token !== '', detail: a.detail };
};
/** X: `ws-audit --session <id> --expire`'s document. By default the expiry's cwd probe reads `FAKE_PROC_SELF`. */
const X = (pre: string = FAKE_PROC_SELF): Outcome => {
  const r = expireAudit(h, { pre });
  const doc = lastJson(r);
  return {
    word: doc['verdict'] !== undefined ? String(doc['verdict']) : `no document (exit ${r.code})`,
    minted: typeof doc['token'] === 'string' && doc['token'] !== '',
    detail: String(doc['detail'] ?? `${r.stdout}${r.stderr}`),
  };
};
/** The dead child the collector's row rule is asked about: no row, a temp-root leaf. */
const leafC = (): string => path.join(h.home, '.cc-tmp', COL_ID);
/** C: `_ws_collect_rows_clear` with the leaf as the workdir, contained as its callers ask it. */
const C = (): Outcome => {
  const [rc = '', why = ''] = h.sh(`_ws_reclaim_contained _ws_collect_rows_clear ${COL_ID} '${leafC()}'; rc=$?;`
    + ' printf \'%s\\x1f%s\' "$rc" "$_WS_COLLECT_ROWS_WHY"').split('\x1f');
  return { word: rc, minted: rc === '0', detail: why };
};
/** O: `_ws_reclaim_owned`, the tail's re-ask, called directly. */
const O = (wd: string, main: string, pre = ''): Outcome => {
  const [rc = '', why = ''] = h.sh(`${pre} _ws_reclaim_owned ${CHILD_ID} "${wd}" "${main}"; printf '%s\\x1f%s' "$?" "$_WS_OWNED_WHY"`)
    .split('\x1f');
  return { word: rc, minted: rc === '0', detail: why };
};
/** V or E: the verb's document, read as a word. */
const verb = (r: Run, tail: Tail): Outcome => {
  const doc = lastJson(r);
  const done = doc['reclaimed'] !== undefined || doc['expired'] !== undefined;
  const said = doc['failed'] ?? doc['refused'];
  return {
    word: said !== undefined ? String(said) : (done ? 'done' : `no document (exit ${r.code})`),
    minted: done,
    detail: String(doc['detail'] ?? `${r.stdout}${r.stderr}`),
    tail,
  };
};
const childTail = (c: Child, stands: readonly string[], more: readonly string[] = []): Tail => ({
  id: CHILD_ID, act: 'reclaim', stands, branches: [CHILD_BRANCH, ...more].map((name) => ({ main: c.main, name })),
});
const expiryTail = (a: Archived, stands: readonly string[]): Tail => ({
  id: EXP_ID, act: 'expire', stands, branches: [{ main: a.main, name: EXP_BRANCH }],
});
const reclaimToken = (): string => {
  const a = evalOf(h);
  expect(a.token, `the CONTROL: the ladder passes — ${a.verdict}: ${a.detail}`).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/);
  return a.token;
};
const expiryToken = (): string => {
  const t = expireToken(h, { pre: FAKE_PROC_SELF });
  expect(t, 'the CONTROL: the expiry ladder passes').toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/);
  return t;
};
/** A reclaim interrupted after its pin, its breadcrumb at `worktree`, and the resume token, minted before any shape. */
const resumedReclaim = (c: Child): string => {
  interrupted(c, 'worktree');
  const t = resumeToken('worktree');
  expect(t, 'the CONTROL: the resumed reclaim mints its token').toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/);
  return t;
};
/** The same for an expiry (`ccd-expire-tail-refuted.test.ts`'s resumed case), its cwd probe on `FAKE_PROC_SELF`. */
const resumedExpiry = (a: Archived): string => {
  h.sh(`${EXP_STUBS} ${FAKE_PROC_SELF} _WS_RCL_ACT=expire; _ws_expire_eval ${EXP_ID} >/dev/null`
    + ` && _ws_reclaim_pin ${EXP_ID} "${a.wt}" "${a.main}" "$REAP_BRANCH" "$EXPIRE_ARCHIVED_AT"`
    + ` && _ws_tombstone ${EXP_ID} '[]' "$(_ws_reclaim_tomb_fields "$EXPIRE_ARCHIVED_AT" present)" >/dev/null`
    + ` && _reg_set ${EXP_ID} reaping expire:worktree`);
  expect(h.reg(EXP_ID, 'reaping'), 'the CONTROL: interrupted at `worktree`').toBe('expire:worktree');
  const t = h.sh(`${EXP_STUBS} ${FAKE_PROC_SELF} _WS_RCL_ACT=expire; _ws_expire_resume_eval ${EXP_ID} worktree >/dev/null;`
    + ' printf \'%s\' "$REAP_TOKEN"');
  expect(t, 'the CONTROL: the resumed expiry mints its token').toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/);
  return t;
};

      return verb(childReclaimVerb(h, tok, { pre: `${WAIT} ${PROC_SPY}` }),
        childTail(c, [...shape.keeps, ...(shape.treeStands ? childFiles(c) : [])]));
    },
  })),
  { id: 'F17.E.0', caller: 'E', title: `a proven refusal planted after the resume token — ${FAMILIES[0]!.name}`, today: 'containment-refuted', crumb: 'expire:worktree', allowed: REFUTED,
    run: () => {
      const a = makeArchived(h);
      const shape = FAMILIES[0]!.make(h, { id: EXP_ID, wt: a.wt, main: a.main });
      const tok = resumedExpiry(a);
      h.sh(shape.plant);
      return verb(expireVerb(h, tok, { pre: `${FAKE_PROC_SELF} ${WAIT} ${PROC_SPY}` }),
        expiryTail(a, [...shape.keeps, ...archivedFiles(a)]));
    } },
  { id: 'F18.X', caller: 'X', title: 'a real process works inside the archived tree', today: 'in-use', allowed: IN_USE,
    run: () => {
      const a = makeArchived(h);
      const s = holdCwd(a.wt);
      try { return X(''); } finally { s.stop(); }
    } },
];

/** Every row's own assertions. The measurement line is printed FIRST, so a red row still reports what it gave. */
const holds = (row: Row, o: Outcome): void => {
  const crumb = o.tail ? h.reg(o.tail.id, 'reaping') : null;
  console.info(`fence ${row.id} word=${o.word} crumb=${o.tail ? String(crumb) : '-'} walks=${o.tail ? linesOf('proc-walks').length : '-'}`);
  if (BASE) expect(o.word, `${row.id}: the word it gives on W2's head — ${o.detail}`).toBe(row.today);
  expect(row.allowed, `${row.id}: ${o.word} is today’s word or a stricter one — ${o.detail}`).toContain(o.word);
  expect(o.minted, `${row.id}: nothing was released — ${o.detail}`).toBe(false);
  if (!o.tail) return;
  for (const f of o.tail.stands) expect(fs.existsSync(f), `${row.id}: ${f} stands`).toBe(true);
  for (const b of o.tail.branches) {
    expect(h.git(b.main, 'branch', '--list', b.name), `${row.id}: the branch ${b.name} stands`).toContain(b.name);
  }
  if (o.word === 'probe-unmeasured') {
    expect(crumb, `${row.id}: the in-lock recompute stopped the act before its pin, so no breadcrumb`).toBeNull();
    expect(unsupervised(), `${row.id}: and before the unit was touched`).toEqual([]);
  } else {
    expect(crumb ?? '', `${row.id}: the breadcrumb stands, for the retry`).toMatch(new RegExp(`^${o.tail.act}:`));
    if (BASE) expect(crumb, `${row.id}: the step it stopped at on W2's head`).toBe(row.crumb);
  }
};

describe.skipIf(!LINUX)('the add-only fence: today’s holds, frozen as a table (path-identity spec §4)', () => {
  it('the table is sane: unique ids, every row’s today among its allowed words, a breadcrumb on tail rows only', () => {
    const ids = FENCE.map((r) => r.id);
    expect(new Set(ids).size, 'ids are unique').toBe(ids.length);
    expect(ids.length, 'forty-eight rows').toBe(48);
    for (const r of FENCE) {
      expect(r.allowed, `${r.id}: its today is allowed`).toContain(r.today);
      expect(r.crumb !== undefined, `${r.id}: a tail row, and only a tail row, names a breadcrumb`)
        .toBe(r.caller === 'V' || r.caller === 'E');

  });

  it.each(FENCE)('$id — $title', (row) => {
    holds(row, row.run());

describe.skipIf(!LINUX)('CONTROL: a clean child passes through every caller, against the host’s own mount table', () => {
