```ts
    expect(b.out).toMatch(/^\[rc=2\] asked with /);
    expect(b.out).toContain(`${UNWALK}any row (the identity walk did not finish within 1s)`);
  }, 60_000);
});

describe('one walk per pass', () => {
  it.each([[0], [1], [10]] as const)('one walk with %i other row(s): evalOf walks once, one link walk and one ancestry per row', (n) => {
    makeChild(h);
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
      const d = path.join(h.home, `elsewhere-${i}`);
      fs.mkdirSync(d);
      row(`demo-r${i}`, d);
    }
    const r = evalOf(h, { pre: walkSpy });
    expect(r.verdict, r.detail).toBe('reclaimable');
    const calls = linesIn('walk-calls');
    expect(calls, 'one walk').toHaveLength(1);
    const toks = calls[0]!.split(' ').slice(1);
    expect(toks.filter((t) => t.startsWith('P')), 'one link walk per row').toHaveLength(n);
    expect(toks.filter((t) => t.startsWith('A')), 'one ancestry per row').toHaveLength(n);
    expect(toks).toContain('T0');
    if (LINUX) expect(toks).toContain('M0');
    else expect(toks).not.toContain('M0');
  }, 60_000);
});

describe('a request stream cut short is unmeasured, never "no row"', () => {
  /** `_ws_reclaim_idwalk`, wrapped: it hands the real walk only the FIRST request it was given, target 0, as a
   *  request stream whose writer stopped after one record would reach it, so the table's `M` (on Linux) and the row's
   *  `P` and `A` are dropped (R64). The walk answers that one request whole, rc 0. */
  const FIRST_ONLY = 'eval "_t_walk_real()$(declare -f _ws_reclaim_idwalk | tail -n +2)";'
    + ' _ws_reclaim_idwalk() { local _t_q=\'\'; IFS= read -r -d \'\' _t_q || :;'
    + ' _t_walk_real "$@" < <(printf \'%s\\0\' "$_t_q"); };';

  it('short stream: the walk handed target 0 alone answers it whole, and the rung, matching the reply with its own requests, holds every row', () => {
    makeChild(h);
    const d = path.join(h.home, 'elsewhere-0');
    fs.mkdirSync(d);
    row('demo-r0', d);
    const r = evalOf(h, { pre: FIRST_ONLY });
    expect(r.verdict, r.detail).toBe('unmeasured');
    expect(r.token).toBe('');
    expect(r.detail).toContain(`${UNWALK}any row (the walk answered a request list it was not given whole)`);
  }, 60_000);
});

describe.skipIf(!LINUX)('parity: the walk’s mount point arm answers what `_ws_collect_mounts_clear` answers, on the same tables (R13)', () => {
  /** One copied table plus `lines`, then the walk asked T0 and M of `child`, and the collector's own reader asked of
   *  `child`: `[<walk rc>, <its M line>, <_ws_collect_mounts_clear rc>]`. */
  const both = (child: string, lines: string[]): string[] => {
    realMounts(h);
    for (const l of lines) mountAt(l);
    return h.sh(`${MOUNTS_SEAM} MI=$(_ws_collect_mountinfo);`
      + ' _ws_reclaim_idwalk "$MI" < <(printf \'T\\t0\\t%s\\0M\\t0\\t%s\\0\' "$W3_CHILD" "$MI"); w=$?;'
      + ' m=$(printf \'%s\\n\' "$_WS_IDWALK_OUT" | grep \'^M 0 \'); _ws_collect_mounts_clear "$W3_CHILD";'
      + ' printf \'%s|%s|%s\' "$w" "$m" "$?"', { W3_CHILD: child }).split('|');
  };
  const expectParity = (got: string[], want: 'point' | 'clear'): void => {
    const [w = '', m = '', rc = ''] = got;
    expect(w, 'the walk answered').toBe('0');
    if (want === 'point') {
      expect(m).toBe('M 0 hold point');
      expect(rc, '_ws_collect_mounts_clear: a mount stands').toBe('1');
    } else {
      expect(m).toMatch(/^M 0 clear \d+$/);
      expect(rc, '_ws_collect_mounts_clear: none').toBe('0');
    }
  };

  it.each([
    ['clean', (_c: string): string[] => [], 'clear'],
    ['a mount point AT the child', (c: string): string[] => [c], 'point'],
    ['a mount point UNDER it', (c: string): string[] => [`${c}/m`], 'point'],
    ['a SIBLING, `<child>-x`', (c: string): string[] => [`${c}-x`], 'clear'],
  ] as const)('parity %s', (_what, plant, want) => {
    const child = path.join(h.home, 'pc', 'c');
    fs.mkdirSync(child, { recursive: true });
    expectParity(both(child, plant(child)), want);
  });

  it('parity a child spelled with a space, compared encoded', () => {
    const child = path.join(h.home, 'sp ace', 'c');
    fs.mkdirSync(child, { recursive: true });
    expectParity(both(child, [`${child}/m`]), 'point');
  });
});

describe('the mount table has exactly two readers, both through its one seam (R13)', () => {
  it('two readers: the call graph’s callers of `_ws_collect_mountinfo` are `_ws_collect_mounts_clear` and the rows rung', () => {
    const callers = ccdCallGraph().filter((e) => e.callee === '_ws_collect_mountinfo').map((e) => e.caller).sort();
    expect(callers).toEqual(['_ws_collect_mounts_clear', '_ws_reclaim_workdir_shared']);
  });

  it('one literal: /proc/self/mountinfo stands in ccd’s code only in the seam and in `_carry_py`’s own CCD_MOUNTINFO reader', () => {
    const holders = new Set<string>();
    let fn = '';
    for (const l of fs.readFileSync(CCD, 'utf8').split('\n')) {
      const m = CCD_FUNCTION_DEF.exec(l);
      if (m) fn = m[1]!;
      if (bashCodeOf(l).includes('/proc/self/mountinfo')) holders.add(fn);
    }
    expect([...holders].sort()).toEqual(['_carry_py', '_ws_collect_mountinfo']);
  });
});
```

**2b. `server/test/collect-audit-budget.test.ts`.** Replace the whole file with:
```ts
// Child reclamation wave 9 (spec 2026-09-22 §5.10, "The idle floor"): `ws-audit --collect` keeps `ws-audit`'s runner
// row. Its bounded probes run in sequence (the idle walk, the in-use probe, the checkout scan and, since path-identity
// W3, the registry row pass's one identity walk), and a probe that reaches its bound ends the audit, so ONE
// TERM-to-KILL grace is paid. That sum must stay under the row, at the default grace and at the widest. The halves
// live in two languages and neither can import the other's number, so each is read from source as TEXT, and each
// read asserts it matched exactly once (`docs-budget.test.ts`'s method). Stated residual: the row pass's git reads of
// a gone row's repository carry no bound of their own and are not in the sum (`rows-rung-git-reads-unbounded`). A
// runner kill there answers no document, which the lane reads as `no-document` and paces as a failure, so it fails
// closed.
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const ROOT = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..');
const readRel = (r: string): string => readFileSync(path.join(ROOT, r), 'utf8');

/** The one match of `re` (a `g` regex) in `text`; throws on zero or on more than one. */
function exactlyOne(text: string, re: RegExp, what: string): RegExpMatchArray {
  const hits = [...text.matchAll(re)];
  if (hits.length !== 1) throw new Error(`${what}: ${hits.length} matches; exactly one is expected`);
  return hits[0]!;
}

interface CollectAuditBudget {
  readonly idleS: number; readonly usersS: number; readonly scanS: number; readonly walkS: number;
  readonly graceS: number; readonly graceMaxS: number; readonly rowS: number;
}

function collectAuditBudgetIn(ccd: string, runner: string): CollectAuditBudget {
  const int = (re: RegExp, what: string): number => Number(exactlyOne(ccd, re, what)[1]!);
  const row = exactlyOne(runner, /^[ \t]*'ws-audit':[ \t]*([\d_]+),/gm, "CCD_VERB_TIMEOUT_MS['ws-audit']");
  return {
    idleS: int(/^WS_COLLECT_IDLE_SCAN_S=(\d+)\b/gm, 'WS_COLLECT_IDLE_SCAN_S'),
    usersS: int(/^WS_PATH_USERS_SCAN_S=(\d+)\b/gm, 'WS_PATH_USERS_SCAN_S'),
    scanS: int(/^REAP_SCAN_SECONDS=(\d+)\b/gm, 'REAP_SCAN_SECONDS'),
    walkS: int(/^WS_RECLAIM_WALK_S=(\d+)\b/gm, 'WS_RECLAIM_WALK_S'),
    graceS: int(/grace="\$\{CCD_TIMEOUT_KILL_AFTER:-(\d+)\}"/g, "_plat_timeout's default grace"),
    graceMaxS: int(/\[ "\$grace" -gt (\d+) \] && grace=\1\b/g, "_plat_timeout's grace ceiling"),
    rowS: Number(row[1]!.replace(/_/g, '')) / 1000,
  };
}

const ccdSrc = (): string => readRel('ccd/ccd');
const runnerSrc = (): string => readRel('server/src/remote/runner.ts');
const probesS = (b: CollectAuditBudget): number => b.idleS + b.usersS + b.scanS + b.walkS;

describe('the collect audit fits ws-audit’s runner row (spec §5.10)', () => {
  it('reads 30 + 10 + 30 + 5 s of probes and a 3 s grace capped at 8, against a 90 s row', () => {
    expect(collectAuditBudgetIn(ccdSrc(), runnerSrc()))
      .toEqual({ idleS: 30, usersS: 10, scanS: 30, walkS: 5, graceS: 3, graceMaxS: 8, rowS: 90 });
  });

  it('the probes and ONE grace sum under the row: 78 s at the default grace, 83 s at the widest', () => {
    const b = collectAuditBudgetIn(ccdSrc(), runnerSrc());
    expect(probesS(b) + b.graceS).toBeLessThan(b.rowS);
    expect(probesS(b) + b.graceMaxS).toBeLessThan(b.rowS);
  });
});

describe('CONTROL: the reads refuse zero and two, and a longer probe breaks the sum', () => {
  it('a renamed or doubled binding throws', () => {
    const ccd = ccdSrc(); const runner = runnerSrc();
    expect(() => collectAuditBudgetIn(ccd.replace(/^WS_COLLECT_IDLE_SCAN_S=/m, 'WS_COLLECT_IDLE_S='), runner)).toThrow(/WS_COLLECT_IDLE_SCAN_S: 0 matches/);
    expect(() => collectAuditBudgetIn(`${ccd}\nREAP_SCAN_SECONDS=30\n`, runner)).toThrow(/REAP_SCAN_SECONDS: 2 matches/);
    expect(() => collectAuditBudgetIn(`${ccd}\nWS_RECLAIM_WALK_S=5\n`, runner)).toThrow(/WS_RECLAIM_WALK_S: 2 matches/);
    expect(() => collectAuditBudgetIn(ccd, runner.replace("'ws-audit': 90_000,", '// gone'))).toThrow(/ws-audit'\]: 0 matches/);
  });

  it('a 50 s idle walk would not fit', () => {
    const b = collectAuditBudgetIn(ccdSrc().replace(/^WS_COLLECT_IDLE_SCAN_S=30\b/m, 'WS_COLLECT_IDLE_SCAN_S=50'), runnerSrc());
    expect(probesS(b) + b.graceS).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(b.rowS);
  });

  it('a 13 s walk would not fit at the widest grace', () => {
    const b = collectAuditBudgetIn(ccdSrc().replace(/^WS_RECLAIM_WALK_S=5\b/m, 'WS_RECLAIM_WALK_S=13'), runnerSrc());
    expect(b.walkS, 'the CONTROL: the 13 s walk was read').toBe(13);
    expect(probesS(b) + b.graceS, 'it still fits at the default grace').toBeLessThan(b.rowS);
    expect(probesS(b) + b.graceMaxS).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(b.rowS);
  });
});
```

After:

```bash
  # re-points the spelling by replacement. And `complete` places the
```

```bash
  # session entered through it also resolves complete and outside, and only
  # an entry identity the session itself recorded can answer that
  # (path-identity spec §4.3); a row with none is placed as its spelling reads
```

**4d. The two header paragraphs, and the locals.** Before:
```bash
  # other not-asked arm, outranked by a SHARED, NESTED or THROUGH row.
  local id="$1" wd="$2" mine='' minewhy='' names n o w wr rok basis rc lit unread='' unplaced='' unmine='' unproc='' unres=''

```
After:
```bash
  # other not-asked arm, outranked by a SHARED, NESTED or THROUGH row.
  #
  # AND BY DEVICE AND INODE, BESIDE THE STRINGS (path-identity spec §4.5 and
  # §4.8; PI3 B, PI6 M4). A string says where a spelling reads now, and a bind
  # mount or a link gives one directory two spellings that share no prefix. So
  # every row whose spelling resolved `complete` is also placed by the device
  # and inode of each directory on its resolved path, from `/` down: a row
  # whose path IS the child's tree is SHARED, and one with the child's tree, or
  # a standing directory leaf, above it is NESTED — the strings' own words, and
  # no new one. The child is a target only when its own spelling resolved
  # `complete` and its tree stands: a vanished child is the eval's vanished
  # fork, unchanged, and the collector's moved leaf has nothing here to ask.
  # EVERY ROW SPELLED ABSOLUTE IS ALSO WALKED FOR A LINK INTO `/proc` (m1): a
  # link whose raw target is `/proc` behind any number of `/`, or a walk whose
  # physical position enters `/proc` through a relative one, names the reading
  # process's own cwd exactly as the literal row above does, and is collected
  # with it (`unproc`). AND THE CHILD'S TREE IS HELD WHERE A MOUNT COULD GIVE IT
  # ANOTHER SPELLING: a mount point at or under it, a mount of its file system
  # whose root lies at or under its device-relative path (`//deleted`
  # included), or a table that cannot place it (empty, unreadable, malformed,
  # or a containing line whose `major:minor` is not the child's device) is
  # collected (`unmount`), unmeasured and never "no row". The table is read
  # through the collector's one seam, by this walk as its declared second
  # reader; `_ws_collect_mounts_clear` is the first. Every answer only ADDS: a
  # placement, or a not-asked arm decided after the loop and outranked by any
  # SHARED, NESTED or THROUGH row. Nothing the walk answers removes a row from
  # any bucket.
  #
  # ONE WALK, BOUNDED (path-identity spec §4.9; PI8 B2). The targets, every
  # row's ancestry and link walk, and the mount table are asked in ONE
  # `_ws_reclaim_idwalk` call per pass, under `WS_RECLAIM_WALK_S`, and its maps
  # live for this call only. A walk that did not finish, failed or answered
  # short, and any row, target or leaf it could not answer for, is collected
  # (`unwalk`), never "no row". On Darwin no table is asked (one line below), so
  # the ancestry arm stands alone there. THE WALK FOLLOWS LINKS (`stat`), as
  # the kernel does for a process entering the spelling, which leaves four
  # things to judgement, stated here: a real bind answers its source's device
  # and inode for every path below it, a bind from another file system
  # included; `pwd -P` and `/proc/<pid>/cwd` read the bind's spelling in this
  # process's mount namespace, the one the verbs run in; mountinfo's field 3
  # equals `stat`'s major:minor on the fleet's file systems (measured on the
  # fleet box before this was built; where it does not, the device check
  # answers unmeasured); and a link that appears after the resolve is walked as
  # the namespace reads it now, which can only add. The gone-row recovery's git
  # reads (its two arms) are outside the walk and have no bound of their own
  # (`rows-rung-git-reads-unbounded`).
  local id="$1" wd="$2" mine='' minewhy='' names n o w wr rok basis rc lit unread='' unplaced='' unmine='' unproc='' unres=''
  local llit lhit lw lr k unleaf=''
  local -a lspell=() lres=()
  local minebasis='' mi='' mreq=0 nbt=0 jb t0='' ri hk hi hw ha hrest q unwalk='' unmount=''
  local -a rid=() req=()
  local _WS_IDWALK_OUT='' _WS_IDWALK_WHY=''
```

**4f. The walk's targets and its table, queued before the row loop.** Before:
```bash
    lspell+=("$lw"); lres+=("$lr")
  done
  while IFS= read -r n; do
```
After:
```bash
    lspell+=("$lw"); lres+=("$lr")
  done
  # THE WALK'S TARGETS AND ITS TABLE, asked first (path-identity spec §4.5).
  # The child is target 0 only when its own spelling resolved `complete` and
  # its tree stands. Bash's `pwd -P` keeps a link target's leading `//`, which
  # Linux reads as `/` and the table never writes, so it is collapsed. Each
  # standing directory leaf is target 1 or 2. The table is asked only with
  # target 0; a seam that names no table holds the child, never "no mount".
  if [[ "$minebasis" == complete && -d "$mine" ]]; then
    t0="$mine"; [[ "$t0" != //[!/]* ]] || t0="${t0#/}"
    req+=("T"$'\t'0$'\t'"$t0")
    [[ "$CCD_OS" == darwin ]] || mreq=1   # Darwin keeps no mount table: the ancestry arm stands alone there
    if (( mreq )); then
      mi=$(_ws_collect_mountinfo)
      if [[ -n "$mi" ]]; then req+=("M"$'\t'0$'\t'"$mi"); else unmount=unreadable; fi
    fi
  fi
  for (( k = 0; k < ${#lres[@]}; k++ )); do
    [[ -z "${lres[k]}" ]] || req+=("T"$'\t'"$(( k + 1 ))"$'\t'"${lres[k]}")
  done
  while IFS= read -r n; do
```


After:


**4j. The one walk, its reply match (R64) and pass B, before the outrank line.** Before:
```bash
  done <<< "$names"
  [[ -z "$_WS_SHARED_ROWS$_WS_NESTED_ROWS$_WS_THROUGH_ROWS" ]] || return 0
```
After:
```bash
  done <<< "$names"
  # THE ONE WALK, and its answers, which only ever ADD (pass B). A walk that
  # did not answer is collected whole; a row, target or leaf it could not
  # answer for is collected by name. A row a string arm already placed is not
  # placed twice.
  _ws_reclaim_idwalk "$mi" < <(for q in ${req[@]+"${req[@]}"}; do printf '%s\0' "$q"; done); rc=$?
  (( rc == 0 )) || unwalk="any row ($_WS_IDWALK_WHY)"
  # THE REPLY IS MATCHED WITH THIS PASS'S OWN LIST (path-identity spec §4.9).
  # The walk matches its reply with the requests it READ, and a request stream
  # cut short reads to it as a clean end of file, so it can answer a shorter
  # list whole. So a walk that answered 0 is matched here too: before its
  # `end`, one line per element of `req`, in order, naming that request's kind
  # and index, then one `B <j>` line per birth-time path the call above hands
  # it (`nbt`), in order. Any other reply is a list the walk was not given
  # whole, and answers for no row.
  if (( rc == 0 )); then
    k=0; jb=0
    while read -r hk hi hrest; do
      [[ "$hk" != end ]] || break
      if [[ "$hk" == B ]]; then
        (( k == ${#req[@]} )) && [[ "$hi" == "$jb" ]] || { k=-1; break; }
        jb=$(( jb + 1 )); continue
      fi
      q="${req[k]-}"; hw="${q#*$'\t'}"
      (( jb == 0 )) && [[ -n "$q" && "$hk" == "${q%%$'\t'*}" && "$hi" == "${hw%%$'\t'*}" ]] || { k=-1; break; }
      k=$(( k + 1 ))
    done <<< "$_WS_IDWALK_OUT"
    (( k == ${#req[@]} && jb == nbt )) || { _WS_IDWALK_WHY="the walk answered a request list it was not given whole"; unwalk="any row ($_WS_IDWALK_WHY)"; rc=2; }
  fi
  if (( rc == 0 )); then
    while read -r hk hi hw ha hrest; do
      o=''
      [[ "$hi" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && o="${rid[hi]-}"
      case "$hk $hw" in
        "A ok")
          case ", $_WS_SHARED_ROWS, $_WS_NESTED_ROWS, $_WS_THROUGH_ROWS, " in
            *", $o, "*) : ;;
            *) case "$hrest" in
                 eq:0) _WS_SHARED_ROWS+="${_WS_SHARED_ROWS:+, }$o" ;;
                 in:0|eq:[12]|in:[12]) _WS_NESTED_ROWS+="${_WS_NESTED_ROWS:+, }$o" ;;
               esac ;;
          esac ;;
        "A gone"|"A un"|"P un") unwalk+="${unwalk:+, }row $o (${ha:-gone})" ;;
        "P proc") unproc+="${unproc:+, }$o" ;;
        "T gone"|"T un")
          if [[ "$hi" == 0 ]]; then unwalk+="${unwalk:+, }$id's own tree (${ha:-gone})"
          else unwalk+="${unwalk:+, }a leaf of $id (${ha:-gone})"; fi ;;
        "M hold"|"M un") unmount="$ha" ;;
      esac
    done <<< "$_WS_IDWALK_OUT"
  fi
  [[ -z "$_WS_SHARED_ROWS$_WS_NESTED_ROWS$_WS_THROUGH_ROWS" ]] || return 0
```

**8a. `server/test/ccd-reclaim-tail-mounts.test.ts`: the helper.** Insert directly after the `ASK_LOG` definition (the two lines ending `_t_ask_real "$@"; };';`):
```ts
/** `_ws_removal_mounts_clear`, wrapped: directly before its `nth` call for the path spelled `spelling`, a mount at `p`
 *  (`MOUNT_LINE`) is appended to the faked table, then the real one is asked. Since path-identity W3 the rows rung
 *  reads the same table at the verb's in-lock recompute and at the tail's owned call, and holds the child there, so a
 *  mount planted before the verb is caught before any of these asks (`w2-mount-asks-shadowed-by-the-reask`). A case
 *  that pins one of the tail's own asks plants its mount at that ask. With `ASK_LOG`, it goes first, so `ASK_LOG`
 *  wraps it and logs each call once. */
const MOUNT_AT_ASK = (spelling: string, p: string, nth: number): string =>
  'eval "_t_at_ask_real()$(declare -f _ws_removal_mounts_clear | tail -n +2)";'
  + ` _ws_removal_mounts_clear() { if [[ "$1" == '${spelling}' ]]; then _T_AT_ASK_N=$(( \${_T_AT_ASK_N:-0} + 1 ));`
  + ` (( _T_AT_ASK_N != ${nth} )) || printf '%s\\n' '${MOUNT_LINE(p)}' >> "$HOME/mountinfo"; fi; _t_at_ask_real "$@"; };`;
```

- [ ] **Step 10: Mutation table**

First, one Bash call. It copies the restamped file into the gitignored ledger and writes the one-mutation helper (W2's):

```bash
M=.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-20-path-identity-w3-worktree-identity/task3-mut; mkdir -p "$M" && cp ccd/ccd "$M/ccd.task3" && cat > "$M/mut.mjs" <<'EOF'
// One exact mutation of one file, refused unless every anchor matches exactly once.
//   node mut.mjs FILE sub OLD NEW          replace the ONE occurrence of OLD with NEW
//   node mut.mjs FILE del NEEDLE...        delete each ONE line holding NEEDLE
import fs from 'node:fs';
const [file, mode, ...a] = process.argv.slice(2);
const src = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
const lines = src.split('\n');
const fail = (m) => { console.error(`mut: ${m}`); process.exit(3); };
const one = (needle) => {
  const at = lines.flatMap((l, i) => (l.includes(needle) ? [i] : []));
  if (at.length !== 1) fail(`${JSON.stringify(needle)} is on ${at.length} lines, not one`);
  return at[0];
};
let out;
if (mode === 'sub') {
  const [o, n] = a;
  const k = src.split(o).length - 1;
  if (k !== 1) fail(`${JSON.stringify(o)} occurs ${k} times, not once`);
  out = src.replace(o, () => n);
} else if (mode === 'del') {
  const drop = new Set(a.map(one));
  out = lines.filter((_, i) => !drop.has(i)).join('\n');
} else fail(`unknown mode ${mode}`);
fs.writeFileSync(file, out);
console.log(`mut: ${mode} applied to ${file}`);
EOF
```

How each row runs:
- Each row is ONE Bash call, from the workspace root, in the foreground, with a timeout of at least 600000 ms.
- It applies the mutation, runs the named cases, restores the file whatever vitest answered, and proves the restore with `cmp`.
- No mutation is restamped, because no suite these rows run reads the stamp.
- Every red below was drafted, not measured, so record the measured text in the ledger.
- A case listed red that stays green is a STOP, reported by its row. A case listed as a NAMED SURVIVOR is recorded green.

**Interfaces:**
- Produces, exactly as §Interfaces spells them:
  - **The field grammar** at `$REG/<id>.workdirid`. It is one line with no trailing newline, and its one regex lives in `_ws_workdirid_read`:
    ```
    valid:   v1 TAB <dev>:<ino>:<btime> TAB <at_ms> TAB <physical> TAB <logical>
    pending: v1 TAB pending TAB <at_ms> TAB - TAB <logical>
    ```
  - **`_plat_workdirid_pane() { …; }   # reg id logical -> …`** (K). One line in the platform block, byte-identical in `ccd/ccrc`.
    - It prints `/bin/sh -c '<script>' ccd-workdirid '<reg>' '<id>' '<logical>' 2>/dev/null && ` followed by a space.
    - It prints nothing when reg, id or logical is empty, when any of them holds a control character or a `'` (both of which `.workdir` refuses, in `cmd_start` and `cmd_ws_add`), or when the id holds a `/` (R60).
    - A `\` is carried, never refused (R54, the coordinator's addendum): the composer spells each `\` of reg, id and logical as `\0134` inside its single-quoted argument, and the script decodes each argument once with `printf %b` before any use, so the line it writes is byte-equal to `.workdir`.
    - Its rc is always 0. It calls no function.
    - The script's per-OS parts are chosen from `$CCD_OS` when the fragment is composed.
  - **`_WS_WDID_STATE=''; _WS_WDID_WHY=''; _WS_WDID_IDENT=''; _WS_WDID_AT=''; _WS_WDID_PHYS=''`** and **`_ws_workdirid_read ID LOGICAL`** (C4):
    - rc 0 `valid`, which sets `_WS_WDID_IDENT` (`<dev>:<ino>:<btime|->`), `_WS_WDID_AT` and `_WS_WDID_PHYS`;
    - rc 1 `legacy-absent`, `legacy-link`, `legacy-unparseable` or `legacy-stale`;
    - rc 2 `pending`, or `unmeasured` with `_WS_WDID_WHY`;
    - `_WS_WDID_STATE` always names the answer;
    - the rule order is P6's (§Interfaces, the nine rules).
  - **The seed statement:** `( CDPATH= builtin cd -- "<wd>" >/dev/null 2>&1 && eval "$(_plat_workdirid_pane "$REG" "$id" "<wd>"):" ) || :`. It appears in `cmd_start` (with `$workdir`) and on `cmd_ws_add`'s `.workdir` line (with `$wt`).
  - **Test-local, read by name later:**
    - `writeField(h, id, body)` (P18), filled here;
    - `WORKDIRID_SPELLERS` in `ccd-workdirid.test.ts`, which Task 5 extends with `_spawn_workdirid_pending`.
- Consumes:

  - `makePrHarness` and `PrHarness` (`ccdPrHelpers.ts`);

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test `server/test/ccd-workdirid.test.ts`, and fill `writeField`**

Create the file with one Bash call: `cat > server/test/ccd-workdirid.test.ts <<'EOF'`, the content below, then `EOF`. The delimiter is quoted, so every backslash and every `$` lands as written.

```ts
// path-identity W3, Task 4 (path-identity spec §4.3 and §4.4; PI1 B, PI2 L1): each session's entry identity has ONE
// field, `$REG/<id>.workdirid`, in ONE grammar held by ONE reader's regex (`_ws_workdirid_read`), and every VALID line
// is written by ONE composer, the platform block's `_plat_workdirid_pane`. The composer prints a brace-free
// `/bin/sh -c` fragment: the pane runs it after its `cd` and before its `exec`, and `start` and `ws-add` run it once to
// seed the row. The reader's answers are never folded: valid (0); legacy-absent, legacy-link, legacy-unparseable and
// legacy-stale (1); pending and unmeasured (2). The pending line's writer is the spawn's (the next task); here it is
// read by its grammar only.
// FIXTURE HOME ONLY (`makePrHarness`): every field, workdir, link, shim and wrapper lives under the harness's HOME,
// and ccd runs as sourced functions. No tmux server is started: ccd composes the pane's command, and the shell under
// test runs it from inside a harness snippet. Nothing here walks a process table.
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { makePrHarness, type PrHarness } from './ccdPrHelpers.js';
import { CCD, WS_ADD } from './ccdWsHelpers.js';
import { CCD_FUNCTION_DEF, bashCodeOf, ccdCallGraph, ccdFunctionDefinitions } from './consolidationCensus.js';
import { spawnSyncGroup } from './spawnGroup.js';
import { writeField } from './worktreeIdentityFixture.js';

const CCRC = path.join(path.dirname(CCD), 'ccrc');
const ID = 'demo-x';
const T = '\t';
const AT = '1760000000000';
const ROOT_USER = process.getuid?.() === 0;
const esc = (s: string): string => s.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
/** The first executable `name` on the suite's own PATH, or '' (read from the file system: no shell is spawned). */
const onPath = (name: string): string => (process.env['PATH'] ?? '').split(':').filter(Boolean)
  .map((d) => path.join(d, name))
  .find((p) => { try { fs.accessSync(p, fs.constants.X_OK); return fs.statSync(p).isFile(); } catch { return false; } }) ?? '';
/** The host's own tools, which a shim stands in front of. */
const REAL = { stat: onPath('stat'), mv: onPath('mv'), date: onPath('date') };
/** The host stat's device-and-inode format, for a shim that prints a birth time of its own. */
const DEVINO = process.platform === 'darwin' ? '-f %d:%i' : '-c %d:%i';

/** The functions whose CODE may spell `.workdirid` (the next task adds the spawn's pending writer here). */
const WORKDIRID_SPELLERS: readonly string[] = ['_plat_workdirid_pane', '_ws_workdirid_read'];
/** The grammar's one definition, as the reader spells it. */
const GRAMMAR = String.raw`local re=$'^v1\t(([0-9]+):([0-9]+):([1-9][0-9]*|-)|pending)\t([0-9]{13})\t([^[:cntrl:]]+)\t(/[^[:cntrl:]]*)$'`;

/** The function whose region holds line `i`, by the call graph's own rule: from a definition to the first column-0
 *  `}`, or to the next definition. */
const ownerIn = (lines: readonly string[]) => {
  const defs = lines.flatMap((l, i) => { const m = CCD_FUNCTION_DEF.exec(l); return m ? [{ name: m[1]!, at: i }] : []; });
  return (i: number): string => {
    const d = [...defs].reverse().find((x) => x.at <= i);
    if (d === undefined) return '<top level>';
    for (let j = d.at + 1; j < i; j++) if (lines[j]!.startsWith('}')) return '<top level>';
    return d.name;
  };
};

let h: PrHarness;
beforeEach(() => { h = makePrHarness('ccrc-workdirid-'); });
afterEach(() => { h.cleanup(); });

const regDir = (): string => path.join(h.home, '.cc-sessions');
const field = (id: string = ID): string => path.join(regDir(), `${id}.workdirid`);
const W = (): string => path.join(h.home, 'w');
const tmps = (): string[] => fs.readdirSync(regDir()).filter((n) => n.endsWith('.tmp'));
/** A valid line for `logical`, its physical spelling `phys`. */
const line = (phys: string, logical: string = W(), ident = '11:22:33'): string =>
  `v1${T}${ident}${T}${AT}${T}${phys}${T}${logical}`;
/** A valid line of exactly `n` bytes, its physical spelling padded. */
const padded = (n: number): string => line(`/${'a'.repeat(n - line('/').length)}`);

/** The reader, and its answer on one line: `[rc=<n>] <state>|<ident>|<physical>|<why>`. */
const READ = (logical: string, id: string = ID): string =>
  `_ws_workdirid_read ${id} '${logical}'; echo "[rc=$?] $_WS_WDID_STATE|$_WS_WDID_IDENT|$_WS_WDID_PHYS|$_WS_WDID_WHY"`;
const read = (logical: string = W(), id: string = ID): string => h.sh(READ(logical, id));
/** `snippet` with ccd sourced, in the harness's own environment (`h.env()`, built by ghContainedEnv) and HOME, in a
 *  process group of its own that is killed whole at `ms`: for a case whose failure is a hang. */
const timed = (snippet: string, ms: number) => spawnSyncGroup('bash',
  ['-c', 'ccd_t_src=$T4_CCD ccd_t_snippet=$T4_SNIPPET; unset T4_CCD T4_SNIPPET; source "$ccd_t_src"; eval "$ccd_t_snippet"'],
  { cwd: h.home, encoding: 'utf8', timeout: ms, env: { ...h.env(), T4_CCD: CCD, T4_SNIPPET: snippet } });

/** A workdir reached through a link: `link` -> `real` (returned resolved). */
const linked = (): { link: string; real: string } => {
  const real = path.join(h.home, 'wreal');
  const link = path.join(h.home, 'wlink');
  fs.mkdirSync(real);
  fs.symlinkSync(real, link);
  return { link, real: fs.realpathSync(real) };
};
/** The pane's command as the spawn builds it, run by `shell`:
 *  `cd '<logical>' && <fragment>true; cd '<logical>' && exec '<wrapper>'`. The fragment ends `&& `, and `true; `
 *  closes it, so the writer's exit gates neither the second `cd` nor the `exec`. The wrapper records the physical
 *  directory it started in. `pre` runs first, in the composing bash. */
const pane = (shell: string, logical: string, pre = ''): string => {
  const wrap = path.join(h.home, 'fakewrap');
  fs.writeFileSync(wrap, '#!/bin/sh\npwd -P > "$HOME/wrapper-ran"\n', { mode: 0o755 });
  return h.sh(`${pre} frag=$(_plat_workdirid_pane "$REG" ${ID} '${logical}'); `
    + `printf '%s' "cd '${logical}' && \${frag}true; cd '${logical}' && exec '${wrap}'" > "$HOME/pane-cmd"; `
    + `'${shell}' -c "$(cat "$HOME/pane-cmd")"; echo "[pane rc=$?]"`);
};
const ran = (): string | null => {
  const p = path.join(h.home, 'wrapper-ran');
  return fs.existsSync(p) ? fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8').replace(/\n$/, '') : null;
};
let shimN = 0;
/** Executables in a directory of their own, returned as the PATH assignment that puts them first. */
const shims = (files: Readonly<Record<string, string>>): string => {
  shimN += 1;
  const d = path.join(h.home, `shims-${shimN}`);
  fs.mkdirSync(d, { recursive: true });
  for (const [name, body] of Object.entries(files)) fs.writeFileSync(path.join(d, name), body, { mode: 0o755 });
  return `PATH='${d}':"$PATH";`;
};
const VALID_AT = (real: string): RegExp =>
  new RegExp(`^\\[rc=0\\] valid\\|[0-9]+:[0-9]+:(?:[1-9][0-9]*|-)\\|${esc(real)}\\|$`);

describe('the reader: one answer per rule, in its fixed order (path-identity spec §4.3)', () => {
  it('a valid line: valid, with its identity and its physical spelling', () => {
    writeField(h, ID, line('/phys/p'));
    expect(read()).toBe('[rc=0] valid|11:22:33|/phys/p|');
  });

  it('a valid line whose birth time is -: valid, the - kept', () => {
    writeField(h, ID, line('/phys/p', W(), '11:22:-'));
    expect(read()).toBe('[rc=0] valid|11:22:-|/phys/p|');
  });

  it('CONTROL: a valid line of exactly 8320 bytes is valid', () => {
    const body = padded(8320);
    expect(Buffer.byteLength(body)).toBe(8320);
    writeField(h, ID, body);
    expect(read()).toMatch(/^\[rc=0\] valid\|11:22:33\|\/a+\|$/);
  });

  it('no name and no link: legacy-absent', () => {
    expect(read()).toBe('[rc=1] legacy-absent|||');
  });

  it('a link at the name, to a valid line: legacy-link, and its target is never opened', () => {
    const target = path.join(h.home, 'a-valid-line');
    fs.writeFileSync(target, line('/phys/p'));
    const past = new Date(1_000_000_000_000);
    fs.utimesSync(target, past, new Date());   // atime before mtime: a read would move it under relatime
    fs.symlinkSync(target, field());
    expect(read()).toBe('[rc=1] legacy-link|||');
    expect(fs.statSync(target).atimeMs, 'the target was never read').toBe(past.getTime());
  });

  it('a directory at the name: unmeasured, never opened', () => {
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(field(), 'inside'), { recursive: true });
    const out = read();
    expect(out).toMatch(/^\[rc=2\] unmeasured\|\|\|the entry field /);
    expect(out).toContain('is not a regular file');
  });

  it('a FIFO at the name: unmeasured, and the reader returns instead of blocking on the open', () => {
    h.sh(`mkfifo "$REG/${ID}.workdirid"`);
    const r = timed(READ(W()), 10_000);
    expect(r.error, 'the reader returned inside the group timeout').toBeUndefined();
    expect(r.stdout.trim()).toMatch(/^\[rc=2\] unmeasured\|\|\|the entry field .* is not a regular file/);
  }, 30_000);

  it.skipIf(ROOT_USER)('a field this process cannot open (mode 000): unmeasured', () => {
    writeField(h, ID, line('/phys/p'));
    fs.chmodSync(field(), 0o000);
    const out = read();
    expect(out).toMatch(/^\[rc=2\] unmeasured\|\|\|the entry field /);
    expect(out).toContain('could not be opened');
  });

  it('a read that fails after the open: unmeasured, never legacy', () => {
    writeField(h, ID, line('/phys/p'));
    const out = h.sh(`${shims({ head: '#!/bin/sh\nexit 1\n' })} ${READ(W())}`);
    expect(out).toMatch(/^\[rc=2\] unmeasured\|\|\|the entry field /);
    expect(out).toContain('could not be read');
  });

  it.each([
    ['a version other than v1', (): string => line('/phys/p').replace(/^v1/, 'v2')],
    ['a missing field', (): string => `v1${T}11:22:33${T}${AT}${T}/phys/p`],
    ['a birth time of 0', (): string => line('/phys/p', W(), '11:22:0')],
    ['a 12-digit time', (): string => line('/phys/p').replace(AT, AT.slice(1))],
    ['a relative physical spelling', (): string => line('phys/p')],
    ['a physical spelling that is not plain', (): string => line('/a/./b')],
    ['a trailing newline', (): string => `${line('/phys/p')}\n`],
    ['an inner TAB', (): string => line(`/ph${T}ys`)],
    ['an inner CR', (): string => line('/ph\rys')],
    ['a pending line whose physical field is not -', (): string => `v1${T}pending${T}${AT}${T}/x${T}${W()}`],
    ['a body of 8321 bytes', (): string => padded(8321)],
    ['an empty body', (): string => ''],
    ['a NUL byte', (): string => line('/ph\0ys')],
  ] as const)('%s: legacy-unparseable', (_what, body) => {

describe('the composer: one line in the platform block, a brace-free fragment or nothing (path-identity spec §4.3)', () => {
  const COMPOSE = (args: string, os = 'linux'): string =>
    h.sh(`CCD_OS=${os}; o=$(_plat_workdirid_pane ${args}); echo "[$o] rc=$?"`);

  it('prints the /bin/sh fragment with its three arguments single-quoted, and no brace outside the script', () => {
    const out = COMPOSE(`"$REG" ${ID} "$HOME/w"`);
    const m = new RegExp(`^\\[/bin/sh -c '([^']+)' ccd-workdirid '${esc(regDir())}' '${ID}' '${esc(W())}' 2>/dev/null && \\] rc=0$`).exec(out);
    expect(m, out).not.toBeNull();
    const script = m![1]!;
    expect(out.replace(`'${script}'`, ''), 'no brace outside the quoted script').not.toMatch(/[{}]/);
    expect(script.startsWith('REG=$(printf %b "$1") id=$(printf %b "$2") l=$(printf %b "$3"); '), 'it decodes each argument once, first')
      .toBe(true);
    expect(script).toContain('p=$(pwd -P && echo .)');
    expect(script).toContain('s=$(stat -c %d:%i:%W . 2>/dev/null) || exit 0;');
    expect(script).toContain('t=$REG/.$id.workdirid.$$.tmp f=$REG/$id.workdirid;');
    expect(script.indexOf('>"$t"'), 'the line is written to the dot-leading temp').toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(script.indexOf('>"$t"'), 'and then renamed over the field').toBeLessThan(script.indexOf('mv -fT "$t" "$f"'));
    expect(script.endsWith('; exit 0'), 'every path ends 0').toBe(true);
  });

  it('the Darwin arm, chosen from CCD_OS when the fragment is composed: BSD stat, and a rename that refuses a directory', () => {
    const out = COMPOSE(`"$REG" ${ID} "$HOME/w"`, 'darwin');
    const script = /^\[\/bin\/sh -c '([^']+)'/.exec(out)?.[1] ?? '';
    expect(script).toContain('s=$(stat -f %d:%i:%B . 2>/dev/null) || exit 0;');
    expect(script).toContain('if [ -d "$f" ] && [ ! -L "$f" ]; then rm -f "$t"; exit 0; fi; [ -L "$f" ] && rm -f "$f"; mv -f "$t" "$f" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "$t"');
    expect(script).not.toMatch(/stat -c|mv -fT/);
  });

  it.each([
    ['a REG holding a single quote', `"$HOME/re'g" ${ID} "$HOME/w"`],
    ['an id holding a TAB', `"$REG" demo$'\\t'x "$HOME/w"`],
    ['a logical spelling holding a newline', `"$REG" ${ID} "$HOME/w"$'\\n'x`],
    ['an id holding a slash', `"$REG" demo/x "$HOME/w"`],
    ['an empty REG', `'' ${ID} "$HOME/w"`],
    ['an empty id', `"$REG" '' "$HOME/w"`],
    ['an empty logical spelling', `"$REG" ${ID} ''`],
  ] as const)('prints nothing for %s, and answers 0', (_what, args) => {
    expect(COMPOSE(args)).toBe('[] rc=0');
  });

  it('is defined once, and calls no function: a call out of K would count', () => {
    expect(ccdFunctionDefinitions().filter((s) => s.text.startsWith('_plat_workdirid_pane()')).map((s) => s.file))
      .toEqual(['ccd/ccd']);
    expect(ccdCallGraph().filter((e) => e.caller === '_plat_workdirid_pane').map((e) => e.callee), 'it names no ccd function')
      .toEqual([]);
  });

  it('it is ONE line, in place of the blank line after _plat_epoch_ms, in ccd and in ccrc alike', () => {
    for (const [name, file] of [['ccd/ccd', CCD], ['ccd/ccrc', CCRC]] as const) {
      const lines = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8').split('\n');
      const at = lines.flatMap((l, i) => (l.startsWith('_plat_workdirid_pane') ? [i] : []));
      expect(at, `${name}: one line defines it`).toHaveLength(1);
      const i = at[0]!;
      expect(lines[i], `${name}: the whole definition is that line`)
        .toMatch(/^_plat_workdirid_pane\(\) \{ .*; return 0; \}   # reg id logical -> /);
      expect(lines[i - 1], `${name}: the line above is a closing }`).toBe('}');
      expect(ownerIn(lines)(i - 1), `${name}: and that } closes _plat_epoch_ms`).toBe('_plat_epoch_ms');
      expect(lines[i + 1], `${name}: the line below is the comment the blank line stood above`)
        .toMatch(/^# `cp --remove-destination` IS GNU\./);
    }
  });

  it('the grammar is spelled once, as the regex of the reader', () => {
    const lines = fs.readFileSync(CCD, 'utf8').split('\n');
    const at = lines.flatMap((l, i) => (bashCodeOf(l).includes('|pending)') ? [i] : []));
    expect(at, 'one code line spells the grammar').toHaveLength(1);
    expect(lines[at[0]!]!.trim()).toBe(GRAMMAR);
    expect(ownerIn(lines)(at[0]!)).toBe('_ws_workdirid_read');
    expect(fs.readFileSync(CCRC, 'utf8'), 'ccrc spells no grammar of its own').not.toContain('|pending)');
  });

  it('the spelling .workdirid stands in the code of these functions only', () => {
    const lines = fs.readFileSync(CCD, 'utf8').split('\n');
    const owner = ownerIn(lines);
    const owners = new Set(lines.flatMap((l, i) => (bashCodeOf(l).includes('.workdirid') ? [owner(i)] : [])));
    expect([...owners].sort()).toEqual([...WORKDIRID_SPELLERS].sort());
  });
});

/** Each shell a pane may have: its name, its binary ('' when absent), and whether the suite needs it. */
const SHELLS: ReadonlyArray<readonly [string, string, boolean]> = [
  ['sh', '/bin/sh', true], ['bash', onPath('bash'), true],
  ['dash', onPath('dash'), false], ['zsh', onPath('zsh'), false], ['fish', onPath('fish'), false],
];

describe('the pane writes the field after its cd and before its exec, under each shell a pane may have', () => {
  for (const [name, bin, needed] of SHELLS) {
    it.skipIf(!needed && bin === '')(`under ${name}: a valid field naming the directory cd reached, and the wrapper ran`, () => {
      expect(bin, `${name} is on the suite's PATH`).not.toBe('');
      const { link, real } = linked();
      expect(pane(bin, link)).toBe('[pane rc=0]');
      expect(ran(), 'the wrapper ran, in the target').toBe(real);
      const [ans, ident] = h.sh(`${READ(link)}; _ws_path_ident '${real}'; echo "ident=$_WS_IDENT"`).split('\n');
      expect(ans).toMatch(VALID_AT(real));
      expect(ans!.split('|')[1], 'its identity is the target’s, measured as ccd measures it').toBe(ident!.replace(/^ident=/, ''));
      expect(tmps(), 'no temp is left').toEqual([]);
    });
  }
});

describe('every spelling .workdir accepts round-trips: a backslash rides as an escape the script decodes (path-identity spec §4.3)', () => {
  /** `logical`, a link spelled with `leaf` under HOME, to a directory made for it (returned resolved). */
  const backslashed = (leaf: string): { logical: string; real: string } => {
    const real = path.join(h.home, 'wreal');
    fs.mkdirSync(real);
    const logical = path.join(h.home, leaf);
    fs.symlinkSync(real, logical);
    return { logical, real: fs.realpathSync(real) };
  };
  /** The fragment for `logical`, composed with the registry word `reg`, run by `shell` from inside `logical`. Bash
   *  enters the directory, so the fragment is under test here, not the spawn's own `cd` quoting: `[rc=<n>]`. */
  const fromInside = (shell: string, logical: string, reg = '"$REG"'): string =>
    h.sh(`cd '${logical}' && frag=$(_plat_workdirid_pane ${reg} ${ID} '${logical}') && '${shell}' -c "\${frag}true"; echo "[rc=$?]"`);
  const SPELLINGS: ReadonlyArray<readonly [string, string]> = [
    ['a backslash inside it', 'w\\x'], ['two backslashes', 'w\\\\y'], ['a trailing backslash', 'w\\'],
  ];
  for (const [what, leaf] of SPELLINGS) {
    for (const [name, bin, needed] of SHELLS) {
      it.skipIf(!needed && bin === '')(`${what}, under ${name}: carried as \\0134, and the field is valid with .workdir byte for byte`, () => {
        expect(bin, `${name} is on the suite's PATH`).not.toBe('');
        const { logical, real } = backslashed(leaf);
        expect(h.sh(`printf '%s' "$(_plat_workdirid_pane "$REG" ${ID} '${logical}')"`), 'each backslash rides as \\0134')
          .toContain(` '${logical.split('\\').join('\\0134')}' 2>/dev/null &&`);
        expect(fromInside(bin, logical)).toBe('[rc=0]');
        expect(read(logical)).toMatch(VALID_AT(real));
        expect(fs.readFileSync(field(), 'utf8').split(T)[4], 'the logical spelling is .workdir, byte for byte').toBe(logical);
        expect(tmps(), 'no temp is left').toEqual([]);
      });
    }
  }

  it('a REG spelled with a backslash: the field lands in the registry that spelling names', () => {
    const { link, real } = linked();
    const alias = path.join(h.home, 're\\g');
    fs.symlinkSync(regDir(), alias);
    expect(fromInside('/bin/sh', link, `'${alias}'`)).toBe('[rc=0]');
    expect(read(link)).toMatch(VALID_AT(real));
    expect(tmps()).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('where the pane writes, and what it writes when it cannot measure', () => {
  it('CONTROL: the host stat, mv and date the shims stand in front of are on PATH', () => {

  });

    expect(fs.existsSync(field())).toBe(false);
    expect(ran()).toBe(fs.realpathSync(real));
  });

  it('a date without %N: the time is whole seconds and 000, and the field is valid', () => {
    const { link, real } = linked();
    const pre = shims({ date: `#!/bin/sh\ncase "$1" in +%s%3N) printf '%s3N\\n' "$('${REAL.date}' +%s)" ;; *) exec '${REAL.date}' "$@" ;; esac\n` });
    expect(pane('/bin/sh', link, pre)).toBe('[pane rc=0]');
    const [ans, at] = h.sh(`${READ(link)}; echo "at=$_WS_WDID_AT"`).split('\n');
    expect(ans).toMatch(VALID_AT(real));
    expect(at).toMatch(/^at=[0-9]{10}000$/);
  });

  it('a directory at the field name stays, no temp is left, and the wrapper still ran', () => {
    const { link, real } = linked();
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(field(), 'inside'), { recursive: true });
    expect(pane('/bin/sh', link)).toBe('[pane rc=0]');
    expect(fs.lstatSync(field()).isDirectory()).toBe(true);
    expect(fs.readdirSync(field())).toEqual(['inside']);
    expect(tmps()).toEqual([]);
    expect(ran()).toBe(real);
  });

  it('a link at the field name is replaced by the field, and the file it named is untouched', () => {
    const { link, real } = linked();
    const theirs = path.join(h.home, 'theirs');
    fs.writeFileSync(theirs, 'their bytes');
    fs.symlinkSync(theirs, field());
    expect(pane('/bin/sh', link)).toBe('[pane rc=0]');
    expect(fs.lstatSync(field()).isSymbolicLink(), 'the link was replaced').toBe(false);
    expect(read(link)).toMatch(VALID_AT(real));
    expect(fs.readFileSync(theirs, 'utf8'), 'the file the link named is untouched').toBe('their bytes');
  });

  it('a stat that prints - for the birth time: a valid field whose birth time is -', () => {
    const { link, real } = linked();
    const pre = shims({ stat: `#!/bin/sh\nprintf '%s:-\\n' "$('${REAL.stat}' ${DEVINO} "$3")"\n` });
    expect(pane('/bin/sh', link, pre)).toBe('[pane rc=0]');
    expect(read(link)).toMatch(new RegExp(`^\\[rc=0\\] valid\\|[0-9]+:[0-9]+:-\\|${esc(real)}\\|$`));
  });

  it('forced Darwin: BSD stat and the Darwin rename write a valid field over a link at the name', () => {
    const { link, real } = linked();
    const theirs = path.join(h.home, 'theirs');
    fs.writeFileSync(theirs, 'their bytes');
    fs.symlinkSync(theirs, field());
    const bsd = process.platform === 'darwin' ? '' : shims({
      stat: `#!/bin/sh\nif [ "$1" = -f ]; then exec '${REAL.stat}' -c "$(printf %s "$2" | sed 's/%B/%W/')" "$3"; fi\nexec '${REAL.stat}' "$@"\n`,
    });
    expect(pane('/bin/sh', link, `CCD_OS=darwin; ${bsd}`)).toBe('[pane rc=0]');
    expect(fs.lstatSync(field()).isSymbolicLink(), 'the link was replaced').toBe(false);
    expect(read(link)).toMatch(VALID_AT(real));
    expect(fs.readFileSync(theirs, 'utf8'), 'the file the link named is untouched').toBe('their bytes');
    expect(ran()).toBe(real);
  });

  it('BSD argument order (POSIXLY_CORRECT stat and mv): a valid field', () => {
    const { link, real } = linked();
    const pre = shims({
      stat: `#!/bin/sh\nPOSIXLY_CORRECT=1; export POSIXLY_CORRECT\nexec '${REAL.stat}' "$@"\n`,
      mv: `#!/bin/sh\nPOSIXLY_CORRECT=1; export POSIXLY_CORRECT\nexec '${REAL.mv}' "$@"\n`,
    });
    expect(pane('/bin/sh', link, pre)).toBe('[pane rc=0]');
    expect(read(link)).toMatch(VALID_AT(real));
  });
});
```

```bash
while (depth > 0 || !/[;}]\s*$/.test(L[e])) { e += 1; if (e >= L.length) fail('the definition never closes'); depth += net(L[e]); }

  if (k < 0) fail('a doc comment with no opening'); s = k;

  '/** Writes `$REG/<id>.workdirid` exactly as given: no newline is added, so a test states every byte of the field',

  '}');

if (lastImport === undefined) {
  const first = L.findIndex((l) => !/^\s*(\/\/|\/\*|\*|$)/.test(l));
  L.splice(first < 0 ? 0 : first, 0, ...imports, '');
} else {

}
```

```bash
# THE ENTRY FIELD'S ONE READER (path-identity spec §4.3 and §4.4). `$REG/<id>.workdirid` holds one line with no
# trailing newline, in ONE grammar, whose single definition is the regex below:
#   valid:   v1 TAB <dev>:<ino>:<btime or -> TAB <at_ms> TAB <physical> TAB <logical>
#   pending: v1 TAB pending TAB <at_ms> TAB - TAB <logical>
# Every valid line comes from ONE composer, `_plat_workdirid_pane` (the platform block): the pane runs its fragment
# after its `cd` and before its `exec`, and `start` and `ws-add` run it once to seed the row. <logical> is
# byte-equal to the `.workdir` the writer was given, and <physical> is `pwd -P` of the directory `cd` reached. A
# pending line is the parent's, written before a pane exists, so a pane that cannot replace it leaves a hold and
# never the entry of an earlier process.
# SEVEN ANSWERS, never folded, each named in _WS_WDID_STATE:
#   0 valid: _WS_WDID_IDENT ("<dev>:<ino>:<btime|->"), _WS_WDID_AT and _WS_WDID_PHYS are set;
#   1 legacy-absent (no name and no link), legacy-link (a link, whose target is never read), legacy-unparseable
#     (over 8320 bytes; outside the grammar; a control character beside the four TABs; a valid line whose
#     physical spelling is not plain; a pending line whose physical field is not `-`) and legacy-stale (its
#     logical spelling is not LOGICAL, the row's current `.workdir`): a caller places that row as it always has,
#     by string and by current identity (path-identity spec §4.4);
#   2 pending (its logical spelling is LOGICAL), and unmeasured (_WS_WDID_WHY: the field is not a regular file,
#     or it could not be opened or read): a caller holds (`workdirid-unreadable-holds`).
# THE ORDER IS FIXED. The type comes before the open, as `_reg_read_to` orders its own, so a directory or a
# FIFO is never opened and a link is never followed; stale is decided before pending, so a pending line from
# another spelling reads legacy. The read is one bounded `head -c` under LC_ALL=C, `_ws_leaf_read_small`'s form:
# a sentinel keeps a trailing newline, and each NUL is read as a newline, which the grammar refuses. BASH_REMATCH
# is copied before anything else is tested. A read that fails after the open reads unmeasured, never legacy:
# bash's `read` answers 1 at the end of the file and on an error alike, so it is not used, and the pipeline's
# status under ccd's `pipefail` is what tells an error from the end. The grammar's two path groups exclude
# every control character, the TAB included, so no second test of the body is needed. The window from
# the type check to the open is `_reg_read_to`'s own: a FIFO swapped in there blocks the open
# (`workdirid-fifo-swap-after-type-check`).
# IT LIVES IN C4, BESIDE THE ROWS RUNG (`_ws_reclaim_workdir_shared`), and mirrors `_reg_read_to`'s refusals
# rather than calling into the registry's context, so the cross-context count does not move.
_WS_WDID_STATE=''; _WS_WDID_WHY=''; _WS_WDID_IDENT=''; _WS_WDID_AT=''; _WS_WDID_PHYS=''
_ws_workdirid_read() {   # id logical -> 0 `valid` (_WS_WDID_IDENT "<dev>:<ino>:<btime|->", _WS_WDID_AT, _WS_WDID_PHYS);
  #                         1 `legacy-absent` | `legacy-link` | `legacy-unparseable` | `legacy-stale`; 2 `pending`, or
  #                         `unmeasured` (_WS_WDID_WHY: not a regular file, or could not be read). _WS_WDID_STATE always
  #                         names the answer. Clears every global first. Prints nothing, never dies, calls nothing in C1
  local LC_ALL=C id="${1-}" logical="${2-}" f body='' fd rc=0
  local -a m=()
  local re=$'^v1\t(([0-9]+):([0-9]+):([1-9][0-9]*|-)|pending)\t([0-9]{13})\t([^[:cntrl:]]+)\t(/[^[:cntrl:]]*)$'
  _WS_WDID_STATE=''; _WS_WDID_WHY=''; _WS_WDID_IDENT=''; _WS_WDID_AT=''; _WS_WDID_PHYS=''
  f="$REG/$id.workdirid"
  [[ -e "$f" || -L "$f" ]] || { _WS_WDID_STATE=legacy-absent; return 1; }
  [[ ! -L "$f" ]] || { _WS_WDID_STATE=legacy-link; return 1; }
  [[ -f "$f" ]] || { _WS_WDID_STATE=unmeasured; _WS_WDID_WHY="the entry field $f is not a regular file, so where that session entered was never read"; return 2; }
  { exec {fd}<"$f"; } 2>/dev/null || { _WS_WDID_STATE=unmeasured; _WS_WDID_WHY="the entry field $f could not be opened, so where that session entered was never read"; return 2; }
  { body=$( { LC_ALL=C head -c 8321 | LC_ALL=C tr '\000' '\n'; } <&"$fd" && printf x); } 2>/dev/null || rc=$?
  { exec {fd}<&-; } 2>/dev/null || :
  [[ "$rc" == 0 ]] || { _WS_WDID_STATE=unmeasured; _WS_WDID_WHY="the entry field $f could not be read, so where that session entered was never read"; return 2; }
  body="${body%x}"
  if (( ${#body} > 8320 )) || ! [[ "$body" =~ $re ]]; then
    _WS_WDID_STATE=legacy-unparseable; return 1
  fi
  m=("${BASH_REMATCH[@]}")
  if [[ "${m[1]}" == pending ]]; then
    [[ "${m[6]}" == - ]] || { _WS_WDID_STATE=legacy-unparseable; return 1; }
  else
    _ws_reclaim_plain_path "${m[6]}" || { _WS_WDID_STATE=legacy-unparseable; return 1; }
  fi
  [[ "${m[7]}" == "$logical" ]] || { _WS_WDID_STATE=legacy-stale; return 1; }
  [[ "${m[1]}" != pending ]] || { _WS_WDID_STATE=pending; return 2; }
  _WS_WDID_IDENT="${m[2]}:${m[3]}:${m[4]}"; _WS_WDID_AT="${m[5]}"; _WS_WDID_PHYS="${m[6]}"
  _WS_WDID_STATE=valid; return 0
}
EOF
```

```bash
L=.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-20-path-identity-w3-worktree-identity; cat > "$L/t4/startseed.block" <<'EOF'
  # THE ENTRY FIELD'S SEED (path-identity spec §4.3; PI1 B). `$REG/<id>.workdirid` records where this session's
  # pane entered: the device, inode and birth time of the directory `cd` reached, the time, its physical spelling,
  # and the logical `.workdir` spelling it was given (`_ws_workdirid_read` is its one reader). Every valid line
  # comes from ONE composer, `_plat_workdirid_pane`, which prints a brace-free `/bin/sh -c` fragment that measures
  # `pwd -P` and the stat of the directory it stands in, refuses a control character, writes temp-then-rename into
  # $REG, and exits 0 on every path; a `\` in its arguments rides as `\0134`, which the script decodes, so every
  # spelling `.workdir` accepts records a valid line.
  # Here it runs once, in a subshell that entered the workdir as the pane does
  # (`CDPATH=` and `builtin cd`, the logical spelling), so the row carries a valid value from its first start; a
  # seed that cannot write leaves what stood, and never stops the start. It sits after the live-pane return above,
  # so a start that spawns nothing never rewrites a live pane's record.
  # THE COMPOSER IS ONE LINE, in place of the platform block's blank line after `_plat_epoch_ms`, because the
  # block lies wholly above the highest line the frozen compaction-card corpus cites, and a line added there
  # would move every cite below it; its call sites carry its contract. `ws-add`'s seed is the same statement,
  # appended to its `.workdir` line for the same reason.

EOF
```

```bash
L=.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-20-path-identity-w3-worktree-identity; cat > "$L/t4/apply.mjs" <<'EOF'
// path-identity W3, Task 4: five in-place edits, refused whole unless every anchor stands exactly once.
import fs from 'node:fs';
const dir = process.argv[2];
const text = (n) => fs.readFileSync(`${dir}/${n}`, 'utf8').replace(/\n$/, '');
const composer = text('composer.line'); const reader = text('reader.block');
const seed = text('startseed.block'); const tail = text('wsadd.tail');
const fail = (m) => { console.error(`apply: ${m}`); process.exit(3); };
const count = (s, n) => s.split(n).length - 1;
const EPOCH = '_plat_epoch_ms() {   # -> epoch milliseconds, 13 digits';
const NEXT = '# `cp --remove-destination` IS GNU.';
const slot = (src, name) => {
  const L = src.split('\n');
  const at = L.flatMap((l, i) => (l === EPOCH ? [i] : []));
  if (at.length !== 1) fail(`${name}: _plat_epoch_ms is defined on ${at.length} lines`);
  let e = at[0] + 1; while (e < L.length && L[e] !== '}') e += 1;
  if (L[e] !== '}' || L[e + 1] !== '' || !(L[e + 2] ?? '').startsWith(NEXT)) fail(`${name}: the line after _plat_epoch_ms is not the blank slot`);
  if (L.some((l) => l.startsWith('_plat_workdirid_pane'))) fail(`${name}: _plat_workdirid_pane is already defined`);
  L[e + 1] = composer;
  console.log(`apply: ${name}: the composer is line ${e + 2}`);
  return L.join('\n');
};
const G = "\n_WS_SHARED_ROWS=''; _WS_NESTED_ROWS='';";
const S = '\n  _reg_set "$id" workdir "$workdir"; _reg_set "$id" uuid "$uuid"\n';
const A = '\n  _reg_set "$id" workdir "$wt";   _reg_set "$id" uuid "$uuid"\n';
let ccd = fs.readFileSync('ccd/ccd', 'utf8'); let ccrc = fs.readFileSync('ccd/ccrc', 'utf8');
for (const [n, what] of [[G, 'the rows rung globals line'], [S, "cmd_start's .workdir write"], [A, "cmd_ws_add's .workdir write"]]) {
  if (count(ccd, n) !== 1) fail(`${what} stands ${count(ccd, n)} times in ccd/ccd`);
}
if (/^_ws_workdirid_read\(\)/m.test(ccd)) fail('_ws_workdirid_read is already defined');
if (!composer.startsWith('_plat_workdirid_pane() { ') || composer.includes('\n')) fail('composer.line is not the one-line definition');
if (tail.includes('\n') || !tail.startsWith('; ( CDPATH=')) fail('wsadd.tail is not the one-line tail');
const ccdBefore = ccd.split('\n').length; const ccrcBefore = ccrc.split('\n').length;
ccd = slot(ccd, 'ccd/ccd'); ccrc = slot(ccrc, 'ccd/ccrc');
ccd = ccd.replace(G, () => `\n${reader}\n${G}`);
ccd = ccd.replace(S, () => `${S}${seed}\n`);
ccd = ccd.replace(A, () => `${A.slice(0, -1)}${tail}\n`);
const grew = ccd.split('\n').length - ccdBefore;
const want = reader.split('\n').length + 1 + seed.split('\n').length;
if (grew !== want) fail(`ccd/ccd would grow by ${grew} lines, not ${want}`);
if (ccrc.split('\n').length !== ccrcBefore) fail('ccd/ccrc would change its line count');
fs.writeFileSync('ccd/ccd', ccd); fs.writeFileSync('ccd/ccrc', ccrc);
console.log(`apply: ccd/ccd +${grew} lines (the reader and the start seed, both below the corpus bound); ccd/ccrc +0`);
EOF
node "$L/t4/apply.mjs" "$L/t4"
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Mutation table**

First, one Bash call. It copies the restamped file into the scratch directory and writes the one-mutation helper, W2's `mut.mjs` verbatim:

```bash
S=.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-20-path-identity-w3-worktree-identity/t4-mut; mkdir -p "$S" && cp ccd/ccd "$S/ccd.task4" && cat > "$S/mut.mjs" <<'EOF'
// One exact mutation of one file, refused unless every anchor matches exactly once.
//   node mut.mjs FILE sub OLD NEW          replace the ONE occurrence of OLD with NEW
//   node mut.mjs FILE del NEEDLE...        delete each ONE line holding NEEDLE
//   node mut.mjs FILE range START END NEW  replace the ONE line holding START, through the first line from there that
//                                          holds END, with the single line NEW
import fs from 'node:fs';
const [file, mode, ...a] = process.argv.slice(2);
const src = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
const lines = src.split('\n');
const fail = (m) => { console.error(`mut: ${m}`); process.exit(3); };
const one = (needle) => {
  const at = lines.flatMap((l, i) => (l.includes(needle) ? [i] : []));
  if (at.length !== 1) fail(`${JSON.stringify(needle)} is on ${at.length} lines, not one`);
  return at[0];
};
let out;
if (mode === 'sub') {
  const [o, n] = a;
  const k = src.split(o).length - 1;
  if (k !== 1) fail(`${JSON.stringify(o)} occurs ${k} times, not once`);
  out = src.replace(o, () => n);
} else if (mode === 'del') {
  const drop = new Set(a.map(one));
  out = lines.filter((_, i) => !drop.has(i)).join('\n');
} else if (mode === 'range') {
  const [start, end, n] = a;
  const s = one(start);
  const e = lines.findIndex((l, i) => i >= s && l.includes(end));
  if (e < 0) fail(`no ${JSON.stringify(end)} at or after line ${s + 1}`);
  out = [...lines.slice(0, s), n, ...lines.slice(e + 1)].join('\n');
} else fail(`unknown mode ${mode}`);
fs.writeFileSync(file, out);
console.log(`mut: ${mode} applied to ${file}`);
EOF
```

Then each row is ONE Bash call, run from the workspace root in the foreground with a timeout of at least 600000 ms. The call:
- applies the mutation in place;
- runs the named cases;
- restores the file from the scratch copy whatever vitest answered;
- proves the restore with `cmp`.

No mutation is restamped: no suite these rows run reads the stamp. Every red below was drafted, not measured, so record the measured text. A case listed as red that stays green is a STOP, reported by its row number. A `mut:` refusal (exit 3) mutated nothing, and is a STOP too.

**Drafter's corrections:**
1. **The grammar's regex is spelled with ANSI-C `$'…\t…'`, not literal TABs.** Its value is byte-identical to §Interfaces' regex. The export's `ccd/ccd` holds no literal TAB (`grep -c $'\t' ccd/ccd` reads 0), and a first literal TAB would be invisible in review. The source pin (`GRAMMAR`) pins this spelling, and Step 4d checks that no TAB entered either file.
2. **Rule 6 also refuses a control character beside the four TABs.** The frame's regex admits CR and LF in `[^	]`. Measured against strings, with the frame's TAB-excluding groups a body ending in a newline reads `legacy-stale`, not `legacy-unparseable`, and a CR inside the physical path reads `valid`. The grammar says no control character but the TABs, and R57 rules the regex's own form: its two path groups are `[^[:cntrl:]]`, which under LC_ALL=C excludes the TAB too. The regex alone then refuses every control character beside the four separators, and the reader runs no second test. §Interfaces' regex reads the same. Rows: the trailing-newline, inner-CR and NUL cases, and F15.
3. **Rule 4's "failed read" is a failed open or a failed read (R57).** Bash's `read` answers 1 at end of file and on an error alike, so the reader does not use it. It reads through `head -c 8321`, piped through `tr '\000' '\n'` and ended by a sentinel (`_ws_leaf_read_small`'s form), and the pipeline's status under ccd's `pipefail` tells an error from the end of the file. A failed open (mode 000) and a failed read (a `head` shim that exits 1) both read unmeasured, never legacy. A NUL becomes a newline, which the grammar refuses, where a command substitution would drop it. Rows: the mode-000, read-error and NUL cases, and F25. The header says so.
4. **The one-line pin is structural, not a merge-base read.** Once the PR merges, `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` is HEAD itself, so a vitest case that compared the base would red on `main` forever. The case pins the neighbours instead: the line above is the `}` that closes `_plat_epoch_ms`, and the line below is the `cp` comment, in both files. The base comparison is Step 8b's hunk check, and F13 reds both.
5. **The FIFO row runs under a 10 s group timeout, with a 30 s case timeout, not 5 s.** The box's `testTimeout` is 20 s, and W2's Task 2 used group timeouts for the same reason: load.
6. **The composer's exact text.**

   - The function ends `return 0`, so a failing `printf` still answers 0.
   - The 13-digit test is a 13-class pattern.

11. **A backslash is carried, never refused (R54, the coordinator's addendum).** `.workdir` accepts a backslash: `cmd_start` refuses only a control character, a `'` and `/proc`. So the composer refuses only an empty argument, a control character or a `'` (both of which `.workdir` refuses, in `cmd_start` and `cmd_ws_add`), and an id holding a `/` (R60). It spells each `\` of reg, id and logical as `\0134` inside its single-quoted argument. No shell a pane may have reads that specially: fish's single quotes treat only `\\` and `\'` as escapes, and every `\` the composer puts in an argument is followed by `0`. The script decodes each argument once with `printf %b` before any use, so the field's logical spelling is byte-equal to `.workdir`, and the one grammar and its reader are unchanged. - [ ] **Step 1: Add `PANE_EXEC` and `paneFragment` to the shared fixture (P18)**

Append this to `server/test/worktreeIdentityFixture.ts`. It needs no import: both names take what they need as arguments.

```bash
cat >> server/test/worktreeIdentityFixture.ts <<'EOF'

/** path-identity W3, Task 5 (P18): a bash `tmux()` stub that EXECUTES the pane, for a snippet that runs the real
 *  `_spawn_start`. No tmux server is started or attached. Every call is recorded to `$HOME/ccd-calls` as the existing
 *  stubs record it (`tmux $*`), and the width query answers from `$HOME/pane-up` (`WIDE_PANE_IF_UP`'s shape). On
 *  `new-session` it counts the pane in `PANE_N`; then, in a subshell started in `$HOME`, it evals `$PANE_PRE` when that
 *  is set and execs `<shell> -c "<last argument>"`, the pane's output going to `$HOME/pane-out`; then it evals
 *  `$PANE_POST` when that is set, in a subshell too. Both hooks run in subshells, so a PATH a hook exports reaches the
 *  pane alone and never `_spawn_start`. The pane stands up (`$HOME/pane-up`, which `has-session` reads) when its argv
 *  matches the glob `PANE_UP`, every pane by default: `PANE_UP='*--session-id*'` is `RESUME_DIES`' substrate, where the
 *  `--resume` pane runs and dies and the `--session-id` retry stands. `sleep` is a no-op, so a resume's settle is free. */
export const PANE_EXEC = (shell: string): string => `sleep() { :; };
  tmux() {
    echo "tmux $*" >> "$HOME/ccd-calls"
    case "$*" in *pane_active*) [[ -e "$HOME/pane-up" ]] || return 1; echo "1 200"; return 0 ;; esac
    case "$1" in
      new-session)
        PANE_N=$(( \${PANE_N:-0} + 1 ))
        ( cd "$HOME" || exit 1; if [[ -n "\${PANE_PRE:-}" ]]; then eval "$PANE_PRE"; fi; exec ${shell} -c "\${@: -1}" ) >> "$HOME/pane-out" 2>&1 < /dev/null
        if [[ -n "\${PANE_POST:-}" ]]; then ( eval "$PANE_POST" ); fi
        case "$*" in \${PANE_UP:-*}) : > "$HOME/pane-up" ;; esac
        ;;
      kill-session) rm -f "$HOME/pane-up" ;;
      has-session) [[ -e "$HOME/pane-up" ]] ;;
      list-sessions) return 0 ;;
    esac
  };`;

/** path-identity W3, Task 5 (R8): the pane's entry-identity writer exactly as `_spawn_start` splices it between a
 *  command string's first `cd '<workdir>' && ` and its `true; cd '<workdir>' && exec env` (R60), read from ccd's
 *  own `_plat_workdirid_pane` (one definition, read twice) and never typed. It ends in a space, which the harness's trim would cut, so it is read
 *  bracketed. `os` composes it as a snippet that sets `CCD_OS=<os>` does (a forced arm); without it, the host's arm.
 *  It is '' when the composer will not quote the input, as the spawn then splices nothing. */
export const paneFragment = (h: { sh(snippet: string): string }, id: string, workdir: string,
  os?: 'linux' | 'darwin'): string =>
  h.sh(`${os === undefined ? '' : `CCD_OS=${os}; `}printf '[%s]' "$(_plat_workdirid_pane "$REG" '${id}' '${workdir}')"`)
    .slice(1, -1);
EOF
grep -c '^export const PANE_EXEC\|^export const paneFragment' server/test/worktreeIdentityFixture.ts   # 2
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the failing test `server/test/ccd-workdirid-spawn.test.ts`**

Create the file with exactly this content:

```ts
// server/test/ccd-workdirid-spawn.test.ts
//
// path-identity W3, Task 5 (path-identity spec §4.3; R2, R7, R8): every spawn records where its pane entered. Before each
// `_tmux_new_session` in `_spawn_start`, the primary launch and its `--session-id` retry, the parent marks
// `$REG/<id>.workdirid` `pending` (`_spawn_workdirid_pending`), and the pane replaces that mark after its `cd` and before
// its `exec`, through the fragment `_plat_workdirid_pane` composes. A pane that cannot record where it entered leaves
// `pending`, a hold, and never the field an earlier pane of the row wrote. A pending write that fails unlinks the field,
// so the row reads `legacy-absent`, today's rule, and never a stale valid field.
//
// FIXTURE HOME ONLY (`makeCcdHarness`). No tmux server is started or attached: `PANE_EXEC` is a bash `tmux()` stub that
// EXECUTES the pane command under the named shell inside the snippet, and the wrapper the pane execs is a fake that
// records `pwd -P`. A failure inside the pane is planted on the pane's PATH (a `stat` that exits 1, or a `mv` that kills the writer), because the pane's
// `/bin/sh` sees PATH, never a shell function. No case reaches a process-table walk: `PROC_SPY` records any, and every
// spawn asserts there was none, so this file joins no load-flake list. The spawn and parity cases run on Linux; the
// writer's rows, the fragment's CONTROLs and the source pins run on both platforms.
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { CCD, makeCcdHarness, type CcdHarness } from './ccdWsHelpers.js';
import { CCD_FUNCTION_DEF, ccdCallGraph, ccdFunctionDefinitions } from './consolidationCensus.js';
import { DEFAULT_TEST_ROSTER } from './helpers/roster.js';
import { PANE_EXEC, paneFragment } from './worktreeIdentityFixture.js';

const LINUX = process.platform === 'linux';
const SRC = fs.readFileSync(CCD, 'utf8');
const UUID = 'deadbeef-0000-4000-8000-000000000000';
const ID = 'demo-quiet-mesa';
const esc = (s: string): string => s.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');

let h: CcdHarness;
beforeEach(() => { h = makeCcdHarness('ccrc-workdirid-spawn-'); });
afterEach(() => { h.cleanup(); });

const at = (...p: string[]): string => path.join(h.home, ...p);
const reg = (name: string): string => at('.cc-sessions', name);
const real = (p: string): string => fs.realpathSync(p);
const linesOf = (name: string): string[] =>
  (fs.existsSync(at(name)) ? fs.readFileSync(at(name), 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean) : []);
/** The grammar's pending form for `logical`, the line alone, with no trailing newline. */
const PENDING = (logical: string): RegExp => new RegExp(`^v1\\tpending\\t\\d{13}\\t-\\t${esc(logical)}$`);

/** The row `_spawn_start` reads: its wrapper, its `.workdir` (the logical spelling, byte for byte) and its uuid. */
const seed = (id: string, workdir: string, wrapper = 'claude'): void => {
  h.sh(`_reg_set ${id} wrapper ${wrapper}; _reg_set ${id} workdir '${workdir}'; _reg_set ${id} uuid ${UUID}`);
};
/** The wrapper the pane execs: it appends the directory it runs in (`pwd -P`) to `$HOME/wrapper-ran`, and exits. */
const fakeWrapper = (wrapper = 'claude'): void => {
  fs.writeFileSync(at('.local', 'bin', wrapper), `#!/bin/sh\npwd -P >> '${at('wrapper-ran')}'\n`, { mode: 0o755 });
};
/** A `stat` that records its call and fails, and the `PANE_PRE` text that puts it first on the pane's PATH only. */
const failingStat = (): string => {
  fs.mkdirSync(at('failbin'), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(at('failbin', 'stat'), `#!/bin/sh\necho called >> '${at('stat-shim-ran')}'\nexit 1\n`, { mode: 0o755 });
  return 'PATH="$HOME/failbin:$PATH"; export PATH';
};
/** A `mv` that records its call and kills the shell that ran it, the pane's writer (`kill -9 "$PPID"`), and the
 *  `PANE_PRE` text that puts it first on the pane's PATH only: the writer dies by a signal before its rename (R56). */
const killingMv = (): string => {
  fs.mkdirSync(at('killbin'), { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(at('killbin', 'mv'), `#!/bin/sh\necho called >> '${at('mv-shim-ran')}'\nkill -9 "$PPID"\nexit 1\n`, { mode: 0o755 });
  return 'PATH="$HOME/killbin:$PATH"; export PATH';
};
/** The one reader's answer (Task 4): `[rc=<n>] <state>|<identity>|<physical>|<why>`. */
const field = (id: string, logical: string): string =>
  h.sh(`_ws_workdirid_read ${id} '${logical}'; echo "[rc=$?] $_WS_WDID_STATE|$_WS_WDID_IDENT|$_WS_WDID_PHYS|$_WS_WDID_WHY"`);
/** `_ws_path_ident`'s identity of a standing directory (Task 2): `<dev>:<ino>:<btime|->`. */
const ident = (p: string): string => {
  const out = h.sh(`_ws_path_ident '${p}'; echo "[rc=$?] $_WS_IDENT"`);
  expect(out, `the CONTROL: ${p} was measured`).toMatch(/^\[rc=0\] \d+:\d+:([1-9]\d*|-)$/);
  return out.slice('[rc=0] '.length);
};
/** A valid field, written by the statement `cmd_start`'s seed runs (Task 4), from inside `wd`. */
const seedValid = (id: string, wd: string): void => {
  h.sh(`( CDPATH= builtin cd -- '${wd}' >/dev/null 2>&1 && eval "$(_plat_workdirid_pane "$REG" ${id} '${wd}'):" ) || :`);
  expect(field(id, wd), 'the CONTROL: the seed wrote a valid field').toMatch(/^\[rc=0\] valid\|/);
};
/** Any process-table walk, recorded: a spawn makes none. */
const PROC_SPY = '_ws_path_users_proc_root() { echo walk >> "$HOME/proc-walks"; printf %s /proc; }; '
  + '_ws_expire_proc_root() { echo walk >> "$HOME/proc-walks"; printf %s /proc; };';
/** `_spawn_start <id> <mode>` over `PANE_EXEC(shell)`, after `vars` (the snippet's own assignments: `PANE_PRE`,
 *  `PANE_POST`, `PANE_UP`). The answer is the snippet's stdout, which holds only the echo it adds: `_spawn_start`
 *  prints nothing, its stderr goes to `$HOME/spawn-err`, and the pane's output to `$HOME/pane-out`. */
const spawnPane = (mode: 'new' | 'resume', vars = '', shell = 'bash', id = ID): string => {
  const out = h.sh(`${PANE_EXEC(shell)} ${PROC_SPY} ${vars} _spawn_start ${id} ${mode} 2>>"$HOME/spawn-err"; echo "[$SPAWN_FROMSWAP]"`);
  expect(fs.existsSync(at('proc-walks')), 'a spawn walks no process table').toBe(false);
  return out;
};
const newSessions = (): string[] => h.calls().filter((c) => c.startsWith('tmux new-session'));
const composed = (line: string): string => {
  const m = /^tmux new-session -d -s \S+ -x \d+ -y \d+ (.*)$/.exec(line);
  expect(m, line).not.toBeNull();
  return m![1]!;
};

describe('_spawn_workdirid_pending: the parent’s pending line (path-identity spec §4.3; R2)', () => {
  const W = (): string => at('W');
  beforeEach(() => {
    fs.mkdirSync(W());
    h.sh(`_reg_set demo-x uuid ${UUID}; _reg_set demo-x workdir '${W()}'`);
  });
  const names = (): string[] => fs.readdirSync(at('.cc-sessions')).sort();
  const temps = (): string[] => names().filter((n) => n.startsWith('.demo-x.workdirid.'));
  /** The writer's rc. Its stderr goes to `$HOME/pending-err`, so a row can assert that it printed nothing. */
  const write = (pre = ''): string =>
    h.sh(`${pre} _spawn_workdirid_pending demo-x '${W()}' 2>"$HOME/pending-err"; echo "[rc=$?]"`);
  const err = (): string => fs.readFileSync(at('pending-err'), 'utf8');

  it('writes the pending line and nothing else: rc 0, the reader says pending, no temp is left, every other name unchanged', () => {
    const before = names();
    const uuid = fs.readFileSync(reg('demo-x.uuid'), 'utf8');
    expect(write()).toBe('[rc=0]');
    expect(err(), 'it prints nothing').toBe('');
    expect(fs.readFileSync(reg('demo-x.workdirid'), 'utf8'), 'the grammar’s pending form, the line alone')
      .toMatch(PENDING(W()));
    expect(field('demo-x', W())).toMatch(/^\[rc=2\] pending\|/);
    expect(temps()).toEqual([]);
    expect(names()).toEqual([...before, 'demo-x.workdirid'].sort());
    expect(fs.readFileSync(reg('demo-x.uuid'), 'utf8')).toBe(uuid);
  });

  it('a temp it cannot write, a VALID field standing: rc 1, the field unlinked (legacy-absent, never the stale valid one), nothing printed', () => {
    seedValid('demo-x', W());
    expect(write('mkdir -- "$REG/.demo-x.workdirid.$BASHPID.tmp";')).toBe('[rc=1]');
    expect(err(), 'it prints nothing').toBe('');
    expect(fs.existsSync(reg('demo-x.workdirid'))).toBe(false);
    expect(field('demo-x', W())).toMatch(/^\[rc=1\] legacy-absent\|/);
    expect(temps().map((n) => fs.statSync(reg(n)).isDirectory()), 'the planted directory stands, and only it')
      .toEqual([true]);
  });

  it('a directory at the field name: rc 2, it stands untouched, the reader says unmeasured, no temp is left, nothing printed', () => {
    fs.mkdirSync(reg('demo-x.workdirid'));
    fs.writeFileSync(reg('demo-x.workdirid/inside'), 'kept');
    expect(write()).toBe('[rc=2]');
    expect(err(), 'it prints nothing').toBe('');
    expect(fs.readFileSync(reg('demo-x.workdirid/inside'), 'utf8')).toBe('kept');
    expect(field('demo-x', W())).toMatch(/^\[rc=2\] unmeasured\|/);
    expect(temps()).toEqual([]);
  });

  it.each([
    ['this host’s arm', ''],
    ['the Darwin arm, forced', 'CCD_OS=darwin;'],
  ] as const)('a link at the field name is replaced by the pending line and never followed (%s)', (_arm, pre) => {
    const elsewhere = at('elsewhere');
    fs.mkdirSync(elsewhere);
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(elsewhere, 'inside'), 'kept');
    fs.symlinkSync(elsewhere, reg('demo-x.workdirid'));
    expect(write(pre)).toBe('[rc=0]');
    expect(err(), 'it prints nothing').toBe('');
    expect(fs.lstatSync(reg('demo-x.workdirid')).isFile(), 'the link was replaced by a file').toBe(true);
    expect(field('demo-x', W())).toMatch(/^\[rc=2\] pending\|/);
    expect(fs.readdirSync(elsewhere), 'what the link named is untouched').toEqual(['inside']);
    expect(temps()).toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe.skipIf(!LINUX)('every writer’s line parses as the state it means (P3)', () => {
  /** One of the two seed statements, read from ccd's own source: the `( CDPATH= builtin cd -- … ) || :` group on the
   *  one line that holds `needle`. */
  const seedStatement = (needle: string): string => {
    const ls = SRC.split('\n').filter((l) => l.includes(needle));
    expect(ls, `the CONTROL: one line of ccd holds ${needle}`).toHaveLength(1);
    const from = ls[0]!.indexOf('( CDPATH= builtin cd -- ');
    const to = ls[0]!.indexOf(') || :', from);
    expect(from >= 0 && to > from, ls[0]).toBe(true);
    return ls[0]!.slice(from, to + ') || :'.length);
  };

  it('the pending writer: pending; the pane under sh: valid; the start and ws-add seeds, as ccd spells them: valid', () => {
    fs.mkdirSync(at('W'));
    h.sh(`_spawn_workdirid_pending demo-p '${at('W')}'`);
    expect(field('demo-p', at('W'))).toMatch(/^\[rc=2\] pending\|/);

describe('R7’s two launch statements, by content (C3, R47)', () => {
  const body = ((): string[] => {
    const s = SRC.indexOf('\n_spawn_start() {');
    return SRC.slice(s + 1, SRC.indexOf('\n}\n', s)).split('\n');
  })();
  const PENDING_LINE = '_spawn_workdirid_pending "$id" "$workdir" || :';
  const pendingAt = (): number[] => body.flatMap((l, i) => (l.trim() === PENDING_LINE ? [i] : []));
  const indent = (l: string): number => l.length - l.trimStart().length;

  it('exactly two pending lines, each directly above a _tmux_new_session line at its own indent', () => {
    const pos = pendingAt();
    expect(pos).toHaveLength(2);
    for (const i of pos) {
      expect(body[i + 1]!.trim().startsWith('_tmux_new_session -d -s "$tname" '), body[i + 1]).toBe(true);
      expect(indent(body[i + 1]!)).toBe(indent(body[i]!));
    }
    expect(body.filter((l) => !/^\s*#/.test(l) && l.includes('_tmux_new_session -d -s "$tname"'))).toHaveLength(2);
  });

  it('exactly two command strings carry the fragment between the cd and a second cd, so the writer never gates the exec (R56)', () => {
    const text = body.join('\n');
    expect(text.split(`cd '$workdir' && $(_plat_workdirid_pane "$REG" "$id" "$workdir")true; cd '$workdir' && exec env \${genenv}COLORTERM=truecolor `)
      .length - 1).toBe(2);
    expect(text, 'no command string is left without the fragment').not.toContain(`"cd '$workdir' && exec env`);
  });

  it('the generation lock is released before each pending line', () => {
    const [first, second] = pendingAt();
    const line = (s: string): number => body.findIndex((l) => l.includes(s));
    const primary = line('_compact_lock_release "$genfd"; genfd=""');
    const retry = line('_compact_lock_release "$rgenfd"; rgenfd=""');
    expect(primary).toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(primary).toBeLessThan(first!);
    expect(retry).toBeGreaterThan(first!);
    expect(retry).toBeLessThan(second!);
  });

  it('the pending writer is defined directly after _spawn, called only from _spawn_start, and calls only K', () => {
    const names = ccdFunctionDefinitions().map((s) => CCD_FUNCTION_DEF.exec(s.text)![1]!);
    expect(names[names.indexOf('_spawn') + 1]).toBe('_spawn_workdirid_pending');
    const graph = ccdCallGraph();
    expect(graph.filter((e) => e.callee === '_spawn_workdirid_pending').map((e) => e.caller)).toEqual(['_spawn_start']);
    expect(graph.filter((e) => e.caller === '_spawn_workdirid_pending').map((e) => e.callee).sort())
      .toEqual(['_plat_epoch_ms', '_plat_mv_notdir']);
  });
});
```
