```ts
    const c = makeChild(h);
    const wd = h.reg(CHILD_ID, 'workdir')!;
    const e = evalOf(h, { pre: LIST_FAILS });
    expect(e.verdict, e.detail).toBe('unmeasured');
    expect(e.detail).toBe(`could not read ${c.main}'s worktree list, so whether git records ${wd} was never asked`);
    const o = owned(c.wt, c.main, LIST_FAILS);
    expect(o.rc, o.why).toBe('2');
    expect(o.why).toBe(`could not read ${c.main}'s worktree list, so whether git records ${c.wt} was never asked`);
    fs.rmSync(c.wt, { recursive: true, force: true });
    const g = evalOf(h, { pre: LIST_FAILS });
    expect(g.verdict, g.detail).toBe('unmeasured');
    expect(g.detail).toBe(`could not read ${c.main}'s worktree list, so whether git still records ${wd} was never asked`);
  }, 120_000);

  it('REC-6 the git arm shadows the reason: asking `_ws_reclaim_recorded_git` never changes what a caller read', () => {
    const c = makeChild(h);
    fs.rmSync(c.wt, { recursive: true, force: true });
    const out = h.sh(`${LIST_FAILS} ${REC_SPY} _WS_REC_WHY=sentinel; _ws_reclaim_recorded_git ${CHILD_ID} "${c.wt}";`
      + ' printf \'[rc=%s] %s\' "$?" "$_WS_REC_WHY"');
    expect(linesIn('rec-calls'), 'the CONTROL: the arm reached the reader, once').toEqual([c.wt]);
    expect(out).toBe('[rc=1] sentinel');
  }, 120_000);

  it('REC-7 the breadcrumb arm shadows the reason too', () => {
    const c = makeChild(h);
    fs.rmSync(c.wt, { recursive: true, force: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(sessions(), `${CHILD_ID}.reaping`), 'branch');
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(sessions(), '.reaped'), { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(sessions(), '.reaped', `${CHILD_ID}.json`),
      JSON.stringify({ id: CHILD_ID, uuid: h.reg(CHILD_ID, 'uuid'), workdir: c.wt }));
    const out = h.sh(`${LIST_FAILS} ${REC_SPY} _WS_REC_WHY=sentinel; _ws_reclaim_recorded_crumb ${CHILD_ID} "${c.wt}";`
      + ' printf \'[rc=%s] %s\' "$?" "$_WS_REC_WHY"');
    expect(linesIn('rec-calls'), 'the CONTROL: the arm reached the reader, once').toEqual([c.wt]);
    expect(out).toBe('[rc=1] sentinel');
  }, 120_000);

  it('REC-8 _ws_reclaim_reset clears the reason', () => {
    expect(h.sh('_WS_REC_WHY=x; _ws_reclaim_reset; printf "[%s]" "${_WS_REC_WHY-<unset>}"')).toBe('[]');
  }, 60_000);

  it('REC-9 a string hit on git’s main stanza, beside a record naming the main checkout under another spelling: rc 0 with RECLAIM_REC_MAIN, and the ladder keeps not-a-workspace', () => {
    const c = makeChild(h);
    const plink = path.join(h.home, 'plink');
    fs.symlinkSync(path.join(h.home, 'projects'), plink);
    const spelled = path.join(plink, 'demo');
    plantEntry(c, 'qb-main', spelled);
    expect(stanzas(c.main), 'the CONTROL: a linked record names the main checkout through the link').toContain(spelled);
    expect(rec(c.main, c.main)).toEqual({ rc: '0', main: '1', prunable: '0', why: '' });
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(sessions(), `${CHILD_ID}.workdir`), c.main);
    const e = evalOf(h);
    expect(e.verdict, e.detail).toBe('not-a-workspace');
    expect(e.token).toBe('');
    expect(e.detail).toBe(`${c.main} is ${c.main}'s main checkout, not a workspace of ${CHILD_ID}`);
    const o = owned(c.main, c.main);
    expect(o.rc, o.why).toBe('1');
  }, 120_000);
});

describe('ws-expire in the record reader’s two rc-2 shapes: answered before the tail, asked afresh, never parked (R75)', () => {
  /** The host's process-table walks recorded (`PROC_SPY`), then the expiry's probe pointed at a fixture root
   *  (`FAKE_PROC_SELF`, after the spy, so its root wins): no case here walks the host's /proc. */
  const EXP_PRE = `${PROC_SPY} ${FAKE_PROC_SELF}`;
  /** A second admin entry for the archived tree: a copy of its own, its `gitdir` naming `<spelling>/.git`, its HEAD
   *  DETACHED at the tree's tip, as `plantEntry` plants one for the child. */
  const plantExpEntry = (a: Archived, name: string, spelling: string): void => {
    fs.cpSync(adminOf(a.main, 'quiet-dune'), adminOf(a.main, name), { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(adminOf(a.main, name), 'gitdir'), `${spelling}/.git\n`);
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(adminOf(a.main, name), 'HEAD'), `${a.tip}\n`);
  };
  /** Everything an unmeasured answer or a refusal leaves standing, and no walk of the host's /proc. */
  const intact = (a: Archived): void => {
    expect(fs.existsSync(path.join(a.wt, 'f1.txt')), 'the archived tree stands').toBe(true);
    expect(h.git(a.main, 'branch', '--list', EXP_BRANCH), 'its branch stands').toContain(EXP_BRANCH);
    expect(h.reg(EXP_ID, 'archived'), 'the archive stands').not.toBeNull();
    expect(h.reg(EXP_ID, 'reaping'), 'no breadcrumb was written').toBeNull();
    expect(fs.existsSync(path.join(sessions(), '.reaped', `${EXP_ID}.json`)), 'no tombstone: nothing was pinned').toBe(false);
    expect(h.calls().filter((l) => l.startsWith('unsupervise')), 'the unit was not touched').toEqual([]);
    expect(h.calls(), 'the pane was not touched').not.toContain(`tmux kill-session -t =cc-${EXP_ID}:`);
    expect(linesIn('proc-walks'), 'no walk of the host’s /proc').toEqual([]);
  };

  it('EXP-1 two records name the archived tree (REC-1’s shape): ws-expire answers unmeasured, removes nothing and mints no token', () => {
    const a = makeArchived(h);
    const wd = h.reg(EXP_ID, 'workdir')!;
    expect(fs.existsSync(adminOf(a.main, 'quiet-dune')), 'the CONTROL: git’s admin entry for the tree').toBe(true);
    const tok = expireToken(h, { pre: EXP_PRE });
    expect(tok, 'the CONTROL: the expiry ladder passes before the plant').toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/);
    const alias = path.join(path.dirname(wtAlias()), 'quiet-dune');
    plantExpEntry(a, 'qd-alias', alias);
    expect(stanzas(a.main), 'the CONTROL: git lists the alias record').toContain(alias);
    expect(stanzas(a.main), 'the CONTROL: and the tree’s own').toContain(a.wt);
    const e = expireEvalOf(h, { pre: EXP_PRE });
    expect(e.verdict, e.detail).toBe('unmeasured');
    expect(e.token).toBe('');
    expect(e.detail).toBe(`two of ${a.main}'s worktree records name the tree at ${wd}, so which one is its record was never settled,`
      + ` so whether git records ${wd} was never asked`);
    const audit = expireAudit(h, { pre: EXP_PRE });
    expect(audit.code, 'an unmeasured audit exits 1').toBe(1);
    const doc = JSON.parse(audit.stdout) as Record<string, unknown>;
    expect(doc['verdict']).toBe('unmeasured');
    expect(doc['token'], 'no token is minted').toBeUndefined();
    expect(doc['detail']).toBe(e.detail);
    const r = expireVerb(h, tok, { pre: EXP_PRE });
    expect(r.code, r.stdout + r.stderr).toBe(1);
    expect(JSON.parse(r.stdout), 'the token minted before the plant carries nothing: the lock asks the ladder again')
      .toEqual({ failed: 'probe-unmeasured', detail: e.detail, crumb: false });
    intact(a);
  }, 120_000);

  it('EXP-2 only another spelling records the archived tree (REC-2’s shape): each pass asks afresh, the lane reads unmeasured with its why, and nothing carries to the next pass', () => {
    const a = makeArchived(h);
    const wd = h.reg(EXP_ID, 'workdir')!;
    const own = path.join(adminOf(a.main, 'quiet-dune'), 'gitdir');
    const recorded = fs.readFileSync(own, 'utf8');
    const tok = expireToken(h, { pre: EXP_PRE });
    expect(tok, 'the CONTROL: the expiry ladder passes before the plant').toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/);
    const alias = path.join(path.dirname(wtAlias()), 'quiet-dune');
    fs.writeFileSync(own, `${alias}/.git\n`);
    expect(stanzas(a.main), 'the CONTROL: git lists the tree under the alias spelling').toContain(alias);
    expect(stanzas(a.main), 'the CONTROL: and under no other').not.toContain(a.wt);
    const why = `${a.main}'s worktree records name the tree at ${wd} only under another spelling, so which one is its`
      + ` record was never settled, so whether git records ${wd} was never asked`;
    // Pass 1, audited twice as the lane audits on each of its passes: each audit asks the whole ladder, mints no token
    // and exits 1, which the lane reads as unmeasured with its why, never as a terminal refusal it would park.
    for (const n of [1, 2]) {
      const audit = expireAudit(h, { pre: EXP_PRE });
      expect(audit.code, `audit ${n} exits 1: unmeasured`).toBe(1);
      const doc = JSON.parse(audit.stdout) as Record<string, unknown>;
      expect(doc['verdict'], `audit ${n}`).toBe('unmeasured');
      expect(doc['token'], `audit ${n} mints no token`).toBeUndefined();
      expect(parseExpireAudit(EXP_ID, audit.code === 0, audit.stdout), `the lane's read of audit ${n}`)
        .toEqual({ kind: 'unreadable', detail: `ws-audit --expire measured nothing: ${why}` });
    }
    expect(refusalsOf(h.home), 'never journaled as the terminal no-worktree-record')
      .not.toContainEqual({ act: 'expire', token: 'no-worktree-record' });
    // The token minted before the plant carries nothing into this state: the verb asks the whole ladder again in its lock.
    const r1 = expireVerb(h, tok, { pre: EXP_PRE });
    expect(r1.code, r1.stdout + r1.stderr).toBe(1);
    expect(parseExpireResult(EXP_ID, r1.stdout, r1.stderr), 'the lane starts its next pass from a fresh audit')
      .toEqual({ kind: 'restart', detail: `probe-unmeasured: ${why}` });
    intact(a);
    // Pass 2: git's record names the tree by its string again. A fresh audit asks the whole ladder and mints its own
    // token, and the verb re-proves the token it is given inside its lock, so one this pass did not mint refuses.
    fs.writeFileSync(own, recorded);
    expect(stanzas(a.main), 'the CONTROL: git lists the tree by its own spelling again').toContain(a.wt);
    const audit2 = expireAudit(h, { pre: EXP_PRE });
    expect(audit2.code, audit2.stdout + audit2.stderr).toBe(0);
    const read2 = parseExpireAudit(EXP_ID, true, audit2.stdout);
    expect(read2.kind === 'document' ? read2.verdict.kind : read2.kind, 'the whole ladder passes, asked afresh').toBe('expirable');
    const r2 = expireVerb(h, 'f'.repeat(64), { pre: EXP_PRE });
    expect(r2.code, r2.stdout + r2.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect((JSON.parse(r2.stdout) as Record<string, unknown>)['refused'], 'a token this pass did not mint').toBe('state-changed');
    intact(a);
  }, 180_000);
});

describe('_ws_reclaim_owned: the project directory by device and inode, asked last (path-identity spec §4.8)', () => {

  it('OWN-4 the tree’s own identity cannot be measured: 2, the project directory’s kept', () => {

  }, 120_000);

  it('OWN-6 CONTROL: the child’s own tree is 0, and both identities are kept, each its own directory’s', () => {
    const c = makeChild(h);

    expect(o.rc, o.why).toBe('0');
    expect(o.why).toBe('');

    expect(o.wdid).toMatch(IDENT);

  it('OWN-7 a vanished tree: 0, the project directory measured and the tree’s identity empty', () => {

    expect(o.wdid).toBe('');

  it('OWN-8 each call clears both identities first: an answer given before the measures leaves them empty', () => {

      + ' printf \'%s|%s|%s\' "$?" "${_WS_OWNED_MAINID-<unset>}" "${_WS_OWNED_WDID-<unset>}"');
    expect(out).toBe('1||');

});

describe('the source: identity only refuses, and the owned check measures last (path-identity spec §4.8)', () => {
  const src = fs.readFileSync(CCD, 'utf8');
  /** `name`'s body, from its head line to its first closing brace at column 0, or '' when it is not defined. */
  const bodyOf = (name: string): string => {
    const a = src.indexOf(`\n${name}() {`);
    const b = a > -1 ? src.indexOf('\n}\n', a) : -1;
    return b > a ? src.slice(a, b) : '';
  };
  const codeOf = (name: string): string[] => bodyOf(name).split('\n').filter((l) => !/^\s*#/.test(l));

  it('SRC-1 the record reader asks -ef once, only under [[ -d "$path" ]], and never sets a hit from it', () => {
    const code = codeOf('_ws_reclaim_record');
    expect(code.length, 'the reader could not be sliced').toBeGreaterThan(20);
    const open = code.findIndex((l) => l.startsWith('  if [[ -d "$path" ]]; then'));
    expect(open, 'the identity pass is guarded by -d').toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    const close = code.findIndex((l, i) => i > open && l === '  fi');
    expect(close).toBeGreaterThan(open);
    const efs = code.flatMap((l, i) => (/\s-ef\s/.test(l) ? [i] : []));
    expect(efs, 'one -ef').toHaveLength(1);
    expect(efs[0]).toBeGreaterThan(open);
    expect(efs[0]).toBeLessThan(close);
    const pass = code.slice(open, close + 1).join('\n');
    expect(pass, 'identity sets no hit, no stanza and no value read from one')
      .not.toMatch(/\b(?:hit|hitn|m)=|RECLAIM_REC_(?:BRANCH|HEAD|PRUNABLE)=/);
    expect(pass).toContain('RECLAIM_REC_MAIN=1');
    expect(pass).toMatch(/\breturn 2\b/);
  });

  it('SRC-2 the ladder asks -ef directly after its string compare of the project directory', () => {
    const code = codeOf('_ws_reclaim_ladder');
    const str = code.findIndex((l) => l.includes('[[ "$(_ws_realpath "$workdir")" != "$(_ws_realpath "$main")" ]]'));
    expect(str).toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(code[str + 2]).toBe('  [[ ! "$workdir" -ef "$main" ]] \\');
    expect(code[str + 3]).toContain(
      '_reap_refuse not-a-workspace "$workdir is the project directory $main itself, under another spelling, not a workspace of $id"');
  });

  it('SRC-3 the owned check measures the two identities after its moved-tree check, directly before its last return 0 (P21)', () => {
    const code = codeOf('_ws_reclaim_owned');
    const rows = code.findIndex((l) => l.startsWith('  _ws_reclaim_workdir_shared "$id" "$wd"'));
    const moved = code.findIndex((l) => l.includes('_ws_reclaim_moved_check '));
    const measures = code.flatMap((l, i) => (l.includes('_ws_path_ident ') ? [i] : []));
    expect(rows).toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(moved).toBeGreaterThan(rows);
    expect(measures, 'two measures: the project directory, followed, and the tree').toHaveLength(2);
    expect(code[measures[0]!]).toBe('  _ws_path_ident "$main" follow \\');
    expect(code[measures[1]!]).toBe('    _ws_path_ident "$wd" \\');
    expect(measures[0]).toBeGreaterThan(moved);
    expect(code[code.length - 1]).toBe('  return 0');
  });
});
```

**The case tags.** Steps 2, 5 and 7 name cases by tag. Each tag is the prefix of its title (`REC-1 `, `OWN-3 `, `LAD-1 `, `DAR-2 `, `SRC-1 ` and so on), so a `-t` pattern selects it. Report a case by its tag.

- [ ] **Step 2: Run it and see it fail**

```bash
(cd server && ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run test/ccd-reclaim-main-identity.test.ts)
```

These texts were drafted, not measured. Record the measured ones.

FAIL:
- REC-1: the reader answers `{ rc: '0', main: '0', prunable: '0', why: '<unset>' }`. Today the alias record is read, never compared.
- REC-2: `{ rc: '1', …, why: '<unset>' }`.
- REC-3: `{ rc: '0', main: '0', …, why: '<unset>' }`.
- REC-9: `{ rc: '0', main: '1', prunable: '0', why: '<unset>' }`. Today's reader answers the main stanza's hit already and sets no reason yet; R67's line has no red of its own here, and Step 7's A9 pins it.
- REC-5a: `why: '<unset>'`.
- REC-8: `expected '[x]' to be '[]'`.
- OWN-1: its CONTROL passes, then `expected '0' to be '1'`.
- OWN-2, OWN-3 and OWN-4: `expected '0' to be '2'`.
- OWN-6: `expected '<unset>' to match /^[0-9]+:[0-9]+:([1-9][0-9]*|-)$/`.
- OWN-7: `expected '<unset>' to be ''`.
- OWN-8: `expected '1|<unset>|<unset>' to be '1||'`.
- LAD-1: its CONTROL passes, then `expected 'branch-elsewhere' to be 'not-a-workspace'`. The drafted verdict is `branch-elsewhere`: the ladder passes the git-directory rung, and the child's branch is checked out at the child's own tree. Record the measured verdict.
- DAR-2: `expected 0 to be 1`. The child is reclaimed today.
- EXP-1 (R75): `expected 'expirable' to be 'unmeasured'`. Today the alias record is read, never compared, so the expiry ladder passes and mints a token.
- EXP-2 (R75): `audit 1 exits 1: unmeasured: expected 0 to be 1`. Today the expiry ladder answers the terminal `no-worktree-record`, in a document that exits 0.
- SRC-1, SRC-2 and SRC-3: each finds no new line.

PASS today, and each must stay green:
- REC-4 and REC-5b (CONTROLs);
- REC-6 and REC-7 (the reader sets no `_WS_REC_WHY` yet; Step 7's A5 rows make them bite);
- OWN-5 (an order pin; Step 7's B3 makes it bite);
- DAR-1 (CONTROL).

Any other case that passes here is a defect in the case: fix the case, never the code. REC-1's red must come from the reader's answer, never from its CONTROLs. A red CONTROL means git did not list the planted record: STOP `rec-1-record-not-listed`. EXP-1's and EXP-2's reds must come after their CONTROLs too (a token minted before the plant, and git listing the planted spelling); a red CONTROL there is a STOP, `exp-control-red`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement in `ccd/ccd`, each edit located by its quoted text**

Use the Edit tool. Each Before is unique (Step 0's p-rows).

**3a. `_ws_reclaim_reset` clears the reason.** Before:
```bash
  RECLAIM_REC_MAIN=0        # 1 = that record is the project's MAIN worktree (git lists it first)
```
After:
```bash
  RECLAIM_REC_MAIN=0        # 1 = that record is the project's MAIN worktree (git lists it first)
  _WS_REC_WHY=''            # `_ws_reclaim_record`'s reason for its last rc 2 ('' = none)
```

**3b. `_ws_reclaim_record`.** Replace the whole function, from its head line through its closing `}`, and add the global line above it. Before (as at the export; Tasks 2 to 7 do not edit it):
```bash
_ws_reclaim_record() {   # main path -> git's worktree record for path, read from $main ONCE: rc 0 with
  #                           RECLAIM_REC_BRANCH ('' = detached) and RECLAIM_REC_HEAD set, and
  #                           RECLAIM_REC_PRUNABLE=1 when git marks that stanza `prunable` (spec §5.5's
  #                           git-record arm reads it); rc 1 when $main
  #                           records no worktree at path; rc 2 when the list could not be READ
  # `_ws_wt_branch`'s matching (the path as given, or resolved through
  # `_ws_realpath`, so a symlinked ancestor cannot hide a record), with the one
  # distinction it folds: its exit 1 is both "no record" and "the list failed",
  # which is right for ws-reap's refusal and wrong here, where "no record" is
  # the TERMINAL `no-worktree-record` and a terminal refusal is never retried.
  # A list that could not be read measured nothing (spec §5.5, rung 8's rule).
  # It also answers the HEAD the record names — a VANISHED worktree's record
  # (`prunable`) is the one place a detached child's last commit is reachable
  # from, and the tail clears that record. And it says whether the record hit
  # is the MAIN worktree's (RECLAIM_REC_MAIN=1): `worktree list` always prints
  # the main worktree's stanza first, and no child is ever that checkout.
  local main="$1" path="$2" real line listing m=0 hit=0 n=0
  RECLAIM_REC_BRANCH=""; RECLAIM_REC_HEAD=""; RECLAIM_REC_MAIN=0; RECLAIM_REC_PRUNABLE=0
  listing=$(git -C "$main" worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null) || return 2
  real=$(_ws_realpath "$path")
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    case "$line" in
      "worktree "*) m=0; n=$(( n + 1 ))
                    if [[ "${line#worktree }" == "$real" || "${line#worktree }" == "$path" ]]; then
                      m=1; hit=1; (( n == 1 )) && RECLAIM_REC_MAIN=1
                    fi ;;
      "HEAD "*)     (( m )) && RECLAIM_REC_HEAD="${line#HEAD }" ;;
      "branch "*)   (( m )) && RECLAIM_REC_BRANCH="${line#branch refs/heads/}" ;;
      prunable|"prunable "*) (( m )) && RECLAIM_REC_PRUNABLE=1 ;;
    esac
  done <<< "$listing"
  (( hit )) || return 1
  return 0
}
```
After:
```bash
_WS_REC_WHY=''
_ws_reclaim_record() {   # main path -> git's worktree record for path, read from $main ONCE: rc 0 with
  #                           RECLAIM_REC_BRANCH ('' = detached) and RECLAIM_REC_HEAD set, and
  #                           RECLAIM_REC_PRUNABLE=1 when git marks that stanza `prunable` (spec §5.5's
  #                           git-record arm reads it); rc 1 when $main
  #                           records no worktree at path; rc 2 (_WS_REC_WHY) when the list could not be READ,
  #                           or when, the tree at path standing and git's main record not naming it, a
  #                           record other than the main one and the string-matched one names it by device
  #                           and inode (path-identity spec §4.8)
  # `_ws_wt_branch`'s matching (the path as given, or resolved through
  # `_ws_realpath`, so a symlinked ancestor cannot hide a record), with the one
  # distinction it folds: its exit 1 is both "no record" and "the list failed",
  # which is right for ws-reap's refusal and wrong here, where "no record" is
  # the TERMINAL `no-worktree-record` and a terminal refusal is never retried.
  # A list that could not be read measured nothing (spec §5.5, rung 8's rule).
  # It also answers the HEAD the record names — a VANISHED worktree's record
  # (`prunable`) is the one place a detached child's last commit is reachable
  # from, and the tail clears that record. And it says whether the record hit
  # is the MAIN worktree's (RECLAIM_REC_MAIN=1): `worktree list` always prints
  # the main worktree's stanza first, and no child is ever that checkout.
  # IDENTITY ONLY REFUSES HERE (path-identity spec §4.8, PI10 O2). A hit is read
  # off the strings alone, and it GRANTS: at the ladder it passes the terminal
  # `no-worktree-record` and names the branch, and in `_ws_reclaim_owned` it
  # passes a standing tree, so an `-ef` hit would grant wherever git records a
  # tree under another spelling. Device and inode therefore never set a hit, a
  # stanza, or a value read from one. Once the strings are read, and only while
  # the tree at path stands (`-d`), each stanza path git listed, but the one the
  # strings matched, is compared with it by `-ef`: git's FIRST stanza, the main
  # checkout, sets RECLAIM_REC_MAIN=1; any other answers 2, because two records
  # name one tree, or its only record names it under another spelling, so which
  # record is its own was never settled. Once git's main stanza names the tree,
  # by its string or by `-ef`, no later stanza is asked: the tree IS the main
  # checkout, so the ladder's terminal refusal and the owned check's proof stand
  # rather than weaken to "never settled". A stanza that cannot be stat'd (a
  # prunable record, or a locked one on a disk that is not mounted) matches
  # nothing, so a sibling's gone tree never holds this one; and a path that does
  # not stand asks nothing (the gone-row arms, the vanished arm and the tail's
  # step 5 ask only of a proven absence). Every rc 2 sets _WS_REC_WHY: the list
  # failure's reads "could not read $main's worktree list", which its three
  # callers continue as they always have.
  local main="$1" path="$2" real line listing m=0 hit=0 n=0 hitn=0 k
  local -a wts=()
  RECLAIM_REC_BRANCH=""; RECLAIM_REC_HEAD=""; RECLAIM_REC_MAIN=0; RECLAIM_REC_PRUNABLE=0; _WS_REC_WHY=''
  listing=$(git -C "$main" worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null) \
    || { _WS_REC_WHY="could not read $main's worktree list"; return 2; }
  real=$(_ws_realpath "$path")
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    case "$line" in
      "worktree "*) m=0; n=$(( n + 1 )); wts+=("${line#worktree }")
                    if [[ "${line#worktree }" == "$real" || "${line#worktree }" == "$path" ]]; then
                      m=1; hit=1; hitn=$n; (( n == 1 )) && RECLAIM_REC_MAIN=1
                    fi ;;
      "HEAD "*)     (( m )) && RECLAIM_REC_HEAD="${line#HEAD }" ;;
      "branch "*)   (( m )) && RECLAIM_REC_BRANCH="${line#branch refs/heads/}" ;;
      prunable|"prunable "*) (( m )) && RECLAIM_REC_PRUNABLE=1 ;;
    esac
  done <<< "$listing"
  if [[ -d "$path" ]]; then   # identity is asked only of a tree that stands
    for (( k = 1; k <= ${#wts[@]}; k++ )); do
      (( k != hitn )) || continue                            # the stanza the strings matched: already read
      [[ "${wts[k-1]}" -ef "$path" ]] || continue            # another tree, or a path that cannot be stat'd
      if (( k == 1 )); then RECLAIM_REC_MAIN=1; continue; fi # git's main checkout, under another spelling
      (( ! RECLAIM_REC_MAIN )) || continue                   # the tree IS the main checkout: that refusal stands
      if (( hit )); then
        _WS_REC_WHY="two of $main's worktree records name the tree at $path, so which one is its record was never settled"
      else
        _WS_REC_WHY="$main's worktree records name the tree at $path only under another spelling, so which one is its record was never settled"
      fi
      return 2   # identity only refuses: never a hit
    done
  fi
  (( hit )) || return 1
  return 0
}
```
The `return 2` line's comment, `# identity only refuses: never a hit`, is the anchor of Step 7's row A1; check m19 confirms that no misspelling of it stands.

```bash
  # THE RECORD MUST NOT BE THE MAIN CHECKOUT'S. A row naming `$main` itself
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Mutation table**

First, one Bash call. It copies the restamped file into the gitignored ledger and writes the one-mutation helper, the shape of W2's:
```bash
S=.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-20-path-identity-w3-worktree-identity/task8-mut; mkdir -p "$S" && cp ccd/ccd "$S/ccd.task8" && cat > "$S/mut.mjs" <<'EOF'
// One exact mutation of one file, refused unless every anchor matches exactly once.
//   node mut.mjs FILE sub OLD NEW          replace the ONE occurrence of OLD with NEW
//   node mut.mjs FILE del NEEDLE...        delete each ONE line holding NEEDLE
import fs from 'node:fs';
const [file, mode, ...a] = process.argv.slice(2);
const src = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
const lines = src.split('\n');
const fail = (m) => { console.error(`mut: ${m}`); process.exit(3); };
const one = (needle) => {
  const at = lines.flatMap((l, i) => (l.includes(needle) ? [i] : []));
  if (at.length !== 1) fail(`${JSON.stringify(needle)} is on ${at.length} lines, not one`);
  return at[0];
};
let out;
if (mode === 'sub') {
  const [o, n] = a;
  const k = src.split(o).length - 1;
  if (k !== 1) fail(`${JSON.stringify(o)} occurs ${k} times, not once`);
  out = src.replace(o, () => n);
} else if (mode === 'del') {
  const drop = new Set(a.map(one));
  out = lines.filter((_, i) => !drop.has(i)).join('\n');
} else fail(`unknown mode ${mode}`);
fs.writeFileSync(file, out);
console.log(`mut: ${mode} applied to ${file}`);
EOF
```

Then each row is ONE Bash call, run from the workspace root, in the foreground, with a timeout of at least 600000 ms. The call:
1. applies the mutation;
2. runs the named cases;
3. restores the file whatever vitest answered, and proves the restore with `cmp`.

No mutation is restamped: no case these rows run reads the stamp. Every red below was drafted, not measured. Record each measured text and vitest's count of tests run and failed. - [ ] **Step 2: Write the failing test `server/test/ccd-cwd-users.test.ts`**

```ts
// path-identity W3 (PI4 D; R21, R22; P12): ONE working-directory probe, `_ws_cwd_users DIR [SAY]` (path-identity
// spec §4.6). It answers 0 when no process has its working directory at DIR or under it; 1 when one does
// (`_WS_CWD_USERS_PIDS`, at most five JSON records in `_WS_CWD_USERS_RECS`, one sentence in `_WS_CWD_USERS_WHY`); and
// 2 when it measured nothing (`_WS_CWD_USERS_WHY` says why), never "nobody" then. A process works inside DIR when the
// STRING of its cwd link equals DIR's PHYSICAL spelling (its parent resolved through `_ws_dir_physical`, its leaf not
// followed) or lies under it, OR, on Linux, when the directory that link names has DIR's st_dev and st_ino on its
// chain of `..`. Linux walks the process table through the seam `_ws_expire_proc_root` in ONE python3 call bounded by
// `WS_CWD_USERS_SCAN_S`, listed again to a fixed point, a leader whose own cwd vanished asked through `task/<tid>`, its
// own chain excluded; Darwin asks `_ws_expire_lsof` and compares strings only. ws-expire's `_ws_expire_cwd_users` is
// now its thin adapter (A10, S2).
// FIXTURE HOME ONLY (`makePrHarness`): every tree asked about is under the harness's HOME, and the probe only reads. A
// FAKE process table (`$HOME/fp/<pid>/{cwd,stat}`, ccd's own `$$` planted by `FAKE_PROC_SELF`) names what a live box
// cannot be made to produce on demand; each fake `cwd` is a symlink to a real directory, so the identity arm opens it
// and walks real `..`. Real processes are started by vitest (`holdProc`), never by ccd. The identity arm opens with
// `O_PATH`, which only Linux has, so its cases run on Linux.
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { makePrHarness, type PrHarness } from './ccdPrHelpers.js';
import { CCD } from './ccdWsHelpers.js';
import { holdProc, type Held } from './pathUsersFixture.js';
import { expireAudit, makeArchived } from './wsExpireFixture.js';
import { DARWIN_LSOF_STUB, FAKE_PROC_SELF } from './worktreeIdentityFixture.js';

let h: PrHarness;
let held: Held[] = [];
beforeEach(() => { h = makePrHarness('ccrc-cwd-users-'); held = []; });
afterEach(() => { for (const p of held) p.stop(); h.cleanup(); });

const LINUX = process.platform === 'linux';
const ROOT_USER = process.getuid?.() === 0;
const src = fs.readFileSync(CCD, 'utf8');
/** `WS_CWD_USERS_SCAN_S` as ccd defines it, or a marker no answer holds while it is undefined. */
const SCAN_S = /^WS_CWD_USERS_SCAN_S=(\d+)\b/m.exec(src)?.[1] ?? '<undefined>';
const real = (p: string): string => fs.realpathSync(p);
const hold = (cwd: string): Held => { const p = holdProc({ cwd }); held.push(p); return p; };
const exists = (name: string): boolean => fs.existsSync(path.join(h.home, name));

/** The tree every case asks about, unless it says otherwise: `<HOME>/worktrees/demo/quiet`, a `sub` directory in it. */
const tree = (): string => {
  const d = path.join(h.home, 'worktrees', 'demo', 'quiet');
  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(d, 'sub'), { recursive: true });
  return d;
};

interface Answer { rc: string; pids: string; why: string; recs: string[] }
/** `_ws_cwd_users`' own answer, read off its globals; `pre` runs first. Each global is read with a default, so before
 *  the probe exists a case reds on its rc (`127`), never on an unbound variable. */
const ask = (dir: string, pre = '', say = ''): Answer => {
  const out = h.sh(`${pre} _ws_cwd_users "${dir}"${say === '' ? '' : ` "${say}"`};`
    + ' rc=$?; printf \'%s\\x1f%s\\x1f%s\\x1f\' "$rc" "${_WS_CWD_USERS_PIDS-}" "${_WS_CWD_USERS_WHY-}";'
    + ' printf \'%s\\n\' ${_WS_CWD_USERS_RECS[@]+"${_WS_CWD_USERS_RECS[@]}"}');
  const [rc = '', pids = '', why = '', rest = ''] = out.split('\x1f');
  return { rc, pids, why, recs: rest.split('\n').filter(Boolean) };
};

/** A fake process table through the seam `_ws_expire_proc_root`, forced Linux so a macOS host reads it too: ccd's own
 *  `$$` first (`FAKE_PROC_SELF`), then `fakep <pid> <cwd> <ppid>` plants one process whose `cwd` is a symlink and whose
 *  `stat` names its parent, the expiry suites' shape. (`fakep`, not the expiry suites' `_fp`: a test-local helper whose
 *  name starts with `_` reads as a stub of a shipped function to `ccd-harness-integrity.test.ts`.) */
const FAKE = `CCD_OS=linux; rm -rf "$HOME/fp"; ${FAKE_PROC_SELF}`
  + ' fakep() { mkdir -p "$HOME/fp/$1"; ln -sfn "$2" "$HOME/fp/$1/cwd"; printf "%s (a b) S %s 1 1 0\\n" "$1" "$3" > "$HOME/fp/$1/stat"; };';

describe.skipIf(!LINUX)('the identity arm (path-identity spec §4.6): a cwd placed inside the tree by device and inode', () => {
  it('A1: a cwd spelled through an ALIAS of the tree is in use by device and inode, though its string names no part of the tree', () => {
    const d = tree();
    fs.symlinkSync(d, path.join(h.home, 'alias'));
    const via = path.join(h.home, 'alias', 'sub');
    const a = ask(d, `${FAKE} fakep 4242 "$HOME/alias/sub" 1;`);
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('1');
    expect(a.pids).toBe('4242');
    expect(a.why).toBe(`process 4242 has its working directory at ${via}, inside ${d} by device and inode`);
    expect(a.recs.map((r) => JSON.parse(r) as unknown)).toEqual([{ pid: 4242, comm: '', cwd: via }]);
  }, 60_000);

  it('A1b: CONTROL — the same alias of a SIBLING (`<tree>2`) places nothing: nobody', () => {
    const d = tree();
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(`${d}2`, 'sub'), { recursive: true });
    fs.symlinkSync(`${d}2`, path.join(h.home, 'alias'));
    const a = ask(d, `${FAKE} fakep 4242 "$HOME/alias/sub" 1;`);
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('0');
    expect(a.pids).toBe('');
  }, 60_000);

  it.skipIf(ROOT_USER)('A3: a cwd whose `..` cannot be walked (its own directory grants no search) is UNMEASURED — never "not inside"', () => {
    const d = tree();
    const nox = path.join(h.home, 'nox', 'in');
    fs.mkdirSync(nox, { recursive: true });
    fs.chmodSync(nox, 0o600);
    try {
      const a = ask(d, `${FAKE} fakep 4242 "$HOME/nox/in" 1;`);
      expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('2');
      expect(a.why).toBe(`the processes of this box could not be measured (${h.home}/fp, exit 3), so whether one works inside ${d} was never asked`);
      expect(a.pids).toBe('');
    } finally { fs.chmodSync(nox, 0o755); }
  }, 60_000);

  it('A11a: a cwd link that READ but names nothing, its stat file standing — not proven gone: UNMEASURED (R21)', () => {
    const d = tree();
    const a = ask(d, `${FAKE} fakep 4242 "$HOME/nowhere/x" 1;`);
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('2');
    expect(a.why).toContain('could not be measured');
  }, 60_000);

  it('A11b: the same with its stat file gone too — the process vanished: skipped, nobody', () => {
    const d = tree();
    const a = ask(d, `${FAKE} fakep 4242 "$HOME/nowhere/x" 1; rm -f "$HOME/fp/4242/stat";`);
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('0');
  }, 60_000);

  it('A10: the expiry ladder sees A1’s alias as `in-use`, with its record — the old string-only probe read it as expirable', () => {
    const a = makeArchived(h);
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(a.wt, 'sub'));
    fs.symlinkSync(a.wt, path.join(h.home, 'alias'));
    const via = path.join(h.home, 'alias', 'sub');
    const nobody = JSON.parse(expireAudit(h, { pre: FAKE }).stdout) as Record<string, unknown>;
    expect(nobody['verdict'], `the CONTROL: nobody in the fake table — ${String(nobody['detail'])}`).toBe('expirable');
    const r = expireAudit(h, { pre: `${FAKE} fakep 4242 "$HOME/alias/sub" 1;` });
    expect(r.code, r.stdout + r.stderr).toBe(0);
    const doc = JSON.parse(r.stdout) as Record<string, unknown>;
    expect(doc['verdict'], String(doc['detail'])).toBe('in-use');
    expect(doc['token']).toBeUndefined();
    expect(doc['inUse']).toEqual([{ pid: 4242, comm: '', cwd: via }]);
    expect(String(doc['detail'])).toContain(`process 4242 has its working directory at ${via}, inside ${a.wt} by device and inode — `);
  }, 90_000);
});

describe('the string arm, against the tree’s PHYSICAL spelling (P12)', () => {
  /** `$HOME/wtreal/demo/quiet` is the real tree and `$HOME/worktrees -> $HOME/wtreal`: the tree is asked by
   *  `$HOME/worktrees/demo/quiet`, the spelling ccd stores, while a cwd link and lsof print the physical one. */
  const linkedRoot = (): { asked: string; phys: string } => {
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(h.home, 'wtreal', 'demo', 'quiet', 'sub'), { recursive: true });
    fs.symlinkSync(path.join(h.home, 'wtreal'), path.join(h.home, 'worktrees'));
    return { asked: path.join(h.home, 'worktrees', 'demo', 'quiet'), phys: path.join(real(path.join(h.home, 'wtreal')), 'demo', 'quiet') };
  };

  it('A2: a dangling cwd under the tree (a removed directory, as /proc prints one) is in use, by its string', () => {
    const d = tree();
    const a = ask(d, `${FAKE} fakep 4242 "${real(d)}/gone (deleted)" 1;`);
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('1');
    expect(a.pids).toBe('4242');
    expect(a.why).toBe(`process 4242 has its working directory at ${real(d)}/gone (deleted)`);
  }, 60_000);

  it('A2b-linux: a tree spelled through a LINKED worktrees root — a dangling cwd under its physical spelling is in use, by its string', () => {
    const t = linkedRoot();
    const a = ask(t.asked, `${FAKE} fakep 4242 "${t.phys}/gone (deleted)" 1;`);
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('1');
    expect(a.why).toBe(`process 4242 has its working directory at ${t.phys}/gone (deleted)`);
  }, 60_000);

  it('A2b-darwin: forced Darwin, the same linked root — lsof lists a live process at the physical spelling: in use, by its string', () => {
    const t = linkedRoot();
    const s = hold(path.join(t.phys, 'sub'));
    const list = `_ws_expire_lsof() { printf 'p%s\\nfcwd\\nn%s\\np%s\\nfcwd\\nn%s\\n' "$$" "$HOME" "${s.pid}" "${t.phys}/sub"; };`;
    const a = ask(t.asked, `CCD_OS=darwin; ${list}`);
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('1');
    expect(a.pids).toBe(String(s.pid));
    expect(a.why).toContain(`process ${s.pid} `);
    expect(a.why).toContain(`has its working directory at ${t.phys}/sub`);
  }, 60_000);

  it.skipIf(!LINUX)('A13: a LIVE process whose working directory was removed under the tree is in use, by its string (the kernel’s ` (deleted)`)', () => {
    const d = tree();
    const gone = path.join(d, 'sub', 'scratch');
    fs.mkdirSync(gone);
    const s = hold(gone);
    fs.rmdirSync(gone);
    const a = ask(d);
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('1');
    expect(a.pids).toBe(String(s.pid));
    expect(a.why).toContain(`has its working directory at ${real(d)}/sub/scratch (deleted)`);
    expect(a.why, 'found by its string, not by the identity walk').not.toContain('by device and inode');
  }, 60_000);
});

describe('the walk: _ws_path_users’ discipline, adopted (R21)', () => {
  it('A4: a walk that outruns its bound is UNMEASURED, and says so', () => {
    const d = tree();
    const a = ask(d, 'CCD_OS=linux; _plat_timeout() { return 124; };');
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('2');
    expect(a.why).toBe(`the walk of /proc did not finish within ${SCAN_S}s, so whether a process works inside ${d} was never asked`);
  }, 60_000);

  it.skipIf(!LINUX)('A5: ccd itself, the subshell that captures the walk, `timeout` and python3 are not users — even with ccd’s own cwd in the tree', () => {
    const d = tree();
    const a = ask(d, `cd "${d}" &&`);
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('0');
    const s = hold(path.join(d, 'sub'));
    const b = ask(d, `cd "${d}" &&`);
    expect(b.rc, `the CONTROL: a process ccd did not start, in the same tree, is a user — ${b.why}`).toBe('1');
    expect(b.pids).toBe(String(s.pid));
  }, 60_000);

  /** 4242's `stat`, the file the probe reads of each candidate, as a FIFO: the probe's own read sequences the race. */
  const STAT_FIFO = '"$HOME/fp/4242/stat"';

  it('A6a: a pid only a SECOND listing holds is read — the walk is a fixed point, never one snapshot', () => {
    // 4242 works in the tree but is a child of ccd, so it is skipped; the probe's read of its stat is what plants 4243
    // (the successor a process forked before it exited), and 4243 works in the tree under another parent.
    const d = tree();
    try {
      const a = ask(d, `${FAKE} fakep 4242 "${real(d)}/sub" 1; rm -f ${STAT_FIFO}; mkfifo ${STAT_FIFO};`
        + ` { exec 3>${STAT_FIFO}; fakep 4243 "${real(d)}/sub" 1; printf '4242 (x) S %s 1 1 0\\n' "$$" >&3; exec 3>&-; } >/dev/null 2>&1 &`);
      expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('1');
      expect(a.pids).toBe('4243');
    } finally {
      // A probe that never read 4242's stat (the red phase) leaves the writer blocked opening the FIFO: an O_RDWR open
      // is a reader, and releases it.
      h.sh(`if [ -p ${STAT_FIFO} ]; then : <> ${STAT_FIFO}; fi`);
    }
  }, 60_000);

  it('A6b: a listing again that fails is UNMEASURED — a walk that cannot list the table again never reads as "nobody"', () => {
    const d = tree();
    try {
      const a = ask(d, `${FAKE} fakep 4242 "${real(d)}/sub" 1; rm -f ${STAT_FIFO}; mkfifo ${STAT_FIFO};`
        + ` { exec 3>${STAT_FIFO}; mv "$HOME/fp" "$HOME/fp-gone"; printf '4242 (x) S %s 1 1 0\\n' "$$" >&3; exec 3>&-; } >/dev/null 2>&1 &`);
      expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('2');
      expect(a.why).toContain('could not be measured');
      expect(exists(path.join('fp-gone', '4242')), 'the CONTROL: the table moved during the walk').toBe(true);
    } finally {
      h.sh('for f in "$HOME/fp/4242/stat" "$HOME/fp-gone/4242/stat"; do if [ -p "$f" ]; then : <> "$f"; fi; done');
    }
  }, 60_000);

  /** 4242's own cwd link reads as VANISHED, and its thread 4243 lives under `task/` with its cwd in the tree. */
  const leaderGone = (d: string): string => `${FAKE} fakep 4242 / 1; rm -f "$HOME/fp/4242/cwd"; mkdir -p "$HOME/fp/4242/task/4243";`
    + ` ln -sfn "${real(d)}/sub" "$HOME/fp/4242/task/4243/cwd";`;

  it('A7a: a thread-group LEADER that exited before its threads is asked through task/<tid> — its live thread works in the tree', () => {
    const d = tree();
    const a = ask(d, leaderGone(d));
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('1');
    expect(a.pids).toBe('4242');
    expect(a.why).toBe(`process 4242 has its working directory at ${real(d)}/sub`);
  }, 60_000);

  it('A7b: CONTROL — the same leader with no thread left IS gone: nobody', () => {
    const d = tree();
    const a = ask(d, `${FAKE} fakep 4242 / 1; rm -f "$HOME/fp/4242/cwd";`);
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('0');
  }, 60_000);

  it.skipIf(ROOT_USER)('A7c: a thread entry this uid may not read, the thread not in exit, is UNMEASURED', () => {
    const d = tree();
    const t = path.join(h.home, 'fp', '4242', 'task', '4243');
    try {
      const a = ask(d, `${leaderGone(d)} chmod 000 "$HOME/fp/4242/task/4243";`);
      expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('2');
      expect(a.why).toContain('could not be measured');
    } finally { if (fs.existsSync(t)) fs.chmodSync(t, 0o755); }
  }, 60_000);

  it.skipIf(ROOT_USER)('A12: a cwd link this uid may not read (EACCES) is the ruled exception — not seen, the stated limit, never a refusal', () => {
    const d = tree();
    const p = path.join(h.home, 'fp', '4242');
    try {
      const a = ask(d, `${FAKE} fakep 4242 "${real(d)}/sub" 1; chmod 000 "$HOME/fp/4242";`);
      expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('0');
    } finally { if (fs.existsSync(p)) fs.chmodSync(p, 0o755); }
  }, 60_000);

  it('A14: six users — five records, the sentence counts the sixth, and every pid is named once', () => {
    const d = tree();
    const pids = ['4241', '4242', '4243', '4244', '4245', '4246'];
    const a = ask(d, `${FAKE} ${pids.map((p) => `fakep ${p} "${real(d)}/sub" 1;`).join(' ')}`);
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('1');
    expect(a.pids.split(' ').sort()).toEqual(pids);
    expect(a.recs).toHaveLength(5);
    expect(a.why).toMatch(/, and 1 more$/);
  }, 60_000);

  it('A15: a walk that exits 0 but whose answer is not whole (a python3 that prints one record and the closing line, nothing else) is UNMEASURED', () => {
    const d = tree();
    const shim = path.join(h.home, 'shim');
    fs.mkdirSync(shim);
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(shim, 'python3'), '#!/bin/sh\nprintf \'{"pid": 4242, "comm": "", "cwd": "/x"}\\n.\\n\'\n', { mode: 0o755 });
    const a = ask(d, 'CCD_OS=linux; PATH="$HOME/shim:$PATH";');
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('2');
    expect(a.why).toBe(`the walk's answer was not read whole, so whether a process works inside ${d} was never asked`);
    expect(a.pids).toBe('');
    expect(a.recs).toEqual([]);
  }, 60_000);

  it('A15b: a walk that exits 0 and prints nothing (a python3 that never ran the scan) is UNMEASURED: an answer with no closing line is never "nobody"', () => {
    const d = tree();
    const shim = path.join(h.home, 'shim');
    fs.mkdirSync(shim);
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(shim, 'python3'), '#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n', { mode: 0o755 });
    const a = ask(d, 'CCD_OS=linux; PATH="$HOME/shim:$PATH";');
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('2');
    expect(a.why).toBe(`the walk's answer did not end with its closing line, so whether a process works inside ${d} was never asked`);
    expect(a.pids).toBe('');
    expect(a.recs).toEqual([]);
  }, 60_000);

  it('A16: python3 runs isolated (`-I`): a json.py in the caller’s working directory is never imported', () => {
    const d = tree();
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(h.home, 'evil'));
    fs.writeFileSync(path.join(h.home, 'evil', 'json.py'), 'import os\nopen(os.path.join(os.environ["HOME"], "evil-ran"), "w").close()\n');
    const a = ask(d, `${FAKE} cd "$HOME/evil";`);
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('0');
    expect(exists('evil-ran'), 'the caller’s json.py never ran').toBe(false);
  }, 60_000);
});

describe('A8: answers that measured nothing are UNMEASURED — never "nobody"', () => {
  it('A8a: a table without ccd’s own pid, and a table that cannot be listed', () => {
    const d = tree();

      const a = ask(p, 'CCD_OS=linux;');
      expect(a.rc, `${p}: ${a.why}`).toBe('2');
      expect(a.why).toBe(`${p} is not one plain absolute path, so whether a process works inside it was never asked`);
    }
  }, 90_000);

  it('A8c: a parent whose physical path holds a newline cannot be resolved: unmeasured, naming the newline', () => {
    const vol = path.join(h.home, 'vol\n');
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(vol, 'quiet'), { recursive: true });
    fs.symlinkSync(vol, path.join(h.home, 'root'));
    const dir = path.join(h.home, 'root', 'quiet');
    const a = ask(dir, 'CCD_OS=linux;');
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('2');
    expect(a.why).toContain(`the directory ${path.join(h.home, 'root')} that holds ${dir} cannot be resolved (`);
    expect(a.why).toContain('newline');
  }, 60_000);

  it.skipIf(ROOT_USER)('A8d: a parent that cannot be searched is unmeasured — the absence guard answers before any resolve', () => {
    const locked = path.join(h.home, 'locked');
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(locked, 'x'), { recursive: true });
    fs.chmodSync(locked, 0o000);
    try {
      const target = path.join(locked, 'x', 'quiet');
      const a = ask(target, 'CCD_OS=linux;');
      expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('2');
      expect(a.why).toContain(`${locked} cannot be searched`);
      expect(a.why).toContain(` — whether a process works inside ${target} was never asked`);
    } finally { fs.chmodSync(locked, 0o755); }
  }, 60_000);

  it('A8e: a tree PROVEN absent is nobody, and nothing is read — no table root asked, no walk run', () => {
    tree();
    const a = ask(path.join(h.home, 'worktrees', 'demo', 'gone'), 'CCD_OS=linux;'
      + ' _ws_expire_proc_root() { : > "$HOME/proc-root-asked"; printf %s /proc; };'
      + ' _plat_timeout() { : > "$HOME/walk-run"; return 124; };');
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('0');
    expect(exists('proc-root-asked'), 'no table root was asked').toBe(false);
    expect(exists('walk-run'), 'no walk was run').toBe(false);
  }, 60_000);
});

describe('A9: Darwin asks lsof and compares strings only — no /proc is read, and the identity arm never runs', () => {
  const POISON = '_ws_expire_proc_root() { : > "$HOME/proc-root-asked"; printf %s /proc; };';

  it('A9a: the stub listing names ccd alone: nobody, and the table root was never asked', () => {
    const d = tree();
    const a = ask(d, `CCD_OS=darwin; ${DARWIN_LSOF_STUB} ${POISON}`);
    expect(a.rc, a.why).toBe('0');
    expect(exists('proc-root-asked'), 'Darwin reads no /proc').toBe(false);
  }, 60_000);

  it('A9b: a live process listed under an ALIAS of the tree is not placed by identity there: nobody; at its physical spelling it is in use', () => {
    const d = tree();
    fs.symlinkSync(d, path.join(h.home, 'alias'));
    const s = hold(path.join(d, 'sub'));
    const listing = (at: string): string =>
      `_ws_expire_lsof() { printf 'p%s\\nfcwd\\nn%s\\np%s\\nfcwd\\nn%s\\n' "$$" "$HOME" "${s.pid}" "${at}"; };`;
    const alias = ask(d, `CCD_OS=darwin; ${listing(path.join(h.home, 'alias', 'sub'))} ${POISON}`);
    expect(alias.rc, alias.why).toBe('0');
    expect(exists('proc-root-asked'), 'Darwin reads no /proc').toBe(false);
    const phys = ask(d, `CCD_OS=darwin; ${listing(`${real(d)}/sub`)} ${POISON}`);
    expect(phys.rc, `the CONTROL: ${phys.why}`).toBe('1');
    expect(phys.pids).toBe(String(s.pid));
  }, 60_000);
});

describe('the source: one probe, its seams by name, one bounded Linux walk; the adapter walks nothing itself', () => {
  /** `name`'s body from its head line to its first closing brace at column 0, or '' when it is not defined. */
  const bodyOf = (name: string): string => {
    const a = src.indexOf(`\n${name}() {`);
    const b = a > -1 ? src.indexOf('\n}\n', a) : -1;
    return b > a ? src.slice(a, b) : '';
  };
  const code = (name: string): string => bodyOf(name).split('\n').filter((l) => !/^\s*#/.test(l)).join('\n');

  it('S1: _ws_cwd_users — one bounded python3 call on Linux, one direct one on Darwin, its seams and its resolve by name, no link-count skip', () => {
    const c = code('_ws_cwd_users');
    expect(c.length, 'the probe could not be sliced').toBeGreaterThan(2000);
    expect(c.split('_plat_timeout "$WS_CWD_USERS_SCAN_S" env LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 python3 -I -c "$py" proc ').length - 1, 'one bounded Linux walk').toBe(1);
    expect(c.split('out=$(LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 python3 -I -c "$py" lsof ').length - 1, 'one Darwin parse').toBe(1);
    for (const n of ['_ws_expire_proc_root', '_ws_expire_lsof', '_ws_dir_physical "$parent"', '_ws_reclaim_absent "$dir"', '_ws_reclaim_plain_path "$dir"']) {
      expect(c, n).toContain(n);
    }
    expect(c).not.toMatch(/st_nlink|WS_PATH_USERS_SCAN_S/);
  });

  it('S2: _ws_expire_cwd_users is the adapter — its preamble and parent resolve kept, the shared probe asked once, no walk of its own', () => {
    const c = code('_ws_expire_cwd_users');
    expect(c.length, 'the adapter could not be sliced').toBeGreaterThan(400);
    expect(c.split('_ws_cwd_users "$wt" "$workdir"').length - 1).toBe(1);
    expect(c).toContain('_ws_dir_physical "$parent"');
    expect(c).toContain('_reap_refuse in-use');
    expect(c).not.toMatch(/python3|_ws_expire_proc_root|_ws_expire_lsof/);
  });

  it('S3: WS_CWD_USERS_SCAN_S is defined once, at 10, and the probe stands in the RECLAIM region directly after _ws_path_users', () => {
    expect(src.match(/^WS_CWD_USERS_SCAN_S=\d+\b/gm)).toEqual(['WS_CWD_USERS_SCAN_S=10']);
    const users = src.indexOf('\n_ws_path_users() {');
    const probe = src.indexOf('\n_ws_cwd_users() {');
    const removal = src.indexOf('\n# ── the ONE removal of a per-session leaf');
    const end = src.indexOf('RECLAIM-END');
    expect(users).toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(probe, 'after _ws_path_users').toBeGreaterThan(users);
    expect(removal, 'and before the ONE removal block').toBeGreaterThan(probe);
    expect(end, 'inside the RECLAIM region').toBeGreaterThan(removal);
  });
});
```

**4a. The probe.** Write the block below to `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-20-path-identity-w3-worktree-identity/task9/probe.sh` with the Write tool, exactly. It contains no single quote between `py='` and its closing `'`, and no `\u`. Then splice it in with the call after the block.

```bash
# ── who works inside a tree: the ONE working-directory probe (path-identity W3, path-identity spec §4.6) ──
WS_CWD_USERS_SCAN_S=10   # bound on the ONE python3 call of the working-directory probe on Linux (healthy: tens of ms)
_WS_CWD_USERS_PIDS=''
_WS_CWD_USERS_WHY=''
_WS_CWD_USERS_RECS=()
_ws_cwd_users() {   # dir [say] -> 0 no process has its working directory at dir or under it, compared by the string of
  #                    its cwd link against dir's PHYSICAL spelling (its parent resolved by `_ws_dir_physical`, its leaf
  #                    not followed) OR by the dev:ino ancestry of the directory that link names (vacuously 0 when dir
  #                    is PROVEN absent); 1 one does (_WS_CWD_USERS_PIDS space-separated, each once; _WS_CWD_USERS_RECS
  #                    up to five JSON lines {"pid":…,"comm":…,"cwd":…}; _WS_CWD_USERS_WHY the "process N (comm) has
  #                    its working directory at P[, …]" sentence, with ", inside <say> by device and inode" for an
  #                    identity-only hit); 2 unmeasured (_WS_CWD_USERS_WHY), never "nobody": dir not one plain absolute
  #                    path, an absence not proven, a parent that cannot be resolved or holds a newline, or the walk.
  #                    say (default dir) is the spelling its reasons use.
  #                    Seams: _ws_expire_proc_root, _ws_expire_lsof, _ws_expire_lsof_fallback
  # PROCESS STATE MAY ONLY REFUSE (path-identity spec §4.6): no answer of this probe grants a removal. ws-expire
  # asks it through `_ws_expire_cwd_users`, its adapter (the fresh ladder's rung 5, and the resume); the spec has
  # the shared reclaim and expiry tail ask it as well, after its kill and before each forced removal.
  # WHAT IS COMPARED. Either arm makes a process a user:
  # - THE STRING ARM, the expiry probe's own: the text of a cwd link equals the tree's physical spelling, or
  #   begins with it followed by `/` (a sibling `<tree>2` is not inside). That spelling is the parent's physical
  #   path, resolved WHOLE here, with the leaf's own name appended and never followed: a cwd link and lsof print
  #   kernel-resolved paths that never go through a link, so a tree spelled through a linked root (a worktrees
  #   root that is a symbolic link, or macOS's /var) would otherwise never match its own spelling. This arm alone
  #   sees a cwd whose directory was removed (the kernel's ` (deleted)` suffix), and on Darwin it is the only one.
  # - THE IDENTITY ARM (Linux): the directory the cwd link names is opened (O_PATH, which follows the link as the
  #   kernel resolves it) and its chain of `..` walked to the root, each step's st_dev and st_ino compared with the
  #   tree's, read by lstat (a link leaf matches nothing here, as it matches nothing by string). It sees a process
  #   that entered through another mount or an alias of the tree, whose string names no part of it. Identities
  #   read in one walk compare dev:ino alone: one inode is one directory at one instant.
  # A PROCESS IS SKIPPED ONLY ON PROOF IT VANISHED, or on the one ruled exception, as the expiry probe always
  # required. Vanished: its cwd link or its stat file answers ENOENT/ESRCH; a cwd link that read but whose open
  # then answers ENOENT is gone only when its stat file answers so too. The exception: a cwd link that answers
  # EACCES (another uid's process, or a SAME-user NON-DUMPABLE one: ssh-agent, a setuid or setgid exec) is NOT
  # SEEN, the stated limit, because refusing on every unreadable link would refuse every removal for ever. Every
  # OTHER failure is UNMEASURED, never a skip: a `..` that cannot be walked (a directory on the chain with no
  # search permission), an open that answers anything but ENOENT, a stat file that does not parse. So one
  # same-uid process sitting in a directory that cannot be searched holds every answer at unmeasured until it
  # moves. There is no skip on a link count of zero: that is a property of a directory, not proof a process left.
  # THE WALK IS `_ws_path_users`' DISCIPLINE (Linux): a fixed point, never one snapshot (the table is listed again
  # until a listing names no pid this walk has not read; the pass that finds a user ends it); a thread-group
  # leader whose own cwd reads as vanished is asked through `task/<tid>`, and a thread entry unreadable for any
  # reason but vanishing is unmeasured unless that thread is in exit (PF_EXITING in its stat flags).
  # WHAT IS NOT A USER: ccd's own process (`$$`, `$BASHPID`), the scan's own chain (on Linux the python3, the
  # `timeout` that bounds it and the subshell that captures it, followed up by the parent each `stat` names; on
  # Darwin the python3) and any child of those. ccd's ANCESTORS are not skipped: a caller whose shell sits in the
  # tree IS using it.
  # WHEN THE LISTING IS TRUSTED: only when it holds ccd's own process, with its cwd link standing. A table that
  # cannot be listed or listed again, an lsof that is missing, fails or prints nothing, or a listing without ccd
  # measured nothing: unmeasured, never "nobody".
  # HOW IT IS ASKED, with no fork per process. Linux: ONE python3 call walks `<root>/<pid>/cwd` (the root is
  # `_ws_expire_proc_root`), bounded by WS_CWD_USERS_SCAN_S through `_plat_timeout` (124 is unmeasured). Darwin:
  # `_ws_expire_lsof`, bounded by WS_EXPIRE_LSOF_DEADLINE_S, and the same python3 parses its listing exactly as
  # the expiry probe always did, unbounded: a caller may shadow python3 with a shell function there (the expiry
  # ladder's suite hides `ps` that way), which no external bound can run, and a here-string is no input to a
  # command the pure-bash arm of `_plat_timeout` puts in the background. python3 runs with -I, so no module in the
  # caller's working directory is imported. The bounds are not absolute: a process in uninterruptible kernel wait
  # (a hung network mount on a cwd's chain) outlives TERM and KILL, and the caller waits for it, the reap lock
  # held; the answer is still never "nobody".
  # THE RECORDS ARE JSON AT THEIR SOURCE: one json.dumps line per user, at most five, the pid an integer and every
  # string as read; then one "#" line, the sentence, and one "=" line, every user's pid. json.dumps escapes every
  # control character, so a newline in a path or a command never starts a second record. An answer that names a
  # user without all three is unmeasured. Every whole answer, users or none, ends with one "." line, written only
  # after the scan returned: an answer without it (a python3 that exited 0 having scanned nothing) is unmeasured.
  local dir="$1" say="${2:-$1}" rc leaf parent wt me=$$ sub=$BASHPID mode=proc root='' listing='' out line py
  _WS_CWD_USERS_PIDS=''; _WS_CWD_USERS_WHY=''; _WS_CWD_USERS_RECS=()
  _ws_reclaim_plain_path "$dir" \
    || { _WS_CWD_USERS_WHY="$dir is not one plain absolute path, so whether a process works inside it was never asked"; return 2; }
  _ws_reclaim_absent "$dir"; rc=$?
  (( rc != 2 )) || { _WS_CWD_USERS_WHY="$_WS_ABSENT_WHY — whether a process works inside $say was never asked"; return 2; }
  (( rc != 0 )) || return 0
  leaf="${dir##*/}"; parent="${dir%/*}"; [[ -n "$parent" ]] || parent=/
  _ws_dir_physical "$parent" \
    || { _WS_CWD_USERS_WHY="the directory $parent that holds $dir cannot be resolved ($_WS_PHYS_WHY), so whether a process works inside it was never asked"; return 2; }
  wt="${_WS_PHYS%/}/$leaf"
  [[ "$CCD_OS" != darwin ]] || mode=lsof
  py='
import json, os, re, subprocess, sys
mode, wt, label, me, sub, root = sys.argv[1:7]
VANISHED = (FileNotFoundError, ProcessLookupError)
PID = re.compile("[0-9]+")
def inside(p):
    return p == wt or p.startswith(wt + "/")
def ppid_of(pid):
    # the parent pid, or None ONLY on proof the process is gone; anything else
    # that goes wrong is unmeasured (exit 3), never a skip
    if mode == "proc":
        try:
            with open("%s/%s/stat" % (root, pid), "rb") as fh:
                raw = fh.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
        except VANISHED:
            return None
        f = raw[raw.rfind(")") + 2:].split() if ")" in raw else []
        if len(f) < 2 or not f[1].isdigit():
            sys.exit(3)
        return f[1]
    r = subprocess.run(["ps", "-o", "ppid=", "-p", pid], capture_output=True, text=True)
    out = r.stdout.strip()
    if r.returncode == 0 and out.isdigit():
        return out
    # ps could not say, and its status and its silence prove nothing: only the
    # KERNEL may say the process is gone
    try:
        os.kill(int(pid), 0)
    except ProcessLookupError:
        return None
    sys.exit(3)
def comm_of(pid):
    # WHAT IT IS, for the operator text: a pid is never named without its
    # command. DESCRIPTIVE ONLY: a command that cannot be read is "" and
    # changes no verdict; its bytes are kept as read (surrogateescape), save
    # the one newline the kernel or ps ends it with
    try:
        if mode == "proc":
            with open("%s/%s/comm" % (root, pid), "rb") as fh:
                raw = fh.read()
        else:
            raw = subprocess.run(["ps", "-o", "comm=", "-p", pid], capture_output=True).stdout
    except Exception:
        return ""
    if raw.endswith(b"\n"):
        raw = raw[:-1]
    return raw.decode("utf-8", "surrogateescape")
def say(s):
    # the sentence is ONE line: a control character in a path or a command is
    # written there as its escape (the record keeps the bytes)
    return "".join(c if c.isprintable() else ascii(c)[1:-1] for c in s)
def exiting(base):
    # True ONLY on proof the task is going: gone, or PF_EXITING (0x4) in the
    # flags field of its stat; anything else is unmeasured
    try:
        with open(base + "/stat", "rb") as fh:
            raw = fh.read().decode("ascii", "replace")
    except VANISHED:
        return True
    except PermissionError:
        sys.exit(3)
    f = raw[raw.rfind(")") + 2:].split()
    if len(f) < 7 or not (f[6].isascii() and f[6].isdigit()):
        sys.exit(3)
    return (int(f[6]) & 4) != 0
def gone(statf):
    # True ONLY on proof the process is gone: its stat file answers ENOENT/ESRCH
    try:
        os.stat(statf)
    except VANISHED:
        return True
    return False
def entries(pid):
    # what to compare for process <pid>, as (cwd, its link, its stat file): its
    # own cwd link; or, for a leader whose own cwd link reads as VANISHED, the
    # cwd link of each of its live threads (a leader that exited before its
    # threads shows a vanished cwd while they still run where it ran)
    base = "%s/%s" % (root, pid)
    try:
        return [(os.readlink(base + "/cwd"), base + "/cwd", base + "/stat")]
    except PermissionError:
        return []   # the ruled exception: NOT SEEN, never a refusal
    except VANISHED:
        pass
    try:
        tids = [t for t in os.listdir(base + "/task") if t != pid]
    except VANISHED:
        return []
    except PermissionError:
        sys.exit(3)
    found = []
    for t in tids:
        tb = "%s/task/%s" % (base, t)
        try:
            found.append((os.readlink(tb + "/cwd"), tb + "/cwd", tb + "/stat"))
        except VANISHED:
            continue
        except PermissionError:
            if exiting(tb):
                continue
            sys.exit(3)
    return found
def placed(link, statf, child):
    # True when the directory the link names has the tree (child: its st_dev and
    # st_ino) on its chain of "..", False when it has not, None ONLY on proof the
    # process is gone; anything else is unmeasured (exit 3)
    try:
        fd = os.open(link, os.O_PATH | os.O_DIRECTORY | os.O_CLOEXEC)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        if gone(statf):
            return None
        sys.exit(3)   # the link named nothing, yet the process was not proven gone
    try:
        for _ in range(4096):
            s = os.fstat(fd)
            if (s.st_dev, s.st_ino) == child:
                return True
            up = os.open("..", os.O_PATH | os.O_DIRECTORY | os.O_CLOEXEC, dir_fd=fd)
            os.close(fd)
            fd = up
            u = os.fstat(fd)
            if (u.st_dev, u.st_ino) == (s.st_dev, s.st_ino):
                return False
    except OSError:
        sys.exit(3)   # a cwd whose ".." cannot be walked: unmeasured, never "not inside"
    finally:
        os.close(fd)
    sys.exit(3)   # a chain deeper than 4096: unmeasured
def scan():
    users, ids = [], set()
    if mode == "proc":
        st = os.lstat(wt)
        child = (st.st_dev, st.st_ino)
        try:
            listed = [n for n in os.listdir(root) if n.isascii() and n.isdigit()]
        except OSError:
            sys.exit(3)
        if me not in listed or not os.path.islink("%s/%s/cwd" % (root, me)):
            sys.exit(3)   # trusted only when it holds ccd itself, its cwd link standing
        mine = {me, sub}
        step = str(os.getpid())
        for _ in range(64):
            mine.add(step)
            pp = ppid_of(step)
            if pp is None or pp in (me, sub, "0", "1"):
                break
            step = pp
        done, todo = set(), listed
        while todo and not users:
            for pid in todo:
                done.add(pid)
                if pid in mine:
                    continue
                hit = None
                for p, link, statf in entries(pid):
                    if inside(p):
                        hit = (p, False)
                        break
                    if placed(link, statf, child):
                        hit = (p, True)
                        break
                if hit is None:
                    continue
                pp = ppid_of(pid)
                if pp is None or pp in mine:
                    continue
                users.append((pid,) + hit)
            if not users:
                try:
                    todo = [n for n in os.listdir(root) if n.isascii() and n.isdigit() and n not in done]
                except OSError:
                    sys.exit(3)
    else:
        cwds, cur = [], None
        for line in sys.stdin.read().split("\n"):
            if line.startswith("p"):
                cur = line[1:]
            elif line.startswith("n") and cur is not None:
                cwds.append((cur, line[1:]))
        if me not in [c[0] for c in cwds]:
            sys.exit(3)
        mine = {me, sub, str(os.getpid())}
        for pid, p in cwds:
            if not PID.fullmatch(pid):
                sys.exit(3)   # a pid that is not ASCII digits: no listing to trust
            if pid in mine or pid in ids or not inside(p):
                continue
            pp = ppid_of(pid)
            if pp is None or pp in mine:
                continue
            ids.add(pid)
            users.append((pid, p, False))
    if not users:
        return
    shown = []
    for pid, p, byid in users[:5]:
        c = comm_of(pid)
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({"pid": int(pid), "comm": c, "cwd": p}) + "\n")
        shown.append("process %s%s has its working directory at %s%s" % (
            pid, " (%s)" % say(c) if c else "", say(p), ", inside %s by device and inode" % say(label) if byid else ""))
    more = ", and %d more" % (len(users) - 5) if len(users) > 5 else ""
    sys.stdout.write("#" + ", ".join(shown) + more + "\n")
    sys.stdout.write("=" + " ".join(u[0] for u in users) + "\n")
try:
    scan()
    sys.stdout.write(".\n")
except Exception:
    sys.exit(3)
'
  if [[ "$mode" == lsof ]]; then
    listing=$(_ws_expire_lsof 2>/dev/null); rc=$?
    # A listing that ran out of time is not a listing, even one that already holds ccd's own pid: unmeasured.
    (( rc != 124 && rc < 128 )) \
      || { _WS_CWD_USERS_WHY="lsof did not finish within ${WS_EXPIRE_LSOF_DEADLINE_S}s, so whether a process works inside $say was never asked"; return 2; }
    out=$(LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 python3 -I -c "$py" lsof "$wt" "$say" "$me" "$sub" '' <<< "$listing" 2>/dev/null); rc=$?
  else
    root=$(_ws_expire_proc_root)
    out=$(_plat_timeout "$WS_CWD_USERS_SCAN_S" env LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 python3 -I -c "$py" proc "$wt" "$say" "$me" "$sub" "$root" </dev/null 2>/dev/null); rc=$?
    (( rc != 124 )) || { _WS_CWD_USERS_WHY="the walk of $root did not finish within ${WS_CWD_USERS_SCAN_S}s, so whether a process works inside $say was never asked"; return 2; }
  fi
  (( rc == 0 )) \
    || { _WS_CWD_USERS_WHY="the processes of this box could not be measured ($( [[ "$mode" == lsof ]] && echo lsof || echo "$root" ), exit $rc), so whether one works inside $say was never asked"; return 2; }
  [[ "$out" == . || "$out" == *$'\n.' ]] \
    || { _WS_CWD_USERS_WHY="the walk's answer did not end with its closing line, so whether a process works inside $say was never asked"; return 2; }
  [[ "$out" != . ]] || return 0
  out="${out%$'\n.'}"
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    case "$line" in
      '{'*) _WS_CWD_USERS_RECS+=("$line") ;;
      '#'*) _WS_CWD_USERS_WHY="${line#\#}" ;;
      '='*) _WS_CWD_USERS_PIDS="${line#=}" ;;
    esac
  done <<< "$out"
  [[ -n "$_WS_CWD_USERS_PIDS" && -n "$_WS_CWD_USERS_WHY" && ${#_WS_CWD_USERS_RECS[@]} -gt 0 ]] \
    || { _WS_CWD_USERS_PIDS=''; _WS_CWD_USERS_RECS=(); _WS_CWD_USERS_WHY="the walk's answer was not read whole, so whether a process works inside $say was never asked"; return 2; }
  return 1
}
```

**4b. The adapter (R22).** Write the block below to `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-20-path-identity-w3-worktree-identity/task9/adapter.sh` with the Write tool, exactly. Then replace the whole of `_ws_expire_cwd_users` (Step 0 (m)'s 197 lines) with it:

```bash
_ws_expire_cwd_users() {   # id workdir -> 0 when no process has its working directory at workdir or under it; else
  #                          rc 1: `in-use` (naming the pids and the paths), or unmeasured
  # AMENDMENT 3 (3962), ASKED OF AN EXPIRY. `_ws_expire_presence` calls it for the fresh ladder's rung 5 and for
  # the resume where nothing has been stopped yet, and `_ws_expire_resume_eval` asks it ALONE at `worktree` (3964),
  # where the tree may still stand; each hands it the worktree explicitly. A reclaim meets a finished child's
  # processes too — the pane's process tree can outlive the tail's kill (measured 2026-10-04: a straggler
  # re-created a removed temp root 3.7 s after `reclaim done`) — and the tail asks `_ws_path_users` of the temp
  # root after its kill (spec §5.6); path-identity spec §4.6 has that shared tail ask this same walk of the tree.
  # A THIN ADAPTER since path-identity W3 (path-identity spec §4.6). The walk is `_ws_cwd_users`', the ONE
  # working-directory probe (RECLAIM region): it compares a cwd by its string AND by its device and inode
  # ancestry, adopts `_ws_path_users`' fixed point, leader-thread walk and own-chain exclusion, and is bounded by
  # WS_CWD_USERS_SCAN_S on Linux. Its header now holds what this one's held: what is compared, when a process is
  # skipped (only on proof it vanished, or on the ruled EACCES exception, with that limit stated), what is not a
  # user, and when a listing is trusted. This keeps its name, its contract and its preamble, at rung 5 where the
  # leaf `-L` rung has not run yet: one plain absolute path; a PROVEN absence answering "nobody" with nothing
  # read; and the parent resolved WHOLE (`_ws_dir_physical`) with the leaf's own name appended, never followed,
  # so a link leaf is judged by its own name and the later rung refuses it. It maps the probe's three answers
  # onto its two: 1 is `in-use`, its records kept exactly as the probe printed them (EXPIRE_IN_USE: this shell
  # never splices a field into JSON); 2 is unmeasured, never "nobody".
  local id="$1" workdir="$2" rc leaf parent preal wt
  _ws_reclaim_plain_path "$workdir" \
    || { _ws_reclaim_unmeasured "$workdir is not one plain absolute path, so whether a process works inside it was never asked"; return 1; }
  _ws_reclaim_absent "$workdir"; rc=$?
  (( rc != 2 )) || { _ws_reclaim_unmeasured "$_WS_ABSENT_WHY — whether a process works inside $workdir was never asked"; return 1; }
  (( rc != 0 )) || return 0
  leaf="${workdir##*/}"; parent="${workdir%/*}"; [[ -n "$parent" ]] || parent=/
  _ws_dir_physical "$parent" && preal="$_WS_PHYS" \
    || { _ws_reclaim_unmeasured "the directory $parent that holds $workdir cannot be resolved ($_WS_PHYS_WHY), so whether a process works inside it was never asked"; return 1; }
  wt="${preal%/}/$leaf"
  _ws_cwd_users "$wt" "$workdir"
  case $? in
    0) return 0 ;;
    1) EXPIRE_IN_USE+=("${_WS_CWD_USERS_RECS[@]}")
       _reap_refuse in-use "$_WS_CWD_USERS_WHY — an archived workspace somebody is working in is never expired" ;;
    *) _ws_reclaim_unmeasured "$_WS_CWD_USERS_WHY" ;;
  esac
}
```

**4f. `_ws_dir_physical`'s census (comment only, by content).** The following script runs inside the function's header only, from `_ws_dir_physical() {` to its `local d="$1" r` line. It makes four changes:
- It moves both `its eleven callers` (Task 2's text) to `its twelve callers` (P12, R61).
- It leaves Task 2's `so it is counted once.` as it stands (R59), and refuses unless that sentence stands once and no `so the census stays` sentence is there.
- It inserts the twelfth call site's sentence directly above `# A bare …`, below Task 2's "The tenth and eleventh are the identity measure" sentence.
- It refuses unless each anchor stands exactly as counted.

```bash
node -e '
const fs = require("fs"); const f = "ccd/ccd"; const s = fs.readFileSync(f, "utf8");
const a = s.indexOf("\n_ws_dir_physical() {"); const b = s.indexOf("\n  local d=\"$1\" r\n", a);
if (a < 0 || b < 0 || s.indexOf("\n_ws_dir_physical() {", a + 1) >= 0) { console.error("census: the header could not be sliced"); process.exit(3); }
let h = s.slice(a, b);
const eleven = h.split("its eleven callers").length - 1;
if (eleven !== 2 || h.includes("its ten callers") || h.includes("its nine callers")) { console.error("census: its eleven callers stands " + eleven + " times, not twice, or a nine or ten callers sentence is there"); process.exit(3); }
h = h.split("its eleven callers").join("its twelve callers");
const once = h.split("so it is counted once.").length - 1;
if (once !== 1 || h.includes("so the census stays")) { console.error("census: the counted-once sentence stands " + once + " times, or a census-stays sentence is there"); process.exit(3); }
const bare = "\n  # A bare `$(cd -- \"$d\" && pwd -P)` dropped EVERY\n";
if (h.split(bare).length - 1 !== 1) { console.error("census: the A bare line is not there once"); process.exit(3); }
h = h.replace(bare, () => "\n  # The twelfth is the shared working-directory probe, `_ws_cwd_users`: the parent of the\n  # directory it is asked is resolved here, a fourth newline site (path-identity spec §4.6)." + bare);
fs.writeFileSync(f, s.slice(0, a) + h + s.slice(b)); console.log("census: twelve");'
```

- [ ] **Step 8: Mutation table**

First, one Bash call. It copies the restamped file and the base's file into the gitignored ledger, and writes the one-mutation helper. The ledger keeps them; nothing deletes them:

```bash
S=.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-20-path-identity-w3-worktree-identity/task9; cp ccd/ccd "$S/ccd.task9" && git show "$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)":ccd/ccd > "$S/ccd.base" && cat > "$S/mut.mjs" <<'EOF'
// One exact mutation of one file, refused unless every anchor matches exactly once.
//   node mut.mjs FILE sub OLD NEW          replace the ONE occurrence of OLD with NEW
//   node mut.mjs FILE del NEEDLE...        delete each ONE line holding NEEDLE
//   node mut.mjs FILE range START END NEW  replace the ONE line holding START, through the first line from there that
//                                          holds END, with the single line NEW
//   node mut.mjs FILE swapfn NAME OTHER    replace FILE's function NAME (its head line through its first column-0 `}`)
//                                          with OTHER's function NAME, byte for byte
import fs from 'node:fs';
const [file, mode, ...a] = process.argv.slice(2);
const src = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
const lines = src.split('\n');
const fail = (m) => { console.error(`mut: ${m}`); process.exit(3); };
const one = (needle) => {
  const at = lines.flatMap((l, i) => (l.includes(needle) ? [i] : []));
  if (at.length !== 1) fail(`${JSON.stringify(needle)} is on ${at.length} lines, not one`);
  return at[0];
};
let out;
if (mode === 'sub') {
  const [o, n] = a;
  const k = src.split(o).length - 1;
  if (k !== 1) fail(`${JSON.stringify(o)} occurs ${k} times, not once`);
  out = src.replace(o, () => n);
} else if (mode === 'del') {
  const drop = new Set(a.map(one));
  out = lines.filter((_, i) => !drop.has(i)).join('\n');
} else if (mode === 'range') {
  const [start, end, n] = a;
  const s = one(start);
  const e = lines.findIndex((l, i) => i >= s && l.includes(end));
  if (e < 0) fail(`no ${JSON.stringify(end)} at or after line ${s + 1}`);
  out = [...lines.slice(0, s), n, ...lines.slice(e + 1)].join('\n');
} else if (mode === 'swapfn') {
  const [name, other] = a;
  const span = (t, what) => {
    const head = `\n${name}() {`;
    const k = t.split(head).length - 1;
    if (k !== 1) fail(`${name} is defined ${k} times in ${what}, not once`);
    const s = t.indexOf(head) + 1;
    const e = t.indexOf('\n}\n', s);
    if (e < 0) fail(`${name} has no closing brace in ${what}`);
    return [s, e + 2];
  };
  const theirs = fs.readFileSync(other, 'utf8');
  const [os0, oe] = span(theirs, other);
  const [s, e] = span(src, file);
  out = src.slice(0, s) + theirs.slice(os0, oe) + src.slice(e);
} else fail(`unknown mode ${mode}`);
fs.writeFileSync(file, out);
console.log(`mut: ${mode} applied to ${file}`);
EOF
```

How every row runs:
- Each row is ONE Bash call, run from the workspace root, in the foreground, with a timeout of at least 600000 ms.
- The call applies the mutation, runs the named cases, restores the file whatever vitest answered, and checks the restore with `cmp`. Each row must print `restored`.
- No mutation is restamped, because no suite these rows run reads the stamp.
- Every red below was drafted, not measured. Record the measured text in the ledger.
- A case listed as red that stays green is a STOP, reported by its row id.
- A row whose only red case skips here (root, or a host without GNU `timeout` for A-M5) is recorded as unmeasurable, never a STOP.
