```ts
// path-identity W3, Task 10 (path-identity spec §4.6; R23, R24): a process working inside the tree stops the forced
// removal. The reclaim and expiry tail asks the one cwd probe, `_ws_cwd_users`, in two places. Inside the post-kill
// bounded wait, which ONLY WAITS: `_ws_reclaim_tmproot_quiet` is given the tree the tombstone names, asks the probe
// beside the temp root's, and ends early only when both say nobody. And at each STANDING forced removal, ahead of
// W2's mount ask, twice a site: before the checkout's or the tree's `_ws_reclaim_keep_of`, and again before its
// `git worktree remove --force`. Step (3) asks of the CHILD's whole tree, a superset of the checkout. A process inside,
// found by its cwd link's string against the tree's physical spelling or by device and inode ancestry, or a probe that
// could not be asked, fails `worktree-remove-failed`, with the breadcrumb, the tree and the branch standing, and the
// probe's reason cut by `_ws_leaf_why_line`. Process state never grants: nobody only lets the mount ask be asked.
// FIXTURE HOME ONLY (`makePrHarness`): both verbs run as sourced functions with the unit and pane calls recorded
// (`CHILD_STUBS`, `EXP_STUBS`), and every path is derived from `h.home`. The processes in the trees are REAL — spawned
// by vitest (`holdProc`), or started inside the verb's own shell by a wrapper with their pid recorded, and killed after
// each case — or FAKE, in a fixture process root (`FAKE_PROC_SELF`). So the Linux cases walk the real `/proc`, and
// CLAUDE.md lists this file as a load flake. The Darwin cases force `CCD_OS=darwin` and name lsof's listing exactly.
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { makePrHarness, type PrHarness } from './ccdPrHelpers.js';
import { CCD } from './ccdWsHelpers.js';
import { eventsOf } from './lifecycleHelpers.js';
import { CHILD_BRANCH, CHILD_ID, childReclaimVerb, evalOf, makeChild, type Child } from './childReclaimFixture.js';
import { verbHelpers } from './childReclaimVerbHelpers.js';
import { EXP_BRANCH, EXP_ID, expireToken, expireVerb, makeArchived } from './wsExpireFixture.js';
import { holdProc, type Held } from './pathUsersFixture.js';
import { DARWIN_IDENT_SHIMS, DARWIN_LSOF_STUB, FAKE_PROC_SELF } from './worktreeIdentityFixture.js';
import { SENTENCES } from '../src/wsaudit.js';

let h: PrHarness;
let held: Held[] = [];
beforeEach(() => { h = makePrHarness('ccrc-reclaim-tail-cwd-'); held = []; });
afterEach(() => { for (const p of held) p.stop(); killEntered(); h.cleanup(); });
const { interrupted, resumeToken, failedPairAgrees } = verbHelpers(() => h);
const hold = (o: Parameters<typeof holdProc>[0]): Held => { const p = holdProc(o); held.push(p); return p; };

const LINUX = process.platform === 'linux';
type Run = { code: number; stdout: string; stderr: string };
type Doc = { failed?: string; detail?: string; reclaimed?: string; expired?: string };
const docOf = (r: Run): Doc => JSON.parse(r.stdout) as Doc;
const linesIn = (name: string): string[] => {
  const p = path.join(h.home, name);
  return fs.existsSync(p) ? fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean) : [];
};

/** `_ws_cwd_users`, wrapped: runs the real one, then logs `<caller>|<dir>|<rc>` to `$HOME/cwd-calls`, and
 *  `<caller>|<reason>`, its reason uncut ('' when it answered 0), to `$HOME/cwd-whys`. */
const CWD_LOG = 'eval "_t_cwd_real()$(declare -f _ws_cwd_users | tail -n +2)";'
  + ' _ws_cwd_users() { local r; _t_cwd_real "$@"; r=$?;'
  + ' printf \'%s|%s|%s\\n\' "${FUNCNAME[1]-}" "$1" "$r" >> "$HOME/cwd-calls";'
  + ' printf \'%s|%s\\n\' "${FUNCNAME[1]-}" "$_WS_CWD_USERS_WHY" >> "$HOME/cwd-whys"; return "$r"; };';
/** `_ws_reclaim_keep_of`, wrapped: logs its `$4` (the path or branch it keeps for) to `$HOME/keep-calls`, runs the
 *  real one, and, once that answered 0 for the spelling in `$HOME/enter-when`, starts a process whose working
 *  directory is that path (`exec sleep 60`, stdio detached, its pid in `$HOME/entered-pid`): a process that enters
 *  between a site's two asks. */
const KEEP_ENTERS = 'eval "_t_keep_real()$(declare -f _ws_reclaim_keep_of | tail -n +2)";'
  + ' _ws_reclaim_keep_of() { local r; printf \'%s\\n\' "$4" >> "$HOME/keep-calls"; _t_keep_real "$@"; r=$?;'
  + ' if (( r == 0 )) && [[ -f "$HOME/enter-when" ]] && [[ "$4" == "$(cat "$HOME/enter-when")" ]]; then'
  + ' ( cd -- "$4" || exit 0; exec sleep 60 </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 & echo "$!" > "$HOME/entered-pid" ); fi; return "$r"; };';
/** A process that enters `dir` at the tail's first act (`_ws_unsupervise`), after every ladder has asked. */
const ENTER_AT_THE_TAIL = (dir: string): string =>
  '_ws_unsupervise() { echo "unsupervise $*" >> "$HOME/ccd-calls";'
  + ` ( cd -- '${dir}' || exit 0; exec sleep 60 </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 & echo "$!" > "$HOME/entered-pid" ); };`;
/** A fake process `$1` of the fixture process root: its cwd link at `$2`, its parent `$3` (the expiry suites' `_fp`). */
const FP = '_fp() { mkdir -p "$HOME/fp/$1"; ln -sfn "$2" "$HOME/fp/$1/cwd"; printf "%s (a b) S %s 1 1 0\\n" "$1" "$3" > "$HOME/fp/$1/stat"; };';
/** The process root missing whole: the probe cannot list it. */
const NO_ROOT = '_ws_expire_proc_root() { printf %s "$HOME/no-such-proc"; };';
/** The probe's process root, counted: each read appends `walk` to `$HOME/proc-walks`, and the real root answers. */
const PROC_SPY = 'eval "_t_root_real()$(declare -f _ws_expire_proc_root | tail -n +2)";'
  + ' _ws_expire_proc_root() { echo walk >> "$HOME/proc-walks"; _t_root_real; };';
/** `_ws_cwd_users`, answering IN USE for the tail's asks only, with a reason a person cannot read raw — a tab, a byte
 *  0xFF and 400 more of those (`ccd-child-reclaim-tmproot-wait.test.ts`'s `dirtyWhy`) — and the real answer to the
 *  wait. Never composed with `CWD_LOG`. */
const DIRTY_AT_THE_TAIL = 'eval "_t_cwd_inner()$(declare -f _ws_cwd_users | tail -n +2)";'
  + ' _ws_cwd_users() { if [[ "${FUNCNAME[1]-}" != _ws_reclaim_tail ]]; then _t_cwd_inner "$@"; return; fi;'
  + ' _WS_CWD_USERS_PIDS=4242; _WS_CWD_USERS_RECS=();'
  + ' _WS_CWD_USERS_WHY="process 4242 (x) has its working directory at $1"$\'\\t\\xff\'"$(printf \'\\xff%.0s\' {1..400})";'
  + ' return 1; };';
/** Every verb case: the wait asks once (its bound 0), and both wrappers log. */
const PRE = `CCD_RECLAIM_TMPROOT_WAIT_S=0; ${CWD_LOG} ${KEEP_ENTERS}`;

/** What `fn`'s cwd asks answered, in order: `<dir>|<rc>`. */
const asksFrom = (fn: string): string[] =>
  linesIn('cwd-calls').filter((l) => l.startsWith(`${fn}|`)).map((l) => l.slice(fn.length + 1));
const tailAsks = (): string[] => asksFrom('_ws_reclaim_tail');
const waitAsks = (): string[] => asksFrom('_ws_reclaim_tmproot_quiet');
const enteredPid = (): number => {
  const f = path.join(h.home, 'entered-pid');
  expect(fs.existsSync(f), 'the CONTROL: the process entered').toBe(true);
  return Number(fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8').trim());
};
/** Kills the process a wrapper started, and only while it still works under this fixture HOME: never a pid recycled. */
function killEntered(): void {
  const f = path.join(h.home, 'entered-pid');
  if (!fs.existsSync(f)) return;
  const pid = Number(fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8').trim());
  try {
    if (fs.readlinkSync(`/proc/${pid}/cwd`).startsWith(fs.realpathSync(h.home))) process.kill(pid, 'SIGKILL');
  } catch { /* gone, or not ours */ }
}

const reclaimToken = (): string => {
  const a = evalOf(h);
  expect(a.token, `the CONTROL: the ladder passes — ${a.verdict}: ${a.detail}`).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/);
  return a.token;
};
const workdirOf = (id: string): string => {
  const w = h.reg(id, 'workdir');
  expect(w, 'the CONTROL: the registry row names a workdir').not.toBeNull();
  return w!;
};
/** A standing nested checkout of the child's own repository, holding a file of its own. */
const nested = (c: Child): string => {
  const inner = path.join(c.wt, 'inner');
  h.git(c.main, 'worktree', 'add', '-b', 'ws/nested', inner);
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(inner, 'f'), 'nested work\n');
  return inner;
};
/** The fleet's layout, made BEFORE the child: `$HOME/worktrees` a link to `$HOME/wtreal`. */
const linkedRoot = (): void => {
  const real = path.join(h.home, 'wtreal');
  fs.mkdirSync(real);
  fs.symlinkSync(real, path.join(h.home, 'worktrees'));
};
/** Exit 1 and `worktree-remove-failed`: the document a cwd answer leaves. */
const cwdFailed = (r: Run): { detail: string } => {
  expect(r.code, r.stdout + r.stderr).toBe(1);
  const o = docOf(r);
  expect(o.failed).toBe('worktree-remove-failed');
  return { detail: String(o.detail) };
};
const atTree = (wd: string): string => ` — the tree at ${wd} stands, and nothing further was deleted`;
const atCheckout = (cpath: string): string => ` — the checkout at ${cpath} stands, and nothing further was deleted`;
/** The reason the tail cut, before the words ccd appends after it. */
const reasonOf = (detail: string, tail: string): string => {
  expect(detail.endsWith(tail), detail).toBe(true);
  return detail.slice(0, -tail.length);
};
/** One short clean line: printable ASCII, at most 300 bytes before the cut's `…`. */
const cutClean = (reason: string): void => {
  const body = reason.endsWith('…') ? reason.slice(0, -1) : reason;
  expect(body, 'printable ASCII only').toMatch(/^[ -~]*$/);
  expect(Buffer.byteLength(body, 'utf8'), 'cut at 300 bytes').toBeLessThanOrEqual(300);
};
const IN_USE = (pid: number | string): string => `a process works inside it: process ${pid} `;

describe('_ws_reclaim_tmproot_quiet, given the tree: it asks both, and only waits (path-identity spec §4.6)', () => {
  /** `fn`, stubbed: each call appends `tag` to `$HOME/quiet-calls` and answers the next of `answers` (the last repeats). */
  const SEQ = (fn: string, tag: string, answers: readonly number[]): string =>
    `${fn}() { echo ${tag} >> "$HOME/quiet-calls"; local n a=(${answers.join(' ')});`
    + ` n=$(grep -c '^${tag}$' "$HOME/quiet-calls"); (( n <= \${#a[@]} )) || n=\${#a[@]}; return "\${a[n-1]}"; };`;
  const calls = (tag: string): number => linesIn('quiet-calls').filter((l) => l === tag).length;
  /** The wait, its answer and the tree's last answer on one line: `<rc> <_WS_QUIET_TREE>`. */
  const quiet = (pre: string, tree = true): string =>
    h.sh(`${pre} _ws_reclaim_tmproot_quiet "$HOME/.cc-tmp/x"${tree ? ' "$HOME/tree"' : ''}; printf '%s %s' "$?" "$_WS_QUIET_TREE"`);

  it('Q1: one argument, as every caller before W3: the tree is never asked, and the answer is the temp root’s', () => {
    expect(quiet(`CCD_OS=linux; CCD_RECLAIM_TMPROOT_WAIT_S=5; ${SEQ('_ws_path_users', 'path', [1, 0])} ${SEQ('_ws_cwd_users', 'cwd', [1])}`, false))
      .toBe('0 0');
    expect(calls('path')).toBe(2);
    expect(calls('cwd'), 'never asked').toBe(0);
  }, 60_000);

  it('Q2: with a tree, the wait ends early only when both say nobody — the temp root at once, the tree on its third ask', () => {
    expect(quiet(`CCD_OS=linux; CCD_RECLAIM_TMPROOT_WAIT_S=5; ${SEQ('_ws_path_users', 'path', [0])} ${SEQ('_ws_cwd_users', 'cwd', [1, 1, 0])}`))
      .toBe('0 0');
    expect(calls('path')).toBe(3);
    expect(calls('cwd')).toBe(3);
  }, 60_000);

  it('Q3: a clock that never advances, and a tree that never leaves: it still ends after bound*4+1 asks of each, answering the temp root’s 0', () => {
    const FROZEN = '_plat_epoch_ms() { echo x >> "$HOME/clock-reads";'
      + ' if (( $(wc -l < "$HOME/clock-reads") > 40 )); then echo clock-escape >> "$HOME/quiet-calls"; printf 9999999999999;'
      + ' else printf 1000000000000; fi; };';
    expect(quiet(`CCD_OS=linux; CCD_RECLAIM_TMPROOT_WAIT_S=1; ${FROZEN} ${SEQ('_ws_path_users', 'path', [0])} ${SEQ('_ws_cwd_users', 'cwd', [1])}`))
      .toBe('0 1');
    expect(linesIn('quiet-calls'), 'the count ended it, not the escape').not.toContain('clock-escape');
    expect(calls('path')).toBe(5);
    expect(calls('cwd')).toBe(5);
  }, 60_000);

  it('Q4: on Darwin, with a tree, each is asked ONCE — the temp root’s answer never looks, and the tree’s is read once', () => {
    const t0 = Date.now();
    expect(quiet(`CCD_OS=darwin; CCD_RECLAIM_TMPROOT_WAIT_S=5; ${SEQ('_ws_path_users', 'path', [2])} ${SEQ('_ws_cwd_users', 'cwd', [1])}`))
      .toBe('2 1');
    expect(calls('path')).toBe(1);
    expect(calls('cwd')).toBe(1);
    expect(Date.now() - t0, 'it did not sit out the bound').toBeLessThan(4_000);
  }, 60_000);

  it('Q5: CONTROL: a tree that says nobody never shortens the temp root’s own wait', () => {
    expect(quiet(`CCD_OS=linux; CCD_RECLAIM_TMPROOT_WAIT_S=5; ${SEQ('_ws_path_users', 'path', [1, 1, 0])} ${SEQ('_ws_cwd_users', 'cwd', [0])}`))
      .toBe('0 0');
    expect(calls('path')).toBe(3);
    expect(calls('cwd')).toBe(3);
  }, 60_000);
});

describe.skipIf(!LINUX)('the post-kill wait waits for a process in the tree, and only waits (R23)', () => {
  /** A straggler in the tree: it leaves once the WAIT has asked about the tree twice — in use at the wait's first two
   *  asks, gone by its third — and after 30 s whatever happens. Spawned by vitest, never by ccd. */
  const LEAVES_AFTER_TWO_WAIT_ASKS = [
    'f="$1"; i=0',
    'while [ "$i" -lt 600 ]; do',
    '  n=$(grep -c "^_ws_reclaim_tmproot_quiet|" "$f" 2>/dev/null) || :',
    '  [ "${n:-0}" -ge 2 ] && exit 0',
    '  sleep 0.05; i=$((i+1))',
    'done',
  ].join('\n');

  it('B1: a process in the tree that leaves during the wait is waited for, and the tree goes after it, asked nobody twice at step (4)', async () => {
    const c = makeChild(h);
    const wd = workdirOf(CHILD_ID);
    const s = hold({ cwd: c.wt, script: LEAVES_AFTER_TWO_WAIT_ASKS, args: [path.join(h.home, 'cwd-calls')] });
    const r = childReclaimVerb(h, reclaimToken(), { pre: `CCD_RECLAIM_TMPROOT_WAIT_S=5; ${CWD_LOG}` });
    const waited = waitAsks();
    expect(waited.length, 'the wait asked the tree until it said nobody').toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3);
    expect(waited.slice(0, 2), 'in use at its first two asks').toEqual([`${wd}|1`, `${wd}|1`]);
    expect(waited.at(-1), 'and nobody at its last').toBe(`${wd}|0`);
    expect(r.code, r.stdout + r.stderr).toBe(0);
    expect(docOf(r).reclaimed).toBe(CHILD_ID);
    expect(tailAsks(), 'then step (4) asked twice, nobody both times').toEqual([`${wd}|0`, `${wd}|0`]);
    const order = linesIn('cwd-calls');
    const lastWait = order.reduce((a, l, i) => (l.startsWith('_ws_reclaim_tmproot_quiet|') ? i : a), -1);
    expect(order.findIndex((l) => l.startsWith('_ws_reclaim_tail|')), 'the wait came first').toBeGreaterThan(lastWait);
    await s.exited;
    expect(fs.existsSync(c.wt), 'the tree went').toBe(false);
  }, 120_000);
});

describe('the asks, read from the source (path-identity spec §4.6)', () => {
  const src = fs.readFileSync(CCD, 'utf8');
  /** Whole-line comments dropped, continuations joined (the six-calls census's own reading). */
  const codeOf = (body: string): string[] =>
    body.split('\n').filter((l) => !/^\s*#/.test(l)).join('\n').replace(/\s*\\\n\s*/g, ' ').split('\n');
  const tailCode = (): string[] => {
    const tail = src.slice(src.indexOf('\n_ws_reclaim_tail() {'), src.indexOf('\ncmd_ws_reclaim() {'));
    expect(tail.length, 'the CONTROL: the tail was found').toBeGreaterThan(1000);
    return codeOf(tail);
  };
  const CWD = '_ws_cwd_users "$workdir"; cwrc=$?';
  const MAPPING = `(( cwrc == 0 )) || { _ws_reclaim_fail "$id" "$lctx" worktree-remove-failed "$(_ws_leaf_why_line "$( (( cwrc == 1 )) && printf 'a process works inside it: ' )$_WS_CWD_USERS_WHY") — the `;
  const SITES = /_ws_cwd_users "\$workdir"; cwrc=\$\?|_ws_removal_mounts_clear|_ws_reclaim_keep_of "\$main" "\$id" tree "\$(cpath|workdir)"(?! 1)|worktree remove --force/;
  const label = (l: string): string => {
    if (l.includes(CWD)) return 'cwd';
    let m = /_ws_removal_mounts_clear "\$(\w+)"( resolve)?/.exec(l);
    if (m) return `mounts ${m[1]}${m[2] ?? ''}`;
    m = /_ws_reclaim_keep_of "\$main" "\$id" tree "\$(\w+)"/.exec(l);
    if (m) return `keep ${m[1]}`;
    m = /worktree remove --force "\$(\w+)"/.exec(l);
    if (m) return `remove ${m[1]}`;
    return `unlabelled: ${l.trim()}`;
  };

  it('S1: in order — one cwd ask before each mount ask, at the nested checkout and then at the tree', () => {
    expect(tailCode().filter((l) => SITES.test(l)).map(label)).toEqual([
      'cwd', 'mounts cpath', 'keep cpath', 'cwd', 'mounts cpath', 'remove cpath',
      'cwd', 'mounts workdir resolve', 'keep workdir', 'cwd', 'mounts workdir resolve', 'remove workdir',
    ]);
  });

  it('S2: each cwd ask is followed by its own mapping, which cuts its reason, then by the mount ask of its site’s path; none spells git', () => {
    const code = tailCode();
    const at = code.flatMap((l, i) => (l.trim() === CWD ? [i] : []));
    expect(at.length, 'four asks, each a statement of its own').toBe(4);
    const paths = ['cpath', 'cpath', 'workdir', 'workdir'] as const;
    at.forEach((i, k) => {
      const rest = code.slice(i + 1).filter((l) => l.trim() !== '');
      expect(rest[0]!.trim().startsWith(MAPPING), rest[0]).toBe(true);
      expect(rest[0], 'the mapping names its own site').toContain(paths[k] === 'cpath'
        ? ' — the checkout at $cpath stands, and nothing further was deleted"; return 1; }'
        : ' — the tree at $workdir stands, and nothing further was deleted"; return 1; }');
      // The tail's re-ask (its call and its two maps, path-identity spec §4.7) may stand between the map and the mount ask.
      const ask = rest.slice(1).find((l) => !/^\s*(_ws_reclaim_reask |\(\( rarc (!= 1|== 0) \)\) \|\| \{)/.test(l));
      expect(ask!.trim().startsWith(`_ws_removal_mounts_clear "$${paths[k]}"`), ask).toBe(true);
    });
    expect(code.filter((l) => /_ws_cwd_users |cwrc/.test(l) && /\bgit\b/.test(l)), 'a cwd line that spells git').toEqual([]);
  });

  it('S3: the wait is given the tree the tombstone names, read before the tombstone is validated, and its answers are read by nothing', () => {
    const code = tailCode().map((l) => l.trim());
    const q = code.indexOf(`qwd=$(_ws_tomb_str "$tomb" workdir 2>/dev/null) || qwd=''`);
    expect(q, 'the early read').toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(code[q + 1]!.startsWith('_ws_reclaim_tmproot_quiet "$HOME/.cc-tmp/$id" ${qwd:+"$qwd"} || :'), code[q + 1]).toBe(true);
    const full = code.findIndex((l) => l.startsWith('if ! tid=$(_ws_tomb_str "$tomb" id)'));
    expect(full, 'the full read follows the wait').toBeGreaterThan(q + 1);
    expect(code.filter((l) => l.includes('_ws_reclaim_tmproot_quiet ')), 'one wait').toHaveLength(1);
    expect(code.filter((l) => l.includes('_WS_QUIET_TREE')), 'the tail reads nothing the wait answered').toEqual([]);
  });
});

describe('R24: the failure word’s one sentence stays true of a process inside the tree', () => {
  it('R24: it names a process, and still reads as the reused reap word', () => {
    expect(SENTENCES['worktree-remove-failed']).toBe('ccrc stopped: git refused to remove a worktree, or ccrc could not prove that the tree at this workspace’s path — or a checkout inside it — is its own, or a process still works inside it. The session is stopped and nothing further was deleted.');
    expect(SENTENCES['worktree-remove-failed']).toMatch(/could not prove that the tree at this workspace’s path — or a checkout inside it — is its own/);
    expect(SENTENCES['worktree-remove-failed']).not.toMatch(/before removing a worktree/);
  });
});
```

**The cases.** The mutation rows and the record name each case by its title prefix:

| Prefix | Describe | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `Q1:` to `Q5:` | the wait helper | one argument unchanged; both must say nobody; the count with a tree; Darwin asks each once; the temp root's wait unchanged |
| `B1:` | the post-kill wait | the wait waits for the tree, then step (4) asks |
| `N1:`, `N2:` | the standing asks | step (3) before its keep and before its removal |

**3a. The wait helper: a tree, its last answer, and the second walk's worst case.**

Before (the whole function, hints `:33097-33134`):
```bash
_ws_reclaim_tmproot_quiet() {   # path -> `_ws_path_users`' LAST answer (0/1/2), asked until it says nobody
  #                                or `_ws_reclaim_tmproot_wait_s` seconds have passed on the clock between asks
  # Asked every quarter second. ON DARWIN the probe answers unmeasured without
  # looking, so it is asked ONCE: waiting cannot change that answer.
  # TWO ENDS, and the first one reached ends it: the wall clock, and a count
  # of `bound * 4 + 1` asks. The clock alone is not a bound: it is
  # `EPOCHREALTIME`, so a clock stepped backwards would lengthen the wait
  # without limit. The count never shortens a wait the clock would allow:
  # every ask after the first follows a quarter-second sleep, so by the last
  # one counted the bound has already passed.
  # WHAT THE BOUND BOUNDS, STATED (spec §5.6): the clock between asks, never
  # the wait's wall time. An ask that begins just inside the bound still runs
  # its whole walk, which `WS_PATH_USERS_SCAN_S` (10 s) bounds, plus
  # `_plat_timeout`'s kill grace (3 s) when the walk ignores TERM. So on a
  # working clock the worst case is the bound, plus that one walk, plus the
  # tail's own ask at step (6): about 35 s, or 41 s when both walks ignore TERM
  # and run to the end of their grace. With a clock frozen or running
  # backwards only the count ends the loop, and when every walk also runs out
  # its bound that is `(bound * 4 + 1) * (WS_PATH_USERS_SCAN_S + 0.25)`
  # seconds, about 625 s: past the 240 s budget a remote caller allows. THAT IS
  # SAFE, and is stated rather than prevented: a remote kill at the budget
  # lands in this wait, which runs BEFORE the tombstone is read and before
  # anything is deleted, and the breadcrumb the caller wrote already resumes
  # the tail on the next attempt.
  local p="$1" bound end rc n=0 max
  bound=$(_ws_reclaim_tmproot_wait_s)
  max=$(( bound * 4 + 1 ))
  end=$(( $(_plat_epoch_ms) + bound * 1000 ))
  while :; do
    _ws_path_users "$p"; rc=$?
    (( rc != 0 )) || return 0
    [[ "$CCD_OS" != darwin ]] || return "$rc"
    n=$(( n + 1 ))
    (( n < max )) || return "$rc"
    (( $(_plat_epoch_ms) < end )) || return "$rc"
    sleep 0.25
  done
}
```
After:
```bash
_WS_QUIET_TREE=0   # `_ws_reclaim_tmproot_quiet`'s last answer about the TREE (0/1/2); 0 when it was given none
_ws_reclaim_tmproot_quiet() {   # path [tree] -> `_ws_path_users`' LAST answer (0/1/2), asked until it says nobody
  #                                or `_ws_reclaim_tmproot_wait_s` seconds have passed on the clock between asks.
  #                                With `tree`, every ask also asks `_ws_cwd_users` of it, and the wait ends early
  #                                only when BOTH say nobody; _WS_QUIET_TREE holds the tree's last answer. The
  #                                answer is the temp root's either way (path-identity spec §4.6)
  # Asked every quarter second. ON DARWIN the probe answers unmeasured without
  # looking, so it is asked ONCE: waiting cannot change that answer. A tree is
  # asked once there too, beside it.
  # TWO ENDS, and the first one reached ends it: the wall clock, and a count
  # of `bound * 4 + 1` asks. The clock alone is not a bound: it is
  # `EPOCHREALTIME`, so a clock stepped backwards would lengthen the wait
  # without limit. The count never shortens a wait the clock would allow:
  # every ask after the first follows a quarter-second sleep, so by the last
  # one counted the bound has already passed.
  # WHAT THE BOUND BOUNDS, STATED (spec §5.6): the clock between asks, never
  # the wait's wall time. An ask that begins just inside the bound still runs
  # its whole walk, which `WS_PATH_USERS_SCAN_S` (10 s) bounds, plus
  # `_plat_timeout`'s kill grace (3 s) when the walk ignores TERM. So on a
  # working clock the worst case is the bound, plus that one walk, plus the
  # tail's own ask at step (6): about 35 s, or 41 s when both walks ignore TERM
  # and run to the end of their grace. With a tree each ask on Linux is two walks, the
  # second bounded by `WS_CWD_USERS_SCAN_S` (10 s) and its own grace: about
  # 45 s, or 54 s. With a clock frozen or running
  # backwards only the count ends the loop, and when every walk also runs out
  # its bound that is `(bound * 4 + 1) * (WS_PATH_USERS_SCAN_S + 0.25)`
  # seconds, about 625 s, and with a tree
  # `(bound * 4 + 1) * (WS_PATH_USERS_SCAN_S + WS_CWD_USERS_SCAN_S + 0.25)`,
  # about 1235 s: past the 240 s budget a remote caller allows. THAT IS
  # SAFE, and is stated rather than prevented: a remote kill at the budget
  # lands in this wait, which runs BEFORE the tombstone is validated and before
  # anything is deleted, and the breadcrumb the caller wrote already resumes
  # the tail on the next attempt.
  local p="$1" t="${2-}" bound end rc trc=0 n=0 max
  _WS_QUIET_TREE=0
  bound=$(_ws_reclaim_tmproot_wait_s)
  max=$(( bound * 4 + 1 ))
  end=$(( $(_plat_epoch_ms) + bound * 1000 ))
  while :; do
    _ws_path_users "$p"; rc=$?
    if [[ -n "$t" ]]; then _ws_cwd_users "$t"; trc=$?; _WS_QUIET_TREE=$trc; fi
    (( rc != 0 || trc != 0 )) || return 0
    [[ "$CCD_OS" != darwin ]] || return "$rc"
    n=$(( n + 1 ))
    (( n < max )) || return "$rc"
    (( $(_plat_epoch_ms) < end )) || return "$rc"
    sleep 0.25
  done
}
```

- [ ] **Step 9: Mutation table**

First, one Bash call. It copies the restamped file and the server file into the ledger's own scratch directory, and writes the one-mutation helper there. The ledger is gitignored. The scratch is never deleted through a variable: it stays in the ledger.

```bash
S=.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-20-path-identity-w3-worktree-identity/task10; mkdir -p "$S" && cp ccd/ccd "$S/ccd.task10" && cp server/src/wsaudit.ts "$S/wsaudit.task10" && cat > "$S/mut.mjs" <<'EOF'
// One exact mutation of one file, refused unless every anchor matches exactly as counted.
//   node mut.mjs FILE sub OLD NEW                 replace the ONE occurrence of OLD with NEW
//   node mut.mjs FILE suball OLD NEW COUNT        replace every occurrence of OLD, refused unless there are COUNT
//   node mut.mjs FILE subnth OLD NEW N COUNT      replace the N-th (1-based) of exactly COUNT occurrences of OLD
//   node mut.mjs FILE delnth START END N COUNT    delete the N-th of exactly COUNT lines holding START, through the
//                                                 first line at or after it holding END
import fs from 'node:fs';
const [file, mode, ...a] = process.argv.slice(2);
const src = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
const fail = (m) => { console.error(`mut: ${m}`); process.exit(3); };
const count = (o) => src.split(o).length - 1;
let out;
if (mode === 'sub') {
  const [o, n] = a;
  if (count(o) !== 1) fail(`${JSON.stringify(o)} occurs ${count(o)} times, not once`);
  out = src.replace(o, () => n);
} else if (mode === 'suball') {
  const [o, n, c] = a;
  if (count(o) !== Number(c)) fail(`${JSON.stringify(o)} occurs ${count(o)} times, not ${c}`);
  out = src.split(o).join(n);
} else if (mode === 'subnth') {
  const [o, n, k, c] = a;
  const parts = src.split(o);
  if (parts.length - 1 !== Number(c)) fail(`${JSON.stringify(o)} occurs ${parts.length - 1} times, not ${c}`);
  const i = Number(k);
  if (!(i >= 1 && i <= Number(c))) fail(`no occurrence ${k}`);
  out = parts.slice(0, i).join(o) + n + parts.slice(i).join(o);
} else if (mode === 'delnth') {
  const [start, end, k, c] = a;
  const lines = src.split('\n');
  const at = lines.flatMap((l, i) => (l.includes(start) ? [i] : []));
  if (at.length !== Number(c)) fail(`${JSON.stringify(start)} is on ${at.length} lines, not ${c}`);
  const s = at[Number(k) - 1];
  if (s === undefined) fail(`no line ${k}`);
  const e = lines.findIndex((l, i) => i >= s && l.includes(end));
  if (e < 0) fail(`no ${JSON.stringify(end)} at or after line ${s + 1}`);
  out = [...lines.slice(0, s), ...lines.slice(e + 1)].join('\n');
} else fail(`unknown mode ${mode}`);
fs.writeFileSync(file, out);
console.log(`mut: ${mode} applied to ${file}`);
EOF
```

**Drafter's corrections:**
1. **B1's straggler leaves after the wait's second ask of the tree.** The frame said "about 1 s after `$HOME/killed` appears". A timed exit can either outlive a correct wait or slip past a broken one before step (4): between the kill and step (4) come the tombstone read, owned, and the settle's git work. Keyed to the wait's own asks (logged by `CWD_LOG`), B-M1 and B-M2 red deterministically.
2. **The entering processes (`N2:`, `C2:`, `E1:`) run `exec sleep 60` with stdio on `/dev/null`, with no `setsid`.**
   - `h.run` is `execFileSync`, which waits for the snippet's pipes to close. So the background process must not hold them, and the redirect is what matters.
   - With `exec`, `$!` is the sleep's own pid. `afterEach` kills it only while its `/proc/<pid>/cwd` lies under the fixture HOME, so a recycled pid is never killed.
   - Each enters the tree in the foreground subshell BEFORE it forks (`( cd -- <dir> || exit 0; exec sleep 60 … & echo "$!" > … )`). The background child inherits that working directory at fork, so the next ask can never meet it still at the fixture HOME. With `cd … && exec … &` the `cd` itself ran in the background child, and nothing ordered it before the next ask: a load flake at `cwdFailed`. A `cd` that fails writes no `entered-pid`, so `enteredPid()`'s CONTROL reds.
3. **`E1:` plants its process at the tail's first act (`_ws_unsupervise`), not before the verb.** ws-expire's in-lock ladder asks rung 5 (`_ws_expire_cwd_users`) directly before the tail. A process planted before the verb is refused `in-use` there and never reaches the tail.
4. **`C5b:` is added, and C-M5 names `C5:` as its survivor.** `C5:`'s real unmeasured reason is short, clean ASCII, so "drop the cut" cannot red it. `C5b:` feeds a long, dirty reason through a wrapper that answers the tail only.
5. **C1 is split into `C1:` (no nested checkout: step (4)) and `C1b:` (a nested checkout standing: step (3)).** The frame's C1 sentence names both outcomes. C-M7 (step (3) asking `$cpath`) is added to pin R23's "against the child".
6. **B2 and B3 are unit cases, and B-M4 is added.**
   - B2 and B3 are `Q1:` to `Q5:` (B3 is `Q3:`, and "Darwin asks once" with a tree is `Q4:`). B2's one-argument suite is re-run unedited as a gate.
   - B-M4 pins `_WS_QUIET_TREE`. The tail itself reads it nowhere (`S3:`).
7. **The Darwin in-use row lists a live pid of its own.** `DARWIN_LSOF_STUB` lists only ccd's own process at `$HOME` (nobody), so `D1:` uses its own listing, in the ladder suite's `p…`/`n…` shape, naming a live `holdProc` pid at the tree's physical path.  *  row and the document carry one word and one detail. */
```ts
const stoppedAt = (r: Run, t: Subject, word: string, phase: string, why: string): Doc => {
  for (const f of ['f1.txt', 'f2.txt']) {
    expect(fs.existsSync(path.join(t.wt, f)), `the ${t.act}’s ${f} stands — ${r.stdout}`).toBe(true);

  h.sh(`${EXP_STUBS} _WS_RCL_ACT=expire; _ws_expire_eval ${EXP_ID} >/dev/null`
    + ` && _ws_reclaim_pin ${EXP_ID} "${a.wt}" "${a.main}" "$REAP_BRANCH" "$EXPIRE_ARCHIVED_AT"`
    + ` && _ws_tombstone ${EXP_ID} '[]' "$(_ws_reclaim_tomb_fields "$EXPIRE_ARCHIVED_AT" present)" >/dev/null`
    + ` && _reg_set ${EXP_ID} reaping expire:worktree`);
  expect(h.reg(EXP_ID, 'reaping'), 'the CONTROL: interrupted at `worktree`').toBe('expire:worktree');
  const tok = h.sh(`${EXP_STUBS} _WS_RCL_ACT=expire; _ws_expire_resume_eval ${EXP_ID} worktree >/dev/null; printf '%s' "$REAP_TOKEN"`);
  expect(tok, 'the CONTROL: the resume token').toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/);
  return tok;
};

describe('`_ws_reclaim_reask` itself, and the identity `_ws_reclaim_nested_proven` records (path-identity spec §4.7)', () => {
  interface Subj { c: Child; wd: string; wdid: string; mainid: string }
  const identOf = (p: string, follow = ''): string => h.sh(`_ws_path_ident "${p}" ${follow} && printf '%s' "$_WS_IDENT"`);
  /** The child, and its tree's and its project directory's identities as the tail records them. */
  const subject = (): Subj => {
    const c = makeChild(h);
    const wd = workdirOf(CHILD_ID);
    const wdid = identOf(wd);
    const mainid = identOf(c.main, 'follow');
    expect(wdid, 'the CONTROL: the tree measures').toMatch(IDENT);
    expect(mainid, 'the CONTROL: the project directory measures').toMatch(IDENT);
    return { c, wd, wdid, mainid };
  };
  /** One re-ask: its answer and its reason. */
  const reask = (s: Subj, wdid: string, mainid: string, o: { cpath?: string; cid?: string; pre?: string } = {}): string =>
    h.sh(`${o.pre ?? ''} _ws_reclaim_reask ${CHILD_ID} "${s.wd}" "${s.c.main}" "${wdid}" "${mainid}"`
      + `${o.cpath === undefined ? '' : ` "${o.cpath}" "${o.cid ?? ''}"`}; rc=$?;`
      + ` printf '[rc=%s] %s' "$rc" "\${_WS_REASK_WHY-<unset>}"`);
  /** `_ws_path_ident`, wrapped: logs every path the re-ask itself measures to `$HOME/reask-idents`. */
  const IDENT_SPY = 'eval "_t_pid_real()$(declare -f _ws_path_ident | tail -n +2)";'
    + ' _ws_path_ident() { [[ "${FUNCNAME[1]-}" != _ws_reclaim_reask ]] || printf \'%s\\n\' "$1" >> "$HOME/reask-idents"; _t_pid_real "$@"; };';
  /** One nested proof: its answer and the three globals it sets. */
  const proven = (c: Child, p: string, pre = ''): string =>
    h.sh(`${pre} r=$(cd "${c.wt}" && pwd -P); _ws_reclaim_nested_proven "$r" "${p}"; rc=$?;`
      + ` printf '[rc=%s] gone=%s ident=%s why=%s' "$rc" "$_WS_NPROOF_GONE" "\${_WS_NPROOF_IDENT-<unset>}" "$_WS_NPROOF_WHY"`);

  it('U0: the CONTROL: everything recorded still measures the same: 0', () => {
    const s = subject();
    expect(reask(s, s.wdid, s.mainid)).toBe('[rc=0]');
  }, 60_000);

  it('U1: a project directory that is no longer the one recorded: 2', () => {
    const s = subject();
    expect(reask(s, s.wdid, '1:1:-')).toBe(
      `[rc=2] the project directory is not the one the act proved when it began: ${s.c.main} measures ${s.mainid}, recorded 1:1:-`);
  }, 60_000);

  it('U2: no project-directory identity recorded: 2, never a match', () => {
    const s = subject();
    expect(reask(s, s.wdid, '')).toBe(
      `[rc=2] no identity of the project directory was recorded when the act began, so whether ${s.c.main} is still that directory was never asked`);
  }, 60_000);

  it('U3: a tree that is no longer the one recorded: 2', () => {
    const s = subject();
    expect(reask(s, '1:1:-', s.mainid)).toBe(
      `[rc=2] the tree is not the one the act proved when it began: ${s.wd} measures ${s.wdid}, recorded 1:1:-`);
  }, 60_000);

  it('U4: an EMPTY tree identity with the tree standing (the owned call proved it gone): 2, never a match', () => {
    const s = subject();
    expect(reask(s, '', s.mainid)).toBe(
      `[rc=2] a tree stands again where the act proved none when it began, at ${s.wd}, so it is not the tree the act proved`);
  }, 60_000);

  it('U5: the checkout: its recorded identity is 0, another is 2, an empty one is 2', () => {
    const s = subject();
    const realInner = fs.realpathSync(nested(s.c));
    const cid = identOf(realInner);
    expect(cid, 'the CONTROL: the checkout measures').toMatch(IDENT);
    expect(reask(s, s.wdid, s.mainid, { cpath: realInner, cid }), 'the CONTROL: the checkout proven').toBe('[rc=0]');
    expect(reask(s, s.wdid, s.mainid, { cpath: realInner, cid: '1:1:-' })).toBe(
      `[rc=2] the checkout is not the one proven inside the tree: ${realInner} measures ${cid}, recorded 1:1:-`);
    expect(reask(s, s.wdid, s.mainid, { cpath: realInner, cid: '' })).toBe(
      `[rc=2] no identity of the checkout was recorded when it was proven, so whether ${realInner} is still that checkout was never asked`);
  }, 60_000);

  it('U6: owned is asked first: its proof is 1 even when every measure would fail, and nothing was measured before it', () => {
    const s = subject();
    fs.writeFileSync(reg('demo-twin.uuid'), 'u-demo-twin');
    fs.writeFileSync(reg('demo-twin.workdir'), s.wd);
    expect(reask(s, s.wdid, s.mainid, { pre: `${IDENT_SPY} _plat_devino() { return 1; };` }))
      .toBe(`[rc=1] ${s.wd} is also named by registry row(s) demo-twin`);
    expect(linesIn('reask-idents'), 'no identity was measured before the proof').toEqual([]);
  }, 60_000);

  it('U7: a measure that fails is 2, never a pass', () => {
    const s = subject();
    const pre = 'eval "_t_pid_real()$(declare -f _ws_path_ident | tail -n +2)";'
      + ` _ws_path_ident() { if [[ "\${FUNCNAME[1]-}" == _ws_reclaim_reask && "$1" == "${s.wd}" ]]; then`
      + ` _WS_IDENT=''; _WS_IDENT_KIND=''; _WS_IDENT_WHY='stub: no stat'; return 2; fi; _t_pid_real "$@"; };`;
    expect(reask(s, s.wdid, s.mainid, { pre })).toBe(
      `[rc=2] the tree could not be measured again (stub: no stat), so whether ${s.wd} is still the one the act proved was never asked`);
  }, 60_000);

  it('NP1: a standing checkout’s proof records its identity', () => {
    const c = makeChild(h);
    const realInner = fs.realpathSync(nested(c));
    const cid = identOf(realInner);
    expect(cid, 'the CONTROL: the checkout measures').toMatch(IDENT);
    expect(proven(c, realInner)).toBe(`[rc=0] gone=0 ident=${cid} why=`);
  }, 60_000);

  it('NP2: a checkout PROVEN gone records no identity', () => {
    const c = makeChild(h);
    const realInner = fs.realpathSync(nested(c));
    fs.rmSync(realInner, { recursive: true, force: true });
    expect(proven(c, realInner)).toBe('[rc=0] gone=1 ident= why=');
  }, 60_000);

  it('NP3: a checkout whose identity cannot be measured is 1, never proven', () => {
    const c = makeChild(h);
    const realInner = fs.realpathSync(nested(c));
    const out = proven(c, realInner, '_plat_btime() { echo x; };');
    expect(out.startsWith(`[rc=1] gone=0 ident= why=the checkout at ${realInner} could not be measured by device and inode (`), out).toBe(true);
  }, 60_000);

  it('NP4: an identity left by an earlier proof is cleared at entry', () => {
    const c = makeChild(h);
    const realInner = fs.realpathSync(nested(c));
    const lnk = path.join(fs.realpathSync(c.wt), 'lnk');
    fs.symlinkSync(realInner, lnk);
    const first = `r=$(cd "${c.wt}" && pwd -P); _ws_reclaim_nested_proven "$r" "${realInner}" || exit 9;`;
    expect(proven(c, lnk, first)).toBe(
      `[rc=1] gone=0 ident= why=${lnk} is a symbolic link — ccd never follows a link to a tree it would remove`);
  }, 60_000);
});

describe('the re-asks, read from the source (path-identity spec §4.7)', () => {
  const src = (): string => fs.readFileSync(CCD, 'utf8');
  /** Code lines: whole-line comments dropped, `\`-continuations joined (the six-calls census's reading), blanks dropped. */
  const codeOf = (body: string): string[] => body.split('\n').filter((l) => !/^\s*#/.test(l)).join('\n')
    .replace(/\s*\\\n\s*/g, ' ').split('\n').filter((l) => l.trim() !== '');
  const fn = (name: string): string => {
    const s = src();
    const at = s.indexOf(`\n${name}() {`);
    expect(at, `the CONTROL: ${name} is defined`).toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    return s.slice(at, s.indexOf('\n}\n', at) + 2);
  };
  const tailCode = (): string[] => {
    const s = src();
    const tail = s.slice(s.indexOf('\n_ws_reclaim_tail() {'), s.indexOf('\ncmd_ws_reclaim() {'));
    expect(tail.length, 'the CONTROL: the tail was found').toBeGreaterThan(1000);
    return codeOf(tail);
  };
  const SITES = /_ws_reclaim_reask |_ws_cwd_users "\$workdir"; cwrc=|_ws_removal_mounts_clear|_ws_reclaim_keep_of "\$main" "\$id" tree "\$(cpath|workdir)"(?! 1)|worktree remove --force/;
  const label = (l: string): string => {
    if (/_ws_reclaim_reask /.test(l)) return /"\$cpath" "\$cid"/.test(l) ? 'reask cpath' : 'reask workdir';
    if (/_ws_cwd_users "\$workdir"; cwrc=/.test(l)) return 'cwd';
    let m = /_ws_removal_mounts_clear "\$(\w+)"( resolve)?/.exec(l);
    if (m) return `mounts ${m[1]}${m[2] ?? ''}`;
    m = /_ws_reclaim_keep_of "\$main" "\$id" tree "\$(\w+)"/.exec(l);
    if (m) return `keep ${m[1]}`;
    m = /worktree remove --force "\$(\w+)"/.exec(l);
    if (m) return `remove ${m[1]}`;
    return `unlabelled: ${l.trim()}`;
  };

  it('SRC1: in order at each standing site: cwd, re-ask, mounts, keep_of; then cwd, re-ask, mounts, the forced removal', () => {
    expect(tailCode().filter((l) => SITES.test(l)).map(label)).toEqual([
      'cwd', 'reask cpath', 'mounts cpath', 'keep cpath', 'cwd', 'reask cpath', 'mounts cpath', 'remove cpath',
      'cwd', 'reask workdir', 'mounts workdir resolve', 'keep workdir',
      'cwd', 'reask workdir', 'mounts workdir resolve', 'remove workdir',
    ]);
  });

  it('SRC2: each re-ask follows the cwd ask and its map, and is its call and its two cut maps, then the mount ask of its own path', () => {
    const code = tailCode();
    const at = code.flatMap((l, i) => (/_ws_reclaim_reask /.test(l) ? [i] : []));
    expect(at.length, 'four re-asks in the tail').toBe(4);
    for (const i of at) {
      const call = code[i]!.trim();
      expect(call).toMatch(/^_ws_reclaim_reask "\$id" "\$workdir" "\$main" "\$wdid" "\$mainid"( "\$cpath" "\$cid")?; rarc=\$\?$/);
      const cp = call.includes('"$cpath" "$cid"');
      const what = cp ? 'the checkout at $cpath' : 'the tree at $workdir';
      expect(code[i + 1]!.trim(), 'the proof map').toBe('(( rarc != 1 )) || { _ws_reclaim_fail "$id" "$lctx" containment-refuted'
        + ` "$(_ws_leaf_why_line "$_WS_REASK_WHY") — ${what} stands; the session was stopped, nothing further was deleted,`
        + ' and a retry finds the same until that tree or row is moved or removed"; return 1; }');
      expect(code[i + 2]!.trim(), 'the unasked map').toBe('(( rarc == 0 )) || { _ws_reclaim_fail "$id" "$lctx" worktree-remove-failed'
        + ` "$(_ws_leaf_why_line "$_WS_REASK_WHY") — ${what} stands, and nothing further was deleted"; return 1; }`);
      expect(code[i - 2]!.trim(), 'after the working-directory probe').toBe('_ws_cwd_users "$workdir"; cwrc=$?');
      expect(code[i - 1]!.trim(), 'and its map').toMatch(/^\(\( cwrc == 0 \)\) \|\| \{/);
      expect(code[i + 3]!.trim(), 'then the mount question, of the same path')
        .toMatch(cp ? /^_ws_removal_mounts_clear "\$cpath" \|\|/ : /^_ws_removal_mounts_clear "\$workdir" resolve \|\|/);
    }
  });

  it('SRC3: no re-ask line spells git, and no vanished arm holds a re-ask', () => {
    const code = tailCode();
    expect(code.filter((l) => /_ws_reclaim_reask /.test(l)).length, 'the CONTROL: four re-asks to look at').toBe(4);
    expect(code.filter((l) => /_ws_reclaim_reask |_WS_REASK_WHY/.test(l) && /\bgit\b/.test(l)), 'a re-ask line that spells git').toEqual([]);
    const vanished = code.flatMap((l, i) => (/_ws_reclaim_keep_of "\$main" "\$id" tree "\$(cpath|workdir)" 1 /.test(l) ? [i] : []));
    expect(vanished.length, 'the CONTROL: the two vanished arms').toBe(2);
    for (const i of vanished) {
      expect(code.slice(Math.max(0, i - 6), i).filter((l) => /_ws_reclaim_reask /.test(l)),
        `before ${code[i]!.trim().slice(0, 70)}`).toEqual([]);
    }
  });

  it('SRC4: `_ws_reclaim_reask` is defined between `_ws_reclaim_nested_record` and `_ws_reclaim_kept_read`, before the tail', () => {
    const s = src();
    const at = ['_ws_reclaim_nested_record', '_ws_reclaim_reask', '_ws_reclaim_kept_read', '_ws_reclaim_tail']
      .map((n) => s.indexOf(`\n${n}() {`));
    expect(at.every((x) => x > -1), at.join(',')).toBe(true);
    expect([...at].sort((a, b) => a - b)).toEqual(at);
  });

  it('SRC5: `_ws_reclaim_reask` asks `_ws_reclaim_owned` once, before any measure, and asks neither the cwd probe nor git', () => {
    const code = codeOf(fn('_ws_reclaim_reask'));
    const owned = code.flatMap((l, i) => (/_ws_reclaim_owned /.test(l) ? [i] : []));
    expect(owned.length, 'one owned call').toBe(1);
    const firstIdent = code.findIndex((l) => /_ws_path_ident /.test(l));
    expect(firstIdent, 'the CONTROL: it measures').toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(owned[0]!, 'owned is asked before the first measure').toBeLessThan(firstIdent);
    expect(code.filter((l) => /_ws_cwd_users|\bgit\b/.test(l)), 'a cwd ask or a git call inside the re-ask').toEqual([]);
  });

  it('SRC6: the tail records the identities once: the tree’s and the project directory’s at the owned call, the checkout’s at its proof', () => {
    const code = tailCode().map((l) => l.trim());
    const o = code.indexOf('_ws_reclaim_owned "$id" "$workdir" "$main"; orc=$?');
    expect(o, 'the owned call').toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(code.slice(o + 1, o + 3)).toEqual(['case "$orc" in', '0) wdid="$_WS_OWNED_WDID"; mainid="$_WS_OWNED_MAINID" ;;']);
    const p = code.indexOf('if ! _ws_reclaim_nested_proven "$wdreal" "$cpath"; then');
    expect(p, 'the nested proof').toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(code[code.indexOf('fi', p) + 1], 'the checkout’s identity, directly after its proof').toBe('cid="$_WS_NPROOF_IDENT"');
    expect(code.filter((l) => /(^|[\s;])(wdid|mainid|cid)=/.test(l)), 'assigned nowhere else').toEqual([
      "local wdid='' mainid='' cid='' rarc", '0) wdid="$_WS_OWNED_WDID"; mainid="$_WS_OWNED_MAINID" ;;', 'cid="$_WS_NPROOF_IDENT"']);
  });
});
```

**3a. The texts, as files** (one Bash call; every heredoc is quoted, so nothing in it expands):

```bash
T=.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-20-path-identity-w3-worktree-identity/task11; mkdir -p "$T"
cat > "$T/np-sig.new" <<'EOF'
  #                                  (_WS_NPROOF_GONE=1: it no longer exists; otherwise _WS_NPROOF_IDENT, the
  #                                  identity of the checkout that stands); 1 (_WS_NPROOF_WHY) when not
EOF
cat > "$T/np-header.add" <<'EOF'
  # AND ITS IDENTITY IS RECORDED HERE (path-identity spec §4.7). A checkout
  # that stands is measured once it has resolved to itself (`_ws_path_ident`:
  # its parent resolved, its leaf never followed), and `_WS_NPROOF_IDENT`
  # carries that identity ('' on GONE and on 1) for `_ws_reclaim_reask` to
  # compare directly before the checkout's keep and again directly before its
  # forced removal. A measure that fails is 1, never a pass: what was not
  # measured is never an identity.
EOF
cat > "$T/np-measure.add" <<'EOF'
  _ws_path_ident "$p" || { _WS_NPROOF_WHY="the checkout at $p could not be measured by device and inode (${_WS_IDENT_WHY:-it reads as $_WS_IDENT_KIND})"; return 1; }
  _WS_NPROOF_IDENT="$_WS_IDENT"
EOF
cat > "$T/reask.sh" <<'EOF'
# ── the tail's re-ask before every standing forced removal (path-identity spec §4.7) ──
_WS_REASK_WHY=''
_ws_reclaim_reask() {   # id workdir main wdid mainid [cpath cid] -> 0 nothing refuses; 1 (_WS_REASK_WHY)
  #                        `_ws_reclaim_owned` PROVED the tree is not only the child's own; 2 (_WS_REASK_WHY) anything
  #                        else. In order, each fresh, nothing cached: (1) `_ws_reclaim_owned` whole, 1 -> 1, any other
  #                        non-zero -> 2; (2) `_ws_path_ident "$main" follow` against mainid, `_ws_path_ident "$workdir"`
  #                        against wdid (an EMPTY wdid with the tree standing is `reappeared-tree-refuses`), and with
  #                        cpath, `_ws_path_ident "$cpath"` against cid. An empty recorded value, `_ws_ident_eq` 1 or 2,
  #                        or a measure that is not 0 -> 2
  # THE WINDOW BEFORE A FORCED REMOVAL, NARROWED (path-identity spec §4.7).
  # `_ws_reclaim_tail` asks `_ws_reclaim_owned` once, before the settle, and the
  # settle and the nested steps run after it. Before this re-ask, none of these
  # was asked again before `git worktree remove --force`: a row another
  # session's start writes inside the child; an ancestor re-pointed; a checkout
  # or the child swapped for a copy; the project directory re-pointed; or a tree
  # that stands again after the owned call proved it gone. So the tail asks this
  # before each standing nested checkout's and the child's
  # `_ws_reclaim_keep_of`, and again before each forced removal, each time
  # directly before the site's mount question, and stops on any answer but 0.
  # - OWNED, WHOLE AND FRESH. The registry is re-listed and every row re-read,
  #   with one new identity walk and one new read of the mount table
  #   (`_ws_reclaim_workdir_shared` keeps its maps for one call only); the
  #   record and the main checkout are asked again. Nothing an earlier call
  #   answered is read. Its 1 is a PROOF and stays 1, which the tail prints
  #   `containment-refuted`; its 2, a question not asked (a walk that ran out
  #   of its bound included), stays 2.
  # - THEN THE IDENTITIES THE ACT RECORDED, each measured again as it was first
  #   measured (`_ws_path_ident`: a tree's parent resolved and its leaf never
  #   followed; the project directory followed whole, as `git -C` follows it),
  #   and compared by `_ws_ident_eq` (device and inode, and the birth times
  #   where both carry one). Owned comes first, so a proof is never pre-empted
  #   by a measure that failed. An EMPTY recorded value matches nothing: for the
  #   tree it means the owned call proved it gone, so a tree that stands at a
  #   removal now is not the tree the act proved (`reappeared-tree-refuses`).
  # - NOT HERE: the working-directory probe (`_ws_cwd_users`) is the site's own
  #   line, asked directly BEFORE this one, so its bounded walk of the process
  #   table never sits between the last compare here and the removal. The
  #   mount question (`_ws_removal_mounts_clear`) comes directly after this
  #   one. Owned's own read of the mount table catches a mount under the child
  #   first, so the mount question is the backstop for one that appears after
  #   it (`w2-mount-asks-shadowed-by-the-reask`).
  # - STATED, NOT PREVENTED. The identities are per attempt: a resumed attempt
  #   records them again at its own owned call (`reask-identity-is-per-attempt`).
  #   The window from the last compare here, through the mount question's
  #   read of the table, to git's own opendir stays (`reask-to-opendir-window`).
  #   Each re-ask's walk is bounded
  #   (`WS_RECLAIM_WALK_S`), but its git reads are not
  #   (`rows-rung-git-reads-unbounded`, and owned's own worktree list, as
  #   before). An act makes two re-asks per standing tree, so together they can
  #   outrun the runner's act row. A kill there lands at a step the breadcrumb
  #   resumes, and the next attempt re-proves from its start
  #   (`tail-reasks-can-outrun-the-act-row`).
  local id="$1" wd="$2" main="$3" wdid="$4" mainid="$5" cpath="${6-}" cid="${7-}" rc
  _WS_REASK_WHY=''
  _ws_reclaim_owned "$id" "$wd" "$main"; rc=$?
  (( rc != 1 )) || { _WS_REASK_WHY="$_WS_OWNED_WHY"; return 1; }
  (( rc == 0 )) || { _WS_REASK_WHY="${_WS_OWNED_WHY:-the containment check answered $rc, an answer it never gives, so whether $wd is still owned by the child was never asked}"; return 2; }
  [[ -n "$mainid" ]] || { _WS_REASK_WHY="no identity of the project directory was recorded when the act began, so whether $main is still that directory was never asked"; return 2; }
  _ws_path_ident "$main" follow || { _WS_REASK_WHY="the project directory could not be measured again (${_WS_IDENT_WHY:-it reads as $_WS_IDENT_KIND}), so whether $main is still the one the act proved was never asked"; return 2; }
  _ws_ident_eq "$_WS_IDENT" "$mainid" || { _WS_REASK_WHY="the project directory is not the one the act proved when it began: $main measures $_WS_IDENT, recorded $mainid"; return 2; }
  [[ -n "$wdid" ]] || { _WS_REASK_WHY="a tree stands again where the act proved none when it began, at $wd, so it is not the tree the act proved"; return 2; }
  _ws_path_ident "$wd" || { _WS_REASK_WHY="the tree could not be measured again (${_WS_IDENT_WHY:-it reads as $_WS_IDENT_KIND}), so whether $wd is still the one the act proved was never asked"; return 2; }
  _ws_ident_eq "$_WS_IDENT" "$wdid" || { _WS_REASK_WHY="the tree is not the one the act proved when it began: $wd measures $_WS_IDENT, recorded $wdid"; return 2; }
  [[ -n "$cpath" ]] || return 0
  [[ -n "$cid" ]] || { _WS_REASK_WHY="no identity of the checkout was recorded when it was proven, so whether $cpath is still that checkout was never asked"; return 2; }
  _ws_path_ident "$cpath" || { _WS_REASK_WHY="the checkout could not be measured again (${_WS_IDENT_WHY:-it reads as $_WS_IDENT_KIND}), so whether $cpath is still the one proven inside the tree was never asked"; return 2; }
  _ws_ident_eq "$_WS_IDENT" "$cid" || { _WS_REASK_WHY="the checkout is not the one proven inside the tree: $cpath measures $_WS_IDENT, recorded $cid"; return 2; }
  return 0
}
EOF
cat > "$T/owned-header.add" <<'EOF'
  #
  # ASKED AT THE ACT'S START, AND AGAIN BEFORE EVERY STANDING FORCED REMOVAL
  # (path-identity spec §4.7). `_ws_reclaim_tail` asks it once, before the
  # settle, and `_ws_reclaim_reask` asks it again, whole, directly before each
  # standing nested checkout's and the child's keep and again before each
  # forced removal. Each call re-lists the registry, re-reads every row and
  # makes its own identity walk and its own read of the mount table; nothing
  # an earlier call answered is read. The two identities it measures last are
  # what the tail records from its first call, and what each re-ask compares
  # its own fresh measures with.
EOF
cat > "$T/tail-owned-para.old" <<'EOF'
  # THE TREE IS RE-PROVEN THE CHILD'S OWN (spec §5.5, §5.6) — on a resumed arm
  # the only identity check there is — and a refusal says how it was reached. A

EOF
cat > "$T/tail-owned-para.new" <<'EOF'
  # THE TREE IS RE-PROVEN THE CHILD'S OWN (spec §5.5, §5.6) — asked here, at
  # the act's start, and again before every standing forced removal
  # (`_ws_reclaim_reask`, path-identity spec §4.7) — and a refusal says how it
  # was reached. A PROOF that it is not (rc 1) is `containment-refuted`, from
  # this call site and from each re-ask's: a retry meets the same thing until
  # the other tree or row is moved or removed. A question that could not be

  # always stopped: the unit stopped and the pane killed, the tombstone and the
  # breadcrumb standing, nothing further deleted, and no step after this one
  # run. On 0, the two identities this call measured are recorded, once, for
  # every re-ask to compare: the tree's ('' when it was proven gone) and the
  # project directory's.
EOF
cat > "$T/step3-header.add" <<'EOF'
  # AND EACH STANDING CHECKOUT IS RE-PROVEN FIRST (path-identity spec §4.7).
  # Before its `_ws_reclaim_keep_of`, and again before its forced removal,
  # each time after the working-directory probe and directly before the
  # mount question, `_ws_reclaim_reask` asks `_ws_reclaim_owned` whole and
  # fresh, then compares the project directory, the child's tree and the
  # checkout with the identities the act recorded: the checkout's as
  # `_ws_reclaim_nested_proven` proved it in this iteration (`cid`). Owned's
  # proof fails `containment-refuted`; anything else fails
  # `worktree-remove-failed`; either leaves the breadcrumb and the checkout
  # standing, and both reasons are cut to one journal line
  # (`_ws_leaf_why_line`). The probe stands before it, so the probe's bounded
  # walk stays outside the window the re-ask narrows. Like the tail's owned
  # call, each re-ask asks the rows rung's mount hold of the child's whole
  # tree again. A checkout PROVEN gone takes no re-ask.
EOF
cat > "$T/step4-header.add" <<'EOF'
  # AND THE TREE IS RE-PROVEN FIRST (path-identity spec §4.7), as step (3)
  # re-proves each standing checkout: inside the `-d` arm, after the link
  # test, `_ws_reclaim_reask` runs before the tree's `_ws_reclaim_keep_of` and
  # again before its forced removal, each time after the working-directory
  # probe and directly before the mount question. A tree the owned
  # call proved gone, which stands here again, is refused
  # (`reappeared-tree-refuses`): it is not the tree the act proved. A tree
  # PROVEN gone takes no re-ask.
EOF
cat > "$T/site-cpath.add" <<'EOF'
_ws_reclaim_reask "$id" "$workdir" "$main" "$wdid" "$mainid" "$cpath" "$cid"; rarc=$?
(( rarc != 1 )) || { _ws_reclaim_fail "$id" "$lctx" containment-refuted "$(_ws_leaf_why_line "$_WS_REASK_WHY") — the checkout at $cpath stands; the session was stopped, nothing further was deleted, and a retry finds the same until that tree or row is moved or removed"; return 1; }
(( rarc == 0 )) || { _ws_reclaim_fail "$id" "$lctx" worktree-remove-failed "$(_ws_leaf_why_line "$_WS_REASK_WHY") — the checkout at $cpath stands, and nothing further was deleted"; return 1; }
EOF
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Mutation table**

First, one Bash call. It copies the restamped `ccd/ccd` and writes the one-mutation helper:

```bash
T=.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-20-path-identity-w3-worktree-identity/task11; cp ccd/ccd "$T/ccd.task11" && cat > "$T/mut.mjs" <<'EOF'
// One exact mutation of one file, refused (exit 3, nothing written) unless every anchor matches as stated.
//   sub FILE OLD NEW                            replace the ONE occurrence of OLD
//   suball FILE OLD NEW N                       replace every occurrence of OLD; there must be exactly N
//   del FILE NEEDLE...                          delete each ONE line holding NEEDLE
//   delnth FILE NEEDLE NTH TOTAL COUNT          of exactly TOTAL lines holding NEEDLE, delete COUNT lines from the NTH
//   moventh FILE NEEDLE NTH TOTAL COUNT BEFORE  as delnth, then put those lines directly above the ONE line holding BEFORE
//   range FILE START END NEW                    replace the ONE line holding START, through the first line from there
//                                               holding END, with the one line NEW
import fs from 'node:fs';
const [mode, file, ...a] = process.argv.slice(2);
const fail = (m) => { console.error(`mut: ${m}`); process.exit(3); };
const src = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
const L = src.split('\n');
const holders = (n) => L.flatMap((l, i) => (l.includes(n) ? [i] : []));
const one = (n) => { const h = holders(n); if (h.length !== 1) fail(`${JSON.stringify(n)} is on ${h.length} lines, not one`); return h[0]; };
let out;
if (mode === 'sub') {
  const [o, n] = a; const k = src.split(o).length - 1;
  if (k !== 1) fail(`${JSON.stringify(o)} occurs ${k} times, not once`);
  out = src.replace(o, () => n);
} else if (mode === 'suball') {
  const [o, n, c] = a; const k = src.split(o).length - 1;
  if (k !== Number(c)) fail(`${JSON.stringify(o)} occurs ${k} times, not ${c}`);
  out = src.split(o).join(n);
} else if (mode === 'del') {
  const drop = new Set(a.map(one)); out = L.filter((_, i) => !drop.has(i)).join('\n');
} else if (mode === 'delnth' || mode === 'moventh') {
  const [n, nth, total, count, before] = a; const h = holders(n);
  if (h.length !== Number(total)) fail(`${JSON.stringify(n)} is on ${h.length} lines, not ${total}`);
  const cut = L.splice(h[Number(nth) - 1], Number(count));
  if (mode === 'moventh') L.splice(one(before), 0, ...cut);
  out = L.join('\n');
} else if (mode === 'range') {
  const [start, end, n] = a; const s = one(start);
  const e = L.findIndex((l, i) => i >= s && l.includes(end));
  if (e < 0) fail(`no ${JSON.stringify(end)} at or after line ${s + 1}`);
  out = [...L.slice(0, s), n, ...L.slice(e + 1)].join('\n');
} else fail(`unknown mode ${mode}`);
fs.writeFileSync(file, out);
console.log(`mut: ${mode} applied to ${file}`);
EOF
echo ready
```

The sentence goes at the end of the bullet, directly above `- **What CI runs**`, wrapped at 118 columns with the bullet's two-space indent.

Run the script with the worst case from Step 5, rounded up to the next 10 s; it refuses any other number. `<N>` is that number, for example `60`.

```bash
T=.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-20-path-identity-w3-worktree-identity/task11; cat > "$T/claude11.mjs" <<'EOF'
// Appends Task 11's sentence to CLAUDE.md's "Known load flakes" bullet, wrapped at the bullet's width.
import fs from 'node:fs';
const n = process.argv[2] ?? '';
if (!/^[1-9][0-9]*0$/.test(n)) { console.error('claude11: give the measured worst case, rounded up to ten seconds'); process.exit(3); }
const S = '`ccd-reclaim-tail-window` (path-identity W3) runs the real reclaim and expire verbs end to end on git fixtures,'
  + " with the tail's real `/proc` walks (its post-kill wait, and the working-directory probe before every standing forced"
  + ` removal), at about ${n} s a case at worst, so under load it fails as vitest's \`Test timed out in <n>ms\`, or as a`
  + ' `worktree-remove-failed` whose detail says a walk did not finish within its bound; any other red is a real break,'
  + ' so re-run the file alone first.';
const f = 'CLAUDE.md';
const L = fs.readFileSync(f, 'utf8').split('\n');
if (L.join('\n').includes('`ccd-reclaim-tail-window`')) { console.error('claude11: the sentence is already there'); process.exit(3); }
const at = L.flatMap((l, i) => (l.startsWith('- **What CI runs**') ? [i] : []));
if (at.length !== 1) { console.error(`claude11: ${at.length} "What CI runs" bullets, not 1`); process.exit(3); }
const last = at[0] - 1;
if (!/^  \S/.test(L[last])) { console.error("claude11: the line above is not the flake bullet's continuation"); process.exit(3); }
const out = []; let cur = '  ';
for (const w of `${L[last].trim()} ${S}`.split(' ')) {
  const next = cur.trim() ? `${cur} ${w}` : `${cur}${w}`;
  if (next.length > 118 && cur.trim()) { out.push(cur); cur = `  ${w}`; } else cur = next;
}
out.push(cur);
L.splice(last, 1, ...out);
fs.writeFileSync(f, L.join('\n'));
console.log(`claude11: ${out.length} lines`);
EOF
node "$T/claude11.mjs" <N>
grep -c 'ccd-reclaim-tail-window' CLAUDE.md                                                      # 1
git diff -U0 -- CLAUDE.md | grep -c '^@@'                                                        # 1: one hunk, inside the flake bullet
```

```ts
// Path identity W3 (PI7 P1, R16): the rows rung's wordings are true (path-identity spec §4.8).
// - Its two `//` remedies asked the operator to "re-point" a link. Replacing a link is how a spelling is moved off the
//   tree a session entered, so a hold must never invite it. Both now say: restore the link to its original target, or
//   stop the session and purge its row; never replace a link to clear this.
// - Its `..` detail said a `..` "follows a directory that no longer exists, or cannot otherwise be placed", which reads
//   as "outside"; but a pane that entered through that `..` while its path stood still works in the tree it named,
//   which may be this child. It now says the `..` could not be walked the way that session's own `cd` walked it, so
//   where it leads was never placed, even if it names this child.
// - The fail-shut order that makes such a row unresolvable is kept: `_ws_reclaim_resolve` refuses a `..` in the
//   unresolved rest BEFORE it re-walks a `..` in the entered head (the reverse order was reverted after a measured
//   bypass). It is pinned here by source.
// The pinned prefixes elsewhere (`ccd-child-reclaim-hardening`, `ccd-child-reclaim-verb-tail`, and
// `ccd-child-reclaim-ladder`'s `UNPLACED`) end before each remedy, so they stand unedited.
// FIXTURE HOME ONLY (`makePrHarness`): every child, row and link lives under the harness's HOME, and ccd runs as
// sourced functions. No case runs a verb or a tail, so nothing here walks `/proc`. Every spelling holding `..` is built
// by concatenation: `path.join` would normalise away the very input under test.
import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { makePrHarness, type PrHarness } from './ccdPrHelpers.js';
import { CCD } from './ccdWsHelpers.js';
import { CHILD_ID, evalOf, makeChild, type Child } from './childReclaimFixture.js';

let h: PrHarness;
beforeEach(() => { h = makePrHarness('ccrc-worktree-identity-wordings-'); });
afterEach(() => { h.cleanup(); });

/** Remedy 1: the child's OWN workdir resolves to `//` (`_ws_reclaim_workdir_shared`'s `minewhy`). */
const REMEDY_1 = '— restore the link whose target opens with // to its original target, or stop the session and purge its'
  + ' row; never replace a link to clear this';
/** Remedy 2: another row names no plain absolute workdir, or one that resolves to `//` (the `unplaced` clause). */
const REMEDY_2 = '— stop and restart each (ccd start <id> stores a plain absolute workdir), restore a link whose target opens'
  + ' with // to its original target, or stop that session and purge its row; never replace a link to clear this';
const UNPLACED = 'name no plain absolute workdir, or one that resolves to a path opening with //, so ccd cannot place them'
  + ' against this child';
const DOTDOT_CLAUSE = 'a \'..\' in it could not be walked the way that session\'s own cd walked it (it follows a directory that'
  + ' does not exist now, or a path ccd could not enter logically), so where it leads was never placed, even if it names this child';
const OLD_DOTDOT = 'a \'..\' in it follows a directory that no longer exists, or cannot otherwise be placed';
const UNRESOLVED = 'name a workdir that cannot be resolved completely (a directory or link on its path cannot be entered'
  + ' or followed, or no longer exists, so its spelling no longer says where that session lives;'
  + ` ${DOTDOT_CLAUSE}; or it holds a control character), so ccd cannot place them against this child`;

/** A registry row of another session, naming `workdir`, with no entry field (a legacy row). */
const otherRowOf = (id: string, workdir: string): void => {
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(h.home, '.cc-sessions', `${id}.uuid`), `u-${id}`);
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(h.home, '.cc-sessions', `${id}.workdir`), workdir);
};

/** `$HOME/worktrees` moved to `$HOME/wtreal` and replaced by a link whose target opens with `//`, so the child's own
 *  workdir resolves to a `//` spelling wherever bash's `pwd -P` keeps it (Linux, measured). Answers whether the
 *  rung's resolver kept it: read, never assumed. */
const relinkChild = (c: Child): boolean => {
  fs.renameSync(path.join(h.home, 'worktrees'), path.join(h.home, 'wtreal'));
  fs.symlinkSync(`/${path.join(h.home, 'wtreal')}`, path.join(h.home, 'worktrees'));
  return h.sh(`_ws_reclaim_resolve "${c.wt}"; printf '%s' "$_WS_RESOLVED"`).startsWith('//');
};

/** `$HOME/lnk -> $HOME/elsewhere/sub`, with `$HOME/elsewhere/gone` standing: below `lnk/..` the kernel's walk continues
 *  in `elsewhere`, and a logical `cd` in `$HOME` (`ccd-child-reclaim-ladder.test.ts`'s shape). */
const plantLinkedPrefix = (): void => {
  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(h.home, 'elsewhere', 'sub'), { recursive: true });
  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(h.home, 'elsewhere', 'gone'));
  fs.symlinkSync(path.join(h.home, 'elsewhere', 'sub'), path.join(h.home, 'lnk'));
};

/** The two ways a `..` row stops resolving once `$HOME/gone` goes, one per refusal path of `_ws_reclaim_resolve`. */
const DOTDOT_SHAPES: ReadonlyArray<[string, (c: Child) => string]> = [
  ['`$HOME/gone/../<child>`: the unresolved rest holds a `..` below a directory that is gone',
    (c) => `${h.home}/gone/../${path.relative(h.home, c.wt)}`],
  ['`<lnk>/../gone/../<child>`: the logical entry of the head cannot be made',
    (c) => { plantLinkedPrefix(); return `${h.home}/lnk/../gone/../${path.relative(h.home, c.wt)}`; }],
];

/** A shell function's text, from `NAME() {` to the first line that is `}` alone; '' when there is none
 *  (`path-identity-w2-prose.test.ts`'s helper). */
function shFunction(src: string, name: string): string {
  const at = src.indexOf(`\n${name}() {`);
  if (at < 0) return '';
  const end = src.indexOf('\n}\n', at + 1);
  return end < 0 ? '' : src.slice(at + 1, end + 2);
}

/** A function's code. Its first line (the name and its header comment) is dropped, and so is every blank line and
 *  every whole-line `#` comment. Each remaining line's trailing ` #` comment is cut. */
function codeLines(fn: string): string[] {
  return fn.split('\n').slice(1).map((l) => l.split(' #')[0])
    .filter((l) => l.trim() !== '' && !l.trimStart().startsWith('#'));
}

const occurrences = (hay: string, needle: string): number => hay.split(needle).length - 1;

describe('the `//` remedies say restore a link, never re-point one (path-identity spec §4.8, R16)', () => {
  it('a row spelled `//`: unplaced, and its remedy says restore the link or stop that session and purge its row', () => {
    makeChild(h);
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(h.home, 'elsewhere'));
    expect(evalOf(h).verdict, 'the CONTROL: without the row').toBe('reclaimable');
    const row = `/${path.join(h.home, 'elsewhere')}`;
    otherRowOf('demo-dsrow', row);
    const r = evalOf(h);
    expect(r.verdict, r.detail).toBe('unmeasured');
    expect(r.token).toBe('');
    expect(r.detail).toContain(`registry row(s) demo-dsrow ${UNPLACED} ${REMEDY_2}`);
    expect(r.detail, 'no remedy invites re-pointing').not.toContain('re-point');
    expect(r.detail, 'the value is never printed').not.toContain(row);
  }, 60_000);

  it('a CHILD whose own workdir resolves to `//`: another row cannot be placed, and the remedy says restore the link', (ctx) => {
    const c = makeChild(h);
    fs.mkdirSync(path.join(h.home, 'elsewhere'));
    const kept = relinkChild(c);
    if (process.platform !== 'darwin') expect(kept, 'the CONTROL: bash keeps the link target’s leading `//` here').toBe(true);
    if (!kept) { ctx.skip(); return; }
    otherRowOf('demo-outside', path.join(h.home, 'elsewhere'));
    const r = evalOf(h);
    expect(r.verdict, r.detail).toBe('unmeasured');
    expect(r.token).toBe('');
    expect(r.detail).toContain(`registry row(s) demo-outside cannot be placed against this child: ${CHILD_ID}'s own workdir`
      + ` resolves to a path opening with //, so ccd cannot compare another row with it ${REMEDY_1}`);
    expect(r.detail, 'no remedy invites re-pointing').not.toContain('re-point');
  }, 60_000);
});

describe('the `..` detail is true of a row that is the child (path-identity spec §4.8, R16)', () => {
  it.each(DOTDOT_SHAPES)('%s: while `gone` stands the row IS the child (the CONTROL); once it goes, unmeasured, and the detail says where it leads was never placed', (_what, spell) => {

    expect(shared.detail).toContain('is also named by registry row(s) demo-dotdot');

describe('the source: no remedy invites re-pointing, and the fail-shut order stands (path-identity spec §4.8)', () => {
  it('`_ws_reclaim_workdir_shared`’s code says "re-point" nowhere, and each new wording exactly once', () => {
    const fn = shFunction(fs.readFileSync(CCD, 'utf8'), '_ws_reclaim_workdir_shared');

  });
});
```

```bash
// Task 12's mutations of ccd/ccd. Each replaces ONE exact text, and is refused unless that text occurs exactly once.
//   node mut12.mjs FILE T12.1|T12.2|T12.3|T12.4
import fs from 'node:fs';
const [file, row] = process.argv.slice(2);
const REST = '  case "/$rest/" in */../*) return 1 ;; esac';
const HEAD = '  case "/$head/" in */../*) _ws_reclaim_resolve "${real%/}/$rest"; return ;; esac';
const ROWS = {
  'T12.1': [' — restore the link whose target opens with // to its original target, or stop the session and purge its row; never replace a link to clear this"',
            ' — re-point the link whose target opens with //"'],
  'T12.2': ['restore a link whose target opens with // to its original target, or stop that session and purge its row; never replace a link to clear this"',

            "a '..' in it follows a directory that no longer exists, or cannot otherwise be placed;"],
  'T12.4': [REST + '\n' + HEAD, HEAD + '\n' + REST],
};
const pair = ROWS[row];
if (!pair) { console.error(`mut12: unknown row ${row}`); process.exit(3); }
const src = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
const k = src.split(pair[0]).length - 1;
if (k !== 1) { console.error(`mut12: ${row}'s anchor occurs ${k} times, not once`); process.exit(3); }
fs.writeFileSync(file, src.replace(pair[0], () => pair[1]));
console.log(`mut12: ${row} applied to ${file}`);
EOF
```
