- [ ] **Step 1: Write the prose test first:** `server/test/path-identity-w3-prose.test.ts`

```ts
// Path identity W3: what the spec and the programme's rulings file record about the wave as built (path-identity
// spec §4.12 and §7). What the records state is read from the code here, never restated:
// - the entry field's grammar, its cap and its reader's words, from `_ws_workdirid_read`;
// - the walk's bound, the cwd probe's bound and the collect audit's sum, from ccd's knobs and the runner's row;
// - the cwd probe's skip rule, physical resolve and Darwin arm, from `_ws_cwd_users`;
// - the refusals by identity, from the ladder, `_ws_reclaim_owned` and `_ws_reclaim_record`;
// - the remedies and the `unproc` clause, from the rows rung; the re-ask's sites and order, from the tail;
// - the refusal's sentence, from `SENTENCES` in `server/src/wsaudit.ts`.
// So a later change to any of them reds this suite until the record is corrected with it. The carries, and the two
// departures that exist only if the code lacks what they name, are decided from the code too. W1b's and W2's records
// belong to their own prose suites: this file reads §4.12 alone, counts only its own cells, and re-counts theirs
// unchanged.
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { SENTENCES } from '../src/wsaudit.js';

const root = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..');
const read = (f: string): string => readFileSync(path.join(root, f), 'utf8');
/** Flattened: the records wrap their sentences, so a phrase is matched across line breaks. */
const flat = (s: string): string => s.replace(/\s+/g, ' ');
const SPEC = 'docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-path-identity-design.md';
const CONTRACT = 'docs/superpowers/programs/child-reclamation-contract.md';
const CCD = 'ccd/ccd';
const DEVIATION_TOKEN = /\bD-\d/;
const FOUR_DIGIT_RANGE = /[0-9]{4} ?(–|\.\.|-) ?[0-9]{4}/;
/** A slot the plan's draft left for a measured value, `<n:…>`. None may survive into a record. */
const UNFILLED = /<n:[^>]*>/;
const HEADING = '\n### 4.12 As built (W3)\n';
const NEXT = '\n## 5. The collector switch in Settings\n';
const LAST_ROW_OF_4_11 = "\n  - A record that names the child's directory only through another spelling answers rc 1 or 2 at the "
  + 'ladder, never a hit.\n';

/** §4.12 alone, from its heading to the next `## ` heading; '' when the heading is missing. */
function asBuilt(): string {
  const s = read(SPEC);
  const at = s.indexOf(HEADING);
  if (at < 0) return '';
  const end = s.indexOf('\n## ', at + 1);
  return s.slice(at, end < 0 ? s.length : end);
}

/** TEXT from the line that starts with LEAD to the next line that starts with `**`, flattened; '' when LEAD is
 *  missing. The records' lists are bulleted, so only a bold lead starts a line with `**`. */
function block(text: string, lead: string): string {
  const at = text.indexOf(`\n${lead}`);
  if (at < 0) return '';
  const next = text.indexOf('\n**', at + 1);
  return flat(text.slice(at, next < 0 ? text.length : next));
}

/** A shell function's text, from `NAME() {` to the first line that is `}` alone; '' when there is none. */
function shFunction(src: string, name: string): string {
  const at = src.indexOf(`\n${name}() {`);
  if (at < 0) return '';
  const end = src.indexOf('\n}\n', at + 1);
  return end < 0 ? '' : src.slice(at + 1, end + 2);
}

/** A function's code. Its first line (the name and its header comment) is dropped, and so is every blank line and
 *  every whole-line `#` comment. Each remaining line's trailing ` #` comment is cut. */
function codeLines(fn: string): string[] {
  return fn.split('\n').slice(1).map((l) => l.split(' #')[0])
    .filter((l) => l.trim() !== '' && !l.trimStart().startsWith('#'));
}

/** The prose of ccd's collector header, from its banner to its first state variable, `#` marks folded away; '' when
 *  either anchor is gone. */
function collectorHeader(ccd: string): string {
  const at = ccd.indexOf('\n# ── ws-audit --collect: ');
  const end = at < 0 ? -1 : ccd.indexOf("\n_WS_COLLECT_PROBE=''", at + 1);
  if (end < 0) return '';
  return flat(ccd.slice(at, end).split('\n').filter((l) => l.startsWith('#')).map((l) => l.replace(/^#\s?/, '')).join(' '));
}

/** The one integer that `re` (a `g` regex with one group) captures in `text`; throws on zero matches or on two. */
function one(text: string, re: RegExp, what: string): number {
  const hits = [...text.matchAll(re)];
  if (hits.length !== 1) throw new Error(`${what}: ${hits.length} matches; exactly one is expected`);
  return Number(hits[0]![1]!.replace(/_/g, ''));
}

interface Budget {
  readonly walkS: number; readonly cwdS: number; readonly highS: number; readonly rowS: number; readonly sentence: string;
}

/** The collect audit's sum, read as `collect-audit-budget.test.ts` reads it: the idle walk, the in-use probe, the
 *  checkout scan and the rows rung's identity walk, plus ONE `_plat_timeout` grace, against ws-audit's runner row. */
function budget(ccd: string): Budget {
  const idle = one(ccd, /^WS_COLLECT_IDLE_SCAN_S=(\d+)\b/gm, 'WS_COLLECT_IDLE_SCAN_S');
  const users = one(ccd, /^WS_PATH_USERS_SCAN_S=(\d+)\b/gm, 'WS_PATH_USERS_SCAN_S');
  const scan = one(ccd, /^REAP_SCAN_SECONDS=(\d+)\b/gm, 'REAP_SCAN_SECONDS');
  const walkS = one(ccd, /^WS_RECLAIM_WALK_S=(\d+)\b/gm, 'WS_RECLAIM_WALK_S');
  const cwdS = one(ccd, /^WS_CWD_USERS_SCAN_S=(\d+)\b/gm, 'WS_CWD_USERS_SCAN_S');
  const grace = one(ccd, /grace="\$\{CCD_TIMEOUT_KILL_AFTER:-(\d+)\}"/g, "_plat_timeout's default grace");
  const graceMax = one(ccd, /\[ "\$grace" -gt (\d+) \] && grace=\1\b/g, "_plat_timeout's grace ceiling");
  const rowS = one(read('server/src/remote/runner.ts'), /^[ \t]*'ws-audit':[ \t]*([\d_]+),/gm,
    "CCD_VERB_TIMEOUT_MS['ws-audit']") / 1000;
  const probes = idle + users + scan + walkS;
  return {
    walkS, cwdS, highS: probes + graceMax, rowS,
    sentence: `about ${probes + grace} s, or ${probes + graceMax} s at the widest grace, against ws-audit's ${rowS} s runner row`,
  };
}

/** R49's branch, read from ccd's collector header: the rows rung's git reads stand unbounded. */
const gitReadsStand = (ccd: string): boolean =>
  collectorHeader(ccd).includes("The row pass's git reads of a gone row's repository have no bound of their own");

const q = (w: string): string => `\`${w}\``;
const count = (text: string, cell: string): number => text.split(cell).length - 1;
const COUNT_WORD: Readonly<Record<number, string>> = { 1: 'one', 2: 'two', 3: 'three', 4: 'four' };
/** Every `R<n>` a text cites, once each. */
const ruleNumbers = (t: string): string[] => [...new Set([...t.matchAll(/\bR(\d+)\b/g)].map((m) => `R${m[1]}`))];

/** The entry field reader's words (no overloaded answer). */
const STATES = ['valid', 'pending', 'legacy-absent', 'legacy-stale', 'legacy-unparseable', 'legacy-link', 'unmeasured'] as const;

/** This wave's new ccd test files. Each one CLAUDE.md lists as a load flake is named in §4.12. */
const W3_FILES = ['ccd-worktree-identity-fence', 'ccd-reclaim-idwalk', 'ccd-rows-rung-identity', 'ccd-workdirid',
  'ccd-workdirid-spawn', 'ccd-rows-rung-entry', 'ccd-reclaim-moved-identity', 'ccd-reclaim-main-identity',
  'ccd-cwd-users', 'ccd-reclaim-tail-cwd', 'ccd-reclaim-tail-window', 'ccd-worktree-identity-wordings'] as const;

/** §7 rows this wave leaves to the programme's closing records, with the Status each keeps. */
const UNTOUCHED: ReadonlyArray<readonly [number, string]> = [[10, 'Proposed'], [13, 'Proposed'], [15, 'Proposed'],
  [21, 'Proposed'], [37, 'Deferred'], [39, 'Proposed'], [41, 'Ruled in principle']];

/** The contract rules each record may cite. Plan rulings share the `R<n>` spelling, so any other number is one. */
const SPEC_RULES = ['R31', 'R54', 'R94', 'R97'];
const NOTE_RULES = ['R31', 'R54', 'R56', 'R83', 'R89', 'R93', 'R94', 'R95', 'R97'];

/** The substantive departures this wave made, by slug. */
const DEPARTURES = ['workdirid-pending-form', 'workdirid-unreadable-holds', 'rows-walk-second-mountinfo-reader',
  'unproc-also-by-walked-position', 'ladder-main-checkout-ef', 'record-main-hit-keeps-the-terminal-refusal',
  'record-by-another-spelling-reads-unmeasured', 'record-two-spellings-reads-unmeasured', 'reappeared-tree-refuses',
  'cwd-wait-only-waits',
  'cwd-refusal-reuses-worktree-remove-failed', 'reask-words-follow-the-owned-call', 'cwd-probe-adopts-the-path-users-walk',
  'darwin-prefixes-take-the-identity-shims', 'w2-mount-asks-shadowed-by-the-reask', 'collect-reprove-table-moves-to-the-gap',
  'audit-document-key-pins-outside-the-boundary'];

/** The residuals that stand whatever the code says next. */
const BASE_RESIDUALS = ['reg-purge-inventory-omits-workdirid', 'legacy-row-count-has-no-doctor-line',
  'human-gated-removals-ask-no-cwd', 'cwd-probe-sees-no-open-fds', 'cwd-probe-sees-a-session-only-while-it-runs',
  'surviving-background-job-holds-the-reclaim', 'reask-identity-is-per-attempt', 'reask-to-opendir-window',
  'tail-reasks-can-outrun-the-act-row', 'identity-found-after-the-kill-repeats', 'worktree-ask-to-force-window',
  'git-mount-crossing-unmeasured', 'exdev-class-moot-under-pi5-a', 'repointed-alias-for-legacy-rows-until-respawn',
  'other-mount-namespaces-fuse-views-and-overlay', 'ancestry-stands-alone-on-darwin',
  'moved-check-misses-a-subdirectory-of-a-moved-tree', 'workdirid-temp-leaks-on-sigkill',
  'cwd-probe-can-wait-on-a-hung-network-cwd', 'workdirid-pending-unwritable-keeps-the-old-field',
  'failed-pending-write-reads-legacy', 'workdirid-fifo-swap-after-type-check', 'darwin-cwd-parse-unbounded-as-today',
  'fish-spawn-cd-reads-backslash-escapes', 'workdirid-physical-control-byte-stays-pending',
  'relative-workdir-second-cd-does-not-enter', 'human-gated-removals-ask-no-mounts', 'vanished-checkout-arms-ask-no-mounts'];

/** §7 items 1 to 3 and 5 to 8, by slug: closed whatever the code says next. Item 4, `owned-to-worktree-remove-window`,
 *  is narrowed, not closed (its row: "closing is a later wave"), so `carriesAtTheTip` decides it from the re-asks. */
const CLOSED_CARRIES = ['r31-repointed-alias-resolves-complete', 'r31-bind-mount-spelling-resolves-complete',
  'r54-recorded-basis-dev-ino-ancestry', 'proc-symlink-row-places-at-ccds-cwd',
  'unres-false-detail-for-row-that-is-the-child', 'double-slash-remedy-wordings', 'owned-main-checkout-ambient-realpath'];

/** What each task found while building, by slug. The rulings file's "Found while building" list names every one.
 *  Filled at Step 1 from the ledger (Step 0's (e30)). */
const FOUND_WHILE_BUILDING: readonly string[] = [
];

/** Two departures exist only if the code lacks what they name: the expire document's count (R45) and the ws-add
 *  seed (R5). */
function conditionalDepartures(ccd: string): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  if (!/"legacyRows":/.test(shFunction(ccd, '_ws_expire_audit_contained'))) out.push('legacy-count-expire-half-fenced');
  if (!codeLines(shFunction(ccd, 'cmd_ws_add')).some((l) => l.includes('_plat_workdirid_pane "$REG" "$id" "$wt"'))) {
    out.push('ws-add-seed-subsumed-by-spawn-pending');
  }
  return out;
}
const departuresAtTheTip = (ccd: string): string[] => [...DEPARTURES, ...conditionalDepartures(ccd)];

/** The carries whose state the code decides. A carry is closed or narrowed only while the code shows what closes or
 *  narrows it; otherwise it is a residual. */
function carriesAtTheTip(ccd: string): { residuals: string[]; closed: string[]; narrowed: string[] } {
  const residuals = [...BASE_RESIDUALS];
  const closed = [...CLOSED_CARRIES];
  const narrowed: string[] = [];
  const rung = codeLines(shFunction(ccd, '_ws_reclaim_workdir_shared')).join('\n');
  const tail = codeLines(shFunction(ccd, '_ws_reclaim_tail'));
  const mountHold = /\b_ws_collect_mountinfo\b/.test(rung);
  const reasks = tail.filter((l) => /\b_ws_reclaim_reask "\$id"/.test(l)).length;
  const ownedAtStart = tail.some((l) => l.includes('_ws_reclaim_owned "$id" "$workdir" "$main"; orc=$?'));
  (mountHold && ownedAtStart && reasks === 4 ? closed : residuals).push('no-whole-child-mount-ask-before-step-3');
  (mountHold ? narrowed : residuals).push('audit-normalise-has-no-mount-ask');
  if (reasks === 4) narrowed.push('worktree-ask-to-force-window');
  (reasks === 4 ? narrowed : residuals).push('owned-to-worktree-remove-window');
  if (gitReadsStand(ccd)) {
    residuals.push('rows-rung-git-reads-unbounded');
    narrowed.push('registry-row-pass-carries-no-bound');
  } else closed.push('registry-row-pass-carries-no-bound');
  (shFunction(ccd, '_ws_cwd_users') !== '' ? narrowed : residuals).push('in-use-probe-misses-another-mount');
  return { residuals, closed, narrowed };
}

describe('the path-identity spec records W3 as built (path-identity spec §4.12, §7)', () => {
  const spec = read(SPEC);
  const raw = asBuilt();
  const s = flat(raw);
  const ccd = read(CCD);

  it("§4.12 stands after §4.11's last row, and directly above §5", () => {
    const p411 = spec.indexOf('\n### 4.11 Proof\n');
    const last = p411 < 0 ? -1 : spec.indexOf(LAST_ROW_OF_4_11, p411);
    const p412 = spec.indexOf(HEADING);
    const p5 = spec.indexOf(NEXT);
    expect(p411, '§4.11 is missing').toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(last, "§4.11's last row is missing").toBeGreaterThan(p411);
    expect(p412, "§4.12 is missing, or stands above §4.11's last row").toBeGreaterThan(last);
    expect(p5, '§5 must follow §4.12').toBeGreaterThan(p412);
    expect(spec).toContain(`${LAST_ROW_OF_4_11}${HEADING}`);
    expect(spec.slice(p5 - 2, p5 + 1), 'one blank line above §5').toMatch(/^[^\n]\n\n$/);
  });

  it("states the field grammar its one reader holds, the reader's cap and its seven words", () => {
    const reader = codeLines(shFunction(ccd, '_ws_workdirid_read')).join('\n');
    expect(reader, '`_ws_workdirid_read` not found in ccd/ccd').not.toBe('');
    expect(reader, 'the reader holds no 13-digit time').toContain('{13}');
    expect(reader, 'the reader holds no pending form').toMatch(/\bpending\b/);
    const n = /\bhead -c ?(\d+)/.exec(reader);
    expect(n, 'the reader reads no bounded count (head -c)').not.toBeNull();
    const cap = Number(n![1]) - 1;
    for (const w of STATES) {
      expect(reader, `the reader never answers ${w}`).toMatch(new RegExp(`(?<![A-Za-z0-9-])${w}(?![A-Za-z0-9-])`));
    }
    const field = block(raw, '**The entry field');
    expect(field, 'the entry-field block is missing').not.toBe('');
    expect(field).toContain('`v1<TAB><dev>:<ino>:<btime or -><TAB><at_ms><TAB><physical pwd -P><TAB><logical spelling>`');
    expect(field).toContain('`v1<TAB>pending<TAB><at_ms><TAB>-<TAB><logical>`');
    expect(field).toContain(`A body over ${cap} bytes is unparseable`);
    for (const w of STATES) expect(field, w).toContain(q(w));
  });

  it("states the walk's bound and the collect audit's sum, from ccd's knobs and the runner's row", () => {
    const b = budget(ccd);
    expect(b.highS, 'the sum at the widest grace no longer fits the row').toBeLessThan(b.rowS);
    expect(collectorHeader(ccd), "ccd's collector header states another sum").toContain(b.sentence);
    expect(s).toContain(`\`WS_RECLAIM_WALK_S\` (${b.walkS} s)`);
    expect(s).toContain(b.sentence);
  });

  it("states the cwd probe's bound, skip rule, physical resolve and Darwin arm, each as the code has it", () => {
    const probe = shFunction(ccd, '_ws_cwd_users');
    const code = codeLines(probe).join('\n');
    expect(code, '`_ws_cwd_users` not found in ccd/ccd').not.toBe('');
    expect(code, 'the probe resolves no parent').toMatch(/\b_ws_dir_physical\b/);
    expect(code, 'the probe has no Darwin arm').toMatch(/\b_ws_expire_lsof\b/);
    expect(code, 'the probe names no bound of its own').toMatch(/\bWS_CWD_USERS_SCAN_S\b/);
    for (const e of ['ENOENT', 'ESRCH', 'EACCES']) expect(probe, `the probe has no ${e} rule`).toContain(e);
    expect(codeLines(shFunction(ccd, '_ws_expire_cwd_users')).some((l) => /\b_ws_cwd_users\b/.test(l)),
      'ws-expire does not ask the shared probe').toBe(true);
    expect(s).toContain(`\`WS_CWD_USERS_SCAN_S\` (${budget(ccd).cwdS} s)`);
    expect(s).toContain("skips a process only on ENOENT or ESRCH of that process's own cwd link or stat file, or on the "
      + 'ruled EACCES exception');
    expect(s).toContain(q('_ws_dir_physical'));
    expect(s).toContain(q('_ws_expire_lsof'));
  });

  it('names the refusals by identity at the ladder, at owned and in the record reader, as the code makes them', () => {
    const ladder = codeLines(shFunction(ccd, '_ws_reclaim_ladder'));
    expect(ladder.filter((l) => l.includes('-ef "$main"')), "the ladder's main-checkout compare has no -ef").toHaveLength(1);
    const owned = shFunction(ccd, '_ws_reclaim_owned');
    expect(codeLines(owned).some((l) => l.includes('_ws_path_ident "$main" follow')), 'owned measures no main checkout').toBe(true);
    expect(owned, "owned's refusal is not the other-spelling why").toContain('under another spelling');
    const rec = codeLines(shFunction(ccd, '_ws_reclaim_record'));
    expect(rec.some((l) => /\s-ef\s/.test(l)), 'the record reader compares no identity').toBe(true);
    expect(rec.join('\n'), "the record reader's two-records why is gone").toContain('worktree records name the tree at');
    for (const p of [q('ladder-main-checkout-ef'), 'under another spelling', q('RECLAIM_REC_MAIN'),
      'Identity never makes a hit', q('_WS_REC_WHY')]) expect(s, p).toContain(p);
  });

  it("quotes the restore remedies and the unproc clause, and the rows rung's code says re-point nowhere", () => {
    const rung = codeLines(shFunction(ccd, '_ws_reclaim_workdir_shared')).join('\n');
    expect(rung, '`_ws_reclaim_workdir_shared` not found in ccd/ccd').not.toBe('');
    expect(rung).not.toContain('re-point');
    expect(rung).toContain('restore the link whose target opens with //');
    expect(rung).toContain('never replace a link to clear this');
    expect(rung).toContain('under /proc, or one reached through a link into /proc');
    const words = block(raw, '**The wordings');
    expect(words, 'the wordings block is missing').not.toBe('');
    expect(words).toContain('restore the link whose target opens with // to its original target, or stop the session and '
      + 'purge its row; never replace a link to clear this');
    expect(words).toContain('under /proc, or one reached through a link into /proc');
    expect(s).not.toContain('re-point the link');
  });

  it("states the new clause of the worktree-remove-failed sentence, as the server spells it", () => {
    expect(SENTENCES['worktree-remove-failed'] ?? '', "the server's sentence lost its clause")
      .toContain('or a process still works inside it');
    expect(s).toContain(q('worktree-remove-failed'));
    expect(s).toContain('or a process still works inside it');
  });

  it("states the re-ask at each of the tail's four sites, in the order the code asks", () => {
    const tail = codeLines(shFunction(ccd, '_ws_reclaim_tail'));
    expect(tail.length, '`_ws_reclaim_tail` not found in ccd/ccd').toBeGreaterThan(0);
    const seq = tail.map((l) => (/\b_ws_reclaim_reask "\$id"/.test(l) ? 'R'
      : /\b_ws_cwd_users "\$workdir"/.test(l) ? 'C'
        : /\b_ws_removal_mounts_clear "\$(?:cpath|workdir)"/.test(l) ? 'M' : '')).join('');
    const sites = (seq.match(/R/g) ?? []).length;
    expect(seq, 'each site asks the cwd probe, then the re-ask, then the mount question').toBe('CRM'.repeat(4));
    expect(s).toContain(q('_ws_reclaim_reask'));
    expect(s).toContain(`at each of the ${COUNT_WORD[sites] ?? String(sites)} sites`);
    expect(s).toContain("the cwd ask, then the re-ask, then W2's mount ask, then `keep_of` or the forced removal");
  });

  it("states the legacy count's keys, and the expire half and the ws-add seed as the code has them", () => {
    expect(shFunction(ccd, 'cmd_ws_audit'), 'the reclaim document carries no count').toContain('"legacyRows":%s,"pendingRows":%s,');
    expect(codeLines(shFunction(ccd, 'cmd_start')).some((l) => l.includes('_plat_workdirid_pane "$REG" "$id" "$workdir"')),
      'start writes no seed').toBe(true);
    for (const k of ['`"legacyRows"`', '`"pendingRows"`']) expect(s, k).toContain(k);
    const dep = conditionalDepartures(ccd);
    const expire = 'The expiry audit document carries the same two keys.';
    if (dep.includes('legacy-count-expire-half-fenced')) expect(s).not.toContain(expire);
    else expect(s).toContain(expire);
    const seed = 'ws-add appends the same statement to its `.workdir` line in place';
    if (dep.includes('ws-add-seed-subsumed-by-spawn-pending')) expect(s).not.toContain(seed);
    else expect(s).toContain(seed);
  });

  it("names every file of this wave that joined CLAUDE.md's load-flake list", () => {
    const md = read('CLAUDE.md');
    const at = md.indexOf('- **Known load flakes**');
    expect(at, "CLAUDE.md's load-flake bullet is missing").toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    const end = md.indexOf('\n- **', at + 1);
    const bullet = md.slice(at, end < 0 ? md.length : end);
    expect(s).toContain("CLAUDE.md's load-flake list");
    for (const f of W3_FILES) {
      if (new RegExp(`(?<![A-Za-z0-9-])${f}(?![A-Za-z0-9-])`).test(bullet)) expect(s, f).toContain(q(`${f}.test.ts`));
    }
  });

  it('carries the entry counts as numbers only, and names what was judged instead', () => {
    const lead = 'Measured on the fleet box before the first edit, counts only:';
    const judged = 'Not measured, and judged instead:';
    const at = s.indexOf(lead);
    const to = s.indexOf(judged, at + 1);
    expect(at, 'the entry-counts bullet is missing').toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(to, 'the judged bullet must follow the counts').toBeGreaterThan(at);
    const counts = s.slice(at + lead.length, to);
    expect(counts).toMatch(/\d/);
    for (const bad of ['/', '~', 'demo-']) expect(counts, bad).not.toContain(bad);
    expect(counts).not.toMatch(UNFILLED);
    expect(counts).toContain('legacy rows');
    for (const cls of ['leaf ancestry', "the agent's mount namespace"]) expect(s.slice(to), cls).toContain(cls);
  });

  it('names every departure, residual and carry by slug, decided at the tip, and no number', () => {
    for (const d of departuresAtTheTip(ccd)) expect(s, d).toContain(q(d));
    const residuals = block(raw, '**Stated residuals');
    const carries = block(raw, '**Closed and narrowed carries');
    expect(residuals, 'the stated-residuals list is missing').not.toBe('');
    expect(carries, 'the carries list is missing').not.toBe('');
    const cut = carries.indexOf('- Narrowed, not closed:');
    expect(cut, 'the narrowed list is missing').toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    const closed = carries.slice(0, cut);
    const narrowed = carries.slice(cut);
    const k = carriesAtTheTip(ccd);
    for (const r of k.residuals) expect(residuals, r).toContain(q(r));
    for (const c of k.closed) {
      expect(closed, c).toContain(q(c));
      expect(residuals, `${c} is closed, so it is no residual`).not.toContain(q(c));
    }
    for (const n of k.narrowed) {
      expect(narrowed, n).toContain(q(n));
      expect(closed, `${n} is narrowed, not closed`).not.toContain(q(n));
    }
    expect(s).not.toMatch(DEVIATION_TOKEN);
    expect(s).not.toMatch(FOUR_DIGIT_RANGE);
    expect(s).not.toMatch(UNFILLED);
    expect(s, 'a task number').not.toMatch(/\bTask \d/);
    expect(ruleNumbers(s).filter((r) => !SPEC_RULES.includes(r)), 'a rule number the spec does not cite').toEqual([]);
  });

  it('every ccd name it cites exists in ccd/ccd', () => {
    const names = [...new Set([...s.matchAll(/`(_(?:ws|WS|lc|plat|spawn|reg)_[A-Za-z_]+)`/g)].map((m) => m[1]!))];
    expect(names.length, 'no ccd name read from §4.12').toBeGreaterThan(0);
    for (const n of names) expect(new RegExp(`(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])${n}(?![A-Za-z0-9_])`).test(ccd), n).toBe(true);
  });

  it('marks items 1 to 8 built in W3, item 9 with its git reads standing, and item 20 with its temp-root half standing', () => {
    for (let n = 1; n <= 8; n += 1) {
      expect(spec, `item ${n}`).toMatch(new RegExp(`^\\| ${n} \\|[^\\n]*\\| Built \\(W3\\) \\|`, 'm'));
    }
    const standing = gitReadsStand(ccd);
    const nine = standing ? 'Built \\(W3\\), git reads standing' : 'Built \\(W3\\)';
    expect(spec, 'item 9').toMatch(new RegExp(`^\\| 9 \\|[^\\n]*\\| ${nine} \\|`, 'm'));
    expect(spec, 'item 20').toMatch(/^\| 20 \|[^\n]*\| Built \(W3\), temp-root half standing \|/m);
    expect(count(spec, '| Built (W3) |')).toBe(standing ? 8 : 9);
    expect(count(spec, '| Built (W3), git reads standing |')).toBe(standing ? 1 : 0);
    expect(count(spec, '| Built (W3), temp-root half standing |')).toBe(1);
  });

  it("CONTROL: leaves every other wave's cells as they were", () => {
    expect(count(spec, '| Built (W2) |')).toBe(12);
    expect(count(spec, '| Built (child-reclamation wave 10) |')).toBe(2);
    expect(count(spec, '| Built (W1b) |')).toBe(8);
    for (const [n, cell] of UNTOUCHED) {
      expect(spec, `item ${n}`).toMatch(new RegExp(`^\\| ${n} \\|[^|\\n]*\\|[^|\\n]*\\|[^|\\n]*\\| ${cell} \\|`, 'm'));
    }
  });
});

describe('the programme’s rulings file carries the W3 as-built note (path-identity spec §4.12)', () => {
  const c = read(CONTRACT);
  const ccd = read(CCD);
  const head = /^### §17 as built \(path-identity W3, run \d+\)$/m.exec(c);
  const at = head ? head.index : -1;
  const next = at < 0 ? -1 : c.slice(at + 1).search(/\n#{2,3} /);
  const raw = at < 0 ? '' : c.slice(at, next < 0 ? c.length : at + 1 + next);
  const note = flat(raw);

  it('stands in §17, after the W2 note, and before any §18', () => {
    expect(at, 'the as-built note is missing, or its heading names no run number').toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    const w2 = c.search(/^### §17 as built \(path-identity W2, run \d+\)$/m);
    expect(w2, "W2's note is missing").toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(at).toBeGreaterThan(w2);
    const s18 = c.search(/^## 18\. /m);
    if (s18 > -1) expect(at).toBeLessThan(s18);
  });

  it("records R94 as built, naming R31's bullet by its own words, and R31 and R94 stand unedited", () => {
    expect(note).toContain('**R94 as built (process state may only refuse).**');
    expect(note).toContain('"Process state never grants deletion consent. A pane\'s cwd');
    expect(note).toContain('"Process state never grants deletion consent; it may only refuse"');
    const r31At = c.indexOf('\n- **R31 —');
    const r32At = c.indexOf('\n- **R32 —', r31At + 1);
    expect(r31At, 'R31 is missing').toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(r32At, 'R32 must follow R31').toBeGreaterThan(r31At);
    expect(flat(c.slice(r31At, r32At))).toContain("Process state never grants deletion consent. A pane's cwd, or a modelled "
      + 'session that is up, gone or unaskable, is not an input.');
    expect(flat(c)).toContain('R31\'s last bullet now reads: "Process state never grants deletion consent; it may only refuse."');
  });

  it("records R93, R54, R97, R95's backstop and the collect audit's sum", () => {
    for (const lead of ["**R93 (the programme's shape).**", '**R54 as W3 leaves it (the identity moved-check).**',
      "**R97's reach, unchanged (PI9 K1).**", "**R95's asks, now a backstop (`w2-mount-asks-shadowed-by-the-reask`).**",
      "**The collect audit's budget.**"]) {
```

```markdown
### 4.12 As built (W3)

W3 built this section's PI1 B, PI2 L1, PI3 B, PI4 D, PI5 A, PI6 M4, PI7 P1 (P2 for a row with a valid field), PI8 B2
and PI10 O2, and items 1 to 9 and the worktree half of item 20 of §7. PI9 K1's reach was stated in W0 and is unchanged.
This subsection records where what W3 built narrows, corrects or spells out §4.1 to §4.11, and names the residuals it
leaves. It amends, and rewrites none of the text above. Every claim is measured at the wave's tip unless it says
otherwise. Every identity input W3 added may only add a placement or a hold: none releases a row, or turns a refusal
into a pass.

**The entry field (PI1 B, PI2 L1).**
- Each session's entry identity is one field, `$REG/<id>.workdirid`: one line with no trailing newline, in one of two
  forms:
  - valid: `v1<TAB><dev>:<ino>:<btime or -><TAB><at_ms><TAB><physical pwd -P><TAB><logical spelling>`;
  - pending: `v1<TAB>pending<TAB><at_ms><TAB>-<TAB><logical>`.

  `<at_ms>` is exactly 13 digits. A birth time is a positive integer or `-`. The physical path is plain and absolute,
  and no control character stands anywhere but the four TABs. A body over 8320 bytes is unparseable. One regex, held
  by the one reader, `_ws_workdirid_read`, is the grammar's single definition.
- `workdirid-pending-form`: §4.3's grammar has one form, and as built it has two. The parent writes the pending form
  through `_spawn_workdirid_pending` directly before each of `_spawn_start`'s two `_tmux_new_session` calls, the
  primary and the retry. The pane replaces it after its `cd` succeeds and before `exec`. A pending field whose logical
  spelling equals the row's current `.workdir` holds every child, and its detail names the row and the remedy,
  "restart that session". So a pane that cannot record where it entered leaves a hold, as §4.11 asks. A pending write
  that fails unlinks the field, so a stale valid field never survives it.
- The reader answers one of seven words in `_WS_WDID_STATE`, by rules taken in a fixed order: `legacy-absent` (no
  field), `legacy-link` (a link, whose target is never read), `unmeasured` (not a regular file, or a failed open or
  read), `legacy-unparseable` (over the cap, a failed regex, or a physical path that is not plain), `legacy-stale` (its
  logical spelling differs from the current `.workdir`), `pending`, and `valid`. It returns 0 for `valid`, 1 for every
  `legacy-*` word, and 2 for `pending` and `unmeasured`. The stale rule comes before the pending one, so a stale
  pending line reads legacy.
- `workdirid-unreadable-holds`: §4.3 names a missing, unparseable or link field legacy. As built, a field that is not a
  regular file (a directory, a FIFO), or that cannot be read, answers `unmeasured`, a hold, as `.workdir`'s own
  unreadable rule does. The reader checks the type before it opens the file, and reads a bounded number of bytes. It
  mirrors `_reg_read`'s refusals and calls nothing of the registry's own.
- The pane's writer is one composer, `_plat_workdirid_pane`: one line in the platform layer, byte-identical in
  `ccd/ccrc`. It prints a brace-free `/bin/sh -c '<script>'` fragment, ending ` 2>/dev/null && `, for every workdir
  that `.workdir` itself accepts, a backslash included. It prints nothing only for an empty argument, an argument
  holding a control character or a `'` (both of which `.workdir` refuses too), or an id holding a `/`. Each `\` rides
  inside the fragment's single-quoted arguments as `\0134`, which the script decodes with `printf %b` before it writes,
  so the field holds the logical spelling byte-equal to `.workdir`, and the one reader and its grammar are unchanged.
  The script measures `pwd -P` and
  the stat of `.`, in the form `_plat_btime` uses on that system, writes temp-then-rename, and exits 0 on every path.
  It runs under sh, bash, zsh and fish, and the field round-trips to `valid` under sh, bash and zsh, and under fish
  for every spelling without `\\` or a trailing `\` (`fish-spawn-cd-reads-backslash-escapes`, below).
- Each launch command enters the workdir, runs the writer with its errors discarded, then enters the workdir again and
  execs: `cd '<wd>' && <fragment>true; cd '<wd>' && exec env …`, which reads `cd '<wd>' && true; cd '<wd>' && exec env …`
  when the composer printed nothing. So a writer that cannot start, is killed or fails never stops the `exec`, and a failed first `cd` execs
  nothing. For an absolute `.workdir`, the only form `cmd_start` and ws-add store, both `cd`s enter the same directory,
  so no transcript path changed; a relative one is `relative-workdir-second-cd-does-not-enter`, below. A re-point
  between the two `cd`s can only leave a field that adds a hold.
- <n:seeds> The pending line has the one writer above.
- `_reg_purge`'s loop already unlinks the field, so purging needed no code. Its inventory comment was not edited.

**The rows rung (PI3 B, PI6 M4, PI8 B2).**
- `_ws_reclaim_workdir_shared` makes one walk per call, `_ws_reclaim_idwalk`: one `python3 -I` exec under
  `_plat_timeout`, bounded by `WS_RECLAIM_WALK_S` (5 s). In that one exec it:
  - stats every prefix of each row's complete resolved spelling;
  - walks the link components of each row's raw spelling;
  - reads the mount table;
  - asks `_plat_btime` for the birth times, inside the same bound.

  Its reply carries indices and numbers, never a path, and ends with its own line count. A timeout, a failure, or a
  reply not read whole answers unmeasured, never "no row". The rung then matches the reply with its own list of
  requests, one line each in order, so a list cut short on its way to the walk holds too, and the walk refuses a last
  request cut before its end. Its maps live for one call, so every re-ask builds its own.
- Ancestry. A row whose resolved identity equals the child's is SHARED, and a row with the child's identity in its
  ancestor chain is NESTED, as well as by today's strings. The standing leaves are targets too, as NESTED. Identities
  measured at one instant compare device and inode alone. Identities compared across time compare through
  `_ws_ident_eq`, which adds the birth time when both sides carry one.
- `rows-walk-second-mountinfo-reader`: the walk asks §4.5 step 3's mount hold, reading the table as a declared second
  reader through `_ws_collect_mountinfo`'s seam. It holds the child unmeasured when a mount point lies at or under it,
  or when a mount on its device has a root at or under its device-relative path (`//deleted` included). A device that
  mountinfo and the stat of the child disagree on fails closed. A parity pin holds the walk's mount-point answer equal
  to `_ws_collect_mounts_clear`'s on the same tables, and a source pin names exactly two readers of the seam. On Darwin
  the caller does not ask (one line), and the ancestry arm stands alone.
- The rung has three callers, and each now places by identity: the reclaim and expiry ladder, `_ws_reclaim_owned`, and
  the collector's row rule, `_ws_collect_rows_clear`.
- `w2-mount-asks-shadowed-by-the-reask`: three askers now read the mount table through this rung: the ladder's
  in-lock recompute, `_ws_reclaim_owned` at the tail's start, and the tail's re-ask before every standing forced
  removal. So a mount under the child is caught before W2's step-3 and step-4 asks (§3.10). Those asks are now a
  backstop for a mount that appears in the instant after the re-ask. W2's behavioural cases moved their plants to that
  instant, and their assertions are unchanged.
- `collect-reprove-table-moves-to-the-gap`: the collector's row rule now reads the table before its move, so a table
  that cannot be read answers `probe-unmeasured` before the move. One collector reprove case moved its unreadable table
  to the `moved` gap, and its assertions are unchanged.
- `unproc-also-by-walked-position`: §4.8's m1 refuses a link whose raw target matches `^/+proc(/|$)`. As built, a row
  is also refused `unproc` when the walk's link-free position enters `/proc` through a relative target.
- What following links leaves to judgement:
  - that a real bind's `stat` returns the source's device and inode for every path below it, a source on another file
    system included;
  - that `pwd -P` and `/proc/<pid>/cwd` read the bind's spelling in ccd's namespace;
  - that mountinfo's device field equals `stat`'s on the fleet's file systems (measured on the fleet box before the
    first edit);
  - that a link appearing after the resolve is measured as the namespace reads it now, which only adds.
- Each new not-asked answer (`unwalk`, `unmount`, `unpend`, `unfield`, `unrec`) is decided after the outrank line, so a
  string placement still answers the terminal `containment-unproven`. Each names rows by id only.
- The rung's git reads of a gone row's repository stay unbounded (`rows-rung-git-reads-unbounded`). A runner that kills
  the audit there gets no document, which the server reads as a failed audit and retries: it fails closed.
- The budget. The collect audit's probes are `WS_COLLECT_IDLE_SCAN_S` (30 s), `WS_PATH_USERS_SCAN_S` (10 s),
  `REAP_SCAN_SECONDS` (30 s) and now `WS_RECLAIM_WALK_S` (5 s), with one `_plat_timeout` grace: about 78 s, or 83 s at
  the widest grace, against ws-audit's 90 s runner row. ccd's collector header states the same sum.

**Entry placement (PI3 step 2, PI7 P2).**
- A valid field may only add. For a row with a valid field:
  1. its recorded identity, or its recorded physical path, equal to the child's is terminal SHARED (PI7 P2);
  2. its recorded physical path at, under or through the child or a standing leaf, by string, places it as today's
     chain places that string;
  3. its recorded path's identity equal to the child's, or with the child or a leaf in its ancestor chain, is SHARED or
     NESTED;
  4. the mismatch rule: when its recorded identity differs from its current one, and the recorded path no longer stands
     with that identity, it is unmeasured (`unrec`), "entered a directory other than the one their workdir names now".
- The mismatch rule is asked only of a row whose current spelling resolved complete. A gone row gets rules 1 to 3,
  never 4, and is released only by R54's arms, as before. A recorded path outside the child never moves a row out of
  any placement.
- Birth times are read only where a rule compares across time: the field against the child, and the mismatch rule. A
  birth time that could not be read holds (`unwalk`), and is never read as "none". A recorded path that is gone adds
  nothing by itself. It only tells the mismatch rule that the path does not stand.
- A pending field holds (`unpend`), and so does a field that is not a regular file or cannot be read (`unfield`). A
  legacy field, whatever its word, leaves its row to today's string rule plus the ancestry above.
- The count. The reclaim audit document carries `"legacyRows"` and `"pendingRows"`: `legacyRows` counts the other
  rows whose field is in a `legacy-*` state, and `pendingRows` those whose field reads `pending`. A field that reads
  `unmeasured` is in neither, and it holds the child. `null` means not counted: the ladder never reached the rung, or the rung could not list
  the registry. <n:expire-half> No server reader was added.

**The moved-check (R54).**
- R54's identity moved-check is built in `_ws_reclaim_moved_check`. The rung records each gone row's valid field in
  `_WS_RECORDED_IDS`, beside the git directories it already recorded. Each nested checkout's identity is compared with
  every recorded identity, birth time included. A match holds the child, and a checkout whose identity cannot be read
  holds it unmeasured. It never releases a row.
- Its limit stands: a gone row whose field records a subdirectory of a moved tree is not matched.

**The main checkout and the record (PI10 O2).**
- `_ws_reclaim_owned` measures two identities after its moved-check and directly before its pass: the main
  checkout's, followed whole, and the tree's own when it stands. So a failed measure (2) never pre-empts a proof (1).

- `_ws_reclaim_record` uses identity only to refuse. After its string scan, a first (main) stanza that is the tree by

  of … worktree records name the tree". `record-main-hit-keeps-the-terminal-refusal`: once the first stanza names the
  tree, by its string or by `-ef`, no later stanza is asked, so a row naming the main checkout keeps the terminal
  `not-a-workspace`, and the owned check its proof, rather than weakening to unmeasured.
  `record-by-another-spelling-reads-unmeasured`: when only a stanza naming the tree under another spelling records it,

  `no-worktree-record`, whose detail was false (git does record the tree), and the owned check answers 2. Both refuse,

  its three callers print, and a list failure keeps its exact sentence. The comments that said no `_ws_realpath` answer
  is read there were corrected.

**The cwd probe (PI4 D).**
- `cwd-probe-adopts-the-path-users-walk`: one probe, `_ws_cwd_users`, answers nobody (0), in use (1, with the pids) or
  unmeasured (2). A process is in use when the string of its cwd link meets the tree's physical spelling, OR the
  device and inode ancestry of the directory that link names meets the tree.

    took <n:probe-stats> stats in <n:probe-ms> ms.
- Not measured, and judged instead: leaf ancestry (no stat was taken under the clips or temp-root leaves), the agent's
  mount namespace against the panes' (no service manager was read), and a hung network cwd. Each is held or refused
  where it is met, never released.

**Stated residuals.**
- `reg-purge-inventory-omits-workdirid`: `_reg_purge`'s inventory comment does not name the field. Its loop unlinks it.
- `legacy-row-count-has-no-doctor-line`: the legacy count rides the audit document alone, and no doctor line counts it.
  A doctor line would need a second parser of the grammar.
- `rows-rung-git-reads-unbounded`: the rung's git reads of a gone row's repository have no bound of their own (above).
- `human-gated-removals-ask-no-cwd`: ws-reap's tail and the other human-gated removals ask no cwd question. Forwarded
  to workspace lifecycle.
- `cwd-probe-sees-no-open-fds`: open file descriptors are not probed.
- `cwd-probe-sees-a-session-only-while-it-runs`: the probe sees another session only while it has a live process inside
  the tree. Entry identity is the cure.
- `surviving-background-job-holds-the-reclaim`: a background job of the child's own pane that outlives the kill holds
  the reclaim until it exits, as it holds an expiry.
- `reask-identity-is-per-attempt`: the recorded identities live for one attempt, and no tombstone field carries them.
  A resumed attempt re-proves them.
- `reask-to-opendir-window`: the window from the last identity compare, through W2's mount read, to git's own opendir
  (§4.7). The cwd probe's bounded walk comes before the re-ask, outside that window.
- `tail-reasks-can-outrun-the-act-row`: a tail with N standing nested checkouts makes 2N+2 bounded re-asks against the
  act's 240 s runner row. A kill there fails closed at a breadcrumbed step, and a timed-out re-ask answers unmeasured.
- `identity-found-after-the-kill-repeats`: an identity, cwd or row refusal found at step 3 or step 4 comes after the
  pane kill, so every retry fails the same way until the cause is gone, as W2's `mount-found-after-the-kill-repeats`.
- `worktree-ask-to-force-window`: narrowed by the re-ask, not closed.
- `git-mount-crossing-unmeasured`: no session runs a privileged container, so nobody measured whether
  `git worktree remove --force` crosses a bind or FUSE mount. Every ask comes before git runs and only refuses. The
  operator may measure it on a throwaway box of their own choosing.
- `exdev-class-moot-under-pi5-a`: the EXDEV class belongs to closing the window (PI5 B), which was not ruled. The
  operator may measure it on the same terms.
- `repointed-alias-for-legacy-rows-until-respawn`: a legacy row's re-pointed alias stays unseen until that session
  respawns and records its entry. The cwd probe covers it while a process lives inside.
- `other-mount-namespaces-fuse-views-and-overlay`: §4.5's out-of-scope set stands.
- `ancestry-stands-alone-on-darwin`: Darwin has no mount table, so ancestry is its one identity arm.
- `moved-check-misses-a-subdirectory-of-a-moved-tree`: a gone row whose field records a subdirectory of a moved tree is
  not matched.
- `workdirid-temp-leaks-on-sigkill`: a writer killed between its temp write and its rename leaves the dot-leading temp,
  as `_reg_set`'s does.
- `workdirid-pending-unwritable-keeps-the-old-field`: when both the pending write and its unlink fail, the earlier
  field stands.
- `failed-pending-write-reads-legacy`: a pending write that fails, when its unlink succeeds, leaves the row
  `legacy-absent` (today's rule) until a later spawn's writes succeed.
- `workdirid-fifo-swap-after-type-check`: a FIFO swapped in between the reader's type check and its open blocks the
  open. It is the registry reader's own window.
- `cwd-probe-can-wait-on-a-hung-network-cwd`: a child in uninterruptible sleep outlives the bound's TERM.
- `darwin-cwd-parse-unbounded-as-today`: on Darwin the probe parses lsof's listing directly, as ws-expire did, and never
  under `_plat_timeout`, so that parse has no bound of its own.
- `fish-spawn-cd-reads-backslash-escapes`: under a fish pane shell, the launch command's own `cd '<wd>'`, which W3 did
  not change, reads `\\` and a trailing `\` inside single quotes as escapes, so a pane whose workdir holds either never
  enters it, and its field stays `pending`, a hold that restarting the session does not clear. That pane never started
  before W3 either, and purging the row clears the hold. The composer's fragment carries every backslash as an escape
  of its own, so the field round-trips to `valid` under sh, bash and zsh, and under fish for every spelling without
  `\\` or a trailing `\`.
- `workdirid-physical-control-byte-stays-pending`: `.workdir`'s control-character guard, the composer's and the pane
  script's each run in their own process's locale, and the reader in the C locale. So a byte that one locale classes as
  a control character and another does not (a C1 byte, 0x80 to 0x9f, under a UTF-8 locale), or a control byte in the
  physical path alone, can leave a field `pending` for good. It fails closed: such a row holds, and is never released.
  Before the first edit no `.workdir` on the fleet box held a C1 byte.
- `relative-workdir-second-cd-does-not-enter`: the launch command asks `cd '<wd>'` twice, and for a relative `.workdir`
  the second `cd` resolves against the directory the first one entered, so that row's next respawn, made with the
  stored value, execs nothing, or execs in another directory. `cmd_start` and ws-add store an absolute spelling, so
  only an older row can hold a relative one. Before the first edit no `.workdir` on the fleet box was relative. On any
  other deployment, restarting such a row with `start`, which stores the absolute spelling, or purging it clears it.
- W2's standing set, unchanged: `human-gated-removals-ask-no-mounts`, `vanished-checkout-arms-ask-no-mounts` and the
  rest of §3.10's list, but for the carries closed or narrowed below.

**Closed and narrowed carries.**
- Closed, each verified at the tip by this spec's prose suite:
  - `no-whole-child-mount-ask-before-step-3`: the rung's mount hold covers the whole child. Owned asks it at the tail's
    start, and the re-ask asks it before every standing forced removal, so a mount anywhere under the child is asked
    before step 3's loop.
  - §7 items 1 to 3 and 5 to 8: `r31-repointed-alias-resolves-complete`, `r31-bind-mount-spelling-resolves-complete`,
    `r54-recorded-basis-dev-ino-ancestry`, `proc-symlink-row-places-at-ccds-cwd`,
    `unres-false-detail-for-row-that-is-the-child`, `double-slash-remedy-wordings` and
    `owned-main-checkout-ambient-realpath`.
- Narrowed, not closed:
  - `owned-to-worktree-remove-window` (§7 item 4): narrowed by the identity compares and the fresh re-asks, as its row
    says. Closing it is a later wave, and no scheduled wave closes it.
  - `audit-normalise-has-no-mount-ask`: the worktree half is asked now, because the ladder's rung holds a mount under
    the child at the audit. The clips leaf's half stands, forwarded to workspace lifecycle.
  - `registry-row-pass-carries-no-bound`: child reclamation's carry. The identity walk is bounded and the gone rows'
    git reads are not, so §7 item 9 reads `Built (W3), git reads standing`.
  - `in-use-probe-misses-another-mount` (§7 item 20): its worktree half is built. Its temp-root half was W4's, and
    stands.
  - `worktree-ask-to-force-window`: narrowed by the re-ask.
```

  - `<n:conditional-departures>` lists, backticked, `legacy-count-expire-half-fenced` when the expire count is 0 and `ws-add-seed-subsumed-by-spawn-pending` when ws-add's seed count is 0, joined with "and". With neither, it is `none`.
- **(d) `<n:found>`.** For each task (0 to 12) whose ledger entry names a slug in `FOUND_WHILE_BUILDING`, write one bullet, `- Task <k>: \`<slug>\`[, \`<slug>\`].`. Follow it with one plain sentence per slug that says what changed, measured against the tip. Write them in task order. If `FOUND_WHILE_BUILDING` is empty, write the one bullet `- No task recorded a slug beyond the departures and residuals above.`
- **(e) Forbidden phrases.** `collect-lane-prose.test.ts`'s note slice runs to the end of the file, so its forbidden phrases must not appear: not "Left open for the coordinator's ruling", and not "that call's late answer is dropped."

```bash
git diff --numstat -- "$CON" | awk '{print "removed=" $2}'                                                    # removed=0
```


Expected: PASS, 20 of 20 (foreground, timeout 600000 ms).

- [ ] **Step 7: Mutation table.** Each row is ONE Bash call from the workspace root, run in the foreground with a timeout of 600000 ms. Each call:
  1. copies the file to the gitignored scratch `$S`;
  2. applies the edit;
  3. runs the suite;
  4. restores the file with `cp` and proves the restore with `cmp`.

The red texts were drafted, not measured, so measure them. If the edit prints `anchor missing` or `section missing`, find the text as it stands with `grep -n`, adjust the row's pattern, and run the row again. Never weaken a case.

Three editors are used, and each exits 1 when its anchor is absent:
- `ED` replaces in the whole file;
- `SEC` replaces only inside a section, from FROM to the first UNTIL after it (UNTIL `''` means the end of the file). §3.10 spells several of the same phrases, so every §4.12 or note mutation goes through `SEC`;
- `FED` replaces only inside one ccd function.

The fourth argument of each is the regex flags.

**(4b) The start-line table, `_lc_json`'s length, and the hunks at or before line 19162 of `ccd/ccd` (R41).** Write two scratch scripts once. Each takes its inputs as file paths, so (4h) can feed it a seeded copy. `starts.sh` is W2's, plus two additions: a `kind` argument, so `ccd/ccrc` skips the `_lc_json` checks, and a listing of the head-only functions at or before the bound.

```bash
L=.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-20-path-identity-w3-worktree-identity/task14
cat > "$L/starts.sh" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# base head bound [kind] [allowed] -> the start line of every function that starts at or before line bound of base (the
# corpus bound, MAXREF), every function only head defines that starts at or before bound, and for kind ccd (the default)
# _lc_json's length and plan-a's cited line 4896; rc 1 on any move, a vanished function, or a head-only function at or
# before bound that allowed (comma-separated) does not name; rc 2 on a bound that is no line number
b="$1" h="$2" w="${3-}" kind="${4-ccd}" allowed=",${5-},"; rc=0
[[ "$w" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || { echo "W=$w is no line number"; exit 2; }
echo "W=$w"
fns() { awk -v w="$2" '/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\(\) *\{/{n=$0; sub(/\(\).*/,"",n); if (w == "" || NR <= w) print n, NR}' "$1" | LC_ALL=C sort -k1,1; }
fns "$b" "$w" > "$b.starts"; fns "$b" "" > "$b.all"; fns "$h" "" > "$h.starts"
LC_ALL=C join "$b.starts" "$h.starts" | awk '$2 != $3 { print "MOVED", $0; bad = 1 } END { print (bad ? "starts MOVED" : "starts unmoved"); exit bad }' || rc=1
v=$(LC_ALL=C join -v1 "$b.starts" "$h.starts"); [[ -z "$v" ]] || { echo "VANISHED $v"; rc=1; }
while read -r n l; do
  (( l <= w )) || continue
  echo "HEAD-ONLY $n $l"; [[ "$allowed" == *",$n,"* ]] || { echo "UNEXPECTED $n"; rc=1; }
done < <(LC_ALL=C join -v2 "$b.all" "$h.starts")
if [[ "$kind" == ccd ]]; then
  len() { awk '/^_lc_json\(\) *\{/{s=NR} s && /^}/{print NR - s + 1; exit}' "$1"; }
  lb=$(len "$b"); lh=$(len "$h"); echo "_lc_json lines base=$lb head=$lh"; [[ -n "$lb" && "$lb" == "$lh" ]] || rc=1
  if [[ "$(sed -n 4896p "$b")" == "$(sed -n 4896p "$h")" ]]; then echo "line 4896 unchanged"; else echo "line 4896 CHANGED"; rc=1; fi
fi
exit "$rc"
EOF
cat > "$L/hunks-above.sh" <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# base head bound -> every -U0 hunk that changes a line at or before line bound, or inserts before it, as "a,b +c,d ok|SHIFT";
# rc 1 when any is not in place. A hunk that only inserts after line bound lies outside the frozen zone and is not listed
b="$1" h="$2" bound="$3"
git diff --no-index --no-color -U0 -- "$b" "$h" | awk -v bound="$bound" '
  /^@@ / { o = $2; n = $3; sub(/^-/, "", o); sub(/^\+/, "", n); split(o, x, ","); split(n, y, ",")
           a = x[1] + 0; bb = (2 in x) ? x[2] + 0 : 1; c = y[1] + 0; d = (2 in y) ? y[2] + 0 : 1
           if (a < bound || (a == bound && bb > 0)) { k++; v = (a == c && bb == d) ? "ok" : "SHIFT"; if (v != "ok") bad++; print a "," bb " +" c "," d " " v } }
  END { print "hunks at or before line " bound ": " k + 0 ", not in place: " bad + 0; exit (bad > 0) }'
EOF
BASE=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main); git show "$BASE":ccd/ccd > "$L/ccd.base"; git show HEAD:ccd/ccd > "$L/ccd.head"
MAXREF=$(for f in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-09-graphify-compaction-card-design.md docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-10-graphify-compaction-card-plan-a.md README.md; do grep -ohE ':[0-9]+([-–][0-9]+)?' "$f"; done | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | awk -v max="$(wc -l < "$L/ccd.base")" '$1 <= max' | sort -n | tail -1); echo "MAXREF=$MAXREF"; printf '%s\n' "$MAXREF" > "$L/maxref"; [ "$MAXREF" = 19162 ] && echo "MAXREF is R41's" || echo "MAXREF other than 19162: STOP maxref-unmeasured"
s=$(grep -n '^_plat_epoch_ms() {' "$L/ccd.base" | cut -d: -f1); slot=$(awk -v a="$s" 'NR>a && /^}$/{print NR+1; exit}' "$L/ccd.base")
seed=$(grep -nF '_reg_set "$id" workdir "$wt";   _reg_set "$id" uuid "$uuid"' "$L/ccd.base" | cut -d: -f1)
pf=$(grep -nF '"mode":"reclaim","childOf":%s,"generation":%s,' "$L/ccd.base" | cut -d: -f1)
echo "slot=$slot [$(sed -n "${slot}p" "$L/ccd.base")] seed=$seed printf=$pf"; printf '%s %s %s\n' "$slot" "$seed" "$pf" > "$L/anchors"
printf '%s\n' "2,1 +2,1 ok" "$slot,1 +$slot,1 ok" "$seed,1 +$seed,1 ok" "$pf,2 +$pf,2 ok" "hunks at or before line $MAXREF: 4, not in place: 0" > "$L/hunks.expected"
bash "$L/starts.sh" "$L/ccd.base" "$L/ccd.head" "$MAXREF" ccd _plat_workdirid_pane; echo "starts rc=$?"

diff "$L/hunks.expected" "$L/hunks.head"; echo "exact rc=$?"
```

```bash

// base head -> _spawn_start differs from base by R7's two launch statements alone (R47): the two inserted

  const L = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8').split('\n');
  const s = L.findIndex((l) => /^_spawn_start\(\) *\{/.test(l));
  if (s < 0) return null;
  const e = L.findIndex((l, i) => i > s && /^}/.test(l));
  return e < 0 ? null : L.slice(s, e + 1);
};
const b = fn(base), h = fn(head);
if (!b || !h) { console.log('_spawn_start MISSING'); process.exit(1); }
const PEND = '_spawn_workdirid_pending "$id" "$workdir" || :';
const FRAG = '$(_plat_workdirid_pane "$REG" "$id" "$workdir")';

const pend = h.flatMap((l, i) => (l.trim() === PEND ? [i] : []));

let frags = 0, fragOk = true;
const back = h.filter((_, i) => !pend.includes(i)).map((l) => {
  const k = l.indexOf(FRAG);
  if (k < 0) return l;
  frags++;
  const t = l.slice(k + FRAG.length).startsWith(TAIL) ? TAIL.length : 0;
  if (!l.slice(0, k).endsWith("cd '$workdir' && ") || t === 0 || !l.slice(k + FRAG.length + t).startsWith('exec env ') || l.indexOf(FRAG, k + 1) >= 0) fragOk = false;
  return l.slice(0, k) + l.slice(k + FRAG.length + t);
});
const same = back.length === b.length && back.every((l, i) => l === b[i]);
console.log(`pending lines ${pend.length}${pendOk ? ', each directly above _tmux_new_session' : ', NOT each directly above _tmux_new_session'}`);
console.log(`fragments ${frags}${fragOk ? ", each between cd '$workdir' && and true; cd '$workdir' && exec env" : ', MISPLACED'}`);
console.log(same ? 'the rest of _spawn_start is byte-identical to the base' : 'the rest of _spawn_start DIFFERS from the base');
console.log(`lines base=${b.length} head=${h.length}`);
process.exit(pendOk && frags === 2 && fragOk && same ? 0 : 1);
EOF

awk '/^_spawn_start\(\) *\{/{f=1} f{print} f&&/^}/{exit}' "$L/ccd.base" > "$L/spawn.base"; awk '/^_spawn_start\(\) *\{/{f=1} f{print} f&&/^}/{exit}' "$L/ccd.head" > "$L/spawn.head"
git diff --no-index --no-color -U0 -- "$L/spawn.base" "$L/spawn.head" | grep '^@@' | sed -E 's/^@@ -([0-9]+)(,([0-9]+))? \+([0-9]+)(,([0-9]+))? @@.*/-\1,\3 +\4,\6/'
```

The existing test files that are licensed only for their timing or their Darwin prefix change no assertion. Write the hunk-licence script once:

```bash
L=.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-20-path-identity-w3-worktree-identity/task14
cat > "$L/test-hunks.mjs" <<'EOF'
// base head [cases] [block] [helper] -> each -U0 hunk of one test file, classed against its licence (R41, R50, R51, P13,
// P19): `case <id>` lies inside an it( whose title starts with one of cases ('|'-separated); `block` lies inside the
// helper that starts on the line holding block, through the first line ending "`;"; `helper` is a pure insert outside
// every it( whose added text names helper; `prefix` removes and adds only lines naming a Darwin prefix, shim or stub,
// comments or blank lines, or is an insert naming the shared fixture. Anything else is UNLICENSED. Any removed or added
// line holding `expect(` is EXPECT. rc 1 on either, or on no hunk at all
import fs from 'node:fs';
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
const [base, head, casesArg = '', blockArg = '', helper = ''] = process.argv.slice(2);
const cases = casesArg ? casesArg.split('|') : [];
const B = fs.readFileSync(base, 'utf8').split('\n');
const OPEN = /^\s*(it|test|describe)(\.[A-Za-z]+(\([^)]*\))?)*\(/;
const ranges = [];
B.forEach((l, i) => {
  const m = /^\s*it(?:\.[A-Za-z]+(?:\([^)]*\))?)*\(\s*['"`](.*)$/.exec(l);
  if (!m) return;
  const id = cases.find((c) => m[1].startsWith(c));
  let e = B.length;
  for (let j = i + 1; j < B.length; j++) if (OPEN.test(B[j])) { e = j; break; }
  ranges.push({ kind: id ? `case ${id}` : 'other-it', s: i + 1, e });
});
if (blockArg) {
  const s = B.findIndex((l) => l.includes(blockArg));
  const e = s < 0 ? -1 : B.findIndex((l, j) => j >= s && /`;\s*$/.test(l));
  if (s >= 0 && e >= 0) ranges.push({ kind: 'block', s: s + 1, e: e + 1 });
}
const r = spawnSync('git', ['diff', '--no-index', '--no-color', '-U0', '--', base, head], { encoding: 'utf8' });
if (r.status !== 0 && r.status !== 1) { console.log('diff unmeasured'); process.exit(2); }
const hunks = []; let cur = null;
for (const l of r.stdout.split('\n')) {
  const m = /^@@ -(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? \+(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? @@/.exec(l);
  if (m) { cur = { a: +m[1], b: m[2] === undefined ? 1 : +m[2], c: +m[3], d: m[4] === undefined ? 1 : +m[4], rem: [], add: [] }; hunks.push(cur); continue; }
  if (!cur) continue;
  if (l.startsWith('-')) cur.rem.push(l.slice(1)); else if (l.startsWith('+')) cur.add.push(l.slice(1));
}
const PREFIX = /DARWIN|_SHIMS\b|_STUB\b|_plat_devino|_plat_btime|_ws_expire_lsof|DEVINO_SHIM/;
const COMMENT = /^\s*(\/\/|\/\*|\*)/;
const within = (h, g) => (h.b === 0 ? h.a >= g.s && h.a <= g.e : h.a >= g.s && h.a + h.b - 1 <= g.e);
let bad = 0, exp = 0;
for (const h of hunks) {
  const all = [...h.rem, ...h.add];
  let cls = 'UNLICENSED';
  const g = ranges.find((x) => x.kind !== 'other-it' && within(h, x));
  if (g) cls = g.kind;
  else if (helper && h.b === 0 && !ranges.some((x) => x.kind !== 'block' && h.a >= x.s && h.a < x.e) && h.add.join('\n').includes(helper)) cls = 'helper';
  else if (all.length && all.every((l) => PREFIX.test(l) || COMMENT.test(l) || l.trim() === '')) cls = 'prefix';
  else if (h.b === 0 && h.add.join('\n').includes('worktreeIdentityFixture')) cls = 'prefix (import)';
  if (cls === 'UNLICENSED') bad++;
  const e = all.filter((l) => l.includes('expect(')).length;
  if (e) { exp += e; cls += ' EXPECT'; }
  console.log(`${h.a},${h.b} +${h.c},${h.d} ${cls}`);
}
console.log(`hunks ${hunks.length}, unlicensed ${bad}, expect lines touched ${exp}`);
process.exit(bad || exp || hunks.length === 0 ? 1 : 0);
EOF
BASE=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)
for f in ccd-reclaim-tail-mounts ccd-ws-collect-reprove ccd-child-reclaim-verb ccd-child-tmproot-witness-drop ccd-collect-aside-settle ccd-tmproot-drop-propagation; do git show "$BASE":server/test/$f.test.ts > "$L/$f.base"; done
node "$L/test-hunks.mjs" "$L/ccd-reclaim-tail-mounts.base" server/test/ccd-reclaim-tail-mounts.test.ts 'N1:|N2:|C1:|C2:|C3:|C4:|C6:|E1:' '' MOUNT_AT_ASK; echo "tail-mounts rc=$?"
node "$L/test-hunks.mjs" "$L/ccd-ws-collect-reprove.base" server/test/ccd-ws-collect-reprove.test.ts 'a table that cannot be read'; echo "reprove rc=$?"
node "$L/test-hunks.mjs" "$L/ccd-child-reclaim-verb.base" server/test/ccd-child-reclaim-verb.test.ts '' 'const darwin = '; echo "verb rc=$?"
for f in ccd-child-tmproot-witness-drop ccd-collect-aside-settle ccd-tmproot-drop-propagation; do node "$L/test-hunks.mjs" "$L/$f.base" "server/test/$f.test.ts"; echo "$f rc=$?"; done
```

```markdown
Wave 4 of 4 of the path-identity programme: the spec's W3 (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-12-path-identity-design.md`, section 4; as built in 4.12). Safety subject: which tree `git worktree remove` may delete.

**Deploy class: `ccd/ccd` plus one server string. The fleet box moves first**, which is `ccrc rollout`'s default order (no `--server-first`). `ccd/ccrc` changes by one byte-identical platform-block line that ccrc's own code never calls. `server/src/wsaudit.ts` changes one sentence. The PWA, the agent and `shared/` do not change. No frame field and no field the server reads changes: ids still come from `*.uuid` names only. The reclaim audit document gains two additive keys, `legacyRows` (the other rows whose field is in a `legacy-*` state) and `pendingRows` (those whose field reads `pending`; a field that reads `unmeasured` is in neither, and it holds the child), with no server reader{{C1 (a): "; the expire document gains the same pair"}}. No `FLEET_PROTO` bump and no coord.db migration.
- Rollback: an older ccd ignores `$REG/<id>.workdirid`, and its `_reg_purge` loop still unlinks it.
- Re-upgrade: a field written before the rollback either matches its logical spelling or reads stale or legacy. A field that went stale under the older ccd can only add a placement or a hold; it never releases a row.
- The window between the two boxes: the old server shows the old `worktree-remove-failed` sentence, which is true of every failure the old ccd emits and slightly incomplete for a new ccd's cwd refusals. Nothing is decided on it.

### What changed (one commit per task)
- Task 1: today's holds on the rows rung, the record, owned and the tail, frozen as an add-only fence, re-run after every later task.
- Task 2: one bounded identity walk (`_ws_reclaim_idwalk`, `WS_RECLAIM_WALK_S=5`) and one identity rule (`_ws_ident_compose`, `_ws_ident_eq`, `_ws_path_ident`).
- Task 3: the rows rung places rows by device and inode ancestry, holds a mount at or under the child, refuses a link into `/proc` by raw target or walked position, and the walk's knob joins the collect budget (78 s, 83 s at the widest grace).
- Task 4: the entry field `$REG/<id>.workdirid`: one grammar, one reader, one in-pane composer in the platform block, and the `start` and ws-add seeds.
- Task 5: every spawn writes `pending` before it starts the pane, and the pane records where it entered after its `cd` and before `exec`.
- Task 6: a row's recorded entry places it against the child, and only ever adds a placement or a hold; the reclaim document's `legacyRows` and `pendingRows`.
- Task 7: a nested checkout that is a gone row's recorded entry holds the child.
- Task 8: the main-checkout and record checks refuse a tree by its identity (`-ef`), and never grant one.
- Task 9: one cwd probe, `_ws_cwd_users`, by path or by device and inode, bounded by `WS_CWD_USERS_SCAN_S`; ws-expire moves onto it.
- Task 10: a process working inside the tree stops the forced removal at step 3 and step 4; the post-kill wait only waits.
- Task 11: each standing forced removal re-proves the tree, the rows and the main checkout first.
- Task 12: the remedies say "restore" a link, never "re-point" it, and the `..` detail is true of a row that is the child.
- Task 13: the spec's 4.12 and section 7 cells; the contract's W3 note; the prose test.

`ccd/ccd` (restamped with `bash ccd/ccrc restamp ccd/ccd`); `ccd/ccrc` (one platform-block line, byte-identical to ccd's); `ccd/contexts.tsv` (nine rows: one K, one C2, seven C4; the cross-context count unchanged at {{BASELINE}}); one sentence in `server/src/wsaudit.ts`; CLAUDE.md's load-flake bullet; fourteen new files under `server/test/`, and {{M}} existing ones edited only where the plan names them; the spec's 4.12 and ten section 7 cells; the contract's W3 note; this plan. A mount planted before the verb is therefore caught earlier. N1, C1, C3, C4, C6 and E1 (first ask) and N2 and C2 (second ask) now plant through one in-file helper, `MOUNT_AT_ASK`, immediately before the ask they test. ```bash
```

```bash
lines.push(fs.readFileSync(prose, "utf8"));
process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ fromId: id, fromUuid: uuid, toId: "coordinator", runId: Number(run), kind: "status", subject: "wave-done", body: lines.join("\n"), artifacts: [] }));
' "$id" "$uuid" "$RUN" "$SUITE" "$FAILURE" "$TIP" "$PR" "$PHASE" "$L/wave-done-prose.md" > "$L/wave-done.json"
```

### Substantive departures, one number each

Each entry, filled at the fix round, names what the spec said, what the code at the tip does, and the ruling.
- **D-6124** (Tasks 4, 5; R1, R2) `workdirid-pending-form`: the spec's §4.3 gives the entry field one grammar, the v1 line, and reads every other state as legacy. At the tip it has two forms: the v1 line and `v1<TAB>pending<TAB><at_ms><TAB>-<TAB><logical>`. The parent writes the pending form through `_spawn_workdirid_pending` directly before each of `_spawn_start`'s two `_tmux_new_session` calls (the primary and the retry), and the pane's fragment (`_plat_workdirid_pane`) replaces it after its `cd` succeeds and before `exec`. A pending write that fails unlinks the field, so a stale valid field never survives it. The one reader, `_ws_workdirid_read`, answers `pending` (rc 2) when the line's logical spelling equals the row's current `.workdir`, a stale pending line reads legacy, and the rows rung holds the child unmeasured (`unpend`) with a detail that names the row and the remedy. Ruling R1 and R2: this is how the spec's "failure to replace the field remains a hold" (§4.11) is built. The hold's reach is named in `rows-rung-holds-mask-later-terminal-words` and the residual `pending-row-holds-every-child-box-wide`.
- **D-6125** (Task 4; R3) `workdirid-unreadable-holds`: the spec names a missing, unparseable or link field legacy. At the tip a field that is not a regular file (a directory, a FIFO), or that cannot be read, answers `unmeasured`, a hold, as `.workdir`'s own unreadable rule does; the reader checks the type before it opens the file and reads a bounded number of bytes. Ruling R3: the reader's states stay distinct (`valid`, `pending`, `legacy-absent`, `legacy-stale`, `legacy-unparseable`, `legacy-link`, `unmeasured`), with no overloaded answer.
- **D-6126** (Task 3; R13) `rows-walk-second-mountinfo-reader`: the spec's §4.5 step 3 asks a mount hold, and the mount table had one reader, `_ws_collect_mounts_clear`, through `_ws_collect_mountinfo`'s path seam. At the tip the identity walk reads the table too, as a declared second reader through the same seam: it holds the child unmeasured when a mount point lies at or under it, or a mount on its device has a root at or under its device-relative path (`//deleted` included), and a device on which mountinfo and the stat of the child disagree fails closed. On Darwin the caller does not ask. Ruling R13: a source pin names exactly two readers, and a parity case holds the walk's mount-point answer equal to `_ws_collect_mounts_clear`'s on the same fixture tables.
- **D-6127** (Tasks 2, 3; R15) `unproc-also-by-walked-position`: the spec's §4.8 m1 refuses a link whose raw target matches `^/+proc(/|$)`. At the tip a row is also refused `unproc` when the walk's link-free position enters `/proc` through a relative target, and the clause reads "under /proc, or one reached through a link into /proc" (R15's words with "one" added so the clause stays grammatical). Ruling R15: each arm is pinned apart, and the mutation that survives because of the other arm is named (W8, W9).
- **D-6128** (Tasks 3, 11; P19) `w2-mount-asks-shadowed-by-the-reask`: W2's §3.10 mount asks at step 3 and step 4 of the tail were the first to catch a mount under the child. At the tip three askers read the mount table first through the rows rung: the ladder's in-lock recompute, `_ws_reclaim_owned` at the tail's start, and the re-ask before every standing forced removal. W2's step-3 and step-4 asks are now a backstop for a mount that appears in the instant after the re-ask. Ruling P19: W2's behavioural cases moved their plants to that instant (six plants in `ccd-reclaim-tail-mounts.test.ts`, no `expect(` line changed), and their assertions are unchanged.
- **D-6129** (Task 8; R17) `ladder-main-checkout-ef`: the spec's §4.8 puts `-ef` in the owned arm only. At the tip the ladder's own main-checkout compare gains it too, beside its string compare, and refuses `not-a-workspace` "under another spelling". Ruling R17: an add-only refusal disjunct, part of the ladder consent.
- **D-6130** (Task 8; R67; narrowed at the fix round, review 790 F1) `record-main-hit-keeps-the-terminal-refusal`: the spec's §4.8 and R31 make `_ws_reclaim_record` use identity only to refuse, with the first (main) stanza excluded from the rc-2 rule. At the tip, once git's main stanza names the tree by its STRING, that is a hit, `RECLAIM_REC_MAIN` is set and no later stanza's answer counts (each is still compared by `-ef` before the main guard skips it, so `record-ef-has-no-deadline` reaches it), so the ladder keeps the terminal `not-a-workspace` and owned its rc 1, rather than the retryable `unmeasured` and rc 2. R67 ruled that narrowing of R31's rc-2 rule. This entry first said "by its string or by `-ef`", and so does the plan's body, which is not edited: R31's and R67's text (about line 333), Task 8's (about lines 945, 10785, 11535, 12213 and 12230) and Task 13's drafted spec text (about line 18192) each say "no later stanza is asked", and this entry corrects them all. That was wrong for `-ef`, because identity never makes a hit (§4.8, §4.12, and the header of `_ws_reclaim_record`). A main stanza that names the tree only by `-ef` (a bind spelling, for example) sets `RECLAIM_REC_MAIN` and no hit, so the reader answers 1, the ladder refuses (the common-directory check before its record branch can refuse first with `containment-unproven`, and what git answers there for a bind spelling is unmeasured; past it, with the terminal `no-worktree-record` whose detail ("has no worktree record") is false where `_ws_reclaim_no_record` reads every admin entry and none names the tree, or with the retryable `unmeasured` where an admin entry cannot be read or names the tree), and owned answers 2 (`worktree-remove-failed`). That shape is refused either way and nothing grants on it. Where such a first stanza is joined by a stanza that hits by string, the reader answers 0 with `RECLAIM_REC_MAIN` set and the refusal stands. Ruling (R82 F1, text and comments only): the keep needs a string hit, the comments in the record reader and the ladder and spec §4.12 say so, and the shape is the named residual `record-main-by-another-spelling-reads-no-worktree-record`, built into the spec and the contract note by commit d5019cae7. Fix C (commit 45677012e) widens the ladder's answers there to the set above, in the record reader's comment and spec §4.12. No code or return code changed.
- **D-6131** (Task 8; R31, R71) `record-by-another-spelling-reads-unmeasured`: REC-2's shape. The spec's §4.8 and R31's rc-2 rule make the record reader answer 2 when only a stanza naming the tree under another spelling records the standing child. At the tip the ladder's terminal `no-worktree-record` (whose detail was false: git does record the tree) therefore becomes the retryable `unmeasured`, and owned answers 2. Ruling R71: it is a refusal either way, no token is minted and nothing is released.
- **D-6132** (Task 11; R29) `reappeared-tree-refuses`: the spec's §4.7 re-ask compares each standing leaf's identity with the recorded one and re-proves owned whole. At the tip a tree that owned proved absent and that stands again at a forced removal is refused as `worktree-remove-failed`. Ruling R29.
- **D-6133** (Task 10; R23) `cwd-wait-only-waits`: the spec's §4.6 asks the cwd probe inside the post-kill wait. At the tip the wait asks it of the tree (read early from the tombstone; a failed read passes no tree) and only waits: it ends when nobody is inside or at its bound, and never refuses. The gates are the asks at step 3 and step 4. Ruling R23.
- **D-6134** (Task 10; R23, R24) `cwd-refusal-reuses-worktree-remove-failed`: the probe is asked of the child before each standing nested checkout's `keep_of` and its forced removal, and before the child's. At the tip an in-use or unmeasured answer fails the reclaim or the expiry as `worktree-remove-failed`, retryable, with the tree, the branch and the breadcrumb kept and the detail cut to 300 bytes by `_ws_leaf_why_line`. Ruling R24: no new word, and the server's one sentence for it (`server/src/wsaudit.ts`, the wave's only server change, a string) now ends "or a process still works inside it".
- **D-6135** (Task 11; R29) `reask-words-follow-the-owned-call`: the spec's §4.7 re-ask re-proves owned whole and says what it re-proves, not which word a failure carries. At the tip the re-ask maps owned's rc 1 to `containment-refuted`, a new emission site in the tail that ws-expire shares, and everything else (an identity that differs or cannot be measured, and owned's rc 2) to `worktree-remove-failed`. Both keep the tree, the branch and the breadcrumb and cut their detail. Ruling R29.
