### Reserved: the wave-time block (R40, R48, R73)

Six single entries were issued with the block, and a seventh, `D-6432`, and an eighth, `D-6433`, were added by R82 after them. Each is defined at the fix round that names a departure found during the wave: a reserved line is rewritten in place to that departure's tasks, rulings, slug and text, keeping its number. If workspace-lifecycle refuses R45's request, `legacy-count-expire-half-fenced` takes the next of them at that ruling; it has no slot of its own (R73). It did not arise: R45's expire half was consented, and both halves were built.
- **D-6155** (Tasks 3, 12; R76, R82) `double-slash-rows-placed-by-identity-pins-move`: the spec's §4.5 places rows by device and inode ancestry in addition to the strings, and bash's `pwd -P` keeps a leading `//` of a link target, so a row spelled through such a link, or a row under a child whose own workdir resolves that way, was unplaced by strings alone: a retryable hold that cannot clear on Linux. At the tip the rows rung places those rows by identity, and where one truly lies inside the child the ladder answers the terminal `containment-unproven` (fresh) and a resumed tail answers `containment-refuted`, in place of the retryable `unmeasured`. R76 licensed it as one follow-up commit (66a94dbf7), on the Task 3 review's four conditions: six pins moved to one platform-independent expectation (the ladder's two cases expect `containment-unproven`; the verb tail's two fresh-arm cases expect `containment-unproven` and its two resumed-tail cases `containment-refuted`), every other assertion, survival assertions included, byte-identical; the resolved-`//` unplaced arm stays measured for a row outside the child (a new case in `ccd-rows-rung-identity.test.ts` pins `unmeasured` and the unplaced clause); a positive pin of the new placement with a mutation row that moves 4i's A request below the two `//` continues; and the plan-text records under D-6143 and D-6152. No row is released and no refusal becomes a pass, so the add-only rule holds, and the fence's F11.L move (`unmeasured` to `containment-unproven`) is inside its allowed list. Both test files joined the boundary for exactly these edits, and child-reclamation's acknowledgement is the coordinator's. The fix round accepts R76's two files as made and names what they carry beyond the six pins (R82 F3): `ladder-double-slash-child-loop-names-the-identity-placed-row` (the ladder's re-plant of `demo-other` outside the child, which keeps the loop's M1 meaning after R76 made the inside row a refusal) and `verb-tail-describe-title-still-says-cannot-be-placed` (the verb tail's describe title, now true, and its "nothing was pinned" and "no breadcrumb" assertions moved above the early return, which strengthens them). The ladder's comment at the loop now reads "…outranks the hold that outside row raises, where it raises one" (parked item 3, commit 127d0ecc6). R82 F4 adds one assertion (commit bddf40edc): the rows rung's DS1 out case in `ccd-rows-rung-identity.test.ts` pins that the reworded remedy is printed (first as `toContain(REMEDY_2)`; commit c35c9c90b, A1 M3, folded it into the `UNPLACED` assertion as `registry row(s) demo-far ${UNPLACED} ${REMEDY_2}`, the adjacency `ccd-worktree-identity-wordings.test.ts` pins it in); with `restore a link` re-worded to `re-point a link` in `ccd/ccd` (the remedy's second clause) the case reds.
- **D-6156** (Task 9; PF-2, C1) `cwd-probe-holds-a-double-slash-physical-root`: the spec's §4.6 and P12 have the adapter resolve the tree's parent with `_ws_dir_physical` and hand the physical spelling to the probe. At the tip `_ws_dir_physical` answers a `//`-leading physical path for a directory reached through a link whose target begins with `//` (bash keeps it; `//` and `//tmp` given directly keep it too), and the probe's plain-path gate refuses `*//*`, so the answer is unmeasured, a hold, where the old probe compared that spelling against kernel-printed cwds (which never begin with `//`) and answered nobody. Ruling PF-2: build P12 as written, fail closed, report the slug; the coordinator accepted it as a named departure. C1 narrowed it: the probe itself now collapses a `//` parent (D-6159), and the adapter's `*//*` gate still holds a `//`-leading physical root. It was measured at the mechanism, not end to end through the adapter.
- **D-6157** (Task 9; R77, R78) `cwd-probe-confirms-a-vanished-link-by-a-second-read`: the spec's R21 skips a process only on ENOENT or ESRCH of its own cwd link or stat file, and confirms an ENOENT at the open of a link already read through the stat file. A process that exits between the readlink and the open answers ENOENT while its stat file still stands, so the probe answered unmeasured on 5 of 150 and 13 of 300 real `/proc` walks (the STOP `cwd-probe-open-races-a-process-exit`). It failed closed. R77 (as amended by R78) rules, with workspace-lifecycle's consent and seven conditions: the second readlink of `placed()` confirms on ENOENT alone (EACCES, another errno or a still-reading link answers 2); a vanished process link is asked through its threads to a bounded fixed point (`WS_CWD_USERS_SCAN_S`), its leader tid kept; R78 reads the link again after every pass and accepts only on a settled listing; a vanished thread link is skipped only under that read once more; the limits `cwd-probe-per-thread-cwd-unasked` and pid reuse are stated in the header. The commits are 44ed8a4fe and 63fa96afd. Measured (the probe's own python against `/proc`, read-only, `ccd`'s role played by the loop's bash; unmeasured answers per walks): at natural load 7/1000 for the first build, 0/1000 for R77 and for R78; under one fork loop 13/300, 2/300 and 0/500; under six fork loops 459/500, 288/500 and 2/100, R78's two being `placed()`'s EACCES, kept at 2 by ruling. `ccd-child-reclaim-leaf-moved-expire` ran 6/6 alone at natural load.
- **D-6158** (Task 9; R78) `cwd-probe-read-once-more-answers-eacces-for-a-reaped-pid`: R77's read once more, after a settled listing, answered unmeasured for a pid reaped between passes, because the read of a reaped pid's link answers EACCES. R78 (2) rules the per-pass read: EACCES exactly, then `gone()` ENOENT or ESRCH, answers the pid as gone, at the per-pass read only (`placed()`'s second readlink stays strict, by (c1)). Measured: one fork loop 2/500 unmeasured for R77 and 0/500 for R78; six fork loops 38/100 and 2/100.
- **D-6159** (Task 9; C1) `cwd-probe-collapses-a-double-slash-parent`: the spec's §4.6 compares the tree's physical spelling with the kernel's (and lsof's) one-slash paths, and D-6156 left a `//`-leading parent unmeasured. At the tip `_ws_cwd_users` collapses a leading `//` right after the parent resolve (one line, the T0 idiom of the walk's request), so a tree whose parent resolves through a `//` link holds through the probe itself, on Darwin too, as well as through the adapter. Ruling (the coordinator's, workspace-lifecycle's consent with four conditions; commit 637a7dbd3): red-first A17a and A17c (A17b, the one-slash CONTROL, green), and mutation M1 (the line deleted) reds both. No residual remains for it.

- **D-6160** (Task 6; C2) `rows-rung-pass-b-holds-an-unlisted-answer`: the plan's pass B reads the walk's answers by their words and has no arm for a word outside the vocabulary (T and A: `ok`, `gone`, `un`; P: `un`, `proc`, `clean`; M: `un`, `hold`, `clear`), so an unlisted word fell through and released the child. At the tip pass B of `_ws_reclaim_workdir_shared` has a `*)` default arm that holds the child unmeasured, with the unwalk clause naming the word as read. Ruling (C2, the same consent as D-6159; commit 637a7dbd3): red-first on "unlisted A, P, T and M word" (each CONTROL green), and mutation M2 (the arm removed) reds four; the words the cases did not list are the no-hold words (`T ok`, `P clean`, `M clear`), so no STOP.

It fails closed, the real walk emits no such word today, and the wording is the one the brief mandated.
- **D-6432** (Tasks 3, 5, 6; R1, R2, R9; review 790 F6; added by R82) `rows-rung-holds-mask-later-terminal-words`: the spec adds the rung's holds as add-only (§4.11) and does not say where in the answer order they stand. At the tip the rows rung runs before most of the ladder's later rungs (about `ccd/ccd` line 31737 at 0135c60b3) and before owned's later proofs (about line 33571 at 0135c60b3), and its new holds answer `unmeasured` (owned: rc 2) there. Those holds are `unpend`, `unfield`, `unrec`, `unwalk` and `unmount`. So a child that would have met a later terminal word answers the retryable one. Each is a refusal either way, and the add-only clause licenses the hold. R82 names it as a departure, as D-6161 does for the record reader. The `unpend` hold is box-wide by design (R1, R2, D-6124 rest on spec §4.12's `workdirid-pending-form` and `gone-row-with-pending-field-holds-despite-its-release-arms`, and the hold §4.11 asks for: a pending field names a pane that "may be entering anywhere", and the plan's own review step asks that its reach be stated as a box-wide hold until that session restarts). Narrowing it to rows placed by their strings would defeat the field, so it stands. Its consequences are the residual `pending-row-holds-every-child-box-wide` (spec §4.12, beside `gone-row-with-pending-field-holds-despite-its-release-arms`, which also now says it holds collection): a spawn's pending window can strike a tail in progress, whose re-ask re-runs the rung and answers `worktree-remove-failed` after the child's session was stopped (the server retries a reclaim); a pending window at the expiry verb's in-lock verdict makes that attempt restart from its audit (a fresh arm) or stay resumable (a resumed arm), and the verdict is final only where the breadcrumb stands unreadable (R82's Amendment 1 corrects its own first reading, which took the fallback line for the rule); and a row that stays pending for good holds every child until it is purged (fish on Linux, a control byte, a gone row's respawn). Workspace-lifecycle has received this reading as the pending hold's, not as new scope; it asks no server change and no arming decision, and W3 changes nothing on the server. The text is in commit e10108b67.
- **D-6433** (Task 11; review 790 F7; added by R82) `reask-re-proves-the-nested-checkouts-path`: the spec's §4.7 has the re-ask compare a standing nested checkout's identity with the one its proof recorded, and Task 11's text does not say that the compare resolves the checkout's parent through any link: `_ws_path_ident` refuses a link only at the leaf. So a checkout moved out of the child with a link left in its parent path measured the same and passed the compare, and `git worktree remove --force` removed it through the link. Measured at the base of this round (the unchanged `ccd/ccd`, case I5 in `ccd-reclaim-tail-window.test.ts`): the reclaim answered `reclaimed` with exit 0, the moved checkout's directory under the moved parent was gone and its branch deleted. At the tip `_ws_reclaim_reask`, directly after the checkout's identity compare and only when it was given a checkout, derives the tree's physical root afresh (`_ws_dir_physical`; a root that cannot be resolved sets `_WS_REASK_WHY` and answers 2) and runs `_ws_reclaim_nested_proven` on it and the checkout again. Only rc 0 with the second proof's own `_WS_NPROOF_GONE` 0 goes on; a refusal, or a checkout that vanished in the window, answers 2 (`worktree-remove-failed`), and the second values are tested before the first proof's `_WS_NPROOF_GONE`, `_WS_NPROOF_WHY` and `_WS_NPROOF_IDENT` are restored, which happens on every exit (the tail reads the first GONE after the removal). `cid` is never reassigned, the tail's call arguments and order are as before, and no pinned line moved. Ruling (R82 F7, the coordinator's, with workspace-lifecycle's consent and its conditions; commit 19bff9f3e): red-first case I5 (the parent moved out and a link planted in its place after the first proof, through `AT_NPROOF`) and case I6 (the checkout vanishes after the identity compare and before the second proof, through a fixture's wrap of `_ws_dir_physical` keyed on `FUNCNAME[1]`, never a shipped seam), each asserting that its hook ran. I6 was red at the base only at its CONTROL, because the window it times is new: the base's re-ask makes no direct `_ws_dir_physical` call, so the hook never fires there. Fix C (commit 6e386cc6c) keys I6's hook on the re-ask's SECOND ask, the re-ask directly before the checkout's forced removal, so the vanish lands in the window the hold guards; its CONTROL also asserts that it was the second ask. Measured again in fix C: mutation (a), the second proof deleted (fix C recorded no exact form for its mutant; the one recorded form is stated below, after case E5, and re-measures I5 and I6 with the same results), reds I5 on its outcome (`reclaimed`) and I6 at its CONTROL; mutation (b), the GONE hold dropped, reds I6 on its OUTCOME (the reclaim answers `reclaimed` and the tree's files are gone), where the hook at the first re-ask, in the build before fix C, had reddened it on its detail only (the second re-ask's identity measure refused that case anyway). The claim is a narrowed race, not an atomic proof: the second proof is one instant, and the window from the re-ask to git's own opendir stands, as `reask-to-opendir-window` says (spec §4.12, the contract note and the prose test's departure list name the slug; commit 74a44561c). `_ws_dir_physical`'s header counts the re-ask as its thirteenth caller, so Task 14's census check `grep -c 'its twelve callers' ccd/ccd` (plan bodies at about lines 439, 547, 13326 and 19411, which expect 2) now prints 0, and `its thirteen callers` prints 2. The reach of `ws-expire` (fix C, review 790's F-5 re-measured at commit 45677012e): `_ws_expire_locked` (`ccd/ccd` about :36877) ends in the shared `_ws_reclaim_tail` (about :36961); the tail's children loop (about :35687) passes the checkout to `_ws_reclaim_reask` at its two re-asks (about :35746 and :35756), so the second proof runs for the expiry verb too; the tail sets `_WS_RCL_CRUMB=true` at its top (about :35381) and `_ws_reclaim_failed_json` prints `"crumb":true` (about :33474-33482); and the server reads `crumb === true` first (`server/src/archivedExpiry.ts:324`) as a failed but resumable attempt, never a final one. So a refusal of the second proof under `ws-expire` is a resumable `worktree-remove-failed`. Case E5 in `ccd-reclaim-tail-window.test.ts` mirrors I5 for `ws-expire` (the coordinator's ruling after the fix round, test-only, built from the helpers that file already uses: `makeArchived`, `expireVerb`, `expiryToken`, `AT_NPROOF` and `nestedBelow`, with no new fixture machinery): it moves a nested checkout's parent out of the archived tree and plants a link in its place after the checkout's first proof, and it asserts that the hook ran. Red-first at the base of the round (the unchanged `ccd/ccd`): the expiry answered `expired` with exit 0 and removed the archived tree, and a temporary measurement showed the link gone, the moved parent standing without its `inner` checkout, and the branch `ws/nested` deleted, so the tail removed the moved checkout through the link. Built: `worktree-remove-failed` at the breadcrumb `expire:children`, its document's `crumb` true (asserted), which the server reads as resumable, the link standing, and the moved checkout, its files and its branch standing. Mutation (a), in one exact form, the same for I5, I6 and E5: `_ws_reclaim_reask`'s second-proof block deleted whole, nine lines of `ccd/ccd`, from `_ws_dir_physical "$wd" ||` (the tree's fresh physical root) through the save of the first proof's three globals, the second `_ws_reclaim_nested_proven` call, the verdict, the restore of the three globals, and the verdict's hold `[[ -z "$np_verdict" ]] || …` (it goes too, because `ccd` runs under `set -u` and the verdict variable is no longer assigned), leaving the function's final `return 0`. Measured with that one diff: I5 red on its outcome (`reclaimed`, the child's files gone), I6 red at its CONTROL (its hook sits on a call the mutant never makes), and E5 red on its outcome (`expired`, the archived tree's files gone). Each was restored with `git checkout -- ccd/ccd`. Fix C's records of mutation (a) say only "the second proof deleted" and name no exact form; this recorded form re-measures I5 and I6 with the same results as fix C's. Spec §4.12's bullet for the slug and the contract note say the reach.
